News.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content.

Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison, after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

In his sentencing remarks, judge Joel Bennathan described Brand as a "sexual predator" and criticised his "staggering arrogance".

The 51-year-old was sentenced to nine years for rape, with an additional 18 months, nine months and eight months for three counts of sexual assault.

The disgraced entertainer was found guilty of the charges involving four women between 2004 and 2009.

Brand did not react in the dock as he was sentenced. Before being taken down to the cells, he mouthed "I love you" to his wife Laura Brand, who was in the court.

The guidelines state offenders jailed for four years or more for some serious violent or sexual offences will be released at the two thirds point. In Brand's case that would be seven years.

Once released, he is likely to spend the rest of his sentence on licence and will have to abide by specific rules such as wearing a tag. His sentence will not be included in the early release scheme. Sex offenders, along with murderers, are exempt from the scheme.

The judge also paid tribute to the bravery of the women who gave evidence during the trial.

News.title: Brand's ex Jemima Goldsmith accuses him of violence and abuse against her
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content.

An ex-girlfriend of Russell Brand has accused him of "violence, coercive control and abuse" while the two were together.

Jemima Goldsmith, who dated the disgraced entertainer for roughly a year around 2014, alleged that she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.

In a lengthy statement on social media, the 52-year-old said she was "in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand's trial" and was "glad and relieved" he had "finally faced justice".

Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison earlier on Monday after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

He was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women.

The judge at the sentencing hearing told Brand that he harboured a "casual arrogant disregard to any woman's right to say no to you", while his fame meant he believed "you could act when you liked and how you liked".

TV producer Goldsmith is also the former wife of ex-Pakistani prime minister and cricketer Imran Khan, the daughter of late billionaire entrepreneur Sir James Goldsmith and sister of ex-Conservative government minister Zac Goldsmith.

The mother-of-two said she had chosen not to pursue legal recourse against Brand over the alleged violent incident in 2014 as she was "worried about the impact of the press attention on my then teenage children".

She wrote on X on Monday evening: "Whilst my pain in relation to this pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact."

Goldsmith said she had not seen nor spoken to Brand since 2014, but claimed to have assisted the journalists who exposed the allegations against him and had been willing to testify to his "abusiveness" were they sued.

In her statement, she also addressed reports of an injunction taken out by her and Brand in October 2015 that banned a woman, Szilvia Berki, from talking about an alleged assault by Brand at Goldsmith's home the prior year.

Goldsmith said on Monday that Berki had visited her house for roughly 30 minutes on 7 June 2014 to give Brand a massage, which she said did not end up taking place once she arrived.

News.title: What happened inside court as Brand was sentenced
News.content:
Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison, after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

In his sentencing remarks, judge Joel Bennathan said Brand harboured a "casual arrogant disregard to any woman's right to say no to you".

The 51-year-old was sentenced on Monday to nine years for rape, with an additional 18 months, nine months and eight months for sexual assault.

The former comedian was found guilty by a jury last week of the charges involving four women between 2004 and 2009.

Senior UK correspondent Sima Kotecha was inside the Southwark Crown Court during the sentencing.

More on this story.

News.title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
News.content:
A recent survey of 1,700 civil servants by the independent think tank Re:State found 76% of respondents thought it did not do a good job of tackling poor performers.

An ex-senior civil servant told the BBC that much of the Civil Service is culturally averse to performance management.

"Whitehall's known for ages it has to be less risk averse. Shrinking the Civil Service and the adoption of artificial intelligence technology make that more vital," they said.

"But don't underestimate the fear factor: fear of drawn-out grievances and fear of being accused of wasting taxpayers' money if the Civil Service was to do what big private sector firms do, which is cut to get rid of poor performers by offering some money and a settlement agreement."

A Defra spokesperson said: "Kashim Chowdhury abused the trust placed in him as a public servant and defrauded taxpayers out of almost Â£285,000. He will now rightly face the consequences for his actions.

"This conviction is the result of a thorough and painstaking investigation led by the Defra Counter Fraud and Investigations team. It sends a clear message that fraud against the public purse will not be tolerated and those responsible will be held to account."

The spokesperson said Defra would use "all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending on behalf of taxpayers".

Chowdhury's case also illustrates a wider issue.

He was engaged in what is being called "polygamous working", where people hold down several jobs secretly. Websites have even been set up offering people advice on how to keep their employers in the dark.

Its rise has been blamed on larger numbers of people working from home.

The government's National Fraud Initiative has identified 23 cases of "polygamous working" across London in its most recent report. It uncovered Â£500,000 of overpaid salaries over a period of a few months.

Alongside the fraud case, Chowdhury is involved in a legal dispute with his three siblings, who accuse him of ''bullying'' their mother into signing over half of her Â£2.1m home to him in the final days of her life. He denies it.

At times during his criminal trial, Chowdhury appeared confused by what he was hearing and blamed trauma for the web of lies he had spun. The jury took seven hours to reach their verdict and decided he was motivated by personal gain - stealing tens of thousands of pounds from the taxpayer.

Chowdhury now faces a significant custodial sentence.

News.title: Ground Force and Homes Under the Hammer star Tommy Walsh dies aged 69
News.content:
Tommy Walsh, the building and DIY expert known for starring on TV shows including Ground Force, Homes Under the Hammer and Challenge Tommy Walsh, has died at the age of 69.

Walsh started his career as a professional builder before rising to fame alongside Alan Titchmarsh and Charlie Dimmock on the BBC's Ground Force from 1997 to 2005.

He went on to also front popular programmes including Clean It, Fix It, and Cowboys and Angels, and joined daytime TV favourite Homes Under the Hammer in 2021.

Walsh's agent told BBC News he died "peacefully after a long illness surrounded by his family", and asked for privacy for the family.

Walsh was previously reported to have had surgery for throat cancer in 2022 and lung cancer in 2023.

News.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case - media reports
News.content:
A Massachusetts judge has denied motions to dismiss the murder case of Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of murdering her three children, according to local US media.

The judge's ruling comes after Clancy's defence team requested dismissal of the case after her first trial ended in a mistrial in September, when a 12-person jury failed to reach a consensus.

The ruling clears the way for prosecutors to pursue the case. They could reduce the charges in a potential second trial or dismiss them altogether.

Clancy has not denied killing her children in 2023, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors say the killings were intentional.

Clancy's defence team had filed three motions, including one to dismiss the case against her due to double jeopardy - a legal standard that says a person cannot be tried for the same crime twice.

Her lawyers argued that Judge William Sullivan, who presided over the August murder trial, acted prematurely when he declared a mistrial on 4 September, saying that he should have sought a viable alternative.

In his ruling on Monday, Sullivan said that a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject her to double jeopardy, according to Reuters news agency.

Sullivan also denied a motion to see records of the lone holdout juror in the case and to question the juror under oath.

The judge scheduled a hearing for 16 November to discuss when to hold a second trial. He has previously suggested it could begin in March.

News.title: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
News.content:
Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.

The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal.

About Â£50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock.

Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for Â£1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment.

Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday.

Access to funds was limited because of a tension between Gordon Brothers' dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected a relaxation of funds in the next two days.

Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, which included Halloween, but said this was Â£1.5m ahead of budget.

He said the business made a profit of Â£18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of Â£68m.

The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited.

News.title: Watch: Rare insight into France's drug gangs recruiting children to commit violence
News.content:
A BBC investigation has found one of Europe's most powerful drug gangs in France is recruiting teenage children from across the country to commit kidnap and murder.

Known as the "DZ Mafia", the gang won a bloody turf war against a rival group in Marseille during 2023, and is now recruiting from further afield.

One member who is in prison awaiting trial after being implicated in several murders told the BBC he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad.

He agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking".

"Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jamsâ¦ it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well."

When challenged over whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality, he says he feels "guilty in-part" but claims to have no regrets.

Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap".

The BBC's Paris Correspondent, James Waterhouse, reports from Marseille.

News.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
News.content:
The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill.

His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work.

She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill.

Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck."

Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up.

After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error.

Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA.

But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months until he left the civil service in September 2023.

He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of civil service databases such as payroll every two years to look for anomalies.

Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died.

In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home.

The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at Â£2.1m.

His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer.

The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed.

Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing.

News.title: Woman says Al Fayed's brother drugged and sexually abused her at Highland estate
News.content:
A woman has told BBC Scotland how she was trafficked to the Highlands, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner by Salah Fayed, the brother of former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed.

Jill, whose name has been changed for legal reasons, said she was a young Harrods employee when she was recruited to what she believed was an executive training scheme in the 1990s.

Speaking for the first time about the abuse that took place in Scotland, Jill said she was flown on the Fayed family's private jet to Balnagown, their estate in Easter Ross, where she was repeatedly assaulted.

She is one of hundreds of women who have alleged abuse by the Fayed brothers.

Since Mohamed Al Fayed's death in 2023, hundreds of women and girls have alleged they were sexually abused by him.

His brother Salah, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2010, has also been accused of abuse by numerous women.

News.title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats
News.content:
A man has been jailed for sending the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch emails threatening to shoot her dead.

Ex-teacher Kieran Kyle sent three emails on 2 May to the Tory party leader in which he made racist references and claimed to have been in the IRA, the court heard.

The 43-year-old, from Gillingham in Kent, pleaded guilty on 22 September at Westminster Magistrates' Court to two counts of sending communications of an indecent or offensive nature.

Kyle was sentenced to 20 weeks in prison at the same court on Monday.

In a victim impact statement read to the court, Badenoch and her husband Hamish said the "malicious communications and targeted harassment" not only had an effect on them, but also undermined "a healthy democracy".

In two of the emails, Kyle had made racist references and written: "I'm ex-IRA, so Bloody Sunday references from you are going to give you trouble," the court heard.

The messages were sent on the day Badenoch apologised for footage from Bloody Sunday being mistakenly used in a social media clip to criticise a parliamentary Bill on legacy issues in Northern Ireland.

The Tory leader had said she did not sign off the video and that it was sent out by "very young people".

The video criticising the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill, posted to her social media channels on 28 April, showed Badenoch saying the Labour legislation would "drag" Troubles veterans back to court.

Thirteen unarmed civilians were shot dead when members of the Army's Parachute Regiment opened fire on civil rights demonstrators in the Bogside area of Londonderry on 30 January 1972, a date that became known as Bloody Sunday.

The court heard Kyle had also sent an email to Badenoch's husband Hamish on 29 April, which used a racist term and said she had a "big mouth" and he should "put a leash on her".

News.title: Electrical items caused fatal fire, inquest hears
News.content:
A house fire on Boxing Day last year which killed a woman and her two children is believed to have been caused by electrical appliances, an inquest has heard.

Fionnghuala Mary Shearman, 38, known as Nu, her seven-year-old daughter Eve and her son Ohner, four, died at their home in Brimscombe, Gloucestershire, in the early hours of 26 December last year.

Partner and serving police officer Tom Shearman, escaped and tried to re-enter the house multiple times to save his wife and children, but was unable to due to the severity of the blaze.

Leroy Hughes, from Gloucestershire Fire and Rescue Service said items such as soft furnishings and the Christmas tree would likely have fueled the flames.

An inquest held at Gloucestershire Coroner's Court on Monday heard the fire likely started in the living room, caused by electrical items connected to the mains power supply.

Emergency services were called at 03:12 GMT and crews found the property "well alight", according to Hughes.

News.title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force
News.content:
A former police detective who stole more than Â£85,000 from her own force while working in a team that investigated high-level drugs gangs has been jailed.

Acting as the exhibits officer and one of only a small number of people with access to a safe that contained hundreds of thousands of pounds, Michelle Kirsty Reason began siphoning off cash in January 2022, Derbyshire Police said.

According to the force, the 54-year-old spent the money - which had been seized from criminals - on a car, a holiday, and tickets to events.

On Monday, Reason pleaded guilty to theft and misconduct in public office and was jailed for four years and two months at Mansfield Magistrates' and County Court.

Detectives said Reason, of Church Lane in Buxton, was a police exhibits officer based in Ripley.

From about January 2022, the force said Reason began siphoning cash after she dealt with a large cash seizure in the region of Â£350,000.

She initially stole Â£15,000 and told officers that, once she found that nobody had noticed, began taking money on a regular basis until she left the force in December 2025.

However, officers then began to review the stored exhibits ahead of an upcoming court case, and began to question where the cash had gone.

Knowing she had been caught out, Reason went to St Mary's Wharf police station to confess to taking the cash.

News.title: Thick fog disrupts travel with further weather warning issued
News.content:
Dense fog disrupted travel for many on Monday morning and is likely to cause further disruption on Tuesday.

A Met Office warning for much of England and eastern Wales expired at 11:00 GMT on Monday. An additional fog warning for Northern Ireland ended at 10:00 GMT.

An area of England and Wales stretching from Canterbury to Cardiff, Hull to St Asaph and Southampton to York, and including London, Birmingham and parts of Greater Manchester was impacted.

The Met Office has issued a further warning for fog from Monday evening into Tuesday morning.

News.title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
News.content:
The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.

Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief".

New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.

But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.

The government has been consulting on reducing its 80% rule and a significant reduction is now expected.

Downing Street has insisted no decision has been made.

A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.

If ministers do decide on a steeper watering-down of the rules, it will arguably be interpreted by some - alongside the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea - as the government prioritising economic considerations over environmental ones.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has recused himself from this issue due to his wife's links to an electric vehicle company.

The key meetings on the subject will instead be chaired by Cabinet Office minister Louise Haigh.

Asked about reports the targets would be reduced, Burnham dismissed this as "speculation", adding: "No decision has been made at this point."

Sustainability groups say any weakening of the 2030 target will threaten the UK's long-term electrification and climate goals.

It could undermine the UK's claim to be providing leadership on climate just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.

Energy UK, the trade association for the energy industry, has also opposed the move.

Last month, it said, external reducing targets could damage "the investment certainty needed to deliver the infrastructure, innovation and services required for the transition to zero-emission transport".

Asked if climate change was no longer a big priority, Health Minister Karin Smyth said the government was committed to its emissions targets.

"This country is doing great work in terms of our transition and looking at renewables â that's a key part of growth in different parts of the country," she told BBC Breakfast.

She added that the prime minister would have "a good story to tell" when meeting other leaders at COP31.

A government spokesperson said: "We are committed to the phase out of all new cars relying solely on petrol and diesel engines by 2030, and to 100% of new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, and our legally binding net zero targets."

The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders welcomed the government's review of the EV targets when it was announced in the summer.

Last week, head of the association Mike Hawes said transitioning to electric vehicles had come at a "heavy cost" with billions spent on discounts to drive demand in electric vehicles.

He said the government's targets could not be achieved "without putting at risk any future investment".

News.title: One of James Bulger's killers to remain in prison
News.content:
Child killer Jon Venables will remain behind bars after he told a Parole Board panel that he should stay in prison.

Venables tortured and murdered two-year-old James Bulger in 1993 after he and Robert Thompson, both then aged 10, snatched him from a shopping centre in Bootle, Merseyside.

Venables told parole staff dealing with his latest review, which took place in private, that he was not seeking release.

A summary of the panel's findings said: "At the outset of the hearing, Mr Venables submitted an opening statement to the effect that he accepted the need to undertake further offending work in custody and so was not seeking release."

The panel considered evidence from probation officers based in the prison and in the community, three psychologists and a psychiatrist.

All bar one concluded that he should remain in prison.

News.title: Russell Brand’s ex Jemima Goldsmith accuses rapist of ‘violence, coercive control and abuse’ against her
News.content:

One of Russell Brand’s ex-partners has accused him of “violence, coercive control and abuse” against her, claiming she once had to call the police to get him removed from her house.

Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years’ imprisonment on Monday for raping one of his fans and sexually assaulting three TV and radio workers during his rise to international fame.

Hours after the sentence was delivered at Southwark Crown Court, Brand’s ex-partner Jemima Goldsmith, the heiress and former wife of cricketer and former prime minister of Pakistan Imran Khan, issued a statement on social media.

Ms Goldsmith, who dated Brand for around a year until September 2014, said: “I am and have always been strongly and unequivocally on the side of all of Brand’s victims. I am in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand’s trial, told their stories, testified and ensured justice was done.

“I have had my own personal experience of his violence, coercive control and abuse. I had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident.

“I chose not to press charges at the time and not to go public with this, as I was worried about the impact of the press attention on my then teenage children.

open image in gallery Jemima Goldsmith dated Russell Brand for around a year until they broke things off in September 2014 ( Getty )

“I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014. Whilst my pain in relation to this, pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact.”

She went on: “I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014. Whilst my pain in relation to this, pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact.”

Ms Goldsmith said she had spent several years assisting the Channel 4 Dispatches, The Times and The Sunday Times journalists who first accused Brand of sexual misconduct in 2023, even undertaking to testify in court about the abuse she suffered if the outlets were sued for their claims.

She partly issued the 1,534-word message on Monday in response to “misleading reports” over a harrassment injunction she and Brand secured against a masseuse in 2015.

The case stemmed from a birthday present massage arranged by Ms Goldsmith for Brand in June 2014, which was not in the end taken up. Masseuse Szilvia Berki had claimed she was assaulted by Brand, which he denied, and the alleged incident was investigated by police, who concluded there was no case to answer.

open image in gallery Russell Brand, seen arriving at Southwark Crown Court with his wife Laura, was sentenced on Monday ( Reuters )

In her social media post, Ms Goldsmith said: “I was present the whole time he was with her, and I did not see anything untoward, despite the fact that he was later found guilty of sexually assaulting other women and he later physically assaulted me. If I saw any man abuse any woman under any circumstances, I would do my utmost to stop them, without hesitation.”

After the claim was made, Ms Berki initiated a campaign of harassment, Ms Goldsmith alleged in her statement, including sending disturbing emails and having untrue stories published in the press. They included anti-semetic comments which were submitted to the judge which granted the injunction, Ms Goldsmith claimed.

Ms Goldsmith said: “Although I was at this point no longer in contact with Brand, I agreed to the suggestion by his lawyer of a harassment order. My sole reason was to stop Ms Berki targeting me and my family.”

She concluded in her social media post: “I hope this information will help clarify speculation about my involvement in the anti-harassment order. I am glad and relieved that Russell Brand has finally faced justice.”

The Independent has been unable to contact Ms Berki.

News.title: Supreme Court won't intervene in license plate dispute in Puerto Rico
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to consider a legal bid by Roberto Clemente’s sons contesting Puerto Rico’s placement of the baseball legend’s image on commemorative vehicle registration tags and license plates, which they claimed breached constitutional safeguards against government taking of trademark rights.

The justices turned away the appeal brought by the three brothers after lower judicial bodies previously rejected their claims against the Caribbean US territory.

A native of Puerto Rico, Clemente played 18 seasons as a right fielder for Major League Baseball's Pittsburgh Pirates between 1955 and 1972. His decorated career featured 15 All-Star appearances and two World Series championships, earning him induction into the Baseball Hall of Fame and a dedicated statue outside the stadium. He died at age 38 in a 1972 airplane crash while transporting humanitarian assistance to earthquake survivors in Nicaragua.

The action was brought against Puerto Rico's government by Roberto Clemente Jr, Luis Roberto Clemente and Roberto Enrique Clemente, along with two family-owned companies established to protect the Roberto Clemente trademark, preserve his legacy, and advance his charitable efforts.

Alleging that the unauthorized likeness generated $15 million for Puerto Rico, the lawsuit asked the courts to halt all future use of their father's image on plates and tags while seeking $45 million in damages alongside $3.15 million in compensation for trademark infringement.

"Although we are disappointed by the court's decision not to hear the important issues presented by our petition, we look forward to litigating the remaining claims in the trial court," Wen Fa, an attorney for the sons, said in a statement.

Puerto Rico released the commemorative plates and registration tags displaying Clemente's face in 2022 without consent from his sons. The official initiative was discontinued at the end of that year. The sons filed suit in federal court within the territory, arguing that officials violated the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution's ban on government takings of private property by seizing his trademark rights.

San Juan-based US District Judge Gina Mendez-Miro dismissed the lawsuit, and the Boston-based 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals partially upheld that decision, turning down the argument that Puerto Rico’s use of the trademarks amounted to an unconstitutional taking.

In petitioning the Supreme Court, attorneys for the family argued that lower courts erred in deciding that the Fifth Amendment fails to automatically apply to intangible property such as trademarks in the same manner as physical property like real estate.

"Left unanswered, the 1st Circuit's ruling would invite government to take trademarks on demand — checked only by a multi-factor balancing test that allows government to destroy much in value and pay nothing in return," they wrote.

In court filings, Puerto Rico argued that the family’s Fifth Amendment claim exaggerated the scope of the appellate ruling. It asserted that the 1st Circuit never declared intangible property to be "categorically" excluded from automatic Fifth Amendment coverage.

"Instead, the court resolved the issues presented by applying existing precedent to the facts of this case," Puerto Rico said.

News.title: Trump’s midterm election denialism sparks fierce backlash from both sides: ‘Figured it would take a few days’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump drew sharp criticism from across the political spectrum after questioning the integrity of the midterm elections.

On Monday, six days after Democrats reclaimed the House and Senate, Trump wrote on Truth Social: “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???”

The post marked a reversal from his initial response to Republicans’ midterm losses, when he congratulated Democrats, faulted weak GOP candidates and told The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results, yeah.”

While politicians and pundits condemned the remarks, many saw them as a predictable return to his longstanding allegations of election fraud. Trump has repeatedly and baselessly claimed the 2020 presidential election was “stolen” and has continued to undermine confidence in U.S. elections throughout his second term.

“Our fave election denier is back,” Jessica Tarlov, a liberal Fox News commentator wrote on X.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump's remarks casting doubt on the integrity of the midterm elections sparked backlash from politicians and pundits across the spectrum ( Getty Images )

“There's our guy - figured it would take a few days for the reality of the electoral annihilation to slip through Natalie's gatekeeping and reach Trump,” wrote Jon Favreau, former speechwriter to Barack Obama and host of Pod Save America. He was referencing Natalie Harp, the president’s executive assistant.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, the favorite to become majority leader, dismissed Trump’s claims and pointed to the scale of Democrats’ victories. As of Monday, they were projected to win 54 Senate seats to Republicans’ 44 and 253 House seats to the GOP’s 160, with some races still uncalled.

“Donald Trump’s pathetic return to election denialism was inevitable,” Schumer, a New York Democrat, wrote on X. “He can whine all he wants, but nothing will stop this inescapable truth: For the last two years of his presidency, Trump will face the largest Democratic congressional majorities in decades, all because he has been an unprecedented failure.”

Rep. Norma Torres, a California Democrat, added: “You lost to American citizens who rejected your nonsense. Pack it up.”

Even everyday people commenting on social media took shots at the president for the flip-flop.

“Here we go again. Surprised it took a week,” commentator Katherine Brodsky wrote. “The election is only honest whenever he wins.”

“The election denial stuff is one of the things that will forever taint his legacy (in the eyes of future historians). I asked Grok to rank the US Presidents. It put Trump in the bottom 5/45, for things like this,” Fellow X user named David noted.

“‘Houston, the Ego has landed.’ Okay, let's face it. We all knew it was just a matter of time,” X poster Donald R. Koelper stated. And now, off we go into the abyss of denialism, where any and all election results are fraudulent unless, of course, he either wins or approves.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

open image in gallery ‘Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???’ Trump wrote on Monday ( @realdonaldtrump, Truth Social )

open image in gallery ‘Our fave election denier is back,’ a Fox pundit proclaimed ( Getty Images )

The criticism extended to some conservatives, including former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, who repeatedly echoed Trump’s false claims about the 2020 election before falling out with him over the Iran war.

“For anyone who believes his bull****, ask yourself, has he ever prosecuted ANYONE from the 2020 election??? NOOOOOOOOOO!!!!!” she wrote on X. “Ask yourself honestly. Why hasn’t Trump, the President of the United States, with control of the DOJ, prosecuted anyone from the 2020 election?”

Greene instead blamed the Republican losses on voters disillusioned with Trump and his party.

“The real truth for the 2026 midterms is that something like 14 million Trump/Republican voters stayed home because, for multiple issues, they couldn’t support Trump and Republicans anymore,” she wrote. “His ego and pride are hurt and he knows the big Democrat victory is 100 percent on him.”

Daniel Horowitz, a senior editor at the conservative outlet The Blaze, also weighed in: “Look, at some point con inc. will have to recognize the choke hold they've ensnared themselves in.”

MAGA podcaster and Trump backer Megyn Kelly simply put: “Just Stop.”

News.title: Elizabeth Holmes’ fiance Billy Evans claims he wrestled Nathan Fielder ‘Borat’ style
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Elizabeth Holmes’ partner Billy Evans has claimed on social media that he wrestled You Can See Everything co-director Nathan Fielder “Borat style.”

Evans, 34, has received widespread attention following his role in the documentary about Holmes’ last days of liberty before she was sent to prison for defrauding investors in her blood-testing startup, Theranos.

Filmmakers Fielder and Lance Oppenheim spent extended periods of time filming Evans and Holmes, both before and after her incarceration. The A24 film raises questions about the nature of truth and the ethics of documentary filmmaking.

In a post on X, Evans wrote: “I really wish they'd kept the scene where I wrestled Nathan, Borat style. Full top mount. His little Canadian frame struggling beneath me. I thought he was in on the joke. Until he wasn't. Imagine realizing that in camera.”

He continued: “This literally wouldn't make the top 10 best deleted scenes. We didn't hold back. We showed them everything. You saw what they wanted to show you.... It was a wild experience. Hate us, live us [sic], the truth or lack there of is in the edit.”

Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans, and 'You Can See Everything' co-director Nathan Fielder ( Getty )

In response to a supportive comment on his post, Evans added: “They filmed us for 3 years. Everything. Imagine your life for 3 years. Every conversation up for debate, with someone else deciding what to show.”

The Independent has approached Fielder for comment.

In a famous, controversial scene in the 2006 mockumentary Borat, Borat (Sacha Baron Cohen) and his producer Azamat Bagatov (Ken Davitian) wrestle while completely naked, with their fight taking them through a busy hotel.

In the last week, Evans has been active on social media, answering questions on X about You Can See Everything.

Evans, who has been engaged to Holmes since 2018 and has two children with her, was asked on X to dispel what he believed to be the biggest misconception of the movie, to which he replied, “That I somehow control Liz.”

“Anyone who actually knows her would find that idea hilarious,” the heir to the Evans Hotel Group added. “She’s fiercely independent, strongwilled, and my best friend. We are partners in every sense. We challenge each other, disagree, and face the world together. Her closest friends are also some of my closest friends. If I ever mistreated her, they’d have my head.”

After the movie’s release, some viewers had interpreted that Evans was controlling Holmes. In it, he is shown to be in charge of Holmes’s social media accounts while she is incarcerated; he appears to negotiate a financial deal with A24 without her knowledge, and he reveals he has power of attorney over her.

“We talk about everything, including X. Nothing happened behind her back,” Evans wrote on the topic. “The POA was simply the legal mechanism that allowed me to act on her behalf while she’s incarcerated. It was not a substitute for her consent.”

When asked if he regrets agreeing to the documentary, Evans wrote, “Not at all.”

News.title: Washington Post columnist fired over Charlie Kirk posts says she won't rejoin paper
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A long-time opinion writer says she won’t return to The Washington Post after the paper was ordered to reverse her dismissal over social media posts about the 2025 killing of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.

Karen Attiah said Sunday on her Substack, “The Golden Hour by Karen Attiah,” that she reached a settlement with the Post and plans to move forward with her life and career.

“While I remain proud of the victory, I came to the painful realization that returning to The Washington Post meant coming back without the guaranteed freedom and institutional support to do what I loved: use my voice, seek truth, and serve readers,” Attiah wrote.

An arbitrator had ordered the newspaper in August to reinstate her after ruling that the Post did not have sufficient cause to fire her. It also ordered the paper to award her full back pay and lost benefits.

open image in gallery ( Getty Images )

The Democracy Defenders Fund and the Washington-Baltimore News Guild, which represented Attiah, did not immediately comment on her decision not to return to the paper. When the arbitrator's ruling came down, the two organizations said it marked a landmark moment for press freedom.

Kirk, 31, was an ally of President Donald Trump and used his popular podcast to espouse rhetoric many critics felt was racist and divisive. He was shot and killed on Sept. 10, 2025, during an event at Utah Valley University.

Attiah posted on social media several times shortly after Kirk’s death, including one post that said, “if anything, the rush to coddle violent white men is self-protective — that we know they are not used to feeling vulnerable and mortal — and will react violently out of fear. And we will all suffer.”

In another post, she wrote, “Part of what keeps America so violent is the insistence that people perform care, empty goodness and absolution for white men who espouse hatred and violence.”

The Post fired Attiah in an email while accusing her of “gross misconduct.”

“Your public comments on social media regarding the death of Charlie Kirk violate the Post’s social media policies, harm the integrity of our organization, and potentially endanger the physical safety of our staff,” it wrote.

Attiah was among dozens of people from various professions who were fired over comments they made about Kirk's killing. The dimissals raised questions over free speech as Trump vowed retribution for remarks he considered disparaging.

News.title: Maya Jama announces 'exciting' Netflix deal after shock Love Island exit
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Maya Jama has signed with Netflix for a selection of "really exciting" upcoming ventures.

The presenter’s next career move was revealed on Monday, just one day after the 32-year-old star announced she was stepping away from ITV's Love Island series.

As reported by Variety, Jama has several new projects in development with the streaming platform, though further details are currently being kept under wraps.

In a statement, she said: "I’m absolutely buzzing to be working with Netflix!

"There are some really exciting things coming and I can’t wait for everyone to see what we’ve been working on.

"I can’t give too much away just yet, but I’m so excited for this next chapter. Watch this space!”

Sharing Variety's announcement on X, she teased: "won’t be off your screens for too long.. @netflix (sic)"

Jama reached the final of Celebrity Traitors last month ( BBC )

Maya is no stranger to Netflix, having played Aisha in season two of The Gentlemen.

Anne Mensah, Netflix’s vice president of UK content, heaped praise on the star, labelling her as “fabulous”.

Ms Mensah added: "She has an infectious energy and an ability to captivate audiences.

"We adored working with her on The Gentlemen, and we’re absolutely delighted for her to be an even bigger part of the Netflix family.”

She rose to further prominence on BBC's Celebrity Traitors, where she made it all the way to the final.

Maya first started a presenter on MTV and BBC Radio 1, before landing a job as the host of the UK's Love Island in 2023.

The Netflix announcement comes after Maya insisted "all good things must come to an end", as she confirmed her Love Island UK exit.

She wrote on Instagram: "I’ve always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then, and now is my time to throw myself into something new.

"While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I’ll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever."

Maya thanked the Love Island UK viewers, and insisted she remains "grateful" for the opportunity.

She added: "I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the 9 incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way.

"I’ve loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show. I’ll forever be grateful for the experience."

News.title: My mother slept with an AK47 by her bed to protect us. Now I want to make London’s streets safer
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Her mother kept an AK47 by her bed to protect her family from marauding gangs – now she wants hopes to be the Tory candidate for London mayor in a bid to help Londoners feel safer.

Sara Gezdari was 13 when she left her native Albania for Italy to escape the civil war which engulfed the country in 1997 after its brutal communist regime had fallen a few years before.

On the shortlist of three to be the Tory candidate for London mayor, Ms Gezdari, a 42-year-old businesswoman, single mum and recent candidate from the London borough of Richmond, has become one of the party’s emerging stars.

But, while she now lives in London’s leafiest borough, she has not forgotten her origins.

open image in gallery Sara Gezdari with her children Edoardo and Sofia ( Sara Gezdari )

“One of the most traumatic experiences that I have is at the time as a child in Albania. Sleeping in this little house and being confined from weeks and weeks, not being able to go to school, not being able to walk on the street unless you had a male figure next to you, like your dad or cousin, someone that would accompany you, because young girls would be kidnapped and sold to the international prostitution market,” she told The Independent.

The constant fear meant her mother Elvana, a former gymnast who became a doctor, slept with an AK47 next to her bed before they moved to Italy.

“It was there just for a sense of security, because we had the internal bands that would jump into the house and rob them, abuse women,” she remembers.

Conservative members in London will on Monday receive their ballot papers to decide whether Ms Gezdari, former foreign secretary Sir James Cleverly or former Bedfordshire police and crime commissioner Festus Akinbusoye should run for mayor in 2028.

open image in gallery Sir James Cleverly is also hoping to be the Tory candidate for London mayor ( The Independent )

Ms Gezdari, who stood in Richmond Park in the 2024 general election, losing to the Lib Dem MP Sarah Olney – who is also expected to run for mayor – admits she is “the wildcard” option for the Tories.

She believes it is her childhood that has shaped her political beliefs.

“I think that’s why I studied politics at Bologna [University],” she muses, a place where one of her lecturers was the former Italian prime minister and European Commission President Romano Prodi.

Despite having a leading Eurocrat help shape her in academia, she is not going to get drawn on her views on Brexit, even though the current Labour mayor and likely opponent Lord Sir Sadiq Khan wants to turn Brexit into a campaign issue.

“He's focused on what happened 10 years ago with Brexit, and very passionate about apologising for the slavery and paying reparations, instead of looking at what the present looks like for Londoners,” she says. “He should be worried about the 349,000 people unemployed in London.”

open image in gallery Number 4 is Sara Gezdari's mother Elvana when she was a gymnast with other Albanian athletes ( Group of Albanian athletes in the 1970s )

Her family connection with the UK began in 1982, two years before she was born, when her father Edmond, a former professional footballer, was playing Belfast club Linfield in the European Cup for his club 17 Nëntori Tiranë. Linfield offered him a contract which he signed.

But his thoughts of escaping the Communist regime were short-lived.

“He got a call from somebody from the government in Albania saying, ‘if you do accept and you stay, your entire family will be persecuted. Your mum, your brother, your dad, your sister. We've got a place already in the mountains.’

“He had to go back even though he was passionate about football and this was the biggest opportunity of his life.”

She describes many of the political issues she is fighting on – whether it is personal freedom, business growth or law and order – as “incredibly personal to me”, especially when she thinks about her two children Edoardo and Sofia.

She says it is why she wants police patrols and focussing on crime hotspots as one of her main policies. But a desire to support freedom is also important to her.

“I want my son, if he wants to play football, to be able to sign with any country because he's got the opportunity to do that and nobody's going to put me to jail if he does.”

open image in gallery Edmond Gezdari playing football for his club ( Shared by his daughter Sara Gezdari )

She carefully sticks to her party’s hard line on leaving the European Convention of Human Rights (ECHR) and clamping down on immigration, things which have helped her in the past.

“I am a successful story of immigration, and there are many people like me. Unfortunately, what we have seen as well in the last couple of years is that a lot of people have come to this country to benefit from the system and make it unsafe.”

But she does have a firm reply to the argument put forward by Reform’s Suella Braverman and Zia Yusuf that she and they cannot be English or British because they have the wrong ethnicity.

She had a spat with Mr Yusuf when he posted on X about the winning Labour Holborn and St Pancras Sagal Abdi-Wali, who came to the UK as a child refugee, not being English because of her name.

“I couldn't disagree more with both Suella Braverman and Zia Yuzuf. I don’t think we should judge people based on the geography of where they were born or where their family was born.”

She adds with a glint in her eye: “Otherwise we wouldn't have Layla Cunningham as a London mayor candidate for Reform.

“I think we should judge people based on culture, values, principles, and respect for laws.

“People like me who come here, embrace, welcome, and really enjoy being British. We have a sense of pride in it.”

News.title: Oh snow! A massive November storm is on the forecast for parts of US
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A nor’easter could form this week, bringing the first snow of the season for tens of millions of Americans.

Frigid air and precipitation from the Northwest and Canada is expected to invade central and eastern states, setting up the potential for falling flakes from Thursday into the weekend.

Communities from the Northeast to New England face the most impacts from the storm, though only minor disruptions to ground travel are anticipated and the forecast is subject to change.

“Locations that could face their first snowflakes of the season include Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Syracuse and Binghamton, New York,” Brandon Buckingham, an AccuWeather meteorologist, wrote in a statement.

“The mountainous terrain of the Poconos, Catskills and Berkshires will also face the risk of snow.”

open image in gallery Snow is on the forecast for much of the northern and eastern U.S., as cool air heads south from Canada ( Getty Images )

Which regions could see snow?

Areas from the interior Northeast to the central Appalachians are the most likely to see snow - though forecasters don’t yet know how much.

That includes higher elevation areas of Massachusetts, upstate New York and as far south as Pennsylvania. Snow may struggle to to accumulate outside of higher elevations.

Winter lovers in major cities along the coast will probably be disappointed. That’s because the Atlantic Ocean waters are still very warm, according to Buckingham. Instead, the cities are forecast to see rain ahead of the weekend.

open image in gallery Higher elevation regions could see snow accumulating into Friday night ( AccuWeather )

A seasonal chill

By Saturday, the storm is projected to pull away toward Canada with some lingering snow showers from rainy Maine through the Appalachian mountains, FOX Weather reports.

Regardless of how the storm takes shape, it could set the stage for a massive temperature drop across the East later in the week. Afternoon temperatures would reach around 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1 degrees Celsius) for more than 110 million people in the Northeast, with lows plummeting into the 20s Fahrenheit (-6.6 degrees Celsius).

open image in gallery Cold air is on the forecast for much of the eastern states into the weekend ( AccuWeather )

That means hard freezes for the Midwest, Ohio Valley and South, as well as nights below freezing in Tennessee, Alabama and Atlanta.

Catch ya later, pollen

The freeze will provide some much welcome relief for people who suffer from fall allergies, marking the end of the growing season. Some 80 million Americans suffer from seasonal allergies that leave them sneezing and tearing through the fall.

Ragweed is the biggest culprit of fall allergies, with a single plant releasing up to a billion grains of pollen, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Ben White reveals heartbreaking reaction to missing World Cup and response to England boos
Sports.content:
Ben White revealed missing the last World Cup left him in tears.

The Arsenal defender, 29, is famed for quitting the England camp in Qatar in 2022. But White’s reaction to missing out last summer through injury paints a very different picture of a player who insists it is still his dream to play for his country in a major tournament.

White was exiled from the England set-up for four years until Thomas Tuchel brought him back in March, only for injury to ruin his chances of going to the United States.

“It was one I had to process quickly. And get my head around as I knew I would not be ready,” he said. “So I had a cry around the pitch when it happened and focused on my career.

‌



“I've been obviously around it and not quite put my foot in the door in these big games. And yeah, it's definitely something I want to do and be involved in for sure.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

White says he still “won’t go into detail” about what happened in Qatar but says he would probably make the same decision again.

‌



Former England boss Gareth Southgate always played down any bust-up with his assistant Steve Holland being the sole reason for White flying home in 2022. But Southgate did go public further down the line when he said that White had made himself unavailable for England and had snubbed a recall. Clearly, the defender has returned to the international fold under new boss Tuchel.

“There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn't great,” said White. “I don't want to throw anyone under the bus; a lot of people try to do that to me so it's something I don't want to do myself.

“I was a bit younger. Obviously, I'm a bit older now. I think, as a person, I'm quite real, and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make.

“I think just people don't know the full story, and because I've never said anything or share any of that because I think it's probably the best way. But it's obviously amazing to be here now.”

‌



And now the slate is clear for White and he is a regular for Arsenal, can play right back and centre half and he is now looking to the future and playing under Tuchel.

White said: “Yeah, obviously, an amazing privilege to be called up, and the feeling is the same every time when you do get this chance to play for England and one I'm really looking forward to this week.

View 3 Images White scored and conceded a penalty on his return to the England squad (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

“Yes, even until now, the manager’s communication is amazing. He's always in contact, and I think a manager that you really want to play for, that you want to give everything to, and someone that I think understands the level that it needs to be.

‌



“It's been obviously amazing for me. Such a privilege to ever get close to playing for your country, something I probably didn't even dream of because I didn't think it would be any anywhere near my reality.

“So yeah, there's been a few bumps, and obviously here now, and looking forward to this story continuing.”

It is fair to say that - somewhat refreshingly - White is not a standard footballer. He is a bit different and maybe that has led to some misunderstandings.

Not least because of those now famous comments about him not liking football - or rather like watching football. We just assume every footballer will love the game and is playing out our dreams.

‌



But White insists he has no regrets saying it. “To be fair, I don't. I don't know if I actually said I don't like it because people say I don't like football, which is obviously not true.

View 3 Images White was exiled for years before Thomas Tuchel took charge of England (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

“It's because I don't watch it, which I think is quite normal for someone that does a job and then doesn't go home and then continue watching that job. But I think it's my way of release from the game because it's so intense, obviously.”

White also insists he has no problem with England fans booing him, though he also says that if supporters “knew the full story” then they might change their mind on giving him stick.

‌



White quit the England squad in Qatar in 2022 and was left out in the cold until Thomas Tuchel brought him back for two World Cup warm-up friendlies last March.

After walking away in 2022, he was booed on his first appearance for the national team since his departure during a friendly against Uruguay, where he both scored and conceded a penalty.

White told the BBC: “I think before the game, I was thinking, just don't not stand out, but just nice and easy, you know. Then I came on and obviously get booed. Then I score. Then I give away a pen. So it was obviously full of emotions that night, and it was a good night.

“Everyone can do whatever they want. Booing is fine. You know, it's fine with me. Whatever they want to do, and I think just think about maybe not knowing the full story. And if they did, maybe they wouldn’t.”

‌

Sports.title: Liverpool's Trey Nyoni hailed for 'thriving on the pitch' as JJ Gabriel comparison made
Sports.content:
Liverpool's Trey Nyoni hailed for 'thriving on the pitch' as JJ Gabriel comparison made

Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni has continued to flourish in midfield as comparisons are made with Manchester United's wantaway youngster JJ Gabriel

View 2 Images Trey Nyoni has continued to blossom in Liverpool's midfield (Image: getty)

Liverpool teenager Trey Nyoni has been hailed for doing his business on the pitch whilst fellow youngster JJ Gabriel is making headlines by pushing for a Manchester United exit.

‌



‌



Gabriel is one of the most high profile and highly thought of young players to come through the United academy in years, playing numerous years above his age and had been tipped for a Red Devils debut this season.

‌



However he stunned the club by demanding to move elsewhere with Real Madrid seen as his most likely destination. Meanwhile at Anfield Nyoni has continued to push his case for more involvement despite the Reds boasting a stellar list of midfield options.

‌



The 19-year-old scored his first professional goal in the loss at Fenerbahce last week and former Red Jason McAteer said "thriving on the pitch is the ultimate message" as Nyoni keeps the likes of Alexis Mac Allister and Dominik Szoboszlai out of the team.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Having come through the ranks McAteer, who spent four years at Liverpool, told Casino Kings: "The fans love that: the energy, the passion, the desire and the commitment. You give that to football fans, and they give back. Nyoni's doing that in his own way through his performances."

He added on the challenges facing Nyoni: "Liverpool, Chelsea, City and Arsenal can go into the transfer market and spend under a million easily. The opportunity is even more limited for these younger players. You have to be special.

‌



"I hope it works out for him. He's a talent, and we've seen very talented youngsters go by the wayside because of the noise around them, the team around them, and their ego pushing them in the wrong direction. They've missed out on a great career. So let's hope that doesn't happen."

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is close to joining Real Madrid (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Nyoni has made 13 appearances in all competitions and is one of several Liverpool youngsters to be given opportunities by Iraola. Lewis Koumas and Rio Ngumoha have both enjoyed outings for the Reds, with Nyoni hailing his coach for backing him.

The teenager said: “I don’t get nervous, never. The faith in youth the manager has and the players around me have in me, that helps me settle a lot more. Being young, there are lots of senior players around me who help me a lot. I just want to stay as I am. For me, I never get nervous."
