Sports.title: Alisson gives agent clear Liverpool instruction as goalkeeper's deal winds down
Sports.content:
Alisson gives agent clear Liverpool instruction as goalkeeper's deal winds down

Alisson's contract is set to expire in the summer but the Liverpool goalkeeper remains hungry for more success at Anfield and is keen to extend his time at the club

View 2 Images Alisson's contract with Liverpool expires this summer

Alisson has confirmed he's begun talks about extending his future at Liverpool - and insists he remains hungry to claim more titles at Anfield.

‌



‌



The Brazilian has been the Reds' No 1 since 2018 when he joined from Roma for a then record £67million and could see his spell on Merseyside extend beyond a decade with his next contract.

‌



Liverpool triggered the one-year extension in the summer as Juventus circled, and Alisson remains the first choice under Andoni Iraola. The Reds have prepared for life after the 34-year-old, dropping £60m on Giorgi Mamardashvili from Valencia and Lucca Brughmans, who remained on loan at Belgian club Genk, in recent years.

‌



Alisson again showcased his quality with Sunday's win over Crystal Palace and the Liverpool star, who has won two Premier Leagues and the Champions League at the club, has instructed in representatives to seek an extension with his deal due to expire at season's end.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said: “Yes, in my mind (I want to say). I’m focused on playing every game but in my mind I’m happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay. I’m happy here, my family is happy here.

"I’m still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that’s my thinking on that. My agent is talking with the club. Yes I feel (as good as ever), of course. In some games, we don’t have the result we want but that’s football, that’s part of football and you just have to keep working hard, having the right motivation to do stuff.

‌



"The same motivation I had coming into today, I had in the other games. This is the game that you want to happen all the time but you know that is not the reality. You’re going to have to deal with different situations and you just need to stay calm, work hard and the result will come in the future.”

View 2 Images The goalkeeper has been a huge success throughout his time at Anfield

‌



Whilst at Liverpool Alisson has twice won the Premier League's Golden Glove and, back in 2019, became the first winner of the Yashin Trophy, which is awarded to the best goalkeeper in the world.

He's been a pillar of Liverpool's success, going back to when Jurgen Klopp first began winning honours. Another of those stalwarts has been Virgil van Dijk. The Dutch defender recently extended his time at Anfield but, now 35, the centre-halves days are ultimately numbered.

Sports.title: Unai Emery butchers Man Utd 'audition' as Aston Villa collapse signals end of link
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is not going to resign. Of course he is not. He has a contract that runs until the summer of 2028. No sane character will throw away a pay-off that will run into the millions.

When he woke up to more incessant ranting on radio phone-ins devoted to the prospect of his dismissal, he might have felt like jacking it all in.

When he woke up to bookmakers trumpeting their latest odds on a decent guy getting the sack, he might have felt as though the job was not worth the ridicule. But if the Manchester United executives believe they made the wrong decision in the summer, they need to pay for it.

For the accomplished job he did in the second half of last season, Carrick should be given longer to prove he can make a decent fist of the long-term task. But there is no doubt his position is precarious. It would surprise no-one if Carrick was dismissed during this international break.

‌



Which Man Utd manager deserved longer as club keep faith with Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Man Utd respond after fans accuse them of 'censorship' over removal of protest banners READ MORE :

What should surprise everyone is if United then seriously pursued Unai Emery’s services. The eight-goal match between United and Villa at Old Trafford confirmed that.

Many observers highlighted Emery’s reactions to the late surrender of a two-goal lead as evidence of his unsuitability for a role that is more than likely to become available soon. There was the premature exit from the arena and then some slightly bizarre, tetchy exchanges during post-match media duties.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Let’s not go over the whole ‘food chain’ business again but it is fair to say that media scrutiny on United will normally be more considerable than it is on Villa. But that would not be a serious concern for United’s decision-makers if they have Emery on a shortlist of candidates to succeed Carrick should they replace him.

What would be a concern is that Emery oversaw a team that twice allowed a deeply flawed United to get back into a game they should have lost. With apologies to Oscar Wilde, to lose one two-goal lead may be regarded as misfortune; to lose two looks like carelessness.

Strip away the madness of Sunday’s match and its ramifications - the fact is that Emery eventually made five changes to a team that held a two-goal lead and that lead was wiped out in the dying stages of the match. Not only did Emery withdraw experience - John McGinn and Leon Goretzka taken out of the fray - he ignored it.

View 2 Images The Spaniard has been strongly linked with the Man Utd job

‌



As promising as he is, the situation was not ideal for 19-year-old George Hemmings, who was sent on ahead of Emi Buendia, who remained unused. Whatever the rights and wrongs of his substitutions, Emery’s record against certain marquee clubs - and for all its issues, United is still a marquee club - stands out. Not in a good way.

Three wins in 31 matches against Barcelona, four in 19 against United, two in 15 against Liverpool, four in 12 against Arsenal, five in 26 against Real Madrid. Yes, the odds have normally been stacked against his team when playing these clubs (although not on Sunday) but it is still eye-catching.

The whole debate might be spurious. Carrick might be given more time, inspire a victory at Anfield and go on a winning rampage. But if Sunday’s madcap draw against Villa does prove to herald the end of Carrick’s reign, it should also herald the end to any idea of Emery succeeding him.

Sports.title: Marc Guehi withdraws from England squad through injury as replacement named
Sports.content:
Marc Guehi withdraws from England squad through injury as replacement named

Newcastle defender Dan Burn has replaced Marc Guehi in the England squad for Nations League clashes against Croatia and Spain

View 2 Images Guehi has pulled out of the England squad (Image: Eddie Keogh/The FA via Getty Images)

Dan Burn has been drafted into England’s squad after Marc Guehi withdrew through injury. Newcastle defender Burn got the call for the Nations League double header after Guehi dropped out because of a hip issue.

‌



‌



Manchester City defender Guehi went off injured at half time during his side’s defeat at Nottingham Forest and was sent for scans. That has led to his withdrawal with the rest of the squad reporting up for duty at Tottenham’s training ground on Monday.

‌



It is a nice story for Burn who was a big part of England’s World Cup squad but then dropped out for the last two squads.

‌



However, England boss Thomas Tuchel said on Friday that Burn is still in his thoughts even though they are looking at the next generation of players ahead of the Euros in 2028.

Meanwhile, Tuchel insists Jordan Pickford is still his No.1 - but admits James Trafford is breathing down his neck. Pickford and Trafford could split the internationals against Croatia and Spain, just as they did in the last international break.

“No, he is," Tuchel said on Pickford being first choice. "But nothing has changed. The competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And Traff gets regular starts now, that's what we wanted.

‌



“James Trafford did well. They shared the matches last time. I'm not sure what we will do. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.

“I have to speak with our goalkeeper coach. But the goalkeepers, they are a bit of an unit for themselves, and rightly so.

“So we had James against Spain, we asked ourselves is this fair for James Trafford to straightaway go against Spain, but I think it's exactly what we need. Because what happens if Jordan Pickford is injured? What happens if he's not available? So it's better to test it."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reveals his England No.1 as goalkeepers set for another job share
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel reveals his England No.1 as goalkeepers set for another job share

Jordan Pickford faces fresh competition from James Trafford to keep hold of the starting goalkeeper berth for England and Thomas Tuchel has had his say on the pair

View 2 Images Pickford is still Tuchel's No.1

Thomas Tuchel has admitted he could do another job share with his keepers - but insisted Jordan Pickford is still his No1.

‌



‌



England boss Tuchel says he could give James Trafford and Pickford a game each for the Nations League double header with Croatia and Spain.

‌



Leeds keeper Trafford got two games in the last camp as it is clear that Tuchel wants to put pressure on Pickford who has been England’s first choice for the best part of a decade.

‌



It could become a throwback to the days of Peter Shilton and Ray Clemence when the two keepers shared the England jersey throughout most of their international careers.

Pickford has 93 caps and wants to stay as England No1 but Trafford is now applying genuine pressure. There is no doubt there is a feeling Trafford has the potential to be first choice in time for Euro 2028 and he appears to have established himself ahead of Dean Henderson.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Pickford did not drop clangers in the World Cup but probably did not have his best tournament with question marks over a couple of goals.

‌



When asked whether Pickford is still his No1, Tuchel said: “No, he is. But nothing has changed. The competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And Traff gets regular starts now, that's what we wanted.

“James Trafford did well. They shared the matches last time. I'm not sure what we will do. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.

‌



“I have to speak with our goalkeeper coach. But the goalkeepers, they are a bit of an unit for themselves, and rightly so."

Tuchel insists that Pickford was “surprisingly” understanding about sharing keeper duties in the Nations League last time.

‌



View 2 Images England rivals: James Trafford and Jordan Pickford (Image: Getty)

The England boss also believes it is vital that Trafford gets proper game time and exposure but surely if there is no debate then Pickford’s status is unchallenged.

‌



Tuchel said: “Yes it's slightly different, but when do I have a chance to see another goalkeeper, if not in Nations League? If not in high pressure matches?

“So we had James against Spain, we asked ourselves is this fair for James Trafford to straightaway go against Spain, but I think it's exactly what we need. Because what happens if Jordan Pickford is injured? What happens if he's not available? So it's better to test it.

‌



“Jordan knows about this. We want to use the Nations League for exactly that. But at the moment, nothing has changed. At the moment, he's the number one. And he just feels a bit of competition. Which is good for him.

"Surprisingly.... I was very impressed and a bit surprised by Jordan’s reaction when we spoke to him. I thought he'd be less of a fan than he proved to be. Because he said he totally understands it. Listen, they all want to get their caps.

‌



“The goalkeepers know: if I'm out, I'm out. I have almost no chance to come in. As an outfield player you can accept it a little bit better because after 60 minutes you still have a chance to get your cap.

"Which you can't as a goalkeeper. But he impressed me a lot last time. We spoke to him, it was a very short conversation. It was very positive. He said 'yeah, let's do this, Traff deserves it, and I will push him'.

Article continues below

“And he didn't change at all. If he changed, he changed even to the positive, he pushed Traff, he gave him a good feeling. So very impressive, he did it very well.”

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or winner Kane not named in FIFPRO World 11
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has not been named in the FIFPRO World 11.

Over 18,000 professional footballers have chosen their best men's team, with the final 11 being chosen from a group of 26 selected finalists.

Kane, who won the Ballon d'Or ahead of Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe by one of the smallest margins in history, was among the 26 finalists but did not make the final team.

Mbappe, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami's Lionel Messi were named in a Kane-less front four, which also excluded Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Olise.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane admits winning this year's Ballon d'Or was 'beyond his wildest dreams' and says he's happy to put England 'back on the map' by being the first Englishman to win the trophy in 25 years

Kane became the first English Ballon d'Or winner last month since Michael Owen in 2001, and only the fifth in history following in the footsteps Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen.

The Bayern Munich star received just 27.6 per cent of votes of all the forwards, with Haaland marginally bettering him at 28.4 per cent. It is the first time since the award's inception in 2005 that the Ballon d'Or winner has not been selected for the XI.

Kane's international team-mate, Jude Bellingham, was named in midfield alongside Barcelona star Rodri and PSG's Vitinha.

Arsenal's David Raya was named in goal, with Pau Cubarsi, Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes rounding things out in a back three.

Sports.title: Man Utd will not rush decision on Carrick future
Sports.content:
Manchester United's bosses will not rush a decision over Michael Carrick's future after their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which leaves them in the relegation zone.

Sky Sports News understands the club's hierarchy are planning to use the international break to fully evaluate the season so far and reassess their options.

Carrick and the players have all had Monday off after rescuing a late point against Villa on Sunday, but the head coach and his staff are due back into Carrington on Tuesday.

With most players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions planned in the coming days, that has bought some breathing space for a full re-evaluation of the season.

One win in 11 games, 30 goals conceded so far in all competitions, the worst record of any team in the top-five European leagues, and a worst-ever start to a Premier League season has ramped up the pressure on Carrick still further.

Those problems have outweighed the positivity brought about by the comebacks of the last two matches.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Adam Binnie shares six stats that show Manchester United's troubles so far this season

It is thought the United hierarchy feel Carrick over-achieved last season, with a third-placed League finish earning Champions League football.

But it is equally clear the bosses are adamant that the club's current crop of players have woefully under-achieved so far this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United fans show their love for Michael Carrick at full-time with a rendition of 'It's Carrick you know, it's hard to believe it's not Scholes' after the Red Devils fight back to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa at Old Trafford

The review will ask the question why that is the case, and how the club - collectively - can quickly reverse the decline.

Sky Sports News understands there are three key reasons why United are not rushing a decision over the head coach position - all of which have given Carrick an extended stay of execution.

Firstly, the supporters are not singing for him to be sacked. It is unlikely that will ever happen, such is the affection of the fanbase for a legendary player who won 11 major trophies with United, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles.

As such, the pressure to change the boss which other clubs often experience from the stands has not materialised at Old Trafford.

Secondly, there is a feeling in the boardroom that Carrick and his coaching staff still retain the support of the players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Aston Villa

Despite the chaotic nature of the last two games, they have produced a Champions League win against Roma and a draw against a good Villa side - with notable comebacks in both.

As such, the assessment seems to be that the players have not downed tools, and they are still fighting for Carrick.

Thirdly, United's bosses remain unconvinced at this stage that changing the head coach will solve the team's problems.

If they did believe that, they could have already made a move to sack Carrick and appoint a candidate such as Julian Nagelsmann or Eddie Howe - both of whom are out of work, available, and thought to be keen to talk to United if a vacancy becomes available.

'It doesn't matter who's in charge at Man Utd'

Sky Sports News chief reporter Kaveh Solhekol:

"The club needs to become Manchester United again. They need to turn into a club who are capable of winning the title regularly, winning the European Cup again.

"It doesn't matter who's in charge, in my opinion. You could have Carlo Ancelotti, Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp. But with the present ownership structure, I don't think things are going to change.

"You could bring in another manager but you would just paper over the cracks. We're talking about a club that used to rub shoulders with Barcelona and Real Madrid.

"If things carry on as they are at the moment, they'll be rubbing shoulders with Lincoln and QPR. There's a circus around the club, everyone talking about what's going wrong and how it can be changed.

"But I think most Man Utd fans think that unless you change the owners, nothing is going to change."

Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Luke Littler grouped with Beau Greaves as he looks to defend title in Wolverhampton

Sports.title: England duo ruled out of rest of Nations Championship
Sports.content:
England will be without Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the remainder of their Nations Championship campaign after both players were ruled out due to injury.

It comes as Steve Borthwick's side has been hit with a series of injuries ahead of their clash against Japan on Saturday.

Seb Atkinson, who came off in the second-half of England's 45-22 win against Australia, is set to miss the match with a hip injury, along with Ollie Chessum (shoulder) and George Furbank (groin).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maro Itoje gave a passionate defence of Steve Borthwick after England's victory over Australia at Twickenham

England are optimistic the trio will be available for their clash against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, November 21.

Feyi-Waboso sustained an injury to his right ankle during the first-half of England's clash against the Wallabies, following a hip-drop tackle by Australia prop Angus Bell.

Bell was later sent to the sin bin, with Henry Pollock coming on to replace Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time. Pollock would go on to score twice.

The Exeter winger's absence could see Borthwick call on Saracens fliers Noah Caluori or Tobias Elliott for England's clash against Japan.

Image: Tom Curry missed England's clash against Australia due to a hip injury he sustained in training

It would be Caluori's third cap for England, having made his senior debut during their Nations Championship clash against Fiji in July.

Centres Joe Marchant and Will Joseph could also be considered as wing options, while Fraser Dingwall or Max Ojomoh are likely to take the No 12 jersey in place of Atkinson.

Curry did not feature in England's win over Australia after he sustained a hip injury during training last week.

Borthwick revealed after Sunday's win that his brother, Ben Curry, was unlikely to start against Japan, despite the openside enjoying an excellent outing against the Wallabies.

It is likely Borthwick could deploy Freddie Steward at full-back in place of Furbank and keep Marcus Smith on the bench as utility cover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Borthwick praised 'excellent' Henry Pollock after a standout performance on the wing for England against Australia

England's 36-player squad returned to Pennyhill Park on Monday to prepare for this weekend's clash, with Jack Kenningham and Max Hicks both being drafted into the squad as back-row cover for Ben Curry and Chessum.

Meanwhile, Archie McParland has returned to the training squad after recovering from a calf injury.

Sports.title: Dubois: I'm the biggest test for Baumgardner's career
Sports.content:
Caroline Dubois is confident she is one fight away from an undisputed showdown with her American rival Alycia Baumgardner.

Baumgardner, formerly an undisputed super-featherweight champion, moved up to lightweight to dominate Elif Nur Turhan and win the IBF lightweight world title.

In El Paso on February 20, live on Sky Sports, Dubois fights Stephanie Han, looking to add the WBA championship to the WBO and WBC lightweight titles she already holds.

She was in Texas on Sunday, to face off with Han and call out Baumgardner.

As much as there is enmity between Dubois and Baumgardner, who have now had a number of fierce confrontations, the Londoner was pleased to see her rival step up to the 135lb division.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Turhan and Baumgardner

"Of course, I knew it was going to happen. I said it. I said that there was nothing left for her at 130," Dubois told Sky Sports. "She's been a position now where she's run out of opponents.

"You have to challenge yourself, you have to test yourself and that test, the biggest test for her career is going to be against me. I knew she was going to have to step up."

To stay on track herself, Dubois must defeat Han in February. Han is unbeaten as a professional and has two high-profile wins on her ledger over Holly Holm as well. But Dubois is determined to overcome her in her hometown and move on.

She insists she will not back down from Baumgardner. She does not want the American to equivocate either.

"What's the point of moving up in weight and having one belt? There's no point going halfway, you go all the way. When you're on a quest for greatness, you go all the way," Dubois said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the lightweight fight between Dubois and Amelia Moore

"I know for myself, I want to be undisputed. I'll be very frustrated if I fight and unify as much as I can and there's just one belt and she's terrified to step in the ring me and prevents me from becoming undisputed. I think that would be a whack move and I would be very disappointed."

But Dubois added: "If she's as great as she says she is then hopefully that's the character she will have and she would relish the opportunity.

"It's something that we both have to work towards, to make sure when the fight happens it's on the biggest platform, the biggest stage and we're given the respect we deserve for putting ourselves on the line."

Watch Dubois vs Han on February 20 live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Norris: McLaren still not at championship level
Sports.content:
Lando Norris believes McLaren are "not at the level to fight for a world championship" despite his dominant win in mixed conditions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Norris converted pole position into victory for the third time this season as McLaren's upgrades in Brazil, including new wings and floor components, gave them immediate performance.

But, Norris feels he benefitted from mistakes, including Kimi Antonelli who spun when leading the race, and George Russell who spun in the pit lane, which exacerbated his 15-second winning margin over Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

"The upgrades we brought this weekend were great. They worked as they should have done, so if we didn't bring them, we'd be further behind. Simple as that. But it's still not enough," he said.

"They're not enough to say you're suddenly always the quickest. I think on a day like Sunday, it's not all about that. It's about good strategy, good pit stops, driving well and not making mistakes.

"I certainly had a car that I could fight for a win with, and that's very important. Those things would help. It's hard to quantify how much it's helped, but upgrades always do, and they worked well. So, the team has done a very good job."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris wins the Sao Paulo GP ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar

Norris' triumph was McLaren's first since August's Dutch Grand Prix, although they were unfortunate to now win September's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid following an untimely Virtual Safety Car.

McLaren fell behind Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull following the European run of races in the pecking order and Norris called for more from the team to mount a title challenge in 2027 as he was unable to put up a serious championship defence this year.

"As much as we're happy we've managed to bring things and take a step forward, and come away with a pole and a win, we're not as happy as we could be because we also know we're not good enough," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix

"We're not at the level we need to be. We're not confident in the package we have just yet. We're getting there slowly. We want to do it quicker, but that's difficult.

"We know we still have work to do, and we're not at the level we need to be to fight for a world championship just yet. So, I'm proud of the team for the work they're doing, but we all know that we still have work to do."

Stella: Norris one of the best drivers in F1 when at his best

Norris admits his performance in Brazil on Sunday was "up there" among his best victories in F1 since joining the sport in 2019.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella says Norris drove "brilliantly" and was "at the top of his game".

"When Lando operates at his best, he's definitely one of the best drivers on the grid," he added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris says his team did a very good job getting on the right tyre at the right time during his Sao Paulo GP win

"We have seen that in these conditions, like in qualifying, it's not the first time that when you have mixed variable conditions, he kind of is one of the fastest in finding the limit.

"And you have seen this in the race as well, when the track was in the middle between dry and wet. It was when he was probably gaining most throughout the races on anybody else.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New angles of Lando Norris shattering his champagne bottle on the podium after winning the Sao Paulo Grand Prix

"He's very sensitive in understanding how much grip is available and very, I would say, even complete as a driver, despite he still [has] many years ahead of him, from a technical point of view, in terms of understanding how to deploy his tools to use the grip that is available, or to adapt to the balance of the car, because you're never going to have a really perfect car.

"You're never going to have the perfect conditions, so adaptability is actually probably the most important feature that you may want to possess as a driver. When there's a need to understand what's best, how to operate, he's definitely a master."

Sports.title: England Wheelchair ready for Australia showdown in RLWC semis
Sports.content:
England Wheelchair take on Australia for a spot in the Rugby League World Cup final; England are the reigning and defending champions after their 2022 triumph; they went undefeated in their pool after facing Ireland, Wales, and USA

England face potentially their toughest test so far against Australia in the semis

If England Wheelchair want to continue the defence of their Rugby League World Cup title, the task is simple: defeat Australia in the semi-finals in their own backyard.

England face the host nation on Tuesday at 9.45am, with a place in the final on the line. France take on Ireland in the other semi-final at 6.45am.

As the reigning and defending champions, England were, of course, the favourites heading into this tournament after getting glory on home soil back in 2022.

England and Australia played each other in last year's Wheelchair Ashes series down under, where England secured a 2-0 series victory.

Image: England went undefeated in their pool with some big victories

For Rob Hawkins, who has starred for England since 2019, a tough test awaits as they know Australia will have improved even from their meetings in 2025.

"I think every game that we have had this tournament has been tough, really," said Hawkins.

"It probably doesn't seem that way when you look at the scorelines that we have had, but every game has been tough in certain ways.

"We don't really think about it in terms of whether this is going to be our toughest game. It is just another game at the end of the day.

"Australia have improved a lot since we faced them in the World Cup in 2022.

"We can see if they have actually improved more since our last meeting last year.

"From my point of view, I'm excited. The game is growing and the teams are improving a lot more. So it's going to be an exciting game against Australia."

England have to prepare for a stronger Australia but they also have to prepare for an atmosphere in which they will be heavily backed against when they take on their fiercest rivals.

It is something Hawkins is ready to embrace as he tries to turn the pressure into a big performance.

"They had to do the same thing with us in 2022. You are going to have those moments. We had it last year and we know how the Aussie fans are," Hawkins added.

"I am excited for the pressure because we can get used to that pressure as well in the sense of the Australian fans, because we know they have been bringing a decent crowd in.

"We know that it is going to be a bit of a difficult game with the atmosphere and with the team that we're facing, but we know that we are confident to basically go and do our game and stick to our game plan as well."

'I thought I was going to wheelchair basketball'

If England can get past Australia, they will then be one match away from being back-to-back world champions.

It is quite the moment for Hawkins and while it would be a dream come true now, it may not have originally been the dream.

Indeed, Hawkins turned up to a Halifax Panthers' session thinking he was trying out for wheelchair basketball but then, gave the sport a go of which he is now one of the main stars.

"It has definitely been building up and up all for this moment and to hopefully win my second World Cup."

Sports.title: Fleming turns to uncapped spinner amid big calls for first Test series as England coach
Sports.content:
England have called up uncapped left-arm finger spinner Liam Patterson-White for this winter's three-Test series in South Africa, while Shoaib Bashir has dropped down to the Lions squad.

All-rounder Patterson-White helped Nottinghamshire win the Championship title in 2025 by taking 26 wickets and scoring 540 runs in 11 appearances, and then claimed 42 wickets and scored 474 runs in 14 appearances last season.

Jacob Bethell did not feature in August and September's 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to a knee problem that required surgery, but he is back to add to England's batting options for a tour that is live in full on Sky Sports across December and January in what will be Stephen Fleming's first series as head coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Africa's Simon Harmer guested on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast and looked at why England are struggling to produce spin bowlers

Jordan Cox deputised for Bethell at No 3 versus Pakistan, scoring a half-century in each of the three Tests at Headingley, Lord's and Edgbaston.

The Essex player's displays have opened up a selection dilemma, with possibly only three spots available between Cox, Bethell, Emilio Gay and Dan Lawrence.

Should England omit opener Gay, who has three fifties across his first six Tests since replacing Zak Crawley at the start of the summer, Cox or Bethell could potentially partner Ben Duckett at the top of the order.

Middle-order batter and part-time bowler Lawrence was recalled against Pakistan following Ben Stokes' international retirement and acted as the chief spinner as England deployed an all-pace frontline attack with great success.

England Men's national selector Marcus North said: "Liam Patterson-White's selection comes on the back of a strong summer in the Rothesay County Championship, when he took the most wickets of any spinner in Division One with 42 at an average of 25.11 and earned his first ECB development contract."

North: Carse can work way back into England team with Lions stint

Image: National selector Marcus North has left the door open for Brydon Carse to feature in England’s upcoming Test series with South Africa after he was included in the Lions squad

Josh Tongue will be unavailable for the first Test in order to return to the UK for the birth of his first child with Brydon Carse, included in a strong England Lions squad, in position to replace him. Carse was dropped by England in the summer after an incident in Derby in August and was subsequently charged by the Cricket Regulator, with a verdict still to come.

Sam Curran is unavailable for the Test series as he is prioritising his wedding.

North confirmed "one or two players" from the Lions squad will be drafted into Fleming's playing group and did not rule out Carse.

"Obviously in the past few months under investigation, it's been a time where he [Carse] has stood back and it's been a time of reflection," North said, after the squad announcement.

"It's obviously been a challenging time for Brydon and it's one we probably haven't at times felt the demands of playing international cricket and what he was dealing with was necessarily right for Brydon or us.

"There has been several conversations between us, myself, (managing director) Rob Key and other people at the ECB with Brydon over this period and the conclusion is we feel he is in a place where we can introduce him back into an England environment.

"We feel the Lions is the right place for him to come.

"Come that first Test, with Josh Tongue unavailable, that will leave us with 14 players and this is where I feel we're using the Lions tour to our advantage.

"You can see there is a very strong bowling group that is in the Lions programme and that enables us to no doubt look at where they are at in competition and under training.

"They will be out there from the [November] 25th, the Lions players, with some of our red-ball Test players, Stephen Fleming will be out there at that time and that enables us to be as informed as possible to then bring one or two players across into that Test squad come that first Test."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain says England 'lack a bit of mystery' when playing on flat pitches

England begin the South Africa series in Johannesburg on December 17, before the Boxing Day Test is held at Centurion and the series concludes in Cape Town from January 3.

They then meet the Proteas in three one-day internationals, with one game in Paarl (January 10) and two in Bloemfontein (January 13 and 15).

Bashir and Carse are joined in the Lions' red-ball squad by James Rew, who featured over the summer in England's Test team.

Bashir backed by North

On Bashir's omission from the senior Test squad, North said: "He's someone that we do still have a very positive outlook for.

"We sit down looking at each Test series in isolation and we feel that Liam gives us the best balance and that spinner for this tour of South Africa. We will continue to be incredibly invested in Shoaib over the winter.

"He [Bashir] is still very young, but he's in a good place. He is determined and is continuing to grow and learn.

"We still value [him], and [he] will continue to develop and [we'll] see where we can get Shoaib in the coming months and year."

Sports.title: Manchester United weighing up Michael Carrick sacking as Wilcox leads review
Sports.content:
Manchester United are deciding whether Michael Carrick should be sacked, with Jason Wilcox, the director of football, leading the review after the head coach was given the Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa games to turn results around.

Wilcox is consulting with Omar Berrada, the chief executive, before a recommendation regarding ­Carrick is made to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who ­controls sporting policy. United are in the Premier League relegation zone and have three victories in 15 games in all competitions.

Carrick came close to being removed after the 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth on 25 October. But after Wilcox and Berrada met the following day at the training ground to discuss his position, Carrick was given the three games until the international break to prove he and the players could reverse a dismal start.

United then lost 2-0 at ­Chelsea, beat Roma 3-2 at Old ­Trafford and shared a 4-4 home draw with Villa on Sunday. In each of the matches United were uneven. At Chelsea, ­Carrick’s side impressed in the first half but failed to convert chances before conceding twice after the interval, the second from a penalty after Lisandro Martínez was sent off.

In the Roma victory they were 2-0 behind in a poor opening 45 minutes before three goals in a rousing second one. On Sunday United twice trailed by two goals and entered added time 4-2 down, strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescuing a point.

After the Roma game Carrick urged his team to build momentum but within four minutes against Villa they were 2-0 down, continuing a pattern of conceding very early. In the 4-1 defeat at Como last month, Nico Paz scored after two minutes. This followed Pablo Barrios’s opener one minute into the 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid the ­previous week.

There is no plan to bolster Carrick’s coaching staff to try to help him and the team, it is understood.

If ­Carrick is removed, Eddie Howe remains Wilcox’s favoured candidate. The former Newcastle manager is taking a break from the game but would be open to considering the job.

Sports.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances.

In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table.

But there is another statistic that should concern Maresca: City have not kept a clean sheet since their victory at Anfield after the last international break, nine games ago. And the game before that, they let in three against Sunderland. In those last eight games, City have conceded 17 goals. It’s true that three of those can at least in part be blamed on errors by Gianluigi Donnarumma, but there are also structural issues. City have a vulnerability in transition that Forest ruthlessly exploited, a weakness not unfamiliar to Maresca’s teams. One of the criticisms he received at both Leicester and Chelsea was that his sides were often extremely cautious in possession, but that makes sense given how high a line he likes to play.

That’s also why duels are so crucial to his teams; losing possession immediately exposes a high back four. Maresca was visibly disappointed at the way City were outfought in the first half against Forest. Lose the ball and the opposition has a run at a back four with space behind it. That is always going to be a problem but especially so when the opposing center-forward is a Liam Delap who has just remembered how to play and is determined to make somebody pay for a year and a bit of disappointing form.

Yet the midfield Maresca picked was clearly vulnerable to being outmuscled. He clearly rates Enzo Fernández extremely highly, to the point that City paid £125m ($167.7m) to sign him from Chelsea. But Fernández, for all his gifts as a footballer, is not especially physical by the standards of the Premier League. When he and Cole Palmer played together, there was often a sense that it made Chelsea a little lightweight. Maresca, though, was so determined to field the Argentinian that he would come up with complex tactical solutions, such as using Malo Gusto as a weird right-back-cum-No-10 hybrid.

City are running into similar problems. Rayan Cherki is an enormously gifted attacking midfielder, but not one who can be relied upon defensively, either in terms of his positioning or his willingness to make tracking runs, something Pep Guardiola acknowledged last season. He can be physically outmatched. That is not necessarily a huge problem with two mobile runners behind him: ideally an Elliot Anderson-style shuttler and a more defensive holding and/or ball-winning presence like Rodri. But Rodri has gone and Fernández leaves Anderson with a huge amount of the physical work to do. If Anderson happens not to be on the spot – if, say, a defender loses the ball in a dangerous area, or a break bypasses him – City are very quickly exposed.

Maresca said he will use this international break to reassess, that this was a rare example where it was better for a team not to have another game straight away to try to put a defeat behind them. Perhaps there is a tactical solution to be found. Perhaps even one that isn’t just: don’t play Fernández and Cherki together. But he must also be aware that by the time the Premier League returns, City could be out of the title race, or effectively even out of the Premier League itself.

It was during the last international break that the independent panel announced City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges brought against them by the Premier League. There is a school of thought that the sanctions could be announced during this international break. It’s all but impossible, of course, to know precisely how it’s affecting players to play under the cloud of a potential huge points deduction, but if initial defiance has faded into a sullen acceptance, that may also lead to battles being lost, to a lack of intensity and desire.

Sports.title: Ben White says he has no complaints at boos from England fans over self-imposed exile
Sports.content:
Ben White has said he has no complaints at being booed by England fans when he ended his international exile during the 1-1 draw with ­Uruguay this year.

The Arsenal defender, who has returned to Thomas Tuchel’s squad after missing last month’s camp because of injury, became unpopular with some supporters after leaving the 2022 World Cup in Qatar early for personal reasons. White made himself unavailable for the rest of Gareth Southgate’s time in charge and was given a frosty reception from the Wembley crowd when he came off the bench to make his first England appearance in almost four years during the friendly with Uruguay last March.

“Everyone can do whatever they want,” White told BBC 5 Live as he prepared for England’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain this week. “It’s fine with me. Whatever they want to do, and I think just think about maybe not knowing the full story. And if they did, maybe they wouldn’t.”

Tuchel has ignored the negative reaction. The England manager wants to work with White, who followed scoring the opening goal against Uruguay by giving away a late penalty for the equaliser.

“Before the game I was thinking: ‘Don’t not stand out, but just nice and easy,’” White said. “Then I came on and obviously get booed. Then I score. Then I give away a pen. It was obviously full of emotions that night, and it was a good night.”

White, who has been in fine form for Arsenal this season, continues to steer clear of giving his take on the events leading to his exit from Qatar. “A load’s been said,” he said. “I’ve probably seen all of it and I think people don’t know the full story because I’ve never said anything and won’t put anyone under the bus or share any of that. I think it’s probably the best way. Obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it’s amazing to be here now.”

The 29-year-old does not think he would have done anything differently. “I don’t think I would,” White said. “I was a bit younger. I’m a bit older now. As a person I’m quite real, and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. One that I’m not happy about but it happened. It’s time to move on.”

Tuchel’s hopes of taking White to the World Cup last summer were dashed by a knee injury at the end of last season. White, who can play at right-back and in central defence, would probably have been part of the squad and he told TalkSport he cried when he realised he was out of contention. Injuries have disrupted his progress in recent years but he has made 12 appearances for Arsenal this season and he hopes to earn a place at Euro 2028.

“I’ve been obviously around it and not quite put my foot in the door in these big games,” White said. “It’s definitely something I want to do and be involved in.”
