Tuchel did not have to work hard to persuade him to return to the England fold, he said: “The boss didn’t need to say too much. The effort he made to speak to me and reach out was so nice, and I really appreciated it. I think when you see a manager like that you want to learn from him. It was a huge thing to play for Thomas.”

Dan Burn has been called into the squad after Marc Guéhi withdrew with an injury.

Sports.title: Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate
Sports.content:
It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” said the sporting director, Ole Book, to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory over Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.”

Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy.

Somebody was needed to break it open, and it was Nmecha. With two majestic sweeps of his right foot, two rockets from outside the area, he won the game for his team. His decisive moments of elevated quality pulled BVB away from their opponents when the game threatened to drift. “In terms of talent, qualities, and technique, he’s one of the best midfielders in the world. Add to that his finishing ability, and there aren’t many who are better,” Book beamed. That they go into the international break neck-and-neck with Bayern is all down to their No 8.

After scoring, Nmecha pointed to the sky, then mimed lifting a crown from his head and placing it on the ground. It was nothing new. He did the same, also in front of the Südtribune, the yawning, world-famous 24,000-capacity terrace in which much of the club’s hardcore support stand, after scoring against Paderborn in September. It was the same celebration that Nmecha used when he struck Germany’s opening goal of the World Cup against Curaçao.

The celebration is a nod to Ballers in God (BIG), the Christian group founded “to use the global platform of football to make Jesus known”, and in particular to their campaign The King’s Return. Yet this latest display provoked a response from BVB’s fan and support department. “When it comes to the values of our club,” it said in a statement the day after the Elversberg game, “discrimination, and the question of what kind of societal image of humanity is given space within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.”

View image in fullscreen The Südtribune at the match against Elversberg. Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/Reuters

The German public broadcaster ARD has linked BIG to ultra-conservative positions on issues including homosexuality and transgender identity. “Footballers are role models for millions of people, especially children and young people,” the fan and support department continued. “If this reach conveys content that excludes certain groups in society, we cannot dismiss this as merely private religious practice. Where religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, our tolerance for intolerance ends.”

Reports suggest the club has been in dialogue with Nmecha since the Paderborn game, and a statement issued in response to Kicker’s inquiries said those talks would continue – while defending Nmecha. “For Borussia Dortmund, it is essential to take the concerns and needs of the fanbase seriously and to address them,” said the club. “Naturally, we also take the current media coverage and the associated questions and discussions very seriously.” Dortmund appear to have been careful not to use any images of the celebration on the club’s official social channels.

These issues and this dialogue have been almost a constant since Nmecha arrived in June 2023, as a de facto Jude Bellingham replacement. His faith had already been a key part of his social media messaging and, as his transfer from Wolfsburg neared completion, some fan groups voiced their opposition, pointing to Nmecha’s sharing of anti-trans posts by the American rightwinger Matt Walsh, among others. A bright yellow banner was hung outside Signal Iduna Park sprayed with the message “@BVB Steh zu deinen worten”, a message to the club to “stick by your words”. In June 2023 Nmecha posted: “I genuinely love ALL people and don’t discriminate against anyone.”

Dortmund’s motto, or marketing strapline, of Echte Liebe (true love), has been used in the last decade-plus to quantify exactly what makes the club special to audiences all over the world. What BVB believe elevates them is a connection with the fans, a mutual respect and understanding that goes way beyond what has increasingly become a company-customer relationship in modern times. Engaging with supporter concerns is important everywhere in German football and, arguably at Dortmund, there is a commercial imperative to visibly do so.

It was widely reported at the time of his arrival that Nmecha had a clause written into his contract that gave Dortmund the power to fine him if he made social media posts which they felt contradicted the club’s values. The club again had words with the player in 2025 after he posted a message of condolence to the family of Charlie Kirk (Nmecha deleted another post which said Kirk had “peacefully stood up for his beliefs and values”).

Quick Guide Bundesliga results Show Hamburg 3-1 Mönchengladbach, Mainz 1-2 Bayern, Paderborn 2-2 Eintracht Frankfurt, RB Leipzig 5-2 Augsburg, Dortmund 2-1 SV Elversberg, VfB Stuttgart 1-0 Werder, Köln 1-2 Leverkusen, Freiburg 2-0 Union Berlin, Hoffenheim 2-1 Schalke Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The difference now is that Nmecha, after a difficult start in Westfalen, has become one of Niko Kovac’s key players, and one of the most recognised in his position in Europe. He scored the first goal of Jürgen Klopp’s Germany tenure, and was linked with big-money moves to the Premier League last summer. So BVB must protect their present, in the sporting sense, their future, in the financial sense, and their very fabric, in terms of their continued relationship with supporters, already strained in recent years by their deal with the arms manufacturer Rheinmetall. For his part Nmecha has responded enigmatically and characteristically, quoting a Bible verse on his socials as a caption to snaps of the game. The one thing the club cannot say is that they never saw this coming.

Talking points

Bayern remain on top but nothing is easy at the moment, even after their brilliant victory at Atlético in midweek. They closed out a narrow in at Mainz but Manuel Neuer was injured again, suffering a partial ligament tear of his right foot on the day he became Bayern’s oldest Bundesliga player at 40 years and 225 days, his sixth substitution in 2026. Whether he will – or should – return is now a fair question, with Jonas Urbig a ready-made replacement. Harry Kane provided assists for both goals to reach double figures in the category, his best-ever assist return in a season already.

View image in fullscreen Manuel Neuer is substituted off for the sixth time this year. Photograph: Sebastian El-Saqqa/firo sportphoto/Getty Images

The mood was not helped, however, by Uli Hoeness’ latest comments on Jamal Musiala, throwing doubt on whether he can recover his best level on the programme Der Sonntags-Stammtisch. “He’s still getting paid,” the honorary president underlined. “But imagine if FC Bayern were to say what he’s capable of now isn’t what’s stipulated in the contract?”

Even if there was another combination of the El Mala brothers – Malek setting up a goal for Saïd this week – for Köln in the derby with Leverkusen, the game had already been decided then, by a typically classy intervention by Patrik Schick.

Sports.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
Sports.content:
In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.”

With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week.

View image in fullscreen Players and staff line up during the tribute in Tenerife to Jesús de Miguel. Photograph: Borja Suárez/Reuters

Two days earlier Tenerife had been in Navahermosa, La Mancha, the tiny village their teammate’s family are from, carrying the coffin of the friend their captain called “our Demigol”. They were supposed to be in Granada on Saturday; instead, they were back on the island, in their home ground, to say goodbye and pay homage. Publicly, this time. Lilies had been laid on the pitch there too, a Tenerife shirt with them, and a stage built at one end. “We’ve seen how fragile life is,” the captain, Enric Gallego, said, offering words he said could never be enough, carrying the burden for all of them. “We think of the journeys, the wins, the losses, and hold on to those moments that seemed normal, but that now … a few days ago we shared that with you. To talk of you in the past tense is unfair. None of us are prepared to live what we’re living through.”

View image in fullscreen Tenerife’s Enric Gallego speaks during his tribute to Jesús de Miguel. Photograph: Borja Suárez/Reuters

No one ever could be. Across Spain this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them. That, Budimir had told his teammates, was something they must think about but not think about too. The players’ union in which De Miguel had a role, a footballer there for others, had asked for the competition to stop. Respect demanded that it did, they said, requesting a judge intervene when the league did not hear them. But it had gone on. The only matches postponed were those involving Tenerife; Andorra, whose goalkeeper Jesús Owono had crashed into De Miguel; and Castellón, who he had taken to the second division, delivering them to segunda for the first time in 16 years and himself for the first time at all, aged 27.

On the eve of the game that opened this weekend’s fixtures, the Sevilla head coach, Luis García, said he thought they should wait. It was too soon, too raw, too theirs. His midfielder Giorgi Kochorashvili had missed training the day before: a former Castellón player, Kochorashvili had asked permission to go to the funeral, leaving early and returning late, his mind elsewhere. Of course he could, García had replied, “we are humans above all else”. And it was not just him. García had worked with Owono – “let’s not make two victims, we have had enough; he is in hell, for sure”, he had pleaded – and now he said: “If there’s a play that’s similar … what do I say to my goalkeeper?

“We need time,” García had said. “We need to reflect.”

Instead, they played. From Seville on Friday night to Madrid on Sunday, via stadiums everywhere. It was, some suggested, the best way to pay homage to De Miguel but no one truly knew. “We can’t ask him what he would have wanted,” José Mourinho said before Madrid went to Valencia and won 3-0, Tenerife’s flag flying at half-mast at Mestalla. He might not have wanted anything at all. “You never wanted any attention,” Gallego said, but this weekend he was on all their minds.

“Forever in our memories,” the league’s line read. At every game in the first and second divisions, the ritual was repeated. Teams came out together wearing the same white shirts bearing his name. Flowers were laid, a little uncomfortably, on the spot inside the centre circle where he had fallen and there was a minute’s silence, players and officials gathered around the wreath. As they stood before Cádiz-Oviedo, tears ran down the cheeks of the Tenerife-based referee Marta Huerta de Aza. On stadium screens, an image of De Miguel appeared. On television screens, a QR code did: a link to a crowdfunding campaign for the young family he left, set up by the former Tenerife player Fran Sol.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé after a minute’s silence in memory of De Miguel at Mestalla. Photograph: Pablo Morano/Reuters

The games began and then, in the ninth minute or as near as the referee could manage, they paused again: the teams stopped, looking up to the screen, where a video of his best moments played out. It was not always an easy watch, and some preferred not to.

At Sevilla, where fans saw Antonio Puerta collapse on the pitch and pass away, applause still offered in the 16th minute every game, Kochorashvili stood by the bench, eyes lost somewhere his mind was not. At Espanyol, where in the 21st minute they applaud Dani Jarque, the captain who died during a pre-season tour and to whom Andrés Iniesta dedicated the winning goal at the 2010 World Cup final, Álex Calatrava and Álvaro González, teammates at Castellón and Tenerife respectively, looked about to break. In the ninth minute at the Metropolitano, the place was still rocking, the timing out of sync: Giuliano Simeone had just scored, so the referee Javier Alberola Rojas allowed a couple of minutes to pass, choosing his moment, Diego Simeone helping him impose silence on the stands when he finally stopped it. Then they started again, expected to carry on regardless.

In Pamplona, Alejandro Catena, who scored the late equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Athletic, raised an Osasuna shirt with De Miguel’s name and number on the back. Theirs was the game that felt most out of place, attention drawn from where it should have been, where it was. It would not be true to say that it did not matter, the Osasuna head coach, Jagoba Arrasate, admitting he had been carried along with it like everyone else, the calmness he thought they had found in the months out of the game soon abandoned again.

View image in fullscreen The Diocese of Tenerife, Eloy Alberto Santiago, speaks during Jesús de Miguel’s tribute. Photograph: Borja Suárez/Reuters

As they played, grateful for the grand day that they had before them, all the days they did, the tribute continued in Tenerife. The Heliodoro had filled early, access by every gate except eight and nine, engulfed by flowers and candles. De Miguel’s shirt lay on the turf where he had, lilies to one side, a spotlight on it. Another wreath occupied the bench. A giant shirt stretched across one end where the stage was, a lectern awaiting the speakers. A cross presided over it. Staff and players wore No 9 badges on their lapels. Supporters came in Tenerife shirts. And in the yellow shirts of rivals Las Palmas, whose president and captain Kirian, who had recovered after cancer, came. “This is the Canaries I want,” said Tenerife’s majority shareholder, Rayco García.

In the seats set up on the pitch, Tenerife’s players and De Miguel’s family sat, their eyes heavy. The archbishop, Eloy Alberto Santiago led a mass. The club’s president and majority shareholder spoke. He promised they would never allow María, De Miguel’s widow, to be alone. He also announced they would adopt Carla, his 14-month-old daughter, supporting her economically until she is 18. Gallego addressed her, football as family meaning something. “I hope one day you can look back and see who your dad was, be proud of him, not just for the footballer he was but the person: for his humility, his goodness,” he said.

Sniffing, his voice breaking, the captain paid homage to his teammate, his strike partner, his friend. The kind of person, he said, who did not seem to be there, and definitely did not demand that people notice he was, but always was. A man, he noted, so disinclined to put anyone out that when his car broke down he walked home from training rather than bother anyone for a lift. That, he insisted, might not seem like much, but it said much. “Today we don’t want to talk only of the player; we want to talk about you, Jesús, about the person that was behind the shirt,” he had begun. “Above any game, any team, what really remains is the person and the impact you leave. And you were a very special person.”

Gallego gave way to the archbishop, orations led by Tenerife staff, and as the act came to a close, difficult days ahead, the spotlight taken elsewhere, the drums began and the fans belted out a familiar tune, once more with more meaningful than ever before:

double quotation mark We have to sing with even more strength if you’re losing

Even those who left us sing, from heaven

This will never stop

We will sing to eternity.”

Then Tenerife’s players departed. They have training on Monday and next week they play.

Sports.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life
Sports.content:
After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football.

The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek loss to Manchester United. That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the last 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had ever made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away to Napoli in Sunday’s early kick-off.

Roma Caput Mundi? The old Latin phrase positions Rome as the capital of the world. Probably a little bit of a stretch, given Roma’s result against United. Lazio are not even competing in European competition this season and their own manager, Gennaro Gattuso, keeps claiming his priority is to avoid relegation.

Still, this is an extraordinary moment for football in the capital. According to Opta, this is the first time two teams from the same city have ever made it through 11 games of a Serie A season without a single defeat. When you consider that Rome’s two leading clubs have won just five Scudetti between them – as compared to 40 combined for Internazionale and Milan – the statistic jumps out even more.

View image in fullscreen Davide Frattesi scored Lazio’s goal at Napoli to keep them unbeaten in the league. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/AP

Acknowledging this detail in an interview after collecting his award, Gasperini could not help but draw a contrast between his team and their rivals. “It’s a bit of a surprise for everyone to have this Scudetto derby situation playing out in November,” he said. “But it’s a reflection of the values of the city. “Rome is an extraordinary city which has a huge enthusiasm for football. For Roma the stadium is always full. Lazio might have some other problems. But the passion for football in Rome is incredible.”

His reference was to the mass boycott of Lazio’s home games by supporters, the reasons for which have been covered in recent editions of this column. Attendance figures for the Biancocelesti’s home games at the Stadio Olimpico this season hover at about 10,000 people. Roma drew 64,674 for Sassuolo on Saturday – in line with their average. Ticket sales do not decide football games. Lazio sit top of the table heading into the international break. But Roma have plenty to feel good about too.

Sassuolo were about the best team they could have faced this weekend. Seeking a bounce-back after their collapse in Manchester, Roma lined up against opponents who had earned a single point from their previous six games and owned the leakiest defence in the division.

Leonardo Balerdi had a header cleared off the line before Mario Hermoso put Roma ahead in the 27th minute, punishing some indecisive defending. Moments later, a scuffed shot from Donyell Malen – bobbling far off target – took deviations off a pair of Sassuolo players and wound up in the back of the net. The only question left was how many goals Roma would add. In the end it was just one, Rodrigo Mora cutting in from the left and swapping passes with Malen before striking back across his body into the bottom corner from the right side of the box.

A third consecutive Serie A game with a goal for the 19-year-old, who also set up Matías Soulé’s opener against United. And the Portuguese even played the initial ball to create the chance that led to their penalty in that game as well.

Gasperini has never been shy in his enthusiasm for Mora. “We’re standing before an extraordinary talent,” said the manager after including the teenager in his starting XI for a season-opening 4-0 win over Fiorentina in August. “Every time he touches the ball something beautiful happens.”

View image in fullscreen Gian Piero Gasperini has tried to temper expectations around a league title for Roma but remains adamant that they are ambitious. Photograph: Alfredo Falcone/LaPresse/Shutterstock

is not alone in noticing. Mora was called up by Portugal this week for their Nations League games against Denmark and Wales. He has trained with the senior team before but not played for them. There will be greater opportunities to do so now Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football, though Mora expressed regret, too, at not getting to train again with a man he described as “my idol”.

Back at Roma, Gasperini has tried not to ask too much, too soon, of Mora, giving him a full 90 minutes only once, in a Champions League rout of Slovan Bratislava. Otherwise, he has alternated starts with opportunities from the bench during this busy early-season stretch.

Only in the last week did that change. Mora started against Udinese, scoring the second goal in a 5-2 win, then was back in the lineup to face United. Gasperini’s decision to take him off at half-time of that game has been widely criticised. These things are always easy to oversimplify, but it is true that Roma’s attacking threat seemed to vanish with Mora missing after the interval.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Venezia 2-1 Udinese, Torino 1-1 Lecce, Cagliari 1-0 Frosinone, Parma 1-2 Bologna, Roma 3-0 Sassuolo, Napoli 1-1 Lazio, Monza 0-1 Atalanta, Genoa 1-2 Milan, Inter 2-0 Como, Fiorentina 2-2 Juventus Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Gasperini spoke at the end of that defeat of it being a lesson that Roma could learn from. His team is still a work in progress, but the trend lines are more than encouraging. Roma secured their Champions League spot by winning six of their final seven games last season. They have not lost a domestic home game for more than 11 months and even their most recent away defeat in Serie A, to Inter, was all the way back in April.

Mora’s rapid ascent has added a new wrinkle. The attack we have seen in Roma’s last three games, with him and Soulé playing either side of Malen in a 3-4-2-1 has carved opponents open with such devastating effectiveness that you could start to wonder whether a healthy Paulo Dybala – for so long the standout talent here – would displace any of them from a first-choice XI.

This is not really a debate anyone needs to have. Roma hope to get Dybala back from his calf injury after the international round, but his body has always imposed breaks for him in every season and the Giallorossi will need rotation in any case to keep everyone fresh through a long campaign.

The improved depth of Roma’s squad, on the other hand, is a reason to believe that they can sustain their strong start. Gasperini, like most managers, would prefer to talk about the next game than discuss title ambitions this early in a campaign, but when a reporter asked if he would sign up now for a guaranteed second place he dismissed the idea out of hand.

“We don’t need to give ourselves false illusions, but we’re not going to knock ourselves down for no reason either,” he said. “I don’t know what we can achieve.”

Sports.title: Lens were humiliated by Como. The pain continued against Marseille
Sports.content:
The Lens striker, Florian Sotoca, was completely motionless as he looked into the middle space from the bench. The game, finely poised at 2-1 with a few minutes remaining, was not beyond his side, but that is not the story his troubled face told.

Marseille had just restored their lead thanks to a goal from substitute Keyliane Abdallah. Bruno Génésio’s men would go on to take all three points and continue their unlikely charge up the table, but the atmosphere at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis was morose before Marseille had even stepped on the pitch. The match did little to lift the mood at the end of a week in which Lens made unwanted history.

A pre-match banner unfurled by Lens fans that called the players a “disgrace” had not even been put away when a miscommunication between Jonathan Gradit and Samson Baidoo gifted Marseille the lead after 82 seconds. The former’s pass dribbled towards the goalline and was tapped in by Amine Gouiri from just a yard out.

It was a disastrous start for Lens, who recorded the joint-heaviest defeat in Champions League history last week. The 9-1 thrashing by Como was also the heaviest home loss in the competition’s history. Yannick Cahuzac, the Lens manager, called it a “humiliation”. The club’s president, Joseph Oughourlian, scrawled the words: “never again” inside the dressing room. Losing to Marseille on Sunday was not as chastening but the defeat posed more questions about the club’s recent decisions.

When Cahuzac, a friend of sporting director Jean-Louis Leca, stepped up from his assistant role in September to replace Dino Toppmöller, who lasted just six games, there were accusations of cronyism. Cahuzac’s stint so far has been a poor advert for the practice.

After three defeats in the league, winless in the Champions League, a derby defeat to Lille, a record-breaking loss to Como, and the wheels have well and truly come off at Lens; the jury is out on whether Cahuzac can set them back in motion. It was one of his former teammates, Florian Thauvin, who equalised for Lens against Marseille – his former club – with a close-range header. The playmaker, a harsh omission from Zinedine Zidane’s latest France squad, has been a rare bright spot in an increasingly gloomy situation.

View image in fullscreen Lens fans unveiled a banner that read: ‘You are a disgrace to 120 years of history.’ Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

Génésio said earlier in the season that these were the kinds of games Marseille could compete in but not win. But, as the French maxim goes, “le foot va vite” (football moves quickly). The tide has turned in Marseille; five league wins in a row have taken Marseille from the relegation zone to the Champions League places.

Génésio says his team’s fragile revival exists on “a knife’s edge”, however recent results – including a win at Bayer Leverkusen in the Europa League last week – have fed into growing optimism that his limited squad (both in quality and quantity) might avoid the abject season that fans had assumed was inevitable. The achievement belongs to Génésio, as does this win, secured by substitute Abdallah.

The academy product was banished to the reserves after his performance against Le Havre last month. Génésio criticised “a kind of lobbying around the young players” (from whom he did not specify) and held firm on his stance. He got the desired response. Re-integrated, Abdallah popped up at the back post to give Marseille a win that has taken them up to fourth in the table. They were second from bottom before the last international break.

View image in fullscreen Marseille players celebrate after their victory in Lens. Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty Images

Lens have replaced Marseille as France’s crisis club. After the match the home players did a tour of the pitch, applauding the fans for their support. In response, the fans unfurled a banner that read: “Shame on you.” Le foot va vite. Just six months ago fans packed into the Bollaert in the wee hours of the morning to welcome home their heroes after they had won the Coupe de France final. That feels like a lifetime ago for the players, fans and Pierre Sage, the manager who delivered that trophy.

“We are sick,” admitted Cahuzac after the match. There has been soul-searching but also plenty of finger pointing. Cahuzac says he “isn’t worried” about his job. Despite the growing pressure, he certainly has reasons to feel reassured but his friend, Léca, is also under a bit of fire after a second summer transfer window considerably less successful than his first. Jean-Clair Todibo, Thorgan Hazard and Franjo Ivanovic all arrived with high expectations but have fallen way short of them.

The fans had a banner for Léca, too, calling out his “shit interview” after the defeat to Como. They wanted an “apology”. They did not get one but it is certainly a sorry state of affairs at Lens.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Rennes 1-2 Lille Angers 0-2 Nice Brest 2-0 Lyon Le Havre 0-2 Lorient Le Mans 1-1 Monaco Lens 1-2 Marseille Auxerre 0-1 Paris FC PSG 1-0 Troyes Toulouse 3-1 Strasbourg Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

Monaco won their third game in a row in the Conference League last week, but their 1-1 draw at Le Mans was their fifth straight game without a win in Ligue 1. Filipe Luís says they need to “cleanse the minds” over the international break. When Monaco last won in Ligue 1 – against Lens in September – they were top of the table. They now sit seventh. The goals have dried up for Paris Brunner, Folarin Balogun – returning from injury – has yet to replicate the form that attracted Premier League interest and Matthis Abline put in an anonymous display against Le Mans. Monaco were reliant on a defensive blunder to open the scoring through Mamadou Coulibaly, who could be in trouble for a throat-slit celebration. Brunner was punished for a similar celebration earlier this season, although on that occasion it was directed towards the opposition fans. Le Mans, who equalised in the 90th minute through Erwan Colas, are also without a league win since September, but there was a strong show of support for manager Patrick Videira from the home fans, who also took a dig at the club’s unpopular football adviser Bruno Cheyrou. He evidently would not have popular support if he were to instigate a managerial change.

From cleansing minds at Monaco to exorcising demons at Nice. The club endured a shocking 2025-26 campaign, during which the relationship between fans, the players, and the club reached breaking point. It ended with Nice narrowly avoiding relegation to Ligue 2, thanks to a playoff win over Saint-Étienne. A new manager, Olivier Pantaloni, and a new sporting director, Roger Ricort, came in over the summer, but the players and Pantaloni continued to speak of the scars of the previous campaign. They showed in the opening four games, none of which Le Gym managed to win. Since then, however, only PSG have taken more points. Nice’s 2-0 win at Angers means they have picked up 15 points from their last possible 18. The club are now in European contention. Pantaloni is once again working his magic, just as he did at Lorient last season.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace poised to sack Pierre Sage and target Frank after Liverpool defeat
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging as the main candidate to succeed him.

The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats.

Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches.

He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

The former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche also has his backers at Palace and would be seen as a safe pair of hands given his vast experience in the Premier League. Vítor Pereira, another former Forest manager, could be an alternative.

Sage signed a three-year contract in south London after leaving Lens, where he won the Coupe de France and qualified for the Champions League in his final season. Palace have lost their two main central defenders this year, Marc Guéhi moving to Manchester City in January and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea in the summer. Two loan players – Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor – were signed as replacements. Palace did not land one of Sage’s top targets, Malick Fofana.

Sage denied after the Liverpool game that his dream job had turned into a “nightmare” but suggested that Palace’s squad needed investment in January. “We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions,” he said.

Sports.title: Arsenal consider move for highly rated Bundesliga striker
Sports.content:
Arsenal are considering a potential move for Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane as they look to bolster their attack.

Despite a near-perfect start to the season, the Gunners have found themselves lacking firepower up front at times and heavily reliant on Kai Havertz as their focal point.



4 Mikel Arteta is yet to find a prolific goalscorer for his Arsenal side Credit: Getty

Six of Arsenal's nine Premier League wins this term have been by a single-goal margin, highlighting goals as a potential area for improvement.

While Viktor Gyokeres is also available, Mikel Arteta has been reluctant to use him - starting the Swede just once in the league.

With the £63.7million man facing an uncertain future, this has prompted speculation that Arsenal could be forced into the market in January.



Kofane interest

A potential Arsenal target has now been identified, with the BBC reporting that Bundesliga star Kofane has emerged as an option.

The 20-year-old has scored three goals in six appearances for Bayer Leverkusen this season in all competitions.



However, his progress has been halted by a hamstring injury, which has kept the frontman out of action since October 10.

Kofane's name will be a familiar one to Arsenal fans, having started in both legs against the Premier League champions last term as Leverkusen lost 3-1 on aggregate in the Champions League last-16.



While the Cameroonian failed to score in either game, his rapid rise in recent years has clearly caught the Gunners' eye.

In 2024, he moved to Spanish second-tier side Albacete from AS Nylon in Cameroon and scored eight goals in 20 LaLiga 2 games.

Kofane's form was noticed by Leverkusen, who then signed the striker in July 2025.

4 Kofane scored five goals in his debut Bundesliga campaign last season Credit: Getty



4 The Cameroonian is in just his second season of top-flight football Credit: Getty

Since then, the striker has scored ten goals and provided a further nine assists in 50 appearances altogether for Leverkusen.

Kofane isn't the only forward option to be linked with Arsenal in recent weeks.

The Gunners were also reported to be considering a January move for Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi following his impressive goalscoring exploits.



Tresoldi has fired in 14 goals in 17 games in all competitions this term, including a hat-trick in the Champions League against Inter Milan.

Arsenal's Achilles heel?

As mentioned, a lack of goals has been Arsenal's only real shortcoming so far this season.

The north Londoners have made an excellent start, winning nine of their opening 10 league games.

4 Kai Havertz has been caught offside 15 times this season - the most in the Premier League Credit: Getty



Their latest victory - a 1-0 home win over Hull - saw them equal their best ever start to a Premier League season, and leaves them five points clear at the top of the table.

However, the Gunners have done so without a main source of goals, with Havertz, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka the joint-top scorers in the league with three goals each.

A lack of clinical finishing appeared to worry Arteta following the Hull win, as he admitted his Arsenal side must improve here.

Speaking afterwards, he said: "We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.



"Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks.

"We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And open, I think, the scoreline much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game."

Sports.title: Ben White sets record straight on suggestion he doesn’t like football
Sports.content:
Does Premier League winner Ben White actually not like football? Well, he's now cleared up all of the rumours...

White shocked fans in 2023 as he admitted that he doesn't watch the sport after his teammates hinted he didn't like it either.

3 White has clarified suggestions that he doesn't like football following some of his comments about the sport in the past Credit: Getty

In an interview three years ago, former Arsenal forward Leandro Trossard joked that the defender's favourite time of the day was when he gets to go home from training or games.

As well as those instances, White had also previously revealed that he never watched football when he was growing up.

But despite that, he has clearly built an impressive career on the pitch, winning the Premier League with the Gunners last season.

In total, he has played over 400 times for five different clubs and his country, becoming one of the best defenders in England.

So, surely he has to like football, right?

Does Ben White like football?

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, White has clarified that he does in fact like football amid the suggestions that he doesn't.

"I think I said a comment that I don’t watch football, that doesn’t mean I don’t like it," the England international said. "I do it everyday so I must like it a little bit."

Going on to explain his more private approach to the sport, he added: "I don’t think anyone really knows my personality really, I probably keep that to my loved ones and my family.

"So, I think it’s all noise when people have an opinion on that stuff because it’s not actually me that’s… people don’t know the me me, you know?

"And I quite like it that way, it’s something I can have for myself and the people that I love."

3 White has admitted that, of course, he does like the sport but that his personal life will always remain private despite interest from curious fans Credit: Getty

When asked whether he feels he has to perfom when playing the game, he continued: "I think you give so much to the game, it’s obviously very intense.

"It’s important to keep some bits for yourself.

"Giving you everything and everything you have can be quite draining, so I think that’s just the way I am and I keep my energy for the people I love."

White hails England captain Harry Kane

White may not watch much football, but one person that does keep him glued to the screen is England teammate Harry Kane.

Kane is set to break the all-time Three Lions appearance record on Thursday against Croatia, live on talkSPORT, and the defender has hailed his captain for his incredible performances.

In fact, the Arsenal star believes the Ballon d'Or winner's showing against the Gunners last month was one of the best ever.

3 White may not always watch football, but he will watch Kane - labelling his performance against Arsenal in October one of the best ever Credit: Getty

"There’s so many things you can say about him," White began.

"Looking from the outside and knowing what’s been done for him on the inside, seeing how he works every day and how he trains, it’s not a surprise to see where he’s at now.

"Playing against him a few weeks ago, it was one of the best performances I’ve seen from a striker.

"I think he’s constantly proving people wrong and constantly stretching the limits out even further for himself."

Sports.title: Ben White stands by decision to leave World Cup camp and insists he isn’t bothered about England fans’ boos
Sports.content:
Ben White stands by decision to leave World Cup camp and insists he isn’t bothered about England fans’ boos

Ben White will not be going into further detail about his decision to leave the England camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

The Arsenal defender, who made a return to the Three Lions set-up in March, has decided not to 'throw anyone under the bus'.

5 White is back in the England squad for a second time since his surprise decision to stay away from the national team after walking away from the World Cup camp Credit: Getty

White left the squad during the World Cup in Qatar four years ago, and went on to make himself unavailable for a call-up up until this year.

The reasoning behind his exit from the camp has never been revealed, with the FA explaining it was due to 'personal reasons' at the time.

Reports of a clash with ex-assistant Steve Holland had done the rounds, but then-England boss Gareth Southgate downplayed the rumours in 2024.

Now, White is back in the England fold under Thomas Tuchel, who ended the right-back's national team hiatus in March.

Tuchel called him back up for the squad and he made two appearances, but his re-inclusion caused some backlash from fans as he was booed when he stepped onto the pitch at Wembley.

The 29-year-old did not represent England at the World Cup last summer, although he was ruled out by a knee ligament injury sustained late in the 2025/26 season.

He is set to play in front of the Three Lions faithful again this week after being picked for the upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, both live on talkSPORT.

Why did Ben White leave the England camp?

Ahead of those clashes, White spoke exclusively to talkSPORT about his controversial decision to leave the England camp in 2022.

White explained: "It's something I haven't spoken about, and I won't go into detail about it. It's a decision I don't want to talk about in a negative way or throw anyone under the bus."

"It wasn't an ideal situation but it's probably one I would still make," he went on to admit.

5 White refused to speak about any details of why he left the England camp and still stands by his decision to depart four years ago Credit: Getty

"Obviously, it's amazing to be (back in camp) in a fresh moment ahead of the two games."

Clarifying whether he refused to play for England following the incident four years ago, he added: "There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn't great.

"I don't want to throw anyone under the bus. A lot of people try to do that to me so it's something I don't want to do myself."

White then went on to discuss the backlash that he faced on his return to the England team under Tuchel's management.

When asked how hard it was for him, he said: "Especially because they didn't know the situation, which is kind of what I put my mind to.

"They don't know my situation, so it's not really about what I've done because they don't actually know why. And I think if they did, they probably wouldn't be booing or saying these things."

5 The Arsenal right-back was booed on his return to Wembley with England, but he isn't bothered by the reaction from the fans Credit: Getty

He concluded: "The booing's fine, I've had it before. It wasn't something that bothered me too much. A few boos weren't going to upset me too much."

White 'proud' to play for England again

With the chapter now over, White appears to be a favourite of the England boss and he has a future with the team.

So, how does he feel to be back playing for his country?

"It's such a different feeling, I'm just immensely proud," he said. "I think of what I've done to get in this position that no one has seen.

"So, just taking a step back and being proud of how much I've done to get into this situation."

The Arsenal star was then asked if he wanted to send any message to the fans who have doubted his commitment to the Three Lions.

5 White has spoken of his pride of playing for England again ahead of their upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain Credit: Getty

He replied: "I don't think I'm looking to win anyone over or say anything that helps them get back on my side.

"It is what it is and there's reason for it.

"I'm just looking forward to playing for England, doing well, helping the team and looking for success."

How did Tuchel convince White to return?

Speaking ahead of England's upcoming fixtures with White in the squad, Tuchel urged fans not to boo White for the incident.

He believes it should be 'a closed book' and praised the 'investment' of the defender when recalled to the Three Lions' camp.

The backing of the manager comes after he got in touch with White and managed to convince him to return to the set-up.

5 Tuchel managed to convince White to return to the England set-up in March and he has called him up again this month Credit: Getty

"I think with the boss, he doesn't need to say too much," White said, revealing what Tuchel did to get him to accept a call-up.

"The effort that he made to speak to me and reach out was so nice and I really appreciated it.

"As soon as you see a manager like that, you want to learn and play under a manager like that, so it was a huge thing playing for Thomas, for sure."

On what Tuchel specifically said to draw him back into international football, he added: "The word 'play' maybe...

"A different option to some of the other full-backs in England now... obviously I had some good moments over the years, playing at a top club, winning things and I think I can bring something different to the team."

Sports.title: Brad Friedel named director of EFL club as US takeover completed
Sports.content:
Brad Friedel named director of EFL club as US takeover completed

Brad Friedel is back in English football after being confirmed as Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director.

The former Tottenham and Liverpool goalkeeper has been appointed after an American consortium completed their takeover of the club.

3 Shrewsbury are in League Two and could do with Friedel's vast expertise Credit: Getty

As a player, Friedel made 450 Premier League appearances for Blackburn Rovers, Aston Villa, Spurs and Liverpool.

Meanwhile, his most recent role in football saw him serve as an advisor at Turkish giants Besiktas in 2024.

Fronted by American businessman Scott Davidson, who 'brings significant experience across financial services, investment, corporate leadership and real estate,' the consortium has invested in the Shrews.

New chairman Davidson also boasts experience of football club ownership with Scottish club Spartans, who are based in Edinburgh.

Friedel, Davidson and chief executive Liam Dooley are set to speak to the media at a press conference on Thursday, which is scheduled for 3pm.

Will Dotson and Craig Graham, who are also board members of Spartans, will join Friedel as directors at Shrewsbury, subject to IFR approval.

How long had Shrewsbury been up for sale?

Former owner Roland Wycherley, who has been at the helm of Shrewsbury since June 1996, had the club up for sale since 2024.

A number of parties expressed their interest in acquiring the Shropshire club, including Mike Harris, who also owns Welsh side The New Saints.

However, Wycherley was reluctant to relinquish Shrewsbury, with Harris claiming it's because the 85-year-old has set an unrealistic price for the club's worth.

How have Shrewsbury performed this season?

Shrewsbury sit 15th in League Two having won five of their opening 14 fixtures.

3 Friedel has been named as Shrewsbury's new sporting director Credit: Getty

Manager Gavin Cowan has overseen an impressive turnaround in recent weeks.

His side made a slow start to the campaign, winning just one of their opening five matches as well as suffering four defeats.

However, a run of one loss in eight matches was only ended by Gillingham on October 31.

The Shrews are also into the second round of this season's FA Cup thanks to a 2-1 away win over National League outfit Eastleigh on Saturday.

Shrewsbury return to League Two action at home to Oldham Athletic on Saturday.

A win could see them move into the play-off places, with just three points separating them from fifth place Cheltenham.

3 Shrewsbury boss Cowan has steadied the ship after a slow start to the season Credit: Getty

The club finished 19th in the fourth tier last term on 49 points, ten clear of relegation.

Sports.title: Harry Kane suffers unprecedented snub from 2026 World XI despite Ballon d’Or glory
Sports.content:
Harry Kane was a shock omission from the 2026 FIFPro World Team of the Year, two weeks after his Ballon d'Or success.

The Bayern Munich superstar enjoyed an historic triumph in October when he became the first Englishman to win the iconic Golden Ball award in 25 years.

4 Harry Kane became just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or last month Credit: AFP

Kane beat off stiff competition to land football's ultimate individual prize, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal.

It capped off a record-breaking campaign for the England captain, which saw him enjoy a stellar 61-goal campaign for Bayern Munich.

However, just two weeks after being crowned the best footballer in the world, Kane has now been dealt a brutal reality check.

Kane misses out

Kane was brutally left out of FIFPro's World XI - a FIFA award voted for exclusively by professional footballers.

With more than 19,000 players from 73 countries selecting their men's and women's teams this year, Kane failed to secure enough votes to make it into the prestigious XI.

England's talisman received a 27.6 per cent share of the vote, which saw him overlooked for the team's four-man attack.

Set up in a bizarre 3-3-4 formation, the front-line instead featured Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Ballon d'Or runners-up Mbappe and Yamal as well as Argentina icon Lionel Messi.

Kane's brutal snub marks the first time a Ballon d'Or winner has been left out of the FIFPro XI in the year they won the award.

The category recognising the annual World XI was first introduced in 2005, making Kane's omission a 21-year first.

There was England representation elsewhere, with Jude Bellingham being selected in midfield after a stunning World Cup campaign.

4 Haaland finished eighth in the Ballon d'Or rankings, but was chosen ahead of Kane for the FIFPro World XI Credit: Getty

4 Kane scored 73 goals for England and Bayern Munich in the 2025/26 season to secure the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

The Real Madrid sensation was named alongside Spain's World Cup-winning captain Rodri and Paris Saint Germain's Vitinha in the middle of the park.

Making up a three-man defence, Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsi was voted in after being named the best young player at the World Cup, joined by Nuno Mendes and Achraf Hakimi either side of him.

There was also a surprise call in goal, as Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya was named in the side ahead of Spain teammate Unai Simon.

It's fair to say this year's world XI will prove controversial for Kane's omission alone, but he wasn't the only huge name to miss out.

Other notable absentees include 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Michael Olise.

Meanwhile, Messi's inclusion ahead of Kane sees the football icon return to the World XI for the first time since 2023, extending his overall record to 18 appearances.

4 Messi, who now plays for MLS club Inter Miami, was named in the World XI despite not playing club football in a top European league Credit: AFP

Spain sensation Yamal also enjoyed another piece of history from his latest selection, having also been named in the 2025 XI.

At just 19, Yamal is the first teenager to earn two World XI selections, which could soften the disappointment of missing out on the Ballon d'Or.

Sports.title: Two England players set for job share as Thomas Tuchel weighs up options for key position
Sports.content:
Two England players set for job share as Thomas Tuchel weighs up options for key position

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he could again split goalkeeping responsibilities between Jordan Pickford and James Trafford.

The Three Lions have a Nations League double header this week - as they host Croatia on Thursday night before travelling to face Spain on Sunday, with both games live on talkSPORT.

4 Pickford is facing his biggest threat yet to his England No.1 spot Credit: Getty

With two games in the space of three days, Tuchel could well look to rotate his 25-man squad to keep legs fresh.

And while England's No.1 shirt has been largely undisputed since Pickford entered the fold in 2017, the last international break saw he and Trafford share the minutes.

In England's extended four-match camp, Tuchel gave the two goalkeepers two games each, and Leeds stopper Trafford has been tipped to continue to stake his claim for a starting berth.

Pickford's position has come in for scrutiny in recent months, with questions being raised over some goals he conceded at the World Cup.

Tuchel: Pickford still No.1

While Trafford's increased game time for England recently has only fed speculation over a potential changing of the guard in goal, Tuchel has insisted that Pickford remains first-choice for now.

However, the England boss admitted he would be tempted to once again give both goalkeepers equal minutes over the coming week.

Tuchel told reporters: “Pickford is number one, but nothing has changed.

“The competition is on there as well, like for the outfield players. They shared the matches last time. I’m not sure what we will do. There’s an opportunity that we maybe do this again. I have to speak with our goalkeeper coach.”

Tuchel also insisted the Nations League is an ideal opportunity to look at his goalkeeping options, as opposed to international tournaments.

He continued: “When do I have a chance to see another goalkeeper, if not in Nations League? If not in high pressure matches?

4 Trafford has earned four England caps to date Credit: Getty

4 Tuchel is hoping to watch two of his goalkeeping options in action this week Credit: Getty

"So we had James against Spain [a 3-2 defeat]. Because what happens if Jordan Pickford is injured? What happens if he’s not available? So it’s better to test it.

"Jordan knows about this, that we want to use Nations League for exactly that.

"But at the moment, nothing has changed. At the moment, he’s the number one. And he just feels a bit of competition. Which is good for him.”

Should Trafford succeed Pickford as No.1, it would mark the end of an era for one of England's most reliable players of the last decade.

Since making his debut in 2017, Pickford has earned 93 Three Lions caps, playing a major role in runs to back-to-back European Championship finals and two World Cup semi-finals.

And despite now facing more pressure on his spot, Tuchel insists the Everton stopper was 'surprisingly' understanding about sharing keeper duties in the Nations League last time.

4 Trafford only had two caps before the last England camp but then played in the first two England matches, against Spain and away to Czechia, ahead of Pickford Credit: Getty

The German coach said: “I was very impressed and a bit surprised by his reaction when we spoke to him.

“I thought he’d be less of a fan than he proved to be. Because he said he totally understands it. He impressed me a lot last time. We spoke to him, it was a very short conversation. It was very positive.

“He said ‘yeah, let’s do this, Traff deserves it, and I will push him’. And he didn’t change at all. If he changed, he changed even to the positive, he pushed Traff, he gave him a good feeling. So very impressive, he did it very well.”

Trafford has earned four senior England caps since making his debut in March, but his recent club form has pushed himself into contention.

After becoming Leeds' record signing in the summer following his departure from Manchester City, the 24-year-old has kept five Premier League clean sheet in ten games.

His impressive form has helped the Whites make a solid start to the season - they currently sit ninth in the table after a home win over Tottenham on Saturday.

Sports.title: Adrian Durham defends Robbie Savage over ‘complete lies’ about Peterborough boss’ commitment
Sports.content:
Robbie Savage's commitment to his role as Peterborough United manager has been defended amid growing fan criticism.

The Posh boss has come under fire for continuing with his media duties despite the League One club's poor recent from.



3 Savage is still doing duties for TNT Sports alongside Credit: Getty

Savage's side have failed to win any of their last six matches in all competitions since his tenure started with back-to-back victories.

A third successive defeat came on Saturday as Peterborough were thrashed 5-0 at home by Reading in the first round of the FA Cup.

Savage defended by Durham

It followed social media speculation surrounding Savage's work as a pundit for TNT Sports earlier in the week.



The 52-year-old provided co-commentary during the Champions League clash between AEK Athens and Real Madrid on Wednesday.

He was then on punditry duty for Friday's FA Cup tie between Oxford City and Leicester City on the eve of Posh's clash with Reading.



His TV appearances led some fans to claim he had not been at training since Tuesday.

However, talkSPORT's Adrian Durham has shut down those suggestions with a social media post of his own.



Writing on X, the Peterborough fan explained: "Fans can question what they want, no problem with that, but they need to get their facts right first.

"Saying he’s missed training and that he was in Athens are two complete lies."

Savage did not travel to Greece to cover Real Madrid's win in Athens, instead providing commentary from a studio in the UK.

3 Durham has slammed 'complete lies' over Savage's media work Credit: PA



talkSPORT verdict

The matter remained up for debate on Monday's Breakfast show between Gabby Agbonlahor, Ally McCoist and Katie Shanahan.

Following the latest supporter criticism, Agbonlahor admitted: "I think for me, when it’s all going rosy and you’re winning games, no one’s going to talk about it.

"But when you are losing games and you lose 5-0, you’re not a manager that’s working in the National League, you’re working in League One, Peterborough.

"I feel like you have to give up your media gigs that you’ve got. I know there’s contracts involved, but when it’s not going rosy, you want your manager to be doing extra work at the training ground...



"Not going off to do other games, having an opinion on Premier League games, working for the radio. That’s my point of view."

Savage's Peterborough tenure

Savage was appointed by Peterborough, replacing Luke Williams in the dugout after leaving National League side Forest Green Rovers.

3 Savage is winless in his last six matches as Peterborough boss Credit: PA

Having won his first two matches, his side's form has since slumped with two draws and four defeats in their last six.



Those results include two losses in League One, where Posh find themselves 22nd in the table and two points from safety.

Peterborough have not played lower than the third-tier of English football since 2008.

They are set to return to action in the EFL Trophy against Luton Town on November 17 after this weekend's league meeting with Oxford United was postponed due to international call-ups.

Sports.title: Raul lands first senior manager role as club ruthlessly sack boss
Sports.content:
Real Oviedo have appointed Raul as their new manager on a two-year deal.

The Real Madrid legend has replaced Julian Calero in the dugout following his brutal sacking on Monday.



3 Raul has been appointed by Oviedo on a deal until 2028 Credit: Getty

Calero was dismissed by the Segunda Division outfit despite overseeing a 2-1 win at Cadiz on Saturday.

The victory proved to be the final match of his tenure, having only been appointed in the summer.

Oviedo have confirmed Calero's coaching staff have also departed the club.



The 56-year-old had been under contract until the end of the season.

His side had previously been knocked out of the Copa del Rey by fourth-tier Numancia last month.

Meanwhile, Oviedo find themselves ninth in the table following their relegation last season.



After 13 matches, they sit a point outside the play-off positions and six adrift of the top two.

Oviedo are aiming to secure promotion back to the top-flight after suffering relegation on their long-awaited return.



Last season marked the club's first LaLiga campaign for 24 years, but ended with them 13 points from safety in last place.

Raul has now taken on his first senior managerial role, with his contract running until the summer of 2028.

3 Calero was sacked on Monday despite winning his final match in charge Credit: Getty

His opening match in charge will come at home to Girona on Saturday.

Raul's coaching career

The 49-year-old has previously worked with Real Madrid's academy and reserve sides since retiring in 2015.



Raul returned to the club in 2018 as a youth team coach before spells managing the Under-18s, Under-19s and Castilla side.

Having guided the Under-19s to UEFA Youth League glory in 2020 he remained in charge of Real Madrid Castilla until departing at the end of the 2024/25 season.

The three-time Champions League winner is Los Blancos' all-time leading appearance maker with 741.

Raul also scored 323 goals for the Spanish giants as well as winning six LaLiga titles.



3 Raul previously spent six years as Real Madrid Castilla boss Credit: Getty

He also had spells with Schalke, Al Sadd and New York Cosmos before hanging up his boots aged 38.

At international level, the centre-forward scored 44 goals in 102 caps for Spain.

Sports.title: 'I've never revealed the whole story': England fans wouldn't boo me if they knew the truth, says Ben White... as he defends World Cup walkout and rejecting call-ups
Sports.content:
Ben White believes England fans would not boo him if they knew the truth behind his 2022 World Cup walkout. The Arsenal defender left the camp in Qatar after the group stages citing 'personal reasons', although a fallout with Gareth Southgate's assistant, Steve Holland, was later reported. He then declined a return to the England set-up while Southgate and Holland were in charge but was included by Thomas Tuchel in March of this year. However, White was booed by fans inside Wembley when he came on in the second-half of a friendly against Uruguay, only to score his first international goal and then concede a late penalty in a 1-1 draw. He was not selected for the World Cup in North America but is back with the squad ahead of this week's Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain. And the 29-year-old, addressing those jeers for the first time, said: 'It was hard to hear, especially because they didn't know the situation, which is kind of what I put my mind to. 'They don't know my situation and it is not really about what I have done, because they don't know why, and if they did they would not be booing or saying these things. I just think about maybe (them) not knowing the full story, and if they did, maybe they wouldn't (boo).' He added: 'Obviously, a load has been said. I've probably seen all of it. I just think people don't know the full story, because I've never said anything, and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that. Ben White has insisted he would not be booed by England fans if they knew the truth behind his World Cup walkout White fell out with former England assistant Steve Holland (left) before heading home during the 2022 World Cup 'There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn't great. I don't want to throw anyone under the bus. A lot of people try to do that to me so it's something I wouldn't want to do myself. I think it's probably the best way. It's a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it's amazing to be here now. It's a privilege to be called up.' White, however, is adamant that he would make the same decision today and leave the World Cup, even if he will not divulge the reasons as to why. 'I don't think I would (do anything different),' he said. 'I think, as a person, I'm quite real, and I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. It's one that I'm not happy about. It wasn't ideal. But it happened, it's time to move on. 'I don't think I am looking to win anyone over or say anything that helps them get back on my side. It is what it is. There are reasons for it and I am just looking forward to playing for England and doing well and looking for success.' White has spoken publicly about not watching football, and this, too, has been used against him by some supporters. 'It doesn't mean I don't like football, because I do it every day, so I must like it a little bit!' he said. 'It's because I don't watch it, which I think is quite normal for someone that does a job and then doesn't go home and then continue watching that job. 'I don't think anyone knows my personality. I keep that to my loved ones and family. It's all noise when people have an opinion on that stuff. It is not actually me. People don't know me and I like it that way. You give so much to the game, which is intense. I think it's important to keep some bits for yourself. I keep the energy for the people I love.'

Sports.title: Paul Scholes calls Man United's bizarre lap of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville claimed stars are risking 'emotional damage' with post-match ritual
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes has branded Manchester United's post-match walks of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville suggested the squad are causing themselves 'emotional damage'. United staged another incredible fightback to snatch a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals heading into injury-time. But it wasn't enough to spare the club from the humiliation of being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks – the longest United have spent there since 1986. After the full-time whistle, the United players conducted a post-match walk of honour as the fans chanted Michael Carrick's name in a defiant show of support for their beleaguered boss – a move a number of ex-United stars have called into question. 'I tell you one thing they have to do, is stop these laps of honour after the game,' Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football. 'What the f***?' Nicky Butt added: 'It's p***ing me off,' before Scholes continued: 'They are so bad. Not so much Michael, the team as well. It's embarrassing. It should be after the last game of the season. I feel sorry for them.' Paul Scholes has torn into Manchester United for their regular post-match laps of honour (Source: YouTube/The Good, The Bad and The Football) Gary Neville, meanwhile, said the habit has become 'painful to watch' as a United fan Neville, meanwhile, said on NBC Sports: 'You have got to admire their persistence, they kept going. 'Defensive errors were shocking and we'll discuss that shortly. But this lap around the pitch... 'I played for Manchester United 602 times and I always appreciated the fans at the end of the game, but this pattern of them walking around the pitch after defeats by Bournemouth and a 4-4 at home against Aston Villa, it's almost painful to watch. They're almost causing themselves emotional damage. 'This just can't go on, can it? It's absolutely desperate. Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation.' Carrick was involved in a spiky back-and-forth with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison when it was suggested to him that he could step down: Davison: 'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? If you thought walking away was the best thing, you'd probably do it.' Carrick: 'It's not going to happen, no.' Davison: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?' Carrick: 'Is there?' Davison: 'You would assume so, right?' Carrick: 'Would you?' Davison: 'What do you think, Michael?' Carrick: 'You're telling me what you think, aren't you?' Davison: 'I'm asking you what you think? What do you expect to happen?' Carrick: 'We understand the situation; we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward and keep working on things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.' He added: 'Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation' (Source: YouTube/NBC Sports) Carrick insisted 'it's not going to happen' when it was put to him that he could walk away if he thought that would be the 'best thing' for the club Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season. 'One hundred per cent,' he said. 'I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times… 'I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games.' Amid a wave of fan protests expressing their discontent towards INEOS and the Glazer family on Sunday, Neville has suggested that the club's hierarchy 'don't have a clue what to do' on Carrick. He added: 'You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years - that's not the answer. 'Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don't know. The ownership don't have a clue what to do. 'It's rinse and repeat. (Ruben) Amorim, (Erik) Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success; there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well. 'None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you've got a poor performance department, a poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail. 'Every organisation in the world will fail if you've not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom - your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football. 'There are real issues within that football club; you've got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.'
