Sports.title: Can Hamilton and Verstappen fight back for F1 Brazilian GP victory?
Sports.content:
With Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen 20th and 21st on the grid of the Brazilian Grand Prix, Sunday’s Formula 1 race promises to be fascinating – regardless of weather conditions.

Hamilton and Verstappen happen to be two drivers who performed memorable recoveries at Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, a track where overtaking has always been easier than most.

Back in 2021, the seven-time world champion was excluded from qualifying results due to a technical breach, meaning he started the sprint from last; he fought his way up to fifth. With a five-place grid drop for a new engine, Hamilton was 10th on the grid for the grand prix but battled to the front and came out on top in a titanic duel against Verstappen.

Three years later, the Dutchman was eliminated in Q2 on a wet Sunday morning and also took a five-place grid penalty for his sixth internal combustion engine, ending up 17th on the grid. The rain also impacted the race, but Verstappen rose to the occasion and comfortably overtook Esteban Ocon for victory.

But the DRS device had facilitated Hamilton’s exceptional drives, and the overtake mode that now features on F1’s new power units instead isn’t as decisive; the Interlagos layout might actually make it worse.

When asked how easy overtaking would be compared to 2021, the Ferrari driver replied: “Harder, because back then we had, obviously, a very long straight, and if you got close, you had the DRS, and maybe a car wouldn't have it – whereas now, everyone is just opening up their wings.

“I think overtaking will be very, very, very hard. I'm not sure you're going to see the same sort of races that you've seen in the past. But maybe the wet conditions will change that.”

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Now we don't have DRS anymore,” Verstappen concurred. “And the overtake mode is very limiting around here because of the long straight, everyone is draining the battery. So, your speed difference on the straight is going to be a lot less – a bit like Mexico, really. So, it will be quite a lot harder to pass than normal.”

So what will Hamilton’s strategy be? “I don't have one,” he responded. “Try to win, somehow.”

Verstappen, meanwhile, is banking on a number of incidents if he is to be a contender for victory. “Lots of safety cars, so they can't pull away, it keeps coming back to me,” the Red Bull racer said. “We'll see. I don't really think about it too much. I'll just go from lap one and see where I end up.”

He added: “I hope [with Lewis] we can clear the cars in front of us as quickly as we can.”

Across 19 grands prix so far in F1 2026, just two races have been won from outside the front row. Verstappen prevailed from fifth on the grid in Mexico, though he was virtually in the lead on lap one, and Antonelli remarkably triumphed from 19th in Italy. But if the expected rain impacts the race, then 2026’s dry-weather history will be meaningless.

Additional reporting by Isa Fernandes and Federico Faturos

Sports.title: The wet-weather challenges thrown up by Brazilian GP qualifying
Sports.content:
One hour, 23 minutes. You could've squeezed most of a football match into the rain delay during Formula 1 qualifying for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, and it looked for all the world like the session wouldn't actually get going again.

A repeat of 2024, where qualifying was squeezed onto Sunday morning, looked likely. Yet, a saviour arrived when a break in the clouds emerged, and the circuit had dried just enough for safety car specialist Bernd Maylander to give his approval of the conditions. It scarcely stopped a handful of drivers from having a moan about the visibility, but they soon accepted that they needed to lock in and focus up on getting around the track.

This meant the use of the lesser-spotted full-wet tyre, or the "x-wet" per the F1 lexicon. Often derided as a tyre only fit for bumbling around on behind the safety car, the blue-walled Pirelli was actually holding up pretty well and proved perfect for the level of standing water around the circuit. Aquaplaning, where the tyre struggles to break the surface tension of the water on-track, was nonetheless prevalent - but water dispersal as the rain held off soon brought the track to a more driveable state.

The downside of using the extreme wet tyre lies in the greater water dispersal (according to Pirelli, around 85 litres of water per second) which drastically cuts visibility as the spray rooster-tails out the back of the car. Yet, the dispersal is a necessary evil: without it, the circuit would just remain wetter for longer.

Although the rain lights ensure that the driver behind has at least some level of visibility, selecting your braking zone remains tricky; poor visibility means the driver must find a reference point in their immediate circle of vision. Stopping distances are also considerably longer, so a driver needs a different marker to their usual point of pedal application in the dry.

Considering all these climatic challenges, it's small wonder why race control takes a more tentative approach to wet conditions. Hence, it was a welcome surprise to see the session reopened - even if the circuit was still sodden with the afternoon downpour. Carlos Sainz reckoned that it was a "punchy" call from the FIA - but it only took a couple of laps to ensure the cars were more stable.

"It felt a bit punchy when we left on the x-wet because we were aquaplaning in sixth and seventh gear down the straights. And if you lose the car at those speeds, it's always going to be a big one," Sainz concluded after the session.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

"Also, very little visibility when you were running close to a car, but we were not forced to run close to cars in quali, so you can create a bit of a buffer to see. But it was very sketchy for two laps.

"Then we managed to create that little bit of dry line and the tyres started working, the aquaplaning started to go away. Everyone managed to keep the car on track until the end of Q1, which was a bit of a surprise, to be honest."

Liam Lawson agreed with Sainz's view of the session, stating that "when we started, it was extremely sketchy - I think we were definitely pushing it. But I like the fact that we were out there and not in the garage; I think obviously it is risky, but there weren't that many incidents."

As expected, the wet conditions delivered chances to those usually not accustomed to fighting at the top; the free practice performance-chasing was effectively rendered obsolete and the power units had slightly more parity as the effects of top-end performance and acceleration were mitigated by the low-grip track conditions.

This put a bit more of a premium on low-speed downforce and, crucially, keeping the tyres warm across Q1 - although Fernando Alonso nonetheless noted that "the engine is very important in terms of drivability and the way it behaves in the corners, and we still have a little bit of an issue there".

The approach through Q1 was, initially, simply about trying to set clean laps and hope that the progression of the circuit and the tyres would yield a lap-on-lap improvement.

Of course, each driver was tested on their reaction times in the event aquaplaning occurred, and the 2026 power units and the control over the rear brakes added another hurdle to overcome. But each driver (largely) became increasingly dialled in, watched as the laptimes improved, and then started to push the braking zones a little bit more as the circuit dried up.

There was a transition point in Q2, however, as the intermediates soon became the tyre to be on. With less standing water, the full wet was starting to overheat and was giving up performance in the middle part of the lap, initially enough to perhaps offset the dampness through the first and final sectors, before all three became much more suitable for the intermediate overall.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

This meant that they could chase the track grip more, and it was evident that the times had begun to peak at the end of Q2 as the circuit approached its best conditions under the downpour. Getting the intermediate timing right, which Lawson reckoned he and his Racing Bulls team had nailed, was key to getting a couple of quicker laps in without risking the threat of falling off the circuit.

A few drivers struggled at this crossover, particularly with harvesting and braking into Turn 12 - Sainz and Ollie Bearman both had offs here, as newcomer Rafael Camara couldn't get the car to slow down enough before he careened into the barrier at the close of Q2.

With more rain impending during Q3, it was more about a mad dash to get a clean lap in, rather than watching the progression. That's perhaps when it felt most like 'normal' qualifying, as the tyres were effectively good enough for one lap with the expected downpour setting something of a timer.

It appeared that the majority of the drivers genuinely enjoyed the rare chance to tackle properly wet conditions, although some had a few qualms about the session restarting. George Russell surmised that "I love driving in the rain - but at some point, if that was a race, that was no way we should be driving in it - the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident is very, very high."

Perhaps there's a bit of a split of opinion between the younger and older drivers; both Lewis Hamilton and Nico Hulkenberg expressed their enjoyment of wet conditions, while new champion Kimi Antonelli labelled them "the wettest conditions I've ever driven [in]. So it was not the nicest of experiences"; both he and Bearman said that the circuit was over the limit at the Q1 restart, although the latter conceded that the early running did at least contribute to the circuit improving.

Regardless, it was valuable data for each of the drivers ahead of Sunday's race - where inclement weather is expected to play a role once again. And so begins the overnight discussions: does anyone risk a pit-lane start for a set-up change?

Sports.title: “The car is steering by itself, don’t you see it?”: How handling trouble baffled Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli looked on course to win his first race as the new world champion as he pulled out an eight-second lead over his pursuers over the opening 12 laps at Interlagos.

But he reported something felt wrong with his Mercedes’ handling soon after switching to slick tyres and spun off, allowing Lando Norris through into the lead. The two Red Bull drivers passed him and by lap 34 Antonelli was 17 seconds off the lead.

Antonelli’s exchanges with race engineer Peter Bonnington underline how he was mystified by his car’s handling. Bonnington kept him supplied with notes on where he could find more time but it was only after he swapped his flat-spotted set of slicks for a fresh set that he began to show more competitive pace.

Unfortunately for Antonelli, the rain returned soon afterwards. He pitted for intermediates again – collecting a penalty for an unsafe release as he did – and the early leader had to settle for a fifth-place finish.

Sports.content: The Formula 1 world championship began in 1950 and is considered the world’s leading form of single-seater motorsport. The 2025 F1 season is the 75th time the championship has been held. [caption id="attachment_530322" align="alignright" width="470"] The 2025 Formula 1 season started in Australia[/caption]A world drivers’ champion has been crowned every year since the series began. Since 1958 a world constructors’ championship title has also been awarded. The most successful F1 drivers in history are seven-times world champions Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher. In 2021 the former became the first and so far only driver to date to win 100 grands prix. While Schumacher retired from F1 at the end of 2012, Hamilton continues to race. His rival world champions in the series are Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso. There are 10 teams active in the championship, each of which field cars for two drivers. Each team is required to design and build the majority of its cars but may source some parts including engines, gearboxes and certain other components. Sports.title: “S***, I missed the pit lane”: Hamilton’s unheard radio from his Brazilian GP struggle | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton could have avoided his high-speed spin when the rain returned in the latter stages of the Brazilian Grand Prix.

His Ferrari team summoned him into the pits before he began the lap. Liam Lawson immediately in front of him did pit but Hamilton stayed out. But the conditions had deteriorated and he spun on his next lap.

Hamilton made a strong start to the race from 20th and briefly ran as high as ninth. But Max Verstappen overtook him and Ferrari then told him to let Oliver Bearman past.

Ferrari made this call because Hamilton went off the track when he passed Bearman on the first lap. However the stewards later ruled Hamilton had not gained an advantage by doing this.

Excerpts from Hamilton’s Brazilian GP radio messages

Hamilton Fronts are working really well, just the rear. Lap: 7/71 HAM: 1’28.148 Santi We need to give the position back to Bearman behind, we were off-track. Lap: 8/71 HAM: 1’30.578 Hamilton Understood. Okay.

Sports.title: Russell explains pit exit spin: ‘I took too much risk because I saw a chance to win’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell says he spun in the pit lane exit during the Brazilian Grand Prix because he thought he had a race-winning opportunity.

The Mercedes driver was running third early in the race as the track was drying. He was within 10 seconds of race leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli when he came in to swap his intermediate tyres for slicks on lap 17.

However Russell spun when he reached the pit lane exit. The error cost him around 16 seconds and dropped him behind several of his rivals.

“Obviously it was a bit of an up and down race,” said Russell, who eventually finished fourth. “I’ve no idea what happened on that pit exit, I probably just took too much risk because I was seeing an opportunity to go for the win at that point, but it happened.”

Russell was one of few drivers who only made two pit stops during the race, keeping his set of slick tyres on until the rain returned in the closing stages.

“Ironically, because that happened, I then didn’t pit for another set of slick tyres and it kind of put me back in the same position as I was before the incident,” he acknowledged.

The Mercedes driver set the second-fastest time in qualifying, and believed he could have been quickest had he not aborted his final run under instruction from his race engineer. He said he was satisfied with his performance.

“I’m probably more happy coming away from the weekend because the performance was good,” said Russell, who started seventh following a penalty for replacing his engine. “At this stage I care more about the performance and I care about the result because that’s what’s been my weak point.

“The performance yesterday was great, the performance on the soft tyre was really great today but obviously I did make that mistake. But it probably would have been a different picture if we’d have started P2.”

Sports.title: Piastri splits from Webber’s management team | Formula 1
Sports.content:
McLaren driver Oscar Piastri has confirmed he is no longer being represented by Mark Webber’s management team.

Webber, who won nine grands prix during his 12 seasons in Formula 1 , has guided Piastri’s career since 2019. Piastri made his F1 debut with McLaren in 2023 and led much of last year’s championship before slipping to third place at the end of the season.

Piastri issued a statement saying he had split from the management team led by Webber and his partner Ann by mutual arrangement.

“I’d like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years,” said Piastri. “Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward.”

Webber said he and Ann were “proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar’s career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early on.

“Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career.”

Sports.title: Stewards ruled Hamilton “gained no advantage” by passing Bearman off-track | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Brazilian Grand Prix stewards ruled Lewis Hamilton did not gain an advantage when he overtook Oliver Bearman off the track during the Brazilian Grand Prix.

Hamilton slowed down and let Bearman overtake him on lap seven after the stewards began investigating the incident.

The stewards do not order drivers to swap positions but can issue penalties of five or ten seconds if they determine a competitor gained a place on a rival by going outside track limits. Teams often instruct drivers to surrender positions to avoid these potentially more costly penalties.

Hamilton passed Bearman at the exit of Descida do Lago on the first lap of the race. Bearman had gone off earlier in the lap at Curva do Sol.

The stewards ruled Hamilton had sufficient speed advantage over Bearman to make the pass and was forced off the track by his rival. However in explaining their decision not to penalise Hamilton they also noted he let Bearman past.

“In defending the position, car 87 [Barman] moved to the right and car 44 [Hamilton] was pushed off the track to avoid a collision. Car 44 clearly had the momentum for the overtake and gained no advantage by going off the track. We also noted that the position was subsequently given back by car 44. We therefore took no further action.”

There have been cases in which the stewards have declined to penalise a driver for overtaking a rival off-track and not giving back the position, notably when Yuki Tsunoda forced Lando Norris off during last year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Anthony Yarde In Line For WBC Title Shot After Benavidez Knockout Loss
Sports.content:
Anthony Yarde was knocked out by David Benavidez and spent a full year on the shelf. Somehow, his reward could be an immediate crack at a world title. Frank Warren is considering using Yarde for Willy Hutchinson’s first WBC light heavyweight title defense in March, effectively granting him championship access without the burden of winning an eliminator.

Hutchinson had to go through the fire with Joshua Buatsi across two fights to capture the vacant belt. Yarde, meanwhile, might walk directly into the challenger’s corner coming off a stoppage defeat and twelve months of inactivity. What has Yarde done since Benavidez demolished him to justify cutting to the front of the line? Nothing inside the ring. His entire argument is built on name recognition and the equity of older wars.

Warren was open about the option on talkSPORT Boxing: “Anthony Yarde was in the ring. I don’t know where we’re going to go with that one. We’ll see if we can agree terms. That’s something we may consider as well.”

Casual British fight fans recognize Yarde from his past encounters with Benavidez, Artur Beterbiev, and Sergey Kovalev. That name value makes him infinitely simpler to sell to television buyers than a high-risk contender like Albert Ramirez. If the WBC blesses a voluntary defense and numbers make sense, Warren converts Hutchinson’s hard-won triumph into a profitable domestic event. If Hutchinson retains, he collects a marquee domestic scalp. If Yarde pulls it off, Warren crowns a long-tenured in-house headliner.

The timing also plays directly into Hutchinson’s hands. Yarde carries sufficient power to make Hutchinson pay if he retreats into the ropes, but Hutchinson possesses the footwork to keep Yarde turning. Forcing Yarde to reset his base prevents him from sitting down on heavy bursts. As the rounds wear on, Yarde faces the grueling reality of sustaining hard combination punching over twelve rounds after such a protracted layoff.

The commercial logic is obvious. The sporting logic is nonexistent. A tune-up win would establish what Yarde has left after the Benavidez beating. Under Warren’s plan, Yarde could skip that test and answer the question with a world title on the line.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Wants Zuffa to Skip the Line
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is calling on Zuffa Boxing to steer him straight back toward middleweight championship hardware. Giving up his WBO belt came as the direct cost of facing Shane Mosley Jr. instead of mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez.

With that bout behind him, Bentley is targeting two stablemates who hold the remaining pieces of the division: IBF champion Aaron McKenna and WBC titlist Carlos Adames.

Scoring a knockdown over Mosley helped Bentley secure a close unanimous decision during his promotional debut. The result delivered a recognizable name for his record, yet the real payoff hinges entirely on what Zuffa delivers next. Stepping straight into a voluntary defense allows Bentley to cash in on that narrow win without slogging through another eliminator. Zuffa controls all three fighters internally, leaving promotional squabbles out of the equation once sanctioning bodies give their blessing.

Bentley told The Ring that McKenna or Adames are the targets. He wants whichever man keeps their title next. “I think McKenna or Adames because they are the ones with the titles. I want to fight one of those two next. Next year, either one of those two; they’ve both got their belts. Whoever keeps their strap, I want them next.”

A clash with McKenna appears simpler to schedule. The newly crowned champion has yet to lock in his first defense, and Bentley publicly offered to travel across the Irish Sea. That willingness hands Zuffa an easy sell for a stadium or arena defense in Ireland against a proven puncher. McKenna cannot afford to march forward upright against someone who sits down on short counter hooks with sudden authority. If McKenna uses his jab and relentless output to keep Bentley backing up, those counterpunching lanes vanish quickly over twelve rounds.

Taking on Adames is asking for a beating. Adames has real power, switches stances smoothly, and loves tearing into guys who linger in mid-range. Bentley could get caught along the ropes, and once Adames starts letting fly with those heavy combinations, it turns into a short night.

Dodging Yoenli Hernandez was pure self-preservation. Hernandez is a sharp power-punching Cuban amateur gold medalist who would have put Bentley through a grueling fight for a modest purse.

Targeting McKenna makes complete sense if they want to stay on the path of least resistance: McKenna is tall, fights upright, and walks into range with his chin up. He throws good volume, but he lacks the one-punch explosiveness to terrify Bentley. Bentley can sit down, wait for McKenna to march forward, and drop those short left hooks that stunned Mosley. If Bentley wants a belt he actually has a puncher’s chance of taking, McKenna is the target.

The sanctioning body optics are an absolute circus. Bentley literally just treated a world title like a disposable bargaining chip. When a fighter turns his nose up at an ordered mandatory defense to chase an off-brand debut bout, why should the IBF or WBC reward him with immediate voluntary status?

Sanctioning bodies care about sanctioning fees, but they also hate champions who abandon obligations the second a tough Cuban contender turns up. Putting Bentley in with McKenna signals to the entire sport that mandatories mean nothing. If Bentley wins the IBF strap, there is zero guarantee he stays in line for their mandatory either. He has already shown he would rather drop a belt and wander off than face a high-risk challenger.

Zuffa might want to push Bentley into McKenna’s first defense because it sells well in the UK and Ireland, but it completely undermines the legitimacy of the rankings. Bentley’s handlers will inevitably steer him away from Adames, but handing him an immediate shortcut to McKenna makes a mockery of the system.

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco Risks Plenty for Little Against Fulghum
Sports.content:
Diego Pacheco takes a real knockout risk against Darius Fulghum on Saturday in Carson without a single guarantee waiting on the other side. Winning keeps his WBC Silver and WBO International belts while handing Eddie Hearn another top-fifteen name to sell.

What it does not do is force a world champion into the ring. Neither organization made this a final eliminator, creating a dangerous setup: real physical risk with almost no official leverage.

At 25, Pacheco has time on his side, but boxing crowds run out of patience fast. Matchroom previously walked away from two separate fights with Christian Mbilli, passing on an IBF eliminator and a WBC interim title bout. Pacheco then pulled out of a vacant WBO world title fight with Hamzah Sheeraz after a purse bid was called. That hesitation backfired once Sheeraz vacated.

Because Pacheco was already tied to Fulghum, the WBO bypassed its No. 2 contender entirely and ordered Janibek Alimkhanuly to negotiate with No. 3 Jacob Bank instead. Turning down official eliminators surrenders control. Contenders waiting around for better timing end up watching guys ranked beneath them step straight into world title shots.

Pacheco’s fight against Kevin Sadjo last December in Stockton exposed the exact survival reflex that makes the Fulghum matchup genuinely dangerous.

When Sadjo put Pacheco down in the eighth round, the technical game plan flew out the window. Pacheco did not regain his composure behind a stiff jab, move to create space, or use ring generalship to recover. He went into pure panic mode, wrapping both arms around Sadjo like a vice the second distance closed. It was excessive, blatant clinching designed to kill the clock rather than fight back, and on another night with a referee less tolerant of persistent holding, Pacheco loses points or faces a disqualification warning. The look in his eyes told everyone watching that he wanted no part of the exchanges once his chin was checked.

That survival instinct becomes a glaring liability against Fulghum. Fulghum is not a crude brawler who gives you room to rest. He is a heavy-handed, aggressive puncher who comes forward with bad intentions inside the pocket. If Fulghum connects and hurts Pacheco early, Pacheco cannot afford to clamp on like a sea lamprey and hope the referee lets him hold for four rounds.

Bringing that specific flaw into the Fulghum analysis exposes the real danger:

Pacheco’s chin and ring composure are already under serious question. When a fighter turns down Mbilli and Sheeraz to preserve a clean record for a Canelo Alvarez or Jaime Munguia payday, getting dragged into deep waters by a live dog like Fulghum is suicidal matchmaking. If Pacheco gets tagged on Saturday and reverts to the octopus routine, a sharp referee will take points, the crowd will turn on him, and any voluntary sales pitch Hearn has for Canelo evaporates before the final bell even sounds.

Hearn wants to bypass sanctioning body politics altogether in favor of high-profile voluntary matchmaking .“If we can get Jaime Munguia, we’ll beat him, then we’ll face Canelo Alvarez as well,” said Hearn to DAZN after Pacheco stopped Immanuwel Aleem. That roadmap sounds great on camera, but voluntary talks depend on rival promoters agreeing to play ball.

Canelo does not hand out voluntary paydays just to do Hearn a favor. Contenders get Canelo by bringing massive commercial demand, undisputed hardware, or pay-per-view leverage to the table. Jaime Munguia earned his shot because he had already held a belt at 154 and had the Mexican fan base to anchor a Cinco de Mayo weekend.

Beating Munguia for the WBA belt would give Pacheco real chips to play with, but Matchroom still has to get Munguia into the ring first. Fulghum is the landmine in the middle of it all. He has 13 knockouts in 15 wins, real amateur credentials, and heavy enough hands to wreck the entire script in one round.

Even an ugly, labored decision win hurts the sales pitch. Emphatic knockout or not, Pacheco still leaves the ring Saturday night depending on Hearn’s salesmanship instead of an enforceable title mandate. Pacheco already passed on fights that offered direct routes to a belt. Taking on that kind of danger for a bargaining chip is why Saturday is such a massive gamble.

Sports.title: Alycia Baumgardner Sweeps Elif Nur Turhan to Win IBF Title
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner took away Elif Nur Turhan’s unbeaten record and her IBF lightweight title on Sunday night, using a sharp jab and quick counters to win all 10 rounds on each judge’s card. All three scored it 100-90 for Baumgardner, who became a two-division world champion in her lightweight debut.

Turhan (14-1, 8 KOs) spent much of the early going trying to get close enough to throw her looping right hand. Baumgardner’s jab made her start those attacks from farther out than she wanted. When Turhan committed to the overhand anyway, Baumgardner (19-1, 7 KOs) could step clear and catch her before she was set to punch again. Turhan kept bringing the fight to her, but Baumgardner landed the cleaner shots while giving the champion few chances to follow up.

The pattern held through the middle rounds. Turhan stayed busy and found openings with hooks and uppercuts when she shortened her punches. Baumgardner took those shots and went back to the jab, making Turhan, 31, work her way inside again. Turhan’s best punches came once she was close enough to throw without reaching. Too often, she had to risk a wide shot just to get there.

Turhan landed clean uppercuts in the ninth and kept pressing in the tenth, still looking for a big shot after spending much of the night behind. Baumgardner, 32, kept her composure and continued to make Turhan miss and pay for coming forward. The three shutout cards gave Baumgardner every round, even with Turhan landing some of her best punches late.

The win gives Baumgardner a belt at 135 pounds after her undisputed run at 130 and puts a potential unification with Caroline Dubois in play. Turhan gave her an immediate test at the new weight. She kept coming for 30 minutes, landed cleanly when she got inside, and made Baumgardner keep working to regain her distance. Baumgardner did it often enough that none of the three judges found a round to give the defending champion.

The fight headlined Most Valuable Promotions at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas. It was contested over 10 three-minute rounds at the 135-pound limit.

Earlier on the card, Ramla Ali won the vacant IBF and WBO super bantamweight titles by split decision over Mikiah Kreps, and Skye Nicolson retained her WBC belt at the same weight by unanimous decision over Miyo Yoshida.

Sports.title: Skye Nicolson Outboxes Miyo Yoshida to Retain WBC Title
Sports.content:
Skye Nicolson kept Miyo Yoshida chasing for 10 rounds, using her longer reach and lead right hand to win a unanimous decision and retain her WBC super bantamweight title Sunday night at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

The judges scored it 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92 for Nicolson in her first defense as full champion at 122 pounds. Neither fighter went down on the ESPN card headlined by Elif Turhan and Alycia Baumgardner.

Less than a pound separated the fighters at the weigh-in, but Nicolson had about five inches of reach on Yoshida. That advantage showed each time Yoshida had to step in to throw. The challenger landed several rights in the opening round, but Nicolson answered with left hands and body shots. By the third, Nicolson (17-1, 3 KOs) was catching Yoshida with the lead right as she came forward.

Yoshida (19-6, 1 KO) had one of her better spells in the fourth, backing Nicolson up with a flurry. Nicolson countered with a right and tied her up before she could build on it. In the fifth, Nicolson went from circling away to pressing Yoshida, 38, toward the ropes, where she landed a right hook. Yoshida had to stay ready for Nicolson to come forward even as she tried to cut off the ring.

The Japanese challenger kept finding short rights in the clinches in the sixth and seventh and landed on the way in during the eighth. The trouble came whenever Nicolson got clear. Yoshida had to start her approach again, and Nicolson, 31, could get back to scoring with both hands from outside. Yoshida put combinations together in the ninth, but Nicolson caught her with a counter left and an uppercut. The champion worked quick uppercuts into her combinations in the tenth as Yoshida pursued her to the final bell.

Yoshida was trying to win a world title in a third weight class after holding belts at 115 and 118 pounds. She showed she could make Nicolson uncomfortable once she got close, particularly when she led with more than one punch. She spent too much of the fight trying to get back there.

For Nicolson, the result was her first successful defense since being elevated from interim to full champion in May. The former WBC featherweight champion had been due to face Yoshida in Britain in August before an injury delayed the bout. She made her MVP debut in Arlington and came away with the belt still in hand and a possible unification ahead.

Sports.title: Hearn Wants Shakur Stevenson. Who Can He Deliver?
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn wants to work with Shakur Stevenson after the unbeaten champion parted ways with Zuffa Boxing without ever entering the ring for the venture. Matchroom holds viable options at 135 and 140 pounds, yet the most lucrative fight on the board remains Gervonta Davis, which demands an agreement with Premier Boxing Champions.

“We’d love to work with him. He can work with anybody he wants,” Hearn said in an interview with by Fighthub. “He’s one of the best fighters in the world.”

Dalton Smith stands as the most accessible internal option if Stevenson remains at 140 pounds. Hearn handles Smith’s career directly, allowing Matchroom to stage a UK event and bank on strong arena attendance to cover fighter compensation. Andy Cruz represents another route at 135 pounds should Stevenson drop back down. Cruz brings elite technical skill, yet matching two defensive purists creates promotional hurdles regarding broad commercial appeal. Hearn cited neither boxer as a firm candidate.

William Zepeda highlights the strengths and limits of DAZN’s network ecosystem. The streaming service handled Stevenson’s 2025 meeting with the Golden Boy contender, proving cross-promotional business can function smoothly on that feed. Stevenson dominated that encounter by wide unanimous decision, blunting the public appetite for a second run.

Davis presents a much larger commercial target. The Baltimore native headlined on Prime Video via PBC against Lamont Roach, establishing where his primary broadcast loyalties sit. Staging Davis against Stevenson forces Hearn to iron out carriage rights and profit sharing with PBC. A third-party financial backer like Riyadh Season could cover enormous purse guarantees, yet distribution rights would remain a contested negotiation.

The contrast between Smith and Davis exposes modern boxing economics. Hearn can finalize terms with Smith quickly. Still, he has to determine whether live gate numbers and British ticket buyers justify Stevenson’s lofty minimum guarantee. Matchroom absorbs the deficit if the venue fails to sell out. Davis brings bona fide pay-per-view muscle, though Premier Boxing Champions holds broadcast control and will demand most of the revenue pie.

A multi-fight contract gives Stevenson guaranteed ring dates along with locked paydays. A bout-by-bout arrangement lets him hunt massive paydays with complete freedom, but leaves him open to long stretches of inactivity while rivals sort out their own schedules.Waiting months for a marquee rival leaves an elite boxer covering ongoing training costs without incoming revenue.

Hearn labeled Stevenson’s brief run with Zuffa an absolute catastrophe while taking aim at Dana White’s promotional output. The most effective recruiting tool Matchroom possesses is an actionable contract. Smith shows what Hearn can deliver in-house, while Davis proves whether he can overcome stubborn industry boundaries.

Hearn omitting Cruz speaks volumes about Matchroom’s true priorities. Promoting that matchup would be commercial suicide. Cruz versus Stevenson is a purist’s dream, but casual fans run from pure chess matches. Staging it requires massive guarantees for both men with virtually zero pay-per-view upside and a dismal gate outside of a niche venue. DAZN would essentially foot the bill for an expensive technical exhibition that drives no new subscriptions.

Beyond the financials, the matchmaking logic falls apart for Hearn. If he shells out heavy money to sign Stevenson, the objective is cashing in on blockbuster dates or building toward Gervonta Davis. Throwing Stevenson directly in with Cruz risks ruining the asset immediately. Stevenson could easily get outpointed or dragged into an unwatchable snoozer that completely kills his market value.

Even if Stevenson wins, beating Cruz does almost nothing to build his crossover profile. Casuals do not know Cruz, so Stevenson gains little public credit while taking maximum technical risk.

From Hearn’s seat, keeping those two far apart is self-preservation. You protect the newly acquired name with high-visibility, lower-risk domestic dates like Dalton Smith, or you swing for the fences with established commercial giants where the reward justifies the danger. Cruz offers all the poison with none of the prize.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Defends His Right Hand Before Lara Fight
Sports.content:
Tim Tszyu rejected the notion that he was too cautious with his right hand against Errol Spence Jr. last July. For Tszyu, getting his hand raised put that debate to bed. Taking on WBA middleweight champion Erislandy Lara presents a far trickier tactical puzzle: how to release that signature power punch without walking directly into a counter straight left.

Tszyu insists he damaged Spence and felt entirely comfortable with the performance. Turning his attention to Lara, he pointed directly to the Cuban veteran’s deceptive lead hand, footwork reads, and sudden left hand deliveries.

“This fight is a game of inches. You really can’t make one mistake at that high level. It’s hard to go and throw 100 punches carelessly in a round because there’s 100 different opportunities that you can get caught,” Tszyu said to The Punch podcast.

Tszyu suggested he anticipates an aggressive Lara hunting for a stoppage, but the veteran can inflict equal devastation by simply giving up an inch of canvas. Southpaws of Lara’s caliber thrive on the classic half step pull counter. If Tszyu overextends with the right hand while searching for Lara’s chin, his momentum leaves his weight trapped over his front knee. That leaves him completely exposed to a sharp left counter while his feet remain stuck. A pawing, noncommittal jab from Lara often serves as bait, coaxing aggressive fighters into lunging from outside range.

Winning the lead foot battle will dictate Tszyu’s success. He cannot allow Lara to consistently step outside his front foot, which forces the orthodox right hand to travel at a wide angle while opening a clean lane down the center for Lara. Tszyu must establish his jab to the chest to measure range, mixing in level changes and double feints to freeze Lara’s back foot before unloading. Targeting the body early with heavy rights will also slow the veteran down and pull his elbows in, unlocking paths to the head.

Patience carries its own severe penalties against a master boxer. Spending entire rounds looking for an ideal opening allows Lara to steal minutes with a flickering jab and isolated straight shots. Tszyu settled for minimal right hands against Spence, but dealing with Lara on the Gold Coast demands far more offensive initiative.

Sports.title: James Toney’s Haney Knockout Pick Ignores Seven Years
Sports.content:
James Toney expects Devin Haney to knock out Liam Paro, but that forecast demands a style Haney abandoned long ago. At 27, Haney has collected world titles for seven consecutive years without a single stoppage victory. Transforming into a finisher against a gritty southpaw means embracing the precise physical exposure his entire system is engineered to avoid.

Toney’s endorsement carries weight after their recent work together in the gym. When asked about the matchup, the Hall of Famer did not mince words.

“You see power. He knock him out,” Toney said to Fighthype.

Gym mitts, however, tell only part of the story. Training equipment offers a compliant target where a puncher can generate torque with settled feet. Real competition forces a different arithmetic entirely. Ripping a leveraged right hand on the pads comes without the immediate threat of eating a live southpaw right hook over the top.

That reality shapes Haney’s actual punching mechanics. Sitting down on a shot requires planting the back foot and committing hip rotation, anchoring him in place for an extra beat. Mobility has always been Haney’s primary defensive insurance policy. Abandoning that fluid perimeter control to load up on heavier leather would compromise his balance, alter his recovery timing, and accelerate fatigue in the late rounds.

The footwork battle against Paro sharpens those stakes. Securing dominant outside position with the lead left foot creates an angle for Haney’s straight right. At the same time, stepping outside is never risk-free. If Haney overreaches to establish that angle or lingers to admire his work, Paro can easily pivot and fire a short counter left down the pipe. For Haney, a clean exit after throwing matters far more than maximum thud.

His 2023 performance against Regis Prograis proved that distinction clearly. Haney dropped the heavy-hitting southpaw with a laser straight right in round three. Instead of swarming to produce a finish, he collected the points, reset the perimeter, and coasted to a wide decision win. A knockdown proved his timing, but it did not change his operational instincts.

Stopping Paro demands sustained combinations. Scoring with a lead punch is simple enough; staying in range to deliver the second, third, and fourth punches is where the peril starts. Paro proved against Subriel Matias that he knows how to survive inside exchanges. He smothered Matias’s offense with smart lateral movement, timely clinches, and sharp counter bursts. If Matias could not break Paro’s defensive resolve on the ropes, Haney will hardly do it with one-off punches.

Toney spent his career thriving in the pocket, rolling with shots on the inside, and returning venomous fire at close range. It makes sense that he sees the game through that aggressive lens. Haney, by contrast, treats close-range trades as an avoidable liability.

Haney might possess sufficient force to stun opponents, but producing an actual stoppage requires living in the pocket. Until Haney shows a genuine appetite for sustained infighting, Toney’s knockout prediction remains completely detached from the fighter Haney chooses to be.

Ghana News.title: JUSAG, SSAJUG suspend indefinite strike effective November 10
Ghana News.content:
The Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) and the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (SSAJUG) have announced the suspension of their indefinite strike following engagements with government over outstanding concerns regarding salary reviews and related allowances.

The two unions, in a statement dated November 9, 2026, said they had received official correspondence from the Office of the President addressing issues surrounding the review of salaries and related allowances for staff of the Judicial Service.

The announcement follows a meeting between the union leadership and management of the Judicial Service, led by the Chief Justice, with support from the President of the Judicial Service, Justice Gabriel Scott Pwamang, and the Judicial Secretary, Mr Ahmed Musah.

The meeting was held to consider a revised approval issued by the government to address the concerns that triggered the industrial action.

According to the unions, the revised government position largely addressed the outstanding issues, prompting their leadership to submit a revised position on the commitments received from the Office of the President.

They described the development as a final pathway towards resolving the impasse and subsequently announced that the strike would be suspended effective Tuesday, November 10, 2026, pending the finalisation of the commitments.

JUSAG and SSAJUG commended President John Dramani Mahama, the Chief Justice, Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, the President of the Supreme Court, Justice Gabriel Scott Pwamang, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, Judicial Secretary Ahmed Musah, and the management of the Judicial Service for their roles in resolving the dispute.

The unions also expressed appreciation to members of staff for their support throughout the industrial action and acknowledged the media for its coverage.

The suspension is expected to pave the way for the resumption of normal activities within the Judicial Service while the outstanding commitments are finalised.

Ghana News.title: Bawumia leads Ato Forson 46% to 43% in 2028 poll – Global InfoAnalytics
Ghana News.content:
A September 2026 tracking poll by Global InfoAnalytics has revealed that former Vice President and flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has a narrow lead over Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson in a hypothetical 2028 presidential election contest in the Ashanti and Eastern regions.

The poll gives the former Vice President 46 per cent support, against 43 per cent for Dr Ato Forson, in a contest that includes former Assin Central MP Kennedy Agyapong.

Mr Agyapong, who previously contested the NPP presidential primary, records eight per cent, while Alan Kyerematen receives two per cent. Nana Kwame Bediako polls one per cent, with other candidates collectively accounting for another one per cent.

However, Global InfoAnalytics says the three-percentage-point difference between Dr Bawumia and Dr Ato Forson falls within the poll's margin of error, placing the two potential contenders statistically neck and neck in the two regions.

The poll also tests a scenario in which Mr Agyapong is excluded from the race.

Under that arrangement, Dr Bawumia's support increases to 48 per cent, while Dr Ato Forson's rises to 45 per cent. Mr Kyerematen's share doubles to four per cent, with Mr Bediako's increasing to two per cent.

Global InfoAnalytics says the results suggest that some of Mr Agyapong's supporters may not automatically switch their allegiance to Dr Bawumia if the former Assin Central MP does not contest the 2028 presidential election.

The September 2026 tracking poll examines possible presidential matchups ahead of the 2028 general election, focusing on voter preferences in the Ashanti and Eastern regions.

Ghana News.title: Tapping pop culture for Ghana’s climate change storytelling
Ghana News.content:
The author, Ekow Quandzie, Head of PR & Sustainability Lead – Global Media Alliance, speaking at the Climate x Culture Summit

A couple of weeks ago, festival producers, art talents, and climate activists shared one platform at the Climate x Culture Summit 2026, themed “Designing Sustainable Creative Experiences for Africa.” They agreed on one thing: if climate action is to mean more than it does today, it has to enter culture, not stand outside it.

As a communications executive invited to speak on storytelling and behaviour change, I left more convinced than ever. Ghana does not lack climate science. It lacks climate stories ordinary people can see themselves in, remember, and act on.

Asked whether climate change is communicated effectively to Ghanaians, speakers said no with most people only learn about it when the impact hits them. Many do not connect their habits to climate consequences. Dumping waste in the street, for instance, clogs drain and turns an hour of rain into a flood.

Why pop culture travels further

A climate song by an artist like Okyeame Kwame could reach more people in a year. Ghanaians learn through music, comedy skits and radio. Few will open a climate report, but many will share a song or retell a story.

Musician and climate activist, Okyeame Kwame at Climate x Culture Summit

Ghanaian artists have already proved this. Stonebwoy’s “Greedy Men” (2021) took illegal small-scale mining (galamsey) into mainstream entertainment, spotlighting the destruction of rivers and forests. Years earlier, M.anifest and Obrafour’s “No Shortcut to Heaven” (2013) was shot at a mining site, dramatising the human and environmental cost.

These works did what a policy brief cannot: they put galamsey into dinner-table conversation and radio rotation. They turned ecological damage into moral narrative, which in Ghana, moves.

The economics support this. Africa’s creative sector generates more than two million jobs in a single year, a figure from four years ago, and in some countries, it now rivals agriculture as an employer. It deserves a seat where climate policy and finance are decided.

Campaigns must give people clear pathways to respond. The best climate stories are local, using familiar places and languages; human, centred on a farmer, trader or student rather than a graph; specific, linking a small action to a visible consequence; and they end with a next step.

Creatives must be involved early, not called in at the end to decorate decisions already made. Artists can also document the indigenous knowledge that has long protected forests. Culture shapes how people understand their environment, organise their communities and decide what to value and protect.

The Coldplay Concert Lesson

Entertainment must also practise what it preaches. Music band Coldplay reports that direct emissions on the first two years of its Music of the Spheres World Tour were 59% lower than its previous stadium tour, verified by the MIT Environmental Solutions Initiative. Solar-charged batteries, kinetic dance floors, sustainable aviation fuel, compostable wristbands and a low-carbon travel app all played a part, and each ticket funded tree planting, with 7 million trees reported so far.

The deeper lesson is participation. Fans were invited to power the show by dancing and to return their wristbands. Behaviour changed because the experience invited it. That is storytelling through participation, and Ghanaian festivals can adapt it, from refill stations and reusable cups to rewards for fans who choose public transport.

Event organisers must establish environmental baselines, track waste generation and energy consumption, and assess their environmental footprint before and after events. Accurate attendance figures are equally important, as inflated projections undermine effective planning and make it difficult to measure the actual impact of sustainability interventions.

Practical solutions must also be built into event production. These include improving waste segregation, reducing dependence on single-use plastics. Existing initiatives, such as the Obroni Wawu Festival by The OR Foundation, offer a glimpse of what is possible, demonstrating how upcycled furniture and event infrastructure can be combined with partnerships involving waste collectors, artisans and community-based cooperatives working on beach clean-ups and the recovery of discarded textiles.

One practical expression of this thinking could be a partnership between the Telecel Ghana Music Awards (TGMA) and The OR Foundation to transform the awards' red carpet into a celebration of circular fashion. Imagine Ghana's biggest music stars arriving in carefully styled second-hand and upcycled outfits sourced from Kantamanto, one of Africa's largest second-hand clothing markets and a significant centre of Ghana's circular economy. Rather than treating second-hand clothing as a symbol of affordability or social stigma, the red carpet would reposition it as a statement of creativity, identity and contemporary African fashion.

Detty December Can Be A Test

Detty December presents perhaps the biggest opportunity to demonstrate Ghana's commitment to sustainable entertainment. With thousands of visitors, diaspora communities, influencers and content creators participating in the festivities, the season offers an influential platform for shaping attitudes towards environmental responsibility.

But the scale of the celebrations also brings significant environmental challenges, particularly plastic waste, energy consumption and event-related pollution. For organisers, sustainability must become an operational priority, not simply a marketing message.

This requires a few practical commitments:

Establish realistic attendance projections and track waste, energy and water consumption. Publish post-event environmental reports organisersrate accountability.

Make waste segregation visible by providing clearly labelled recycling bins at event venues and formally engage waste collectors and recycling cooperatives.

Reduce single-use plastics: Introduce water refill stations, reusable cups and vendor agreements that restrict disposable plastics.

Integrate thrift-fashion showcases, upcycled installations, and climate-conscious music into the festival experience.

Encourage attendees to adopt sustainable habits through reusable bottles, recycling information and shared transport arrangements.

Bring event organisers, sponsors, waste management companies and environmental groups together before December to establish common sustainability standards.

Ghana’s climate future must become part of everyday culture. Through music, fashion, art, festivals and other expressions of pop culture, creatives can make sustainability relatable. The opportunity is to make climate action part of the things people watch, listen to, celebrate and embrace, so that the conversation reaches Ghanaians long before the next environmental crisis.

The author, Ekow Quandzie, is Head of PR & Sustainability Lead at Global Media Alliance

Ghana News.title: JoyNews’ Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi wins GJA award for domestic tourism reporting
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews’ Ahafo Regional Correspondent, Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi, has won the Best Reporter on Domestic Tourism award at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards.

He was recognised for his article, “Speaking Ghana to the world: How indigenous languages can power tourism and economic growth,” at the awards ceremony held in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

The Awards Committee, chaired by former Graphic Communications Group Editor Kobby Asmah, commended the report for demonstrating the value of development journalism and highlighting the role of Ghana’s indigenous languages in promoting tourism and economic growth.

In its citation, the committee said the article drew attention to the potential of local languages as a tool for economic transformation.

“Your article brilliantly illuminates a powerful, yet overlooked truth: that the strategic use of Ghana's rich, local language varieties can serve as a potent engine for economic transformation,” the citation stated.

It also praised Gyamfi’s approach to connecting cultural preservation with tourism development, describing the article as offering an actionable framework for using Ghanaian languages to strengthen the country’s tourism appeal.

The committee further commended him for his contribution to cultural heritage, impactful storytelling and national development.

30th GJA Media Awards

The 30th edition of the GJA Media Awards was held under the theme: “30th GJA Media Awards: Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age.”

The ceremony was attended by President John Mahama, Ga Mantse King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Federation of African Journalists and members of the diplomatic community, among other dignitaries.

The annual awards recognise journalists and media professionals for their contributions to journalism and national development.

The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has released the list of aspirants for its national executive elections scheduled for December 2026, with several key positions attracting no contest.

The list, revealed on Monday, November 9, shows that four candidates are seeking the position of National Chairman, while Fifi Fiavi Kwetey, Joseph Yameen and Ako Gunn are going unopposed for their respective positions.

National Chairman

Four aspirants have filed to contest for the position of National Chairman:

Sofo Azorka

Akwasi Oppong Fosu

Nii Armah Ashitey

Nii Lantey Vanderpuye

Deputy General Secretary

Four candidates are also contesting for Deputy General Secretary:

Barbara Asamoah

Mustapha Gbande

Isaac Kwame

Abdul Rashid Abdul Raman

General Secretary

Fifi Fiavi Kwetey is the sole aspirant for the General Secretary position and is therefore going unopposed.

National Organiser

Joseph Yameen is also going unopposed for the position of National Organiser.

National Communications Officer

Ako Gunn is the only aspirant listed for National Communications Officer and is set to go unopposed.

National Youth Organiser

Three names were provided for the National Youth Organiser position:

Sanicara

Nineteen individuals have filed to contest for the Vice Chair positions, according to the list.

The exercise will see the party elect national officers to steer its affairs for the next four years.

The aspirants are expected to undergo vetting, after which the party is expected to announce further details of the election timetable.

Ghana News.title: COP31: Africa makes progress on adoption of key supplementary priorities on agenda
Ghana News.content:
COP31 must mark the definitive transition from negotiated promises to tangible financial delivery, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) has urged world leaders in a decisive call as the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) opened in Antalya on Monday.

Speaking on behalf of the continent at the opening plenary in Antalya, AGN Chair, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, emphasised that Africa’s ability to fulfil its climate commitments rests entirely on the immediate mobilisation of scaled-up, predictable climate finance.

Aligning the African bloc with the Group of 77 and China, Dr Amoah declared that an implementation-focused summit must be a summit that delivers on finance, setting a firm tone for the two-week negotiations hosted by Türkiye, with Australia presiding over negotiations.

Opening the intervention with congratulations to the incoming Turkish Presidency and gratitude to Australia and the outgoing Brazilian Presidency from Belém, the AGN Chair articulated the stark paradox facing the African continent. Africa contributes the least to global greenhouse gas emissions yet suffers disproportionately from climate-induced disruptions.

While African nations have submitted highly ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), Dr. Amoah highlighted that the vast majority of this ambition remains locked behind unfulfilled financial pledges. He stressed that African countries cannot carry out climate mitigation and adaptation strategies without the promised means of implementation, transforming climate finance from a secondary discussion item into the essential prerequisite for all global progress in Antalya.

"Africa comes to Antalya with one clear message: implementation depends on means of implementation. Our continent contributes the least to this crisis and is among the most exposed to its impacts. African countries have put forward ambitious NDCs and adaptation plans, but most of that ambition depends on finance that has not yet arrived," said Nana Amoah.

Adoption of Africa’s priorities in official agenda

To ensure that core financial and structural priorities were formally integrated into the COP31 proceedings, the African Group pushed for the inclusion of three key supplementary agenda items. Following intense Head of Delegation negotiations that concluded in the early hours of the opening morning, Dr Amoah announced that consensus had been reached to adopt these priorities into the official agenda.

These are to: operationalise and track progress toward tripling adaptation finance flows to address growing vulnerability across developing states; evaluate the impact of unilateral trade-related climate measures on developing economies, protecting African industrialisation under Article 3.5 of the Convention; and conduct a formal assessment of funding necessary and available for the Green Climate Fund ahead of its upcoming third replenishment.

The demand for a dedicated dialogue on trade and climate change represents a pivotal issue for African economies. As unilateral trade regulations and carbon border adjustments proliferate globally, Dr Amoah warned that such measures threaten to shift the financial burden of the green transition onto developing nations, undermining local industrial development in direct contradiction to Article 3.5 of the UNFCCC Convention.

Additionally, the AGN Chair underscored the necessity of evaluating the financial requirements of the Green Climate Fund (GCF). As the GCF prepares for its third replenishment cycle, the African Group called on the COP to fulfil existing commitments by assessing the exact scale of resources needed to meet developing countries' actual climate requirements.

The position outlined by the AGN Chair reflects a unified stance across the Global South, backed by key negotiating coalitions including the Arab Group, the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), the Independent Association of Latin America and the Caribbean (AILAC), and the broader G77 and China alliance chaired by Uruguay.

This collective push comes against the backdrop of alarming contractions in global climate finance. Contextual statements delivered on behalf of the G77 and China highlighted that the Global Environment Facility’s ninth replenishment (GEF-9) suffered a 27 percent decline compared to GEF-8, marking its lowest funding level in 16 years.

Concurrently, major developed nations have announced reductions that cut their signed GCF contributions for 2024–2027 by half. These declines coincide with massive shortfalls in loss and damage funding, where funding requests exceed available resources by over eightfold.

Operationalising equity and industrial growth

For the African Group, the ultimate measure of success at COP31 will be an outcome that balances mitigation ambition with robust financial delivery, equity, and common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities (CBDR-RC).

Dr Amoah reiterated that low-carbon and climate-resilient transitions must foster equitable, shared prosperity, providing African nations with the necessary policy space to industrialise, expand energy access, and eradicate poverty. By securing adoption of its agenda items through collaborative Head of Delegation negotiations, the African Group has positioned financial accountability and trade equity at the core of the Antalya summit.

As committee sessions and ministerial roundtables begin across the Antalya Expo Centre, the AGN Chair’s call serves as a focal point for developing nations demanding that international climate governance shift permanently from pledge-making to guaranteed delivery.

Ghana News.title: Make Me Stay S1 EP1: Tears that led a guy to love
Ghana News.content:
An emotional moment unfolded on Joy Prime’s dating reality show, Make Me Stay, as male contestant Bumba Ibrahim shed tears during his search for love.

Their first 60-second conversation became dramatic when female contestant Grace, also known as Maame Serwaa, challenged Bumba to make her experience love for the first time. Although she admitted that she had never been in love, she expressed her desire to build a genuine connection with him.

Grace made it clear that she was ready to explore a romantic connection, telling Bumba, “I've never fallen in love before. I want you to make me fall in love. Make me fall in love,” she told Bumba Ibrahim, who confidently responded, “Yeah, I will.”

The conversation soon turned to their sexual experiences, with both contestants admitting that they were not virgins. When asked about his views on marriage, Bumba disclosed that polygamy was acceptable in his family, provided a man could adequately cater for his wives.

However, he indicated that he would prefer to have only one wife if he found the kind of woman he desired. Grace appeared open to the possibility, but made it clear that his ability to make her stay would be important to her decision.

“That's if you can make me stay,” she added.

But the conversation took a romantic and emotional turn when the two returned from the Lovers’ Lounge, having decided to give their connection a chance.

Bumba revealed that his time away from the other contestants had given him a different perspective on love and single motherhood, particularly after spending time with Grace, the woman he was interested in.

He expressed gratitude for the opportunity to be part of the programme, describing his experience as a “one touch” because, despite having several ladies to choose from, he had already made up his mind about the woman he wanted to be with. However, he admitted that getting to know her better during their lunch date changed some of his perceptions.

According to him, the experience taught him that being a single mother does not make a woman any less worthy of love. He also suggested that women should not always be blamed when relationships fail, noting that his time with her had helped him see things differently.

“I got to learn that being a single mum doesn't make the lady a bad person,” he said.

He further expressed sympathy for her past relationship, insisting that she was not the one who lost out. He then made a promise to treat her better than her previous partner had, saying, “The guy lost; she did not lose. And I want to make sure I do what the guy could not do for you.

His emotional confession ended with an expression of affection, as he told her, “I love you,” leaving the moment filled with emotion.

Grace also could not hide her feelings, as she confessed her love for Bumba after their heartfelt and insightful conversation in the lounge.

“When I came, I also met a lot of guys here but meeting him is one of the best thing. We’ve talked and discussed a lot and have decided to move on. I think with him, everything will go on successfully,” she said.

The two eventually found a connection and chose to explore their relationship beyond the show, making them the first to find love as the season has commenced.

Other contestants also had the opportunity to make their first impressions within 60 seconds and win over potential partners, but unfortunately, not all were successful.

The emotional display added a dramatic twist to the show, which brings together individuals seeking meaningful romantic connections and gives them an opportunity to explore relationships.

Make Me Stay continues to offer viewers a blend of romance, emotions, entertainment and unexpected moments as contestants navigate the complexities of dating and relationships.

The show airs on Joy Prime every Sunday at 8pm, bringing love seekers together in the hope of finding meaningful and lasting connections.

Ghana News.title: Researchers urge government to fund Ghana-focused health studies and apply findings
Ghana News.content:
Researchers and health professionals have called for increased government investment in local health research, warning that inadequate funding and the limited application of research findings could undermine efforts to address Ghana’s healthcare challenges.

They say stronger support for indigenous research and closer collaboration between scientists, policymakers and healthcare practitioners are necessary to ensure evidence informs public policy and improves service delivery.

The concerns were raised at the second Research Dissemination Day organised by HopeXchange Medical Centre, where experts also highlighted the challenges facing young researchers and the difficulties of translating scientific findings into practical interventions.

Provost of the College of Science, Professor Philip Antwi-Agyei, said Ghana continued to face challenges in healthcare, environmental management, food security and other sectors that required evidence-based solutions.

He observed that although considerable resources had been committed to research over the years, translating findings into policies and practical interventions remained a challenge.

Professor Antwi-Agyei urged young researchers to focus on studies that could inform policymaking and improve public service delivery.

“Young researchers are to engage in meaningful and impactful research that will be translated into policy and practice. What hasn’t been too good is the translation of this research into policies and practice,” he said.

He also called on government to prioritise indigenous research addressing the country’s immediate challenges, arguing that local researchers were well positioned to investigate issues affecting Ghanaian communities.

Ashanti Regional Director of Health Services, Dr Fred Adomako-Boateng, called for stronger collaboration between researchers, policymakers and frontline healthcare professionals to ensure scientific evidence is incorporated into clinical practice.

He said although several research findings had demonstrated their effectiveness, challenges within healthcare facilities often prevented their adoption.

Among the barriers he identified were heavy workloads, time constraints, inadequate funding, staff shortages and limited research skills among healthcare professionals.

“Practitioners will face heavy patient volumes, little time, leaving little to no dedicated time for participating in or even implementing the research,” he said.

To address the challenges, Dr Adomako-Boateng proposed the adoption of learning health systems, increased investment in implementation research, stronger leadership among healthcare professionals and more collaborative research design.

He also recommended digital repositories containing accessible clinical guidelines to help practitioners apply research findings in their work.

Medical Superintendent of HopeXchange Medical Centre, Dr Akosua Frimpomaa Amoateng, said the annual dissemination event was established to provide a platform for researchers to share their findings and demonstrate how research could improve clinical practice.

She explained that research was one of the key foundations of the hospital’s operations, alongside clinical care and health education.

“We realised that we needed to give a boost to research because research goes on every day, but we want to establish a platform where researchers can come together and share their ideas,” she said.

Dr Amoateng said the initiative was intended not only to showcase research findings but also to encourage their application in healthcare delivery and motivate more professionals to pursue research.

The Research Dissemination Day is in its second year.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
