World.title: Gombe: PDP ex-chairman, ex-SSG, others join APC
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Gombe State has recorded another wave of defections, with some of its leaders, including the immediate past state chairman, Joel Jagafa, and former Secretary to the State Government (SSG), James Pisagih, joining the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The development followed a meeting between the defectors and Governor Muhammadu Yahaya, where they formally declared their decision to join the APC and pledged their support for the governor’s leadership.

Others who defected include former PDP State Secretary, Buba Shanu; former Principal Officer of the Gombe State House of Assembly, Sunday Danlele; retired director, Mr Williams; and several other political stakeholders.

The meeting, facilitated by Ali Isa, allowed the former PDP chieftains to formally identify with the APC and express their commitment to the party.

The defectors said their decision was driven by confidence in Governor Yahaya’s leadership, political direction and the performance of his administration.

They also pledged to contribute their political experience, grassroots connections, and networks to strengthen the APC’s structures and mobilise support for the party across the state.

Welcoming them, Governor Yahaya described their decision to join the APC as a positive development, noting that their arrival would expand the party’s membership and strengthen its political base in Gombe State.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He assured the new members of equal opportunities and inclusiveness, stressing that the APC remained open to individuals willing to work towards the party’s ideals and collective aspirations.

The governor expressed confidence that their experience and contributions would support the party’s activities and further consolidate its structures across the state.

World.title: Youth Olympics: Ugoh wins third gold medal for Nigeria
World.content:
Nigeria won its third gold medal at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Monday after Praise Ugoh triumphed in the girls’ 400 metres, lifting the country to 11th position on the medal table.

Ugoh produced an impressive personal-best time of 52.76 seconds to win the 400m title, becoming the first Nigerian to claim gold in the event at the Youth Olympic Games.

The Nigerian finished ahead of Osmary Pacheco, who clocked 52.85 seconds, while Aisha Muhammed settled for bronze in 53.06 seconds.

Her victory adds to Nigeria’s growing success in athletics at the Games, following Sunday’s historic sprint double by Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo and Gift Bright in the girls’ and boys’ 100m events.

Nwankwo won the girls’ 100m in a wind-assisted 11.16 seconds to become Nigeria’s third champion in the event, while Bright made history as the first Nigerian to win the boys’ 100m title, clocking a personal-best 10.28 seconds.

Ugoh’s triumph takes Nigeria’s gold-medal tally to three, making it the country’s most successful campaign at the ongoing competition in terms of gold medals.

Nigeria breaks into medal table’s top 11

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ugoh’s victory has lifted Nigeria to 11th position on the medal table, with three gold medals and no silver or bronze medals, according to the latest standings as at the time of this report.

The latest position represents a significant improvement from Sunday’s joint 14th-place ranking, following the victories of Nwankwo and Bright.

Nigeria is now just outside the top 10, with Kenya occupying fifth position on four gold medals, while Senegal is sixth with four gold medals and three bronze medals.

China leads the standings with 13 gold, seven silver and three bronze medals, giving it 23 medals overall. Japan are second with nine gold, six silver and five bronze medals, while Russia and Egypt occupy third and fourth positions, respectively.

Nigeria’s other athletes also featured in Monday’s athletics programme, although they did not reach the podium.

Rita Chisom Ezeh finished seventh in the second semi-final of the women’s 400m hurdles, recording 1:01.66.

Colombia’s Michell Carolina Gomez won the race in 59.96 seconds, ahead of Switzerland’s Mina Hirsbrunner (1:00.12) and Brazil’s Larissa Schon (1:00.38).

In the men’s high jump final, Obanla Ehuwa finished eighth after clearing a personal-best height of 1.97 metres.

South Africa’s Matao Le Roux won gold with an equal personal-best clearance of 2.16m, while China’s Liu Sen took silver with a personal best of 2.14m. Egypt’s Mohammed Zaki claimed bronze with 2.09m after a countback.

The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first edition to be staged on African soil, began on 31 October and will run until 13 November.

World.title: Lagos hails TEHC’s Louisville mixed-use development in Eko Atlantic
World.content:
The Lagos State Government has commended the ambition and investment strategy behind Louisville, a mixed-use real estate development being undertaken by the TotalEnergies Staff Housing Cooperative Multipurpose Society Ltd (TEHC) in EkoAtlantic City.

The state’s Director of Cooperatives, Dr Adeyemi Adeyinka, gave the commendation during a visit to the project site on Monday, 2 November 2026, where he led a delegation of cooperative officials on an inspection tour.

The delegation was received by TEHC officials, who presented an overview of the project, highlighting its construction progress, financing structure, safety standards and proposed facilities.

Speaking during the visit, Adeyinka described Louisville as a laudable initiative capable of improving members’ welfare while generating sustainable income for the cooperative.

He noted that large-scale cooperative investments could stimulate economic activities beyond the immediate membership of societies, adding that such initiatives demonstrated the potential of collective investment in addressing Nigeria’s development challenges.

However, he urged the project promoters to anticipate possible financing challenges and put adequate measures in place to ensure that construction was not disrupted by funding constraints.

The Deputy Director of Cooperative Services, Mr Omotayo Kazeem, also praised the scale and vision of the development, particularly its location in Eko Atlantic City, which is associated with major corporate and institutional investments.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the project demonstrated that cooperatives could successfully venture into ambitious real estate investments rather than restrict their activities to conventional thrift and credit operations.

Kazeem encouraged other cooperative societies to explore properly structured investments capable of delivering sustainable returns and improving members’ economic fortunes.

Other members of the delegation included Mrs Hunpe Esther, Area Officer; Mr Abimbola Kolawole, Assistant Area Officer; and Mr Arisu Olumide and Mr Olatunji Tawak, Registrars of Cooperatives.

During a roundtable session, TEHC officials outlined the development strategy for Louisville, emphasising its focus on creating long-term value through collective investment.

The project occupies approximately 22,000 square metres in Eko Atlantic City and is being developed in phases. Its first residential phase comprises 157 apartments ranging from two to five bedrooms, which are currently under construction.

Beyond residential accommodation, the master plan includes hospitality facilities, retail and commercial spaces, sports and wellness amenities, as well as supporting infrastructure.

The development is designed to integrate residential living with recreation, commerce and essential services, making it a mixed-use community rather than a conventional apartment complex.

The cooperative explained that its financing model combines members’ contributions and property subscriptions with institutional financing arrangements.

The project team also briefed the delegation on construction challenges, safety measures and the anticipated commercial contributions of the non-residential components.

The President of TEHC, represented at the visit by the Chief Operating Officer, Ehima Uwumarogie, said Louisville reflected the potential of collective investment to create lasting economic value.

“Louisville represents what is possible when people come together with a shared vision, a clear purpose and the commitment to turn collective resources into lasting value,” the cooperative said.

TEHC described the visit as an opportunity to showcase the progress made on the project and deepen the state government’s understanding of its investment and development model.

It added: “With the right leadership, governance and institutional support, cooperatives can play an even greater role in Nigeria’s economic development.”

The visiting officials also emphasised the importance of effective leadership, responsible governance and prudent financial management in sustaining large-scale cooperative investments.

They encouraged greater knowledge-sharing among cooperative societies, including through engagement with the Lagos State Cooperative Federation, to enable other societies to learn from TEHC’s experience.

The visit also provided an opportunity to explore areas of collaboration between TEHC and the state’s cooperative authorities, although no formal partnership was announced.

TEHC said it would sustain engagement with relevant regulatory and professional stakeholders as it works towards delivering the Louisville project.

About TEHC

Established in 2020 by serving and former employees of TotalEnergies in Nigeria, the TotalEnergies Staff Housing Cooperative Multipurpose Society Ltd is a member-owned organisation focused on collective investment and the development of residential and mixed-use communities.

World.title: ANALYSIS: COP31: Nine Key issues to shape talks as UN climate talks open in Türkiye
World.content:
World leaders, government representatives, delegates, civil society groups, researchers and scientists are converging in Antalya, Türkiye, for the 31st session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP31), amid growing calls for countries to translate their climate commitments into concrete action.

The conference, scheduled for 9 through 20 November, is expected to focus on accelerating the implementation of climate pledges, notably efforts to limit global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, in line with the Paris Agreement.

This year’s summit will be conducted under an unusual shared leadership arrangement, with Türkiye hosting the conference, while Australia leads negotiations. Its overarching slogan, “Where Dialogue Becomes Global Action”, reflects the ambition to move beyond climate pledges towards practical implementation.

Beyond the proposed agenda, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN), which includes Nigeria, will push for developed countries to fulfil their existing climate finance obligations under the Paris Agreement.

The African negotiating bloc plans to push for increased support to help developing countries implement their climate commitments, strengthen resilience, and tackle the growing impacts of climate change.

According to the UN Climate Change secretariat, three major reports published ahead of COP31 indicate that governments are increasingly adopting whole-of-economy and whole-of-society approaches to climate policymaking.

Yet, the reports warn that overall progress remains substantially insufficient, highlighting persistent barriers to speeding up climate action and implementing national targets and pledges.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mandated under the UN climate process, the reports include the 2026 Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) Synthesis Report, the Biennial Transparency Report (BTR) Synthesis Report and the National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) Progress Report.

Together, they assess countries’ progress in translating climate commitments into policies, tracking emissions reductions, strengthening adaptation, and mobilising the resources required to deliver climate action.

Consequently, COP31 hopes to offer an important opportunity for countries to advance negotiations on practical measures to address these implementation gaps.

Alongside the formal negotiations, the Global Climate Action Agenda will provide opportunities to boost electrification, improve access to climate finance and cut waste and emissions of super-pollutants such as methane.

Calls for accelerated implementation

In a statement ahead of the conference, UN Climate Change’s executive secretary, Simon Stiell, said the reports showed that more governments are integrating climate action into their economic planning.

“These reports show more governments are taking climate action right across their economies, to bank the vast benefits of clean energy and climate resilience,” he said.

Mr Stiell noted that climate action is increasingly being recognised as a driver of economic growth, job creation and affordable, secure energy.

That said, he warned that global progress remains too slow to meet the goals of the Paris Agreement.

“However, this year’s reports demonstrate again that collective progress remains clearly insufficient, that global transitions are very uneven, and that many countries face substantial barriers to delivering their targets and pledges,” he said.

He said COP31 could help close some of the gaps through ambitious outcomes on mitigation, adaptation, climate finance and just transitions.

Mr Stiell also highlighted the significance of accelerating electrification, curbing methane emissions and advancing zero-waste initiatives.

“By building the support, agreements, and partnerships needed to help convert more pledges into real-world results, COP31 can also bring the vast benefits of climate resilience and cheap, secure clean energy to more people around the world,” he added.

2026 Nationally Determined Contributions Synthesis Report

According to the United Nations, the 2026 Nationally Determined Contributions Synthesis Report assesses how countries are turning their commitments under the Paris Agreement into concrete policies and actions, while identifying existing challenges.

Between 1 January 2024 and 31 August 2026, the UN said it recorded 127 new NDCs from 154 Parties to the Paris Agreement in the NDC registry. Together, they cover approximately 70 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions.

The UN observed that the report shows the latest generation of NDCs is more comprehensive, increasingly incorporating different components of the Paris Agreement, including mitigation, adaptation, climate finance, technology transfer, capacity-building, loss and damage, response measures and just transition.

It also highlights the growing involvement of local and regional authorities, civil society organisations and the private sector in planning, implementing and monitoring climate action.

Reflecting this whole-of-society approach, the report noted that 98 per cent of Parties reported engaging different stakeholders in implementing their NDCs, compared with 70 per cent in previous submissions.

The report further notes that 90 per cent of parties weighed the outcomes of the first global stocktake in preparing their latest NDCs, while 65 per cent highlighted the contribution of clean energy to energy security.

Despite these developments, projected emissions reductions remain far below the levels science requires to achieve the Paris Agreement’s temperature goals.

Current pledges are expected to reduce global emissions by about six per cent by 2035, compared with 2019 levels.

Even with full implementation of all current pledges, emissions could decline by only around nine per cent by 2035, underscoring the need for stronger international cooperation, financial support, and coordinated action across governments, businesses, and other sectors.

2026 National Adaptation Plan Progress Report

The 2026 National Adaptation Plan Progress Report marks a shift from tracking the formulation of national adaptation plans to assessing their implementation.

As of 20 October, 146 countries had initiated or launched the National Adaptation Plan process.

Much as 81 developing countries, including 29 least developed countries (LDCs) and 17 small island developing states (SIDS), have submitted their national adaptation plans, significant barriers remain, particularly in accessing finance.

The report highlights the gulf between countries developing adaptation strategies and their ability to translate those plans into practical interventions.

It identifies challenges in preparing project proposals, securing approval and ensuring that approved funding reaches the countries and communities that need it most.

The report also points to the limited number of accredited entities and difficulties in advancing funding proposals through approval processes.

It warns that approval does not necessarily translate into access to finance, as lengthy processing procedures and delays in disbursing funds continue to impede countries from implementing approved projects.

The findings are expected to reinforce developing countries’ calls for simplified access to adaptation finance and more predictable funding to address growing climate vulnerabilities.

2026 Biennial Transparency Report Synthesis Report

The 2026 Biennial Transparency Report Synthesis Report assesses progress in implementing nationally determined contributions during the reporting period covered by the first round of BTRs (2020–2022).

It indicates that climate policymaking is increasingly integrated into national development strategies, with policies and actions covering wider sections of the economy and involving different segments of society.

For instance, 80 per cent of Parties reported involving non-Party stakeholders in climate action, while 92 per cent linked their climate policies to Sustainable Development Goals.

Since the publication of the inaugural BTR Synthesis Report last year, over 30 additional reports have been submitted, bringing the total number of Parties that have submitted BTRs to 137. These reports now cover approximately 85 per cent of global emissions.

Between 2020 and 2022, 61 Parties, representing about 66 per cent of global emissions in 2020, made progress towards their NDC targets.

The latest report also highlights the growing significance of adaptation in countries’ climate reporting.

Although reporting on adaptation is not mandatory under the framework, 92 per cent of Parties included an adaptation component in their BTRs.

The findings underscore the growing role of transparency and accountability in tracking countries’ climate commitments and assessing implementation progress.

Climate finance: Persistent funding gaps

Climate finance is expected to feature among the most contentious issues at COP31, as developing countries continue to demand greater financial support from developed nations to combat climate change.

Two new reports from the Standing Committee on Finance (SCF), a constituted body under the UN climate process, examine progress in mobilising climate finance and the challenges of ensuring that funding reaches developing countries.

The Third Report on Progress Towards Achieving the $100 Billion Goal assesses progress in the commitment by developed countries to mobilise $100 billion annually to back developing countries’ mitigation action and transparency.

The report finds that climate finance provided and mobilised by developed countries for developing countries increased between 2020 and 2024, according to different sources.

One source indicated that the $100 billion annual target was achieved in 2022, 2023 and 2024.

The report, however, highlights divergence in how progress is measured and persistent challenges relating to access, affordability and the ability of developing countries to secure the funding required to meet their climate needs.

Similarly, the Seventh Biennial Assessment and Overview of Climate Finance Flows evaluates global public and private climate finance, including financial flows from developed to developing countries.

It finds that global climate finance surged 32 per cent to an annual average of $1.9 trillion in 2023 and 2024, alongside improvements in reporting.

Despite this growth, significant disparities exist in the distribution of investments, with developing countries continuing to face barriers to accessing finance and persistent shortfalls in adaptation funding.

The assessment calls for increased investment, improved access and affordability, and stronger alignment of climate finance with countries’ priorities and the objectives of the Paris Agreement.

These findings are expected to strengthen demands at COP31 for developed countries to fulfil their financial obligations and ensure that climate funding is accessible, predictable and affordable.

Key issues shaping COP31 negotiations

Beyond the findings of the reports, several critical issues are expected to shape negotiations and political discussions at COP31.

Limiting and managing 1.5°C overshoot

The 1.5°C temperature threshold is central to international climate negotiations, as global warming approaches the limit established under the Paris Agreement.

With the world facing the prospect of temporarily exceeding this threshold, discussions are anticipated to centre on how countries can step up mitigation efforts, accelerate emissions reductions and limit the duration and scale of any temperature overshoot.

This will require stronger national climate commitments, accelerated transitions to cleaner energy sources and more ambitious policies to pare down greenhouse gas emissions.

Electrification and translating commitments into action

The conference is expected to place greater emphasis on expanding electricity access, strengthening clean energy systems and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.

A proposed target of meeting 35 per cent of final global energy demand through electricity by 2035 is also expected to feature in discussions around the presidency’s implementation agenda.

The broader focus is on moving beyond high-level commitments towards practical roadmaps for clean power generation, green industrialisation, improved electricity grids and energy efficiency across buildings and other sectors.

Climate finance and access to funding

Climate finance remains a major point of contention between developed and developing countries.

Developing nations argue that existing financial commitments must translate into actual funding, rather than relying largely on anticipated private-sector investments and other financing arrangements that may not bear fruit.

They are also demanding simpler procedures for accessing concessional finance, particularly for adaptation projects and programmes addressing the impacts of climate change.

Adaptation and loss and damage

As climate-related disasters intensify, developing countries are expected to demand higher adaptation finance and stronger support for vulnerable communities.

A key issue is the call to scale up adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035, alongside efforts to address the funding needs of countries experiencing climate-related losses and damage.

For African countries grappling with huge climate vulnerabilities despite contributing relatively little to global emissions, access to adequate and predictable adaptation funding is particularly important.

The discussions are expected to focus on how countries can move from developing adaptation plans to implementing projects that protect livelihoods, boost food systems, improve infrastructure and build resilience.

Ultimately, the success of COP31 will depend not only on the agreements reached during negotiations but also on whether countries can address persistent gaps in finance, implementation and accountability that continue to undermine global climate action.

World.title: US lawmaker who made Christian genocide claim against Nigeria re-elected to Congress
World.content:
Republican Congressman Riley Moore, who made repeated claims of Christian genocide in Nigeria, won re-election to the US House of Representatives in the Midterms.

Mr Moore defeated Democratic Party candidate Ace Parsi to retain his seat as the representative for West Virginia’s 2nd District.

He was one of the Republican candidates who won their seats amid the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the elections.

The poll was fiercely contested, with Mr Moore winning his seat with 59.4 per cent of the total votes.

“It’s been an honor of my life to represent West Virginia’s Second Congressional District. I’m proud of the work I’ve done to advance critical infrastructure investments, strengthen our aerospace and defense industries, and bring new economic opportunities and good-paying jobs to West Virginia.

“I’ll never stop fighting for West Virginians!” he wrote on X after his victory.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that amid US President Donald Trump’s antagonism towards Nigeria, the Republican lawmaker repeatedly criticised the Nigerian government for not doing enough to protect the country’s Christians.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He repeatedly claimed there was a Christian genocide in the country and insisted on his claims despite the Nigerian government denying it.

The government, along with local and international organisations, explained that Nigeria’s insecurity was caused by several factors and was not targeted at any particular group.

Mr Moore, first elected to the House in 2024, was also part of the US congressional delegation that visited Nigeria to discuss security in the West African nation.

Mr Moore is among the sponsors of the Nigeria Religious Freedom and Accountability Act of 2026, a bill introduced in February alongside Congressman Chris Smith.

If enacted, the legislation would require the US Secretary of State to regularly submit reports to Congress detailing efforts to address religious persecution and mass atrocities in Nigeria.

He also championed the National Security, Department of State and Related Programs Appropriations Act for 2027, which sought to, among others, cut foreign assistance to Nigeria over alleged targeted violence against Christians and other vulnerable communities.

He had earlier said the US will closely monitor Nigeria’s 2027 general election and pay particular attention to the credibility and conduct of the electoral process.

Democrats won Congress in the midterms and now have the capacity to hamstring Mr Trump’s foreign policy misadventures when the new Congress is sworn in in January 2027.

However, it remains to be seen how the changes in the US political landscape will affect Washington’s relationship with Nigeria and Africa as a whole.

World.title: Atiku’s son leads APC campaign group to Jigawa ahead of Tinubu’s visit
World.content:
Abba Atiku, a son of the presidential candidate of the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, on Monday led his support group to Jigawa State ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s scheduled visit on Tuesday.

Atiku junior, the movement’s founder, announced the collapse of the group’s structure, ‘Haske’, state-wide into the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in support of President Tinubu’s re-election bid.

He stated that the president deserves a second term to fully deliver on his “Renewed Hope” mandate for Nigerians.

Also speaking, Usman Meyari, director-general of the Haske Bola Ahmed Tinubu Organisation, stated that the group—originally founded in 2019 to support Atiku Abubakar—has now resolved to back the incumbent president.

“We believe in the informal agreement on power rotation between the North and the South.

Former President Muhammadu Buhari completed eight years in power. What justification do we have to deny President Bola Ahmed Tinubu the opportunity to complete his own eight-year tenure?

“Attempting to replace Tinubu at this stage invites chaos and instability. That is why we, the youth, are backing the president to safeguard the nation’s stability.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are doing this in the national interest, as every patriotic citizen desires peaceful development and progress. We must avoid selfishness by not insisting on an early northern succession. There is an understanding regarding a rotational presidency, and we must honour it”, Mr Meyare said.

In his remarks, Jigawa State Governor Umar Namadi commended the group for the visit and lauded its decision to support the APC and President Tinubu’s re-election.

The governor expressed his appreciation for the delegation’s commitment to national unity and stability.

“I am with you 100 per cent,” Governor Namadi said. “As a governor and member of the APC, I stand firmly behind you, and we will work hand in hand to ensure that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu secures a second term.

“In Jigawa, our objective is not merely to see Tinubu re-elected; we are focused on delivering an overwhelming majority of the state’s votes for him.”

The Jigawa State Government has promised a rousing reception for President Tinubu when he arrives on Tuesday for a working visit and campaign rally.

World.title: UTME 2027: JAMB releases checklist for candidates ahead of registration
World.content:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has released six essential checklist items for candidates who will register and sit the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME).

In an advisory published on its social media pages on Monday, JAMB said the checklist was intended to help candidates stay organised, prepare effectively, and avoid common mistakes during the registration and admission process.

“As you prepare for the 2027 UTME, there are a few important things to get right before examination day,” the board stated.

Annually, about two million candidates sit the examination, a prerequisite for admission into Nigerian universities and polytechnics. Until this year, applicants to colleges of education were also mandated to sit the UTME.

The checklist

In its checklist, JAMB asked candidates to ensure that their names, dates of birth and other biodata with the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) are correct ahead of the exercise.

The board also asked candidates to have an active email address and maintain a registered phone number before the commencement of the UTME registration.

It urged the candidates to decide on their preferred courses and institutions and ensure they selected the appropriate subject combinations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Maintain an active email address you can easily access. Candidates should ensure they remember their email login details and can receive messages through the account,” it said.

“Be sure about the programme you intend to study. Candidates should understand the requirements for their preferred programmes rather than choosing courses without checking the necessary qualifications.”

The board also directed candidates seeking further information to visit its official website at www.ibas.jamb.gov.ng and follow its verified platforms for updates on the 2027 registration exercise.

2027 UTME

JAMB has not disclosed when the registration exercise will begin.

However, the Ministry of Education has asked the examination body to hold the UTME between 15 and 25 March, 2027.

The directive was part of the education ministry’s harmonisation of examination timetables across the country.

READ ALSO: JAMB plans UTME centre in Canada for Nigerians from 2027

The ministry also asked the West African Examination Council (WAEC) to conduct the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) between 11 May and 18 June 2027.

It also asked the National Examination Council (NECO) to conduct its SSCE between 1 April and 14 May 2027.

World.title: Full list: 2026/2027 FA Cup second round fixtures confirmed
World.content:
Wimborne Town have been handed a home tie against Bradford City in the second round of the FA Cup, while Leicester City will travel to non-league side Dover Athletic.

Seventh-tier Wimborne are among the lowest-ranked teams remaining in the competition after producing one of the biggest upsets of the first round by defeating League Two side Crawley Town.

The Magpies will now welcome League One outfit Bradford City as they look to continue their impressive FA Cup run.

Leicester, who won the competition in 2021, must overcome Dover Athletic away from home to book their place in the third round.

Leyton Orient will host Port Vale, last season’s quarter-finalists, while 2013 FA Cup winners Wigan Athletic have been drawn against Barnsley in an all-League One encounter.

Jack Wilshere’s Luton Town will travel to AFC Fylde, while the winner of the postponed Plymouth Parkway versus Berkhamsted tie will host Barnet.

The second-round fixtures will be played across the weekend of December 5, 2026.

World.title: Jensen Huang: 5 things to know about viral Nvidia CEO’s affair with Chinese executive
World.content:
(FILES) Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced on November 8, 2026 it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. (Photo by Patrick T. Fallon / AFP)

Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, whose chips power the global AI boom and who has the ear of President Donald Trump, has admitted to an affair with a Chinese executive who US intelligence reportedly believes was working for Beijing.

Here is what we know:

– What happened? –

Huang, 63, acknowledged the relationship Sunday in a message to Nvidia employees.

“I was unfaithful to my wife,” he wrote. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang has been married to his wife Lori since 1985.

His admission followed reports in The New York Times that US intelligence officials had concluded the woman, Alice Huang, was passing information to China. She is not related to the Nvidia chief.

Nvidia had previously said that his interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” given their business ties.

– Who is Alice Huang? –

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a senior executive at Megaspeed. The Singapore-based data center company was spun off from a Chinese company in 2023, and it rents out computing power from Nvidia chips.

The Wall Street Journal reported that she and Huang were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025.

According to the Times, a memo circulated among senior US officials this spring cited intelligence that she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

The memo said she had been recruited to gather information on Huang and possibly to steer Nvidia toward pushing for its top chips to be sold in China.

The Journal said that authorities in Singapore and Taiwan also suspected Chinese intelligence had recruited her after learning of her closeness to Huang. Her current whereabouts are unclear.

US officials suspect Megaspeed of helping smuggle restricted chips into China and the Justice Department has taken over a federal investigation into the company.

Megaspeed has previously described itself as a “compliant and legitimate company.”

Beijing rejected the allegations. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Monday that “the narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.”

– Why does it matter? –

Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models. Washington has restricted sales of the most advanced ones to China since 2022 under the Biden administration.

Huang has also been one of Trump’s most influential informal advisers on AI.

The Journal reported that intelligence officials suspected the affair while Huang was lobbying the White House to allow chip exports to China.

Late last year, he pushed to sell Nvidia’s most powerful chips there, an effort that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other officials blocked.

Trump instead allowed sales of a less advanced chip, with the US government taking a 25 percent cut.

According to the Times, Trump was briefed on the intelligence roughly a year ago and did not act on it.

On Fox News on Sunday, Trump was asked whether Huang should remain CEO. “I think so, oh yeah, sure,” he said, calling Huang “an honorable guy.” Trump said he did not regret not acting on the intelligence.

– What is the board doing? –

Nvidia’s board on Sunday said it had opened an independent probe into the matter.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it said.

According to the Times, a committee of independent directors working with outside counsel will lead the review, and Huang will remain CEO in the meantime.

– What comes next? –

Republican House committee leaders, including those on the Select Committee on China, have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s security protocols in Washington on November 18.

Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives predicted the episode would lead to multiple congressional inquiries. He said Huang would likely keep his job in the near term but could be ousted depending on the internal inquiry’s findings.

George Chen of The Asia Group told AFP it would be “premature to conclude that Jensen poses a threat to US national security before the facts are fully established.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Manchester United are becoming a club of survival rather than ambition
World.content:
The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen.

There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation.

Those expectations seem increasingly distant.

On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience.

But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant.

Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory.

That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse.

United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches. They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League.

The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success.

Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend.

Survival has become the immediate ambition.

And that is a remarkable development for a club whose history was built on refusing to accept anything less than excellence.

Sunday’s performance captured both sides of United’s current identity. There was the determination to fight back, the willingness to keep attacking and the refusal to surrender even when the game appeared beyond them. Coming back from 2-0 down, reaching 2-2, falling behind again and eventually recovering from 4-2 demonstrated a spirit that supporters have desperately wanted to see.

However, resilience cannot become an excuse for repeated carelessness.

United conceded twice inside the opening four minutes. They then surrendered their defensive organisation again immediately after half-time, allowing John McGinn to score from the penalty spot before Leon Goretzka extended Villa’s advantage. The attacking response was admirable, but the defensive problems that made such a dramatic recovery necessary were equally concerning.

There is a difference between fighting back from adversity and repeatedly creating adversity for yourself.

For Carrick, the challenge is no longer simply convincing supporters that his team can produce entertaining football. He must demonstrate that Manchester United can become dependable again. The occasional spectacular comeback cannot compensate for a team that struggles to manage the opening minutes of matches, protect advantages or maintain concentration.

There is also a wider question about the club’s direction.

Manchester United’s problems cannot be reduced to one manager, one transfer window or one poor run of results. The instability surrounding the club has created an environment in which every setback becomes another argument about leadership, recruitment and the footballing structure. The manager becomes the immediate subject of scrutiny, but the problems appear considerably deeper.

The danger is that United become accustomed to this existence.

When a club repeatedly lowers its expectations to accommodate its circumstances, mediocrity can gradually become normal. Supporters who once demanded victories begin celebrating draws. A team that once approached matches expecting to dictate proceedings now approaches them hoping to survive the next defensive crisis.

That is perhaps the most disturbing part of United’s current predicament.

The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa should not be dismissed. There was genuine character in the comeback, and the players deserved credit for refusing to surrender. Football supporters should be allowed to enjoy extraordinary moments, even in difficult seasons.

But one dramatic afternoon cannot disguise a deeply troubling campaign.

Manchester United have spent years searching for a return to the standards that made them one of football’s most formidable institutions. Now, with the relegation zone beneath their feet, the immediate concern is no longer how quickly they can return to the summit but whether they can first escape the bottom three.

A draw that once would have been considered two points dropped has become a reason for celebration.

Perhaps that is the clearest indication of how far Manchester United have fallen.

The problem is no longer just that United are struggling to win football matches. It is that a club built on ambition is beginning to look increasingly comfortable with survival.

World.title: 2027: INEC removes 1.6m names from voters register
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why those who registered in the third phase of its Continuous Voter Registration CVR are yet to have their Permanent Voter Cards even as it announced a massive purge of the national voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, disclosed that the commission has successfully removed 1,609,553 invalid and deceased records from the system.

“The Commission recognises that the detection of irregularities raises legitimate questions about how they arose. The response is evidence-led investigation, completed corrective action and stronger preventive controls.

“1,609,553 records have been removed, comprising 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations and 873 verified deceased-voter records. INEC will continue to communicate verifiable aggregate outcomes while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations”, said Amupitan.

Addressing reporters regarding the status of unprinted cards, the INEC Chairman stated: “The distribution of Phases 1 and 2 of the PVC and transferred PVCs is on-going at the various LGAs in Nigeria. Some of the PVC for the third and final Phase are being delivered and they would be dispatched to the States by next week.

“Meanwhile as from 1st December 2026, distribution will go back to the Registration Areas all over Nigeria. We appeal to those that registered in the third pahse to be a little bit patient since the production is done outside the country”.

Vanguard recalls that those who registered in total in the third phase were 2,970,257 before the commission’s de-duplication protocol.

The sweeping clean-up of the register followed widespread public outcry and intense scrutiny over anomalies spotted on the preliminary register displayed between October 9 and 15, 2026.

A rigorous technical audit utilizing the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) uncovered systemic manipulations, including unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs, and fraudulent multiple registrations.

Crucially, the investigation indicted internal personnel who abused their offices. Prof. Amupitan revealed that the commission identified 54 staff members cutting across 10 states who deliberately bypassed standard operating procedures and exploited special provisions meant for vulnerable citizens, such as persons with disabilities. Disciplinary actions and possible prosecutions have been initiated against the culprits.

Reacting to media inquiries surrounding court cases involving political actors, the INEC Chairman maintained that the electoral umpire operates strictly on authenticated legal instruments rather than speculative reports.

“On ADC/Atiku: as of today, we have not received the Certified True Copy of the court judgment and we don’t act based on what we see on the social media”, he said.

INEC noted that while the recent 2025/2026 CVR clean-up resolved immediate anomalies, historical data carried over from 2011 to 2023 continues to present legacy duplications. Consequently, the commission’s board has directed that flagged entries from past cycles be expunged after verification.

To further safeguard the integrity of the upcoming 2027 polls, INEC assured the public that robust mechanisms—including the mandatory physical presence of voters and biometric authentication via the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) using fingerprints or facial recognition—remain firmly in place to prevent multiple voting and unauthorized accreditation.

World.title: Public Notice To Gaming Operators And The General Public.
World.content:
FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY LOTTERY REGULATORY OFFICE (FCT-LRO)

Oﬃce of the Director-General

PUBLIC NOTICE TO GAMING OPERATORS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.

FCT-LRO COMMENCES FULL BUSINESS OPERATIONS

The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulatory Oﬃce (FCT-LRO) hereby informs gaming

operators, industry stakeholders and the general public that the Oﬃce has commenced

operations as the regulatory authority responsible for the oversight, regulation and supervision

of gaming activities within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

1. REGULATORY JURISDICTION

Following the Supreme Court judgment in Attorney-General of Lagos State & 21 Others v.

Attorney-General of the Federation & 15 Others, Suit No. SC/1/2008, the constitutional

position on the regulation of lotteries and gaming has been clarified. By virtue of Section

299 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended),

the FCT has a distinct constitutional status, with the National Assembly exercising

legislative powers ordinarily vested in a State House of Assembly.

Accordingly, gaming operators conducting business within the FCT are required to comply

with the applicable FCT licensing and regulatory requirements and engage with the FCT-

LRO on all regulatory matters.

2. ONLINE GAMING OPERATIONS

The Oﬃce clarifies that the Supreme Court judgment did not expressly settle the full

regulatory framework applicable to online gaming. In particular, the judgment did not

establish that any one State has exclusive regulatory control over the online gaming

market.

Accordingly, the online gaming market remains open to operators and investors. Operators

are free to choose the regulator from whom they wish to obtain their gaming licence or

authorisation, based on their business model, operational needs and the regulatory

framework they consider most suitable and beneficial to their business.

This choice may be exercised without undue interference, intimidation or coercive

treatment by any State regulator solely on the basis that an operator has elected to obtain its

licence from another regulator, as every state is duly empowered to regulate gaming

activities within its relevant jurisdiction.

Operators are, however, reminded that the online nature of a gaming platform does not, in

itself, exempt an operation from applicable licensing and regulatory obligations where

such obligations arise.

The FCT-LRO remains committed to providing a transparent, consistent and predictable

regulatory environment for digital gaming operations within the Federal Capital Territory.

3. NOTICE TO FORMER NLRC LICENSEES

All gaming operators previously licensed by the National Lottery Regulatory Commission

(NLRC) who are currently operating, or intend to operate, within the Federal Capital

Territory (FCT) are hereby required to approach the FCT-LRO to regularise their regulatory

status.

The Oﬃce further clarifies that any NLRC licence that remains valid and has not expired

will be recognised for the remainder of its validity period and converted to the

corresponding FCT-LRO licence. Accordingly, holders of former NLRC licences will

retain the benefit of their unexpired licence terms, subject to the regularisation process

prescribed by the FCT-LRO.

Aﬀected operators are required to present and hand over their former NLRC-issued

licences for verification and documentation, complete the applicable regularisation

procedures and obtain the appropriate FCT gaming licence.

All aﬀected operators are required to commence the regularisation process within 7 days of

publication of this notice.

4. RECOGNISED FCT-LRO OPERATORS

For public awareness and regulatory transparency, the following operators are currently

recognised as licensed operators within the FCT:

(INSERT LIST)

Members of the public are encouraged to verify the licensing status of gaming operators

before engaging their services.

5. OFFICIAL CONTACT DETAILS

All licensing applications, regulatory enquiries, compliance matters and oﬃcial

correspondence should be directed to the FCT-LRO through the following channels:

Oﬃce Address: 2B Embu Crescent, Ishaku Rabiu Estate, Oﬀ Aminu Kano Crescent, Wuse

2, Abuja.

Telephone: +234 802 347 6076 / +234 813 052 5876

The FCT-LRO reiterates its commitment to promoting responsible gaming, protecting

consumers, strengthening regulatory oversight and fostering a transparent and investment-

All operators and stakeholders are advised to take note and ensure compliance.

World.title: 2027: NDC will provide all-inclusive government – Kwankwaso
World.content:
The NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, (BBC)

By Henry Umoru

Ahead of January 16 2027 election, the Vice Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has promised Nigerians that an NDC-led Federal Government under Peter Obi and himself will operate an all-inclusive government.

According to him, the Obi-led government would prioritise the interests of every Nigerian, irrespective of political, ethnic, religious or social affiliations.

The former Kano State Governor spoke while addressing party leaders, stakeholders and supporters during a carnival-like reception organised in his honour at Toru-Orua, the country home of Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, National Leader of the NDC and the party’s Senatorial candidate for Bayelsa West.

In a statement signed by the Coordinator, Ofurumapepe Media of the NDC Campaign Council, Gabriel Ukuta, he explained that Kwankwaso said that what Nigeria needed at this moment in the nation’s political history is a government that would deliberately carry its citizens along in the formulation, implementation of policies and programmes.

He said that governance must be people-oriented and responsive to the needs and aspirations of the population.

Kwankwaso said the NDC has positioned itself as a credible alternative political platform with the capacity, leadership and commitment to deliver the inclusive governance Nigerians desire.

The NDC Vice Presidential Candidate said, “Nigerians deserve a government that will listen to them, accommodate their interests and ensure that no section of the country is left behind. An NDC-led Federal Government will be an all-inclusive government that will carry everybody along in its policies and programmes,”

Kwankwaso who condemned what he described as the prevailing hunger, economic hardship and insecurity under the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government, urged Nigerians to take advantage of the 2027 general elections to vote out the ruling party.

The Vice Presidential Candidate who called on citizens to take collective responsibility for the electoral process by coming out en masse to vote for the NDC and ensuring that their votes count, expressed concern over alleged attempts by anti-democracy forces and agents of the ruling party to manipulate the outcome of the forthcoming elections, insisting that Nigerians must remain vigilant and protect their votes.

“Voting is not enough; Nigerians must also take responsibility for protecting their votes. We must all work together to ensure that the wishes of the people are respected and that the outcome of the elections reflects the collective decision of the electorate,” he added.

He expressed appreciation to Senator Dickson, members of the NDC National Working Committee (NWC), the National Campaign Council (NCC), party stakeholders, candidates and supporters across Bayelsa State for the impressive reception accorded him.

In his remarks, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, who is also the NDC candidate for Bayelsa West Senatorial District, decried what he described as the growing hardship, hunger, insecurity, victimisation, inducement and intimidation allegedly being experienced by the people of Bayelsa State under the APC-led Federal and State Governments.

Dickson maintained that the NDC presidential and vice-presidential candidates were tested and trustworthy leaders with the requisite experience, competence and commitment to restore good governance and bring the dividends of democracy to the doorsteps of Nigerians.

He expressed confidence in the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket, describing both candidates as individuals capable of providing purposeful leadership and addressing the country’s numerous socio-economic challenges.

The former Bayelsa State governor urged Bayelsans to return to their various communities and intensify mobilisation for the NDC, emphasising the need for collective support for all the party’s candidates, from the presidential election to the State House of Assembly polls.

He called on party faithful and supporters to sustain the momentum generated by the reception and translate it into grassroots political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Dickson also thanked the dignitaries, party leaders, candidates, stakeholders and supporters who attended the event, expressing his appreciation in the Ijaw language and reaffirming the inclusive character of the NDC.

He declared that the NDC was a political platform for all Bayelsans and Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds or previous political affiliations.

The statement further said, ” A major highlight of the reception was the participation of Engineer Kwankwaso in the traditional Ijaw war boat display, popularly known as Ama-Aru, alongside Senator Dickson and other NDC leaders and executives in Bayelsa State, all of whom were led to the even by the party’s National Chairman, Sen. Moses Cleopas.

“The colourful cultural display, which took place along the Toru-Orua axis of the River Forcados, showcased the rich cultural heritage and traditional identity of the Ijaw people.

“The event also featured the formal presentation of party flags to the NDC candidates contesting the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections in Bayelsa State, signalling the party’s readiness for the 2027 electoral contest.”

World.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
World.content:
United Kingdom

A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money.

Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him.

After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose.

The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers.

During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing.

Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty.

“This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said.

“He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.”

A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”.

The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending.

Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court.

Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant.

After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments.

Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London.

His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions.

In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency

and the Home Office.

During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days.
