World.title: Gains and Wins of President Tinubu’s Akwa Ibom Visit
World.content:
B𝑦 Anietie Usen

It was a presidential visit that defied conventions and broke all available records.

The reality that the top three Nigerian leaders: President Bola Tinubu and his wife, Oluremi; Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Hajiya Nana, along with Senate President Godswill Akpabio and his wife, Unoma, together with 71 Senators, were all on the same spot, at the same time, in Uyo, capital of Akwa Ibom State, on a working visit, has no parallel anywhere in Nigeria.

To crown it all, the fact that President Tinubu stayed the night in Akwa Ibom State, with his wife and top federal officials, spoke volumes, not just about the success of the working visit, but the confidence the President has reposed in Governor Umo Eno and Akwa Ibom State.

What was even more striking and difficult to ignore was that since he became the President about four years ago, the No.1 citizen of Nigeria had not spent a night in any of the 36 States of Nigeria, except his political base of Lagos State. Not even his home State of Osun has enjoyed the privilege of hosting the President overnight.

“This is a homecoming for me. I worked here in Akwa Ibom as an auditor in Mobil…and I love you with my whole heart “, the President said, as the mammoth crowd responded with a deafening ovation.

With a palpable sense of nostalgia, he went ahead to address the subject matter of the day: “I am happy to inaugurate the airport named after my colleague (Obong Victor Attah) who had served this State very well as a governor. This is the fulfilment of a vision: from vision to reality”. The applause this time was not just for the President alone but for the succession of Akwa Ibom quality governors namely Attah; Godswill Akpabio, Udom Emmanuel and of course, Umo Eno, the man with a finisher’s anointing.

But beyond the applause for the President and a generation of purposeful Governos in the State; beyond the confidence President Tinubu has in both Governor Eno and Senator Godswill Akpabio, the Senate President; and beyond the fact that President Tinubu had earlier in his career in the 1980s worked in Akwa Ibom’s Qua Iboe Terminal of Mobil, there is also a distinguishing feature of Akwa Ibom that would have persuaded the President to break with his tradition and stay the night in the freshly minted ARISE PALM RESORT built by Governor Eno.

That unique selling point of Akwa Ibom is safety. The State is assessed as a low risk environment on national security and risk indices, ranking among the safest States in Nigeria.

Data from the 𝗡𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗥𝗶𝘀𝗸 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗲𝘅 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗘𝗮𝗿𝗹𝘆 𝗪𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 show that Akwa Ibom holds a low risk score of 0.35%, and is placed at the lowest end of the risk spectrum, compared to states with higher conflict activity.

𝙊𝙥𝙚𝙣𝙒𝙖𝙩𝙘𝙝, an independent security analysis and incident tracking platform, says under its 𝙁𝒂𝙩𝒂𝙡𝒊𝙩𝒚 & 𝑰𝙣𝒄𝙞𝒅𝙚𝒏𝙩 𝘿𝒂𝙩𝒂 that Akwa Ibom is ranked 37 out of 37 nationally by reported fatalities. This means Akwa Ibom has the lowest recorded of fatality rate in Nigeria.

To make the State even safer and more secure, the list of projects listed for commissioning by the President, during the working visit, November 6, 2026, included the State Command and Security Control Centre, a major investment in the State’s security architecture by Governor Eno.

“The facility is designed to provide a central platform for security coordination, intelligence gathering, information sharing and emergency response”, Governor Eno said.

Koko Essien, a retired Army General who is the Akwa Ibom State Commissioner of Internal Security and Waterways, told journalists at a recent media parley that “by improving communications and collaboration among security agencies, the Command Centre is strengthening intelligence-led policing and the State’s capacity to respond to security threats”.

The outstanding security and safety credentials of Akwa Ibom State, especially under Governor Eno, has also augured well for foreign investments and tourism which has been flowing into the State, particularly in the last three years of Umo Eno Administration.

Tourism is actually the centrepiece of the Umo Eno Administration. His investments in this sector is pursued as a major cross-cutting pillar of the ARISE Agenda, which integrates tourism development across multiple economic and infrastructure areas.

Under 𝐇𝐨𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧, Governor Eno is upgrading and expanding assets such as the Ibom Hotel and Golf Resort, Four Points by Sheraton and ongoing projects such as the 250-bedroom Ibom International Hotel.

Under 𝐄𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧, Governor Eno has amazed even his critics by developing landmarks like the mind-blowing ARISE Palm Resort (built on a reclaimed erosion site), where President Tinubu, his wife and top federal officials spent their night.

Under 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐯𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧, Governor Eno is enhancing air and ground travel connectivity via Ibom Air, expanding the international airport, and modernizing State transport with a fleet of 50 CNG passenger buses and the building Ibom City Bus Terminal.

In the area of 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥 𝐓𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐦, he is building an audacious Ibom Medical City to elevate healthcare infrastructure and draw medical visitors.

Under 𝐂𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞, 𝐀𝐫𝐭𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐠𝐞, the Governor is revamping sites like the Ibom Unity Museum, the State Center for Arts and Culture, local beach markets and promoting local cuisines and traditions.

And in the 𝐀𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐄𝐜𝐨-𝐓𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐦 sectors, the multiple award winning Governor is developing initiatives like the Ibom Model Farm, a 50-hectare integrated agricultural and economic project located in Ikot Edibon.

Modelled after the Songhai Farm framework and driven by the Akwa Ibom State University, AKSU, with goal of spearheading agricultural education, student training, research, and agro-tourism, it features zero-waste integrated farming, crop cultivation, livestock housing, fish ponds, and bio-processing/bio-energy systems.

None of these accomplishments escaped the attention of President Tinubu. “Pastor Eno, you are a great man of conscience, commitment and vision…These projects speak well of continuity and the benefits of having a great successor”, the president said after commissioning the world-class Victor Attah International Airport.

According to the President: “When you (Governor Eno) requested my approval for an international status for the airport, I did not hesitate to give the consent because you are a man of vision”.

One good job, they say, deserves another. With the good account Governor Eno gave of himself and his Administration, the President did not hesitate to grant the singular request Governor Eno made.

After thanking the President for all the good things he had done for Akwa Ibom State, including the approval for the Federal University of Technology, Ikot Abasi, and the Federal University of Agriculture, Obio Akpa, the international status for the Victor Attah International Airport, and the inclusion of Akwa Ibom State in the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Governor dropped the singular request, an issue very dear to the hearts of Akwa Ibom people.

“Give us Ibom Deep Seaport…This deep seaport is capable of unlocking the economy of the State, the South-South region and Nigeria at large”, Governor Eno said to the ovation of the jam-packed Godswill Akpabio Stadium.

Soon, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio threw his weight behind the request by Governor Eno. He called on President Tinubu to provide the necessary policy and investment for the development of the Ibom Deep Seaport, saying the project holds enormous potential for job creation and the economic transformation of Akwa Ibom and indeed Nigeria. “On Ibom Deep Seaport, we stand”, Senator Akpabio said.

It was clear to the President that Governor Eno and Senator Akpabio were speaking the minds and deep yearnings of Akwa Ibom people. And when it was his turn to speak, the President did not disappoint the hospitable people of Akwa Ibom State.

“It is approved. It is approved. Development must be even, inclusive and reasonable… It must bring progress and create economic value. I heard – the justification from your Governor, who is my friend and my pastor, speaking on behalf of the leadership and people of Akwa Ibom State on the Deep Seaport project. Ibom Deep Seaport will bring associated economic value and economic development… It is approved”, the President said.

Apart from the endorsement of the Seaport which was initiated in 1999 by the Obong Victor Attah Administration, the fact that the President stayed the night in the ARISE PALM RESORT conferred on the State an enviable status of a tourists destination of choice in Nigeria.

Said Professor Udeme Udofia of the University of Calabar: “You cannot measure the benefits of that presidential gesture in Naira and kobo alone. Yes, you cannot rule out the financial impacts on the resort’s balance sheet. But that particular presidential suite, where President Tinubu and his wife slept, should become a tourist trap of sort, where visitors would like to see and pose for pictures”.

“If the President of Nigeria would find the resort good and secure enough to accommodate him and his wife, who would not find his way to the serene and clean capital of Akwa Ibom for holiday and leisure”, Akpan Micah, a former member of the House of Reps said.

For Dr. Sylvia Ekong, an indigene of Uyo municipality, and former Vice Chairman of Uyo LGA, who was familiar with the advancing and deserted erosion site, the courage of Governor Eno to conquer and subdue the menace of the devastated landscape and turn it to a veritable paradise, showcases him nationally as a model leader.

“Our Governor is exceptionally good and brave in tackling prolonged problems that appear intractable. I can count many such problems including abandoned projects and the backlog of gratuities for the sick and aged civil servants. This Governor will always be remembered for good”, she said.

*Anietie Usen writes from Uyo

World.title: ADC Demands Immediate Release of Certified Copy if Justice Lifu’s Judgement
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) demanded the immediate release of Justice Peter Lifu’s judgment.

The ADC said that Justice Lifu had declared in open court that copies of the judgement were ready, but lamented that ”Our counsel applied for the certified copy and paid the required fee, yet the judgment remains out of reach”

In a statement Monday, Phrank Shaibu, the ADC Presidential Campaign Director of Strategic Communication, said that the inability to make the certified true copies of the judgement to party’s lawyers is indefensible.

According to Shalini, ”This is an indefensible denial of access to a ruling that directly affects the party and its members. If the judgment was ready, there is no excuse for keeping it from the parties. Release it now.

”Our counsel for the first defendant filed a formal application for the certified true copy on 6 November 2026 and paid the assessed fee. Counsel for the third defendant applied the day before, on the very day the judgment was delivered.

”Both applications carry the Federal High Court’s “PAID” stamp. Every requirement was met. Yet the applicants are still being denied the judgment.

”This is not a routine administrative delay. It is a denial of access to a court decision that directly affects the rights of the parties. Justice Lifu declared the judgment is ready; the applicants paid for its certified copy; the court has acknowledged payment.

”Why, then, are they still being kept in the dark? A judge cannot announce that a judgment is ready and leave litigants to chase the document they need to understand and challenge it.”, the ADC Director of Strategic Communication stated.

The judgment concerns the leadership of ADC and the rights of its members.

Shauib said that ”Withholding its certified copy prevents the affected parties from knowing the exact orders made and responding fully through the courts. If the ruling is sound, there is no justification for keeping it out of reach.

”The Federal High Court must release the judgment immediately and explain why paid applications have gone unanswered. Public confidence cannot survive a process in which consequential judgments are announced, but their official records are denied to the parties.”

He said that ADC had formally objected to Justice Lifu presiding over this matter as the National Secretary Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola raised serious concerns about the judge’s impartiality, citing previous appellate decisions that, in the party’s view, called his competence and neutrality into question.

According to the ADC Presidential Campaign Director of Strategic Communication, ”Those concerns were placed on record. The unexplained withholding of the judgment now compounds them and demands answers.

”The timing and conduct of this process are indefensible. Justice Lifu delivered the judgment days after the ADC launched its Sokoto campaign; he then declared the copies ready, yet the parties’ paid applications remain unanswered.

”The public is entitled to ask whether this was a judicial process—or a calculated attempt to deliver a political blow while denying the party the document needed to challenge it. Whoever believes that withholding the judgment will bury these questions or shield those responsible from scrutiny is gravely mistaken.”, Shauib stated.

The ADC presidential campaign demanded thus, ”We demand the immediate release of the certified judgment and a public explanation for the delay. Every day it is withheld deepens the damage to confidence in the judiciary.

”Those responsible must understand that the ADC will pursue every lawful remedy, place the full record before the appropriate authorities and ensure that Nigerians know what has happened. No party, official or judicial officer is beyond scrutiny when the rights of citizens and the integrity of the electoral process are at stake.

”The ADC will not be intimidated or denied its right to challenge this ruling. Any attempt to obstruct that right will be met with every lawful action available, and those responsible will be held to account through the proper legal and institutional channels. Justice must be done, its record must be accessible, and the consequences of denying the parties that access must not be evaded”.

World.title: ISSAN Wins NITDA Award for Best Cybersecurity Awareness, Capacity Building Programme in Nigeria, Africa
World.content:
* Recognition highlights the organisation’s longstanding contribution to cybersecurity awareness, professional development and a safer Nigerian digital ecosystem

The Information Security Society of Africa-Nigeria (ISSAN) has received the award for Best Cybersecurity Awareness and Capacity Building Programme in Nigeria and Africa from the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA).

The award, presented at the 2026 International Cybersecurity Conference organised by NITDA in Abuja, recognises ISSAN’s contribution to advancing cybersecurity awareness, knowledge sharing and capacity development within Nigeria’s digital ecosystem.

Established in South Africa in 1996 and subsequently extended to Nigeria, ISSAN is a not-for-profit professional organisation dedicated to protecting Nigeria’s cyberspace and promoting information security across Africa.

Over the years, the organisation has developed into an important platform for collaboration, knowledge exchange and professional engagement among information security practitioners and other stakeholders.

Its membership cuts across the public and private sectors, including banks, telecommunications operators, government institutions, switching companies, information technology and security consultancy firms, legal practitioners and regulatory agencies.

ISSAN’s work focuses on strengthening the security of banking systems and applications, automated teller machines (ATMs), e-government platforms, electronic commerce and the wider digital ecosystem. It also promotes cybersecurity awareness, appropriate legislation and the adoption of information security best practices.

Through its conferences, professional engagements, knowledge-sharing sessions and capacity-building initiatives, the organisation has continued to encourage collaboration among cybersecurity professionals and institutions in addressing emerging digital threats.

The NITDA recognition comes at a time when Nigeria is accelerating its digital transformation, with increased adoption of electronic payments, digital banking, e-commerce, digital public services and other technology-enabled solutions. While these developments create significant opportunities for economic growth and financial inclusion, they also underscore the need for stronger cybersecurity awareness and preparedness.

ISSAN’s recognition reinforces the importance of equipping individuals, businesses and institutions with the knowledge and capabilities to identify cyber threats, protect sensitive information and adopt safer digital practices.

Speaking on the significance of the award, President of ISSAN, Dr David Isiavwe, said the recognition underscores the growing importance of cybersecurity awareness and capacity building in securing Nigeria’s digital future.

He noted that cybersecurity must go beyond technology and technical infrastructure to include continuous education, responsible digital behaviour, institutional preparedness and collaboration among stakeholders.

According to him, building a secure digital ecosystem requires a collective commitment from government institutions, financial services providers, technology companies, businesses, academia and individuals.

The award also highlights the critical role of professional associations such as ISSAN in promoting cybersecurity knowledge, developing professional capabilities and supporting a more resilient digital environment.

As Nigeria expands its digital economy, the protection of digital platforms, personal information and financial transactions remains essential to building public confidence and encouraging greater participation in digital services.

ISSAN’s recognition by NITDA therefore represents an important milestone for the organisation and the wider cybersecurity community. It reinforces the need for sustained investment in awareness, education, skills development and collaboration to support a safer and more trusted digital ecosystem in Nigeria and across Africa.

The association reaffirmed its commitment to working with relevant stakeholders to promote cybersecurity awareness, strengthen professional capacity and contribute to a secure digital future.

World.title: Stallion Group Partners Access Bank to Offer Up to 90% Vehicle Financing
World.content:
Stallion Group has partnered with Access Bank, a subsidiary of Access Holdings, to make vehicle ownership more accessible to individuals and businesses in Nigeria through financing of up to 90 per cent of vehicle costs.

The partnership, announced in Lagos, brings 10 exclusive automotive brands and 72 models within reach of customers through Access Bank’s AutoFest initiative.

Under the arrangement, eligible individual buyers can access financing of up to 90 per cent of their chosen vehicle’s value, with a minimum equity contribution of 10 per cent. For fleet financing, customers are required to make an equity contribution of between 20 and 30 per cent.

The initiative also provides for potential vehicle delivery within 72 hours after equity contribution, subject to credit approval and completion of the required documentation.

Stallion Group, which has more than 50 years of experience in the automotive industry, is bringing its portfolio of international brands, exclusive manufacturer relationships and customer support capabilities to the partnership.

Beyond vehicle sales, the offering includes professional servicing, optimised cost of ownership, genuine spare parts, dedicated bodyshop facilities and manufacturer warranties of up to six years on eligible vehicles.

Electric vehicle buyers can also benefit from battery warranties of up to eight years, subject to manufacturers’ terms and conditions.

The partnership further provides flexible repayment options extending beyond four years, giving individuals and businesses the opportunity to acquire vehicles without paying the full purchase price upfront.

According to the announcement, the collaboration combines Stallion Group’s automotive heritage and after-sales infrastructure with the financial strength and reach of Access Bank, part of one of Africa’s largest banking groups.

World.title: Power Restored to Areas Affected by Disruption, Says Tegbe
World.content:
The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, has said power supply has been restored to many of the areas earlier affected by power disruptions.

Tegbe, while giving an update on the power situation in a statement in Abuja on Monday, listed the areas to include Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Kwara States, as well as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

”I will like to report that power has since been restored to many of the areas earlier affected by disruptions, largely in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the FCT.

”Our teams continue to work to restore full supply to the remaining affected locations,” he said.

The minister also said that the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330 Kilo Volt (kV) power line had been swiftly repaired and deployed to transmit power.

He said that the restored Benin-Egbin 330 Kilo would help to bring the total power supply to the Lagos Complex to over 1,000 megawatts, effectively normalising the condition before the disruption.

”We are working with the key power sector stakeholders, including the generation companies, system operator, transmission company and the distribution companies to ensure sustained and improved availability of power.

”Our priority continues to be the provision of reliable electricity to Nigerians,” he said. (NAN)

World.title: 2027: Nigeria’s Political Stability Rests More on Courageous, Transparent Verdicts, Amupitan Tells Election Petition Judges
World.content:
* Says Kenya, Ghana, others awaiting nation’s leadership role

* Identifies AI as greatest threat to 2027 polls

* As CJN, Fagbemi task lawyers on professionalism

* A’ Court unveils 375 judges for EPT

Alex Enumah in Abuja

With less than 70 days to the conduct of next year’s presidential election, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Professor Joash Amupitan (SAN), has warned that the stability of Nigeria, politically, would be determined by the verdicts delivered by the Election Petition Tribunals (EPTs) set up to handle grievances arising from the conduct of the 2027 general election.

According to Amupitan, while INEC is saddled with the responsibility of managing the ballot, deploying technology and safeguarding the voter franchise, the EPTs on the other hand stand as the ultimate guardians of democratic legitimacy.

Speaking at a three-day workshop for the EPT judges, Amupitan pointed out that when political contestations overflow from polling units into the courtroom, the judiciary provides the constitutional sanctuary where grievances are transformed into peace, unlawful shortcuts are corrected, and the sovereign choice of the electorate is vindicated under the rule of law.

“Let me emphasize, my Lords, that the stability of our electoral process, and as a matter of fact of Nigeria, is very, very important for the continent of Africa. Because Nigeria is the largest democracy in Africa, and so, so many countries look up to Nigeria for guidance.

“I recall at a meeting of EMBs of Africa in Egypt, most people were wishing me well. And I remember all the EMBs’ heads from other African countries, two of them, for that matter, the EMB head of Kenya, said ‘we want you to succeed. Because whatever happens in Nigeria will happen in Kenya’.

“And also, the EMB chair of Ghana echoed the same thing. ‘Whatever happens in Nigeria is just a matter of time. It will happen in Ghana and other African countries.’ So that is why it is so important that we see our role as a tool of political stability, not just in Nigeria, but in the continent of Africa,” Amupitan said.

According to the senior lawyer, the EPT is not a mere post-election administrative panel; but one that serves as a constitutional valve that releases political pressure and prevents electoral friction from devolving into civil disruption.

He stressed that when the tribunal functions with procedural speed, evidentiary rigour, and absolute impartiality, it achieves three vital democratic outcomes: de-escalation of conflict: institutional accountability: and preservation of the social contract.

“Conversely, where judicial adjudication is perceived as unpredictable, excessively technical, or delayed, political stability is threatened.

“The election tribunal is therefore not merely an arbiter of private disputes between candidates; it is an active engine of national stability and constitutional order,” he said.

While observing that electoral litigation has become increasingly complex with the introduction of technology, the chairman argued that technology must be assessed within the framework of the constitution, the Electoral Act and applicable regulations, adding that it should neither be treated as infallible nor discounted simply because the evidence is electronic.

“A clear distinction must be maintained between the generation of technological information, the statutory purpose it serves and the legal standard required to prove a case before a tribunal,” he said.

“My Lords, the threat matrix confronting our democratic process has expanded beyond traditional physical challenges like ballot snatching. We have entered an era of digital information manipulation, powered by Artificial Intelligence, high-fidelity audio cloning, deepfake video generation, and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI),” he added.

According to Amupitan, during election periods, malicious actors will attempt to disrupt the electoral process through three primary digital threat vectors: Synthetic Operational Directives: AI-generated audio or text messages impersonating election officials, claiming that polling units in specific strongholds are relocated or cancelled to suppress voter turnout.

Eve-of-Poll/Blackout Window Attacks: Deepfake audio or video drops released during statutory broadcast blackouts—hours before polls open—impersonating candidates or electoral officials confessing to fraudulent deals, exploiting the timeframe when official rebuttals struggle to gain traction.

Fake Declaration Videos: Cloned videos of returning officers falsely declaring premature election results in battleground constituencies to trigger civil unrest before official collation concludes.

He advised that to safeguard political stability, tribunals must apply rigorous evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act regarding electronic evidence, adding that demonstrating digital provenance, forensic chain of custody, and reliance on certified data directly from INEC will be vital to prevent synthetic digital fabrications from misleading the courts.

Meanwhile, the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF), Prince Lateef Fagbemi (SAN) have canvassed proper conduct and professionalism from lawyers that will represent various litigants at the 2027 EPTs across the federation.

Kekere-Ekun specifically warned lawyers against filing multiple suits on the same subject matter, seeking conflicting orders from courts of coordinate jurisdiction and using ex-parte applications to secure tactical advantages in election disputes ahead of the 2027 general election.

According to the CJN, such practices could undermine the administration of justice and turn the courts into instruments of political contest, urging legal practitioners to uphold professional ethics and respect judicial processes.

She said the judiciary must be prepared adequately to handle election disputes fairly, competently and within the strict timelines prescribed by the constitution and the Electoral Act.

Fagbemi on his part called on the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) to develop ethical guidelines or a code of conduct for lawyers that will be involved in election-related litigations to ensure seamless resolution of disputes.

The minister stated that the code of conduct and guidelines should promote professionalism, restraint and respect for judicial processes, while discouraging conduct capable of undermining public confidence in electoral justice.

Meanwhile, the President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongbam-Mensem, disclosed that a total of 375 judges have been penned down to handle petitions that may likely arise from the conduct of the 2027 general election.

Dongban-Memsen noted that 138 of the judges were returning members with previous tribunal experience, while the remaining 237 were newly nominated judges.

The Appeal Court president observed that the occasion highlighted the collective commitment to constitutional democracy, the rule of law and the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process.

According to her, the inauguration of the tribunal members is an important institutional preparation for one of the most consequential responsibilities entrusted to the judiciary.

“The credibility of democracy depends not only on the conduct of elections but also on the existence of impartial, effective and timely mechanisms for resolving electoral disputes.

“Through the fair determination of such disputes, the judiciary safeguards the people’s mandate, upholds constitutional supremacy and sustains public confidence in democratic governance.

“The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), particularly Section 285(1) and (2), vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and governorship elections.

“Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries.

“These provisions impose a clear obligation on the court to ensure adequate institutional and administrative preparedness.

“Your Lordships must appreciate the magnitude of the responsibility entrusted to you. Your nomination followed consultations with heads of courts and the Nigerian Bar Association, informed by considerations of professional competence, integrity, judicial temperament and experience.

“This confidence must be regarded as a solemn obligation. Your appointment is a call to service, not privilege; a commitment to uphold the law, not an opportunity for personal or political accommodation,” she said.

She therefore called on the judges to remain steadfast in judicial independence, impartiality and fidelity to the constitution.

According to her, the judges must resist every attempt at improper influence, whether through political pressure, inducement, intimidation, personal relationships or other considerations extraneous to the administration of justice.

“Your judicial oath must remain your guiding compass, and your decisions must be determined exclusively by the evidence, applicable law and judicial conscience. No individual, however highly placed, should be permitted to compromise the independence of your courts,” she added.

World.title: Kwara APC Flays Saraki, Popoola Over Alleged Attempt to Rewrite Offa Robbery History
World.content:
* Says 33 victims’ families deserve respect

Kwara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has condemned what it described as insensitive and reckless the statement by the Kwara South Senatorial District candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Saheed Popoola, to rewrite the history of the 2018 Offa robbery, which claimed 33 lives.

Popoola had, at the weekend, admitted that he deliberately linked the incident in which people including policemen were killed to former Senate President Bukola Saraki to settle political scores.

Addressing journalists at the party’s secretariat on Monday in Ilorin, the APC state Publicity Secretary, Alhaji Abdulwaheed Olawale Babatunde, insisted that convict Akinnibosun and other criminals, according to court evidence, linked Saraki to Offa robbery case.

The party’s spokesman said the convicted armed robbers had, in their statements and evidence presented before the court, allegedly linked Saraki to the incident.

The APC further alleged that Yusuf Abdulwahab, a former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Abdulfatai Ahmed, had made a statement to the police linking Saraki to the case, which was subsequently tendered and admitted as evidence in court.

“Whether Saraki likes it or not, he is accessory before and after the fact. The vehicles and arms were given at his instance (without which they couldn’t have attempted a robbery) and the vehicle (instrument of crime) was hidden at Government House in Ilorin after the robbery operation and later moved to the Ministry of Environment under their watch. The number plate (SARAKI) on the vehicle and their photographs together, some at the Saraki daughter’s wedding, all established a strong link with the criminals.

“In fact, some of the armed robbers were arrested wearing clothes (asoebi) commemorating the wedding of Saraki’s child. These are boys that are very well known to Saraki and were in Saraki’s entourage when he went to pay a condolence visit to Offa following the armed robbery incident,” he explained.

He argued that the recent comments attributed to Popoola could not invalidate the judicial proceedings or the evidence considered by the court.

“The purport of Popoola’s statement is not lost on the people of Offa and Kwara State. A man who shamelessly admitted to lying on a matter of such magnitude and consequence has simply told the people that he lacks any credibility and is not worthy of their trust. He may well wake up tomorrow and do worst things.

“Saraki may want to feed the national audience with distorted facts, but the people of Kwara State know the truth because they lived through the dark days under Saraki’s leadership when thugs took control and were often on rampage across the state. It is naive for Saraki to think that a volte face by the characterless Saheed Popoola or his ilk will upturn the well-documented verdict of history on how he enabled the armed robbers,” Babatunde said.

He urged residents of Kwara, particularly those in Offa and Kwara South, to consider the importance of integrity and public trust in choosing their representatives.

The party also expressed confidence in Offa’s continued support for the APC, describing the community as historically progressive and politically conscious.

“Offa had played a significant role in the emergence of the APC-led government in Kwara State and would not abandon the party because of political campaigns or visits by influential personalities,” he added.

Corroborating, the APC Deputy Chairman, Alhaji Abdullahi Samari, described the development as unfortunate and inhuman, noting that the victims left behind children, wives, parents and other family members who were still living with the consequences of the tragedy.

“I think it is rather inhuman and disturbing that an experienced politician who is looking for votes can play with people’s lives as it is now. The 33 people who lost their lives still have family members living. Some of them have children, wives and parents. How would they feel with this kind of statement coming around this time?”

“That statement was carelessly made. Only God knows what some other people will be thinking at this time. It is rather unfortunate. We should not use everything in politics to make sure that we cause havoc to our people,” Samari added.

He noted that the robbery case had already been determined by a competent court and that attempts to introduce alternative narratives would not change the judgment.

Samari asked security forces to charge Popoola for the reckless statement against a case already decided by court.

“As a party, we think we need to address it. A judgment has already been given. The storytelling is immaterial, but I think it is being said to make sure they provoke people,” he said.

World.title: Gbajabiamila: Nigeria Must Deliberately Invest in Next Generation of Leaders
World.content:
* More than 80 LMI graduates serving in State House, National Assembly, ministries, agencies

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, has called for deliberate investment in young Nigerians, declaring that the country’s democratic future and institutional development depend largely on preparing a new generation of competent, ethical and committed leaders.

Gbajabiamila, who is also the founder of the Legislative Mentorship Initiative (LMI), said young Nigerians must be equipped with the knowledge, character, practical experience and institutional exposure required to contribute meaningfully to governance rather than wait until they occupy positions of authority before learning the responsibilities of leadership.

He spoke Monday in Abuja at the opening ceremony of the fifth cohort of the LMI Fellowship Programme, where he disclosed that the initiative had received more than 7,000 applications for the latest edition, from which 50 fellows-in-training were selected through a competitive process.

The former Speaker of the House of Representatives explained that the initiative, established in 2022 to mark his 60th birthday, was conceived to bridge the gap between the enthusiasm and leadership potential of young Nigerians and their limited access to practical knowledge of public institutions.

According to him, his over three decades of experience in public service, including his successive positions as Minority Leader in the 7th House of Representatives, Majority Leader in the 8th House and Speaker of the 9th House, exposed him to the need to deliberately prepare young people for leadership.

He said: “When we started LMI in 2022, our ambition was clear. We wanted to build a community of intentional, well-trained young leaders whose ideas, integrity and courage would strengthen public institutions and contribute to the future of our country and our continent.

“Throughout my journey of national service, I encountered many young Nigerians with intelligence, energy, ambition and a genuine desire to serve. They had ideas. They had the capacity. They had the desire. What was often missing was access to practical training, experienced guidance and the opportunity to understand how public institutions work.”

Gbajabiamila stressed that young people should not be compelled to wait until they attain positions of authority before acquiring the knowledge and exposure necessary to discharge public responsibilities effectively.

He added that providing young Nigerians with access to governance institutions should be regarded as an investment in democracy and national development rather than an act of political favour.

“A young person who understands how a bill becomes law, how a budget is considered, how public policy is developed and how a constituency is served, is not a threat to those institutions. That young person is an asset to our nation,” he stated.

The founder disclosed that the LMI had evolved from a fellowship programme into a growing institutional platform, with more than 80 of its previous fellows currently serving across the state House, National Assembly, federal and state ministries, departments and agencies, state legislatures and the Conference of Speakers and Presidents of African Legislatures (CoSPAL) Secretariat.

He added that some graduates had also secured international volunteer placements in other African countries through the Nigerian Technical Aid Corps.

According to him, the programme’s first four cohorts had trained and graduated 218 fellows, while the completion of the fifth cohort would increase the number to 268.

He explained that the placements were deliberately incorporated into the programme to ensure that participants did not merely acquire theoretical knowledge but also gained practical experience in the workings of government institutions.

Gbajabiamila maintained that the ultimate success of the initiative would not be measured by the number of certificates issued or the identity attached to its graduates, popularly known as the ‘Gbaja Fellows,’ but by the quality, integrity and impact of the public service they would render.

He said: “The legacy of LMI will not be defined by the number of certificates issued or because they are called Gbaja Fellows. It will be defined by the unique quality, integrity and impact of the public service they shall render.”

The Chief of Staff also commended the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, for sustaining and strengthening the initiative despite the change in leadership of the lower legislative chamber.

He described Abbas as a confident and exceptional leader who had chosen to build on the achievements of his predecessors rather than discontinue programmes established by previous occupants of the office.

“In some cases, when one principal leaves office, the next often tries to erase his achievements, but a confident leader takes those achievements and actually builds on them.

“And I dare say Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, Speaker of the House of Representatives, is not only a confident leader but a great one; and a man I call an ally, a brother and someone who has played the role of a father to the fellows of the Legislative Mentorship Initiative,” he said.

He also acknowledged the contributions of the LMI Planning and Advisory Committee, its management and operations team, the selection committee and institutional partners, including TAF Africa, the Leadership Advancement Foundation, Nigerian Technical Aid Corps, Bank of Industry, UN Women, United Nations Development Programme, Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung and Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung.

Gbajabiamila urged the 50 fellows selected for the fifth cohort to approach the three-week intensive programme with seriousness, discipline, curiosity and an open mind.

He challenged them to learn, unlearn and grow, stressing that their selection from thousands of applicants should make them more conscious of the responsibilities attached to the opportunity.

He further urged them to respect institutional procedures, demonstrate humility and recognise that becoming an effective leader also required the ability to work responsibly within a team and follow established leadership structures.

“An important part of becoming a good leader is learning to be a responsible team member and, when required, also a good follower,” he said.

The founder also charged the fellows to extend the benefits of the mentorship programme to other young Nigerians by sharing their knowledge, mentoring those coming behind them and creating opportunities for others.

In his remarks, the Secretary-General of CoSPAL and Chairman of the LMI Planning and Advisory Committee, Ambassador ‘Dapo Oyewole, disclosed that the fifth cohort attracted more than 24,000 expressions of interest, with over 7,000 completed applications received before 50 candidates were selected.

Oyewole described the initiative as a growing institution that had moved beyond leadership training to provide practical opportunities for young Nigerians to participate in governance and public service.

He said the programme had so far trained and graduated 218 fellows, adding that the number would rise to 268 following the completion of the fifth cohort.

According to him, more than 80 fellows are already serving in different government institutions, while the initiative is working towards evolving from a charitable vision into a sustainable institution with stronger systems, partnerships and financial capacity.

He said: “Preparation must lead to participation. That was the underlying philosophy espoused by our Founder, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila.”

Oyewole explained that the initiative was designed not merely to produce graduates with impressive certificates but to develop a pipeline of capable, ethical and service-minded Nigerians who understand how public institutions function and are prepared to strengthen them.

He identified the five guiding principles of the initiative as Decency, Diligence, Discipline, Democracy and Dialogue, urging the new fellows to embody the values throughout their careers.

Also speaking, the Director of LMI and Deputy Chief of Staff, CoSPAL, Mrs. Solape Sonuga, said the programme was established on the conviction that the future of democracy and the quality of public institutions depended significantly on the calibre of people prepared to lead them.

Sonuga said the 50 fellows selected for the fifth cohort emerged from a rigorous process involving more than 7,000 completed applications out of over 24,000 expressions of interest.

She urged the participants to look beyond the prestige of being selected and recognise that the fellowship represented a responsibility to contribute to governance and national development.

“Do not confuse proximity to power with preparedness for leadership. Being in the room is an opportunity. Knowing what to do when you get there is the real work,” she said.

She challenged the fellows to use the three-week programme to understand the processes of government, interrogate public policy and develop the capacity to contribute meaningfully to institutional reforms.

Sonuga also thanked Gbajabiamila for his continued investment in young Nigerians and acknowledged the institutional support provided by CoSPAL, its leadership, partners, mentors, faculty and programme management team.

The LMI was established in 2022 to identify, train, mentor and provide practical institutional exposure for young Nigerians interested in public-sector leadership, legislative processes, governance and nation-building.

World.title: ‘He said I must protect him’: Matlala drops Sibiya bombshell at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
PRETORIA - Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala has accused former police deputy national commissioner for crime detection Shadrack Sibiya of coercing him to lie to Parliament.

Testifying before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on Monday, Matlala alleged that Sibiya did this through his lawyer

He claimed that Advocate Bronwynne Forbay would call Sibiya during breaks at the Ad Hoc Committee sittings and hand Matlala the phone.

READ | LIVE | Madlanga rejects Section 204 submission presented by Matlala's lawyer

He further told the commission that his wife, Tsakane Matlala, told him that Sibiya repeatedly contacted her from a private number, threatening that Matlala should not reveal anything about him at the Ad Hoc Committee.

Some of those threats, he said, were directed at his life and the safety of his family.

World.title: 36 years in igloo homes: Mdantsane residents fed up with broken promises
World.content:
MDANTSANE - For over 36 years, a community in Mdantsane has lived in igloo-shaped homes made of fiberglass.

Originally provided as temporary shelters, the domes now harbour fungus, posing a health threat to children and the elderly.

Some families are crammed with 12 people in a single room, living like sardines in a can.

READ | Bronkhorstspruit residents still waiting for clean water

They say politicians often show up just before elections to canvass for votes, but their living conditions never change.

"We’ve been voting all the time, and then after we’ve cast our votes, nothing changes. Politicians only come here because it suits their campaigns; it makes them look good. Because they use our situation as a promise to bring positive change."

These Nkomponi residents have had enough. They don't care who's elected into power anymore.

All they want is to be treated like human beings and provided with suitable homes.

eNCA's Ronald Masinda filed this story.

World.title: Police probe two brutal murders after bodies found in abandoned buildings
World.content:
THEUNISSEN - Police in the Free State have launched a manhunt for suspect(s) after two women were found murdered and their bodies discovered in separate abandoned buildings in Theunissen over the past weekend.

According to Free State police spokesperson Thabo Covane, the first murder incident was discovered on 7 November.

On the day, at around 03:40 am, members of the Neighbourhood Watch directed police to an abandoned building where they discovered the lifeless body of a woman.

READ | WC Anti-Gang Unit probes triple murder in Grassy Park

Covane said preliminary investigations confirmed that the 35-year-old woman had sustained multiple stab wounds.

“The victim was discovered half-naked with multiple injuries to the head and stomach. The victim was declared deceased on the scene by Emergency Medical Services personnel.

“Police are not ruling out the possibility that the victim may have been sexually violated,” he said.

According to Covan, on 8 November police attended a crime scene of a 25-year-old woman whose body was found in a decomposed state.

READ | Jabulile Ntimba murder: Suspects back in dock

“According to the report, children were playing at an abandoned building near the Day Care Centre in Masilo, Theunissen. The children were exposed to a horrific scene when they discovered the body of a half-naked woman inside a toilet with serious head injuries,” Covane said.

He said no arrests have been made in either case, but a multidisciplinary task team has been established to probe the murders.

World.title: Witness breaks down at tribunal against Eastern Cape judge accused of racial slur
World.content:
EAST LONDON - The Judicial Conduct Tribunal opened its investigation into allegations of gross misconduct against Eastern Cape High Court Judge Belinda Hartle on Monday.

Hartle is accused of using racist and derogatory language towards court employee Thozamile Semekazi in May last year, after reportedly growing frustrated with court file delivery delays.

Semekazi grew emotional while recounting the events of that day.

READ | High Court grants Selby Mbenenge impeachment interdict

In a report by Judges Matter, Semekazi complained that the events of the day constituted "humiliating and demeaning conduct", which caused him to "suffer a major depressive disorder and resulted in his being admitted to hospital for treatment".

The report further revealed that Judge Hartle’s stated that she used only one swear word, and that it was not directed at Semekazi, and accused him of grossly misrepresenting the interaction between them. Judge Hartle disputes ever using a racist word,

World.title: Carrim denies smuggling vehicles
World.content:
MUSINA - Suliman Carrim has denied any involvement in the car-smuggling plot.

Through his affidavit in court on Monday, Carrim claimed he was hospitalised when the alleged crime took place.

Carrim appeared in the Musina Magistrates' Court on charges of cross-border vehicle smuggling.

The state, which is opposing bail claim that Carrim allegedly instructed two employees to smuggle vehicles into Malawi, bypassing the bank's clearance by claiming his upcoming Madlanga Commission appearance blocked the paperwork.

READ | Suliman Carrim back in court over alleged vehicle smuggling

Carrim tried to distance himself from his co-accused.

But prosecutors said WhatsApp messages show frequent communication between them, as well as evidence that Carrim paid for the co-accused' rental accommodation.

The state also revealed the co-accused were working illegally on visitor permits, and that Carrim knowingly ran an unlawful operation.

Carrim has been remanded in custody until 16 November, when he'll find out his fate.

World.title: Former top cop's fraud and corruption trial postponed
World.content:
PRETORIA - The R54-million SAPS software corruption trial against former acting National Police Commissioner Khomotso Phahlane and his five co-accused has been postponed to12 November.

The accused appeared at the High Court in Pretoria, where the State requested a postponement to amend the charges they face.

READ | IDAC withdraws blue light tender case against Phahlane

The case involves two SAPS contracts worth approximately R54 million.

The State alleges that the procurement processes for the police monitoring software systems were manipulated.

The irregularities allegedly took place during Phahlane's tenure as acting National Police Commissioner.

World.content:
Hlungwani says the lack of medical aid is a major concern, particularly when workers seek medical attention.

“It is the reason we are demanding medical aid, because when we come with a certificate from the clinic, the employer does not recognise it,” he says.
