In December, Pillen said the state "won't be adding workforce" to implement the work requirements, a decision those advocates have criticized. Pillen in July also instituted a government-wide hiring freeze.

Nebraska listed at least half a dozen contractors costing more than $250,000 each, including one person whose compensation exceeds $1.8 million, the documents show. Nebraska submitted the records to federal Medicaid regulators as part of a routine process to secure federal money. Powell said the funding requests "may not reflect actual expenditures."

Sarah Maresh, a program director with the social justice advocacy nonprofit Nebraska Appleseed, said the amounts were "shocking."

"When you put in complicated policies like this, there are large corporations making money behind the scenes," Maresh said. "This just further confirms that it's happening in Nebraska quietly."

Confusion and longer wait times

The Medicaid work requirements in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and other changes shepherded by Republicans will curtail insurance gains that came from the Affordable Care Act, also known as Obamacare. The GOP tax and spending law, which the Congressional Budget Office estimated would reduce federal Medicaid spending by more than $900 billion over a decade, adds reporting requirements and restrictions that make it harder for people to stay enrolled.

Sponsor Message

As of early July, most denials related to the work requirements among Nebraska adults applying for Medicaid were due to unsubmitted paperwork, according to internal documents from Nebraska's health department that KFF Health News obtained through a public records request. The state wrote this was "expected."

State data shows that average wait times at a Nebraska health department call center nearly doubled between May and July, going from about 13 minutes to 26 minutes, before declining in August. In interviews, advocates for Medicaid enrollees said they've encountered people who have waited on the phone for hours.

Nebraska received more than 101,000 calls in August, a 66% jump from May.

"If people are working, they just don't have time to be sitting on the phone to go through all of this stuff," said Kenny McMorris, CEO of the Charles Drew Health Center, a federally qualified health center in North Omaha. He said roughly half of Charles Drew's 13,385 patients are on Medicaid, and of those, 42% are subject to the work requirements.

"You can leverage the technology, but you still got to have people there to help," McMorris said.

Then there are experiences the official data may not catch, like what happened to McCreary — saddled with figuring out what happened with his Medicaid benefits amid a health crisis, and whether it was even true that he had to work to keep them.

McCreary had heard about the Medicaid work requirements but didn't know they might apply to him. Powell confirmed McCreary was eligible for Medicaid because of the ACA — putting him in the population subject to work requirements.

His ordeal underscores the fallout from being caught in confusing government systems and silos that aren't obvious to the public.

"This cancer ain't going to stop just because I ain't got insurance," he said. "It's going to keep working on me."

When he received the call from the hospital about his coverage, "I was really in despair," McCreary said. Eventually, he said, he called for help.

Sponsor Message

Nebraska's health department runs AccessNebraska, a call center for help with safety net benefits such as Medicaid and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, commonly known as food stamps. But the number McCreary recalls dialing ended up not being AccessNebraska — it was for a different call center, one for SNAP accounts that Nebraska outsources to a private company. Powell said the state has no record of McCreary calling the health department.

McCreary said the worker didn't have a good explanation for why the Medicaid work requirements would apply to him. Before his health deteriorated, McCreary worked as a driver for an asphalt services company. He said he worked "until I couldn't do the job anymore."

"I really had hoped to work longer," he said. "I kind of enjoyed that job."

Attorneys and policy professionals who work with people on Medicaid and other public benefit programs said that McCreary's substance use treatment, lasting four months starting in November 2025, and other health conditions should have exempted him.

The federal law outlines categories of exemptions, such as being too sick to work. People who are considered too ill include those who have a serious medical condition or a substance use disorder.

Nebraska's health department said it sent tens of thousands of letters, text messages and emails to inform enrollees about the new requirements. According to state documents, Nebraska said it would "implement enhancements" to its computer system and online portal, including allowing people to submit documents online and having "clear, plain-language" enrollee notices. McCreary, however, doesn't have an account on Nebraska Medicaid's online portal, preferring to handle things over the phone or in person.

He also said it's possible he missed letters from Nebraska Medicaid about his coverage.

"I don't know if it's my fault or not," McCreary said.

toggle caption i Chris Machian/KFF Health News

The Cornhusker State's experience could be a harbinger of things to come. Next year, work requirements will apply to millions of adult Medicaid enrollees in more than 40 states.

Sponsor Message

The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office has estimated the policy will lead to 5.3 million more people being uninsured in the U.S. by 2034.

"We definitely had fun"

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act's Medicaid changes are the most complicated in years — changes that government benefit experts say will strain and exacerbate long-standing problems with state technology systems for health benefits.

"It's already a shaky system, and now you've added more burdens on top of that," said Gelila Selassie, director of health advocacy for the nonprofit Justice in Aging.

Nebraska and federal officials, as well as consultants advising the state, detailed the difficulties and successes with the state's May 1 launch during an August panel discussion at a national conference in Oregon.

"They said, 'We're going to go live May 1.' To which CMS said, 'Oh, my God!'" Brent Weaver, an official who specializes in Medicaid IT at the U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, said about Nebraska.

Nebraska officials knew "they weren't as agile as they probably would have liked to have been," Weaver said, "but they didn't let that stop them."

"If they fail, we looked at it as a failure," he added in comments that broadly praised the state's approach.

CMS did not answer questions from KFF Health News about Nebraska's rollout and Weaver's remarks.

In Nebraska, a group of 60 people held hours-long meetings three days a week that were "very exhausting," Michaux, of Public Consulting Group, said during a different session at the conference.

"Our calendars were cleared, and that was the focus," Michaux said.

Because CMS had not yet issued regulations outlining key details such as how people could get exemptions — it would do so June 1 — Nebraska officials said they had to rely on the law's broad language to make initial decisions.

"We had to get comfortable being uncomfortable," Jacob Kawamoto, a deputy director at Nebraska's Medicaid division, said at the conference.

Sponsor Message

Public Consulting Group said it worked with the state to develop new guidance and "process guides" — materials for Nebraska eligibility workers with instructions on how to process Medicaid applications or renewals. Training materials for Nebraska caseworkers reviewed by KFF Health News refer to those guides.

"The training was very robust, and the process guides were very robust," Michaux said.

Maresh disagreed with that characterization. "There are gaps" in the state's training materials, she said, and caseworkers "are confused" about work requirements.

Public Consulting Group also helped the state institute changes to Nebraska's Medicaid IT system, according to the company. "We are preparing for future updates and enhancements," Michaux said.

In response to questions, Public Consulting Group spokesperson Alyssa Brown said the company "has supported Nebraska Medicaid via a broad range of consulting services since 2019, including work on federal and state compliance initiatives." She said Michaux "discussed" the process guides at the conference but Nebraska developed them. Similarly, Brown said the company did not develop training.

Federal taxpayers will largely bear the costs of implementing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's Medicaid policies in Nebraska and elsewhere. Congress allocated $200 million in one-time funding to states. Under federal regulations, the U.S. government picks up most of the tab for state IT system changes, paying as much as 90% of the cost.

"Even though it was not so easy," Michaux said at the conference, "we definitely had fun standing up the Medicaid work requirement program."

Public Consulting Group's employees, Brown told KFF Health News, are "passionate about public service and helping our clients improve the lives of the people they serve."

Dropping Medicaid enrollment

As of August, roughly 1,100 Nebraskans had been denied benefits because of Medicaid work requirements. Most denials were because people did not respond to requests for information.

Nebraska's total Medicaid enrollment has declined by roughly 4,600 people since May, a drop of 1.4%, according to an August report.

Sponsor Message

As for McCreary, the Nebraska health department's Powell maintained he experienced "no lapses in coverage" and said he was disenrolled from Medicaid after turning 65. Despite what McCreary said he was told, Powell said Medicaid work requirements weren't the reason: He aged out of Medicaid and into Medicare before they could be applied to him.

Selassie, from the nonprofit Justice in Aging, said McCreary's care shouldn't have been disrupted.

McCreary is now enrolled in Medicare, and Medicaid covers some of his health costs. He was able to reschedule his canceled appointments.

"The cancer has grown so much," he said.

He had surgery in early November to remove his right kidney.

KFF Health News correspondent Samantha Liss contributed to this report.

KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF — the independent source for health policy research, polling, and journalism.

World.title: Ford says protesters against changes to Ontario’s student aid program should be 'thanking the government'
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Premier Doug Ford pushed back against last week's post-secondary protests over OSAP grant cuts, saying students should be 'thanking the government' for investing in education, and instead 'focus on getting a job of the future.'

Ontario Premier Doug Ford called students who protested Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP) changes and tuition hikes "naive" on Monday — likening them to "sheep" who blindly follow what "looney tunes" post on social media.

Ford was speaking at an unrelated news conference Monday morning when he was asked about last week's "Hands Off Our Education!" campaign protests, which took place on several campuses across Ontario, including York University, the University of Guelph, Trent University and University of Windsor.

"These kids are so naive," he said. "They should be … thanking the government for just investing."

The protests come after the province lifted a seven-year tuition freeze earlier in the year, which allowed universities and colleges to increase fees by up to two per cent each year over the next three years.

Ford's government has also been under fire after announcing changes to OSAP in February, citing "unsustainable" costs.

Students attend a rally calling for an end to cuts to the Ontario Student Assistance Program outside Queen's Park back in March. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

Changes to the student assistance program meant non-repayable grants were reduced from a maximum of 85 per cent to 25 per cent, while the percentage of funds given as loans increased. Many students have said scaled-back OSAP grants will saddle them with high debt loads amid economic uncertainty.

On Monday, Ford went on to say the post-secondary students should be focused on "getting a job of the future," in fields like STEM and health care.

"They read the social media and half the people on social media [are] a bunch of looney tunes," he said. "They all run out like sheep.

"Give your head a shake, kids."

Students 'dissatisfied': federation

Cyrielle Ngeleka, chair of the Canadian Federation of Students (CFS) Ontario, said Monday that although Ford's comments don't come as a surprise, it is concerning that students have been met with insults, rather than solutions.

"Students have made their demands abundantly clear with what they want to see with education. We are completely dissatisfied with what we're seeing," she said. "For the government to keep making very dehumanizing comments about students is a clear indicator that [it] doesn't care about students and never did."

Ngeleka said while students welcome any new and increased funding, thus far it has failed to adequately meet their needs.

"They seem to want to prioritize the given sector and want to create a divide between programs when at the end of the day, everyone should be entitled to study whatever it is that they want," she said. "The government is ultimately leading students to ruins."

WATCH | Post-secondary students across Ontario walk out: 'Hands off our OSAP': Post-secondary students across Ontario walk out | Duration closed caption 2:29 University and college across Ontario students walked out of class Thursday to protest the province's cuts to OSAP. Meanwhile, Ontario has defended the changes, citing a $6.4-billion fund rolling out over the next four years that Minister Nolan Quinn claims will keep universities resilient to growing demands in the future.

Instead of walking out, students should remain in class, Ford said, adding Canada has "incredible students."

"The ones that study, you're going to be successful because the number one thing you need when you leave university or college is a good paying job," he said. "We have the brightest students in the world as far as I'm concerned."

But cost-of-living pressures threaten students' ability to stay in school, Ngeleka says.

"It's making it really hard to be a student on a day-to-day basis," she said. "How are students supposed to stay in class when students are going to class hungry, students are going class tired and students are going to class broke?"

Ngeleka said the provincial government gravely misunderstands the reality of students' lives.

"It's clear that this government is all over the place," she said. "They will say anything and everything except actually meet the demands of students."

Opposition parties support protesting students

In a statement Monday, NDP Leader Marit Stiles called Ford's comments "ridiculous."

"Give your head a shake, Doug," she said. "I've met these students. They're working extra jobs just to stay in school, and now they're staring down a lifetime of debt because he slashed their grants and lifted the tuition freeze. "

"The Premier needs to look past the silver spoon in his mouth and recognize the chaos he has unleashed on people’s lives," Stiles added. "Doug Ford was born on third base, and is telling our students to 'just a hit triple.'"

World.title: U.S. House Republican moves to force vote on impeaching Pete Hegseth
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie moved Monday to force a vote to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, putting pressure on his fellow Republicans to decide whether to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses.

The impeachment resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran. It also includes references to Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.

Hegseth said earlier Monday he's eager to litigate the military actions that he and U.S. President Donald Trump have taken against Iran, Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela's previous leaders.

"If you want to take issue with what we did in Epic Fury or Rough Rider or nabbing Nicolás Maduro, you're taking issue with the troops and what they accomplished, which is historic," Hegseth told reporters Monday, using the military code names for the Iran war and campaign of strikes to halt the Houthis' attacks on shipping in the Middle East.

Hegseth also announced that he would hold a rare news conference on Tuesday — his first in more than 180 days — on the impeachment threat. His last briefing was in May, and he has not held one on the Iran war, strikes on alleged drug-trafficking boats or other U.S. military actions since then.

The Pentagon chief is bearing the brunt of anger and calls for his ouster after the Iran war and its economic impact contributed to severe Republican losses in the midterm elections that cost the party control of Congress. Massie pushed forward an impeachment resolution over the objections of House Republican leadership as momentum grows to hold Hegseth accountable for the conflict.

WATCH | Massie speaks about Hegseth's actions: Republican congressman speaks about his effort to impeach Pete Hegseth LIVE Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky speaks to reporters after filing a resolution in the House to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. The impeachment resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.

Hegseth waves off impeachment push as 'noise'

Hegseth, after giving a speech at the Naval War College in Rhode Island, brushed aside the possible impeachment push.

"There's a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success," he told reporters. He added that "if we want to litigate" the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, "I'm happy to do it all day long."

"My team, we're not worried about the noise — it's what I told the troops, too — don't worry about the noise," he said.

Asked about U.S. Vice-President JD Vance blaming the Iran war for the massive Republican losses in the election, Hegseth noted that Trump said he would do it again, and "I agree."

He largely repeated a line that Secretary of State Marco Rubio said to reporters a day earlier: "It doesn't have to be necessarily popular, but it can be necessary."

Hegseth argued that the war was necessary because "someone had to confront the Iranian regime's pursuit of a nuclear weapon" and said "the choice was don't act and wish it away or take a bold move."

Hegseth gave a State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico, Sept. 30, but has not held a media availablity since May. (Alex Wong/Pool/The Associated Press)

Iran has long maintained that its nuclear program is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kilograms of uranium that is enriched up to 60 per cent purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90 per cent.

Trump defended Hegseth to reporters on Sunday night.

"He's guilty of two things, basically winning two wars," Trump said. "I believe we saved the Middle East and Israel combined. And it's awfully hard to say let's impeach somebody who did that."

WATCH | Trump defends Hegseth: Trump defends Hegseth as Democrats prepare for political war | Duration closed caption 2:19 U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed calls for Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's resignation, despite more Republicans blaming the Iran war for their massive midterm losses. Meanwhile, Democrats are gearing up to flex their new power after taking both houses of Congress.

Hegseth insists 'Iran is devastated'

Hegseth reiterated that "Iran is devastated," even though the Islamic Republic has been able to keep striking military bases in the Middle East that are used by the United States, causing billions of dollars in damage, as well as commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Disruptions to shipping in the waterway, where one-fifth of the world's oil passed before the war, have led to higher energy prices that hit voters' pocketbooks.

He said the next steps on the war are up to Trump, including telling Iran: "Hey, we're done, and we're going to watch your nuclear material. You better not move it."

With anger in Congress rising, Hegseth has been on a social media blitz, posting a video last week acknowledging the threat of impeachment. He said it would be "all about the politics of personal destruction" and insisted that "won't work with me. You can rest assured of that."

Since then, scores of political appointees within the Pentagon have posted images of Hegseth emblazoned with the words, "Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic." The White House also posted a video to social media that featured praise from Trump.

World.title: Payments Canada launches long-delayed instant payments system
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Payments Canada says it has launched its real-time rail national payment system, which is expected to speed day-to-day payments for Canadian businesses and consumers.

It says the new system is expected to enable participating members to exchange, clear and settle payments securely in real time.

"The launch of Canada's real-time rail marks the beginning of a new era for payments in our country," Payments Canada CEO Susan Hawkins said in a news release Monday.

"As a national asset that's designed specifically for our country, the [real-time rail] gives the payment ecosystem a modern foundation to build on."

The system is expected to generate savings from lower processing costs, reduced use of cash and cheques and a shorter period during which funds are temporarily unavailable to the recipient.

The initial participants include Wealthsimple, Questbank, Peoples Trust Co., Paramount Commerce, Koho, DoBusiness.com, Digital Commerce Bank and Bank of America. Additional participants are expected to be added in the coming months, including all of the major Canadian financial institutions.

WATCH | How bank scams are different outside of Canada: Marketplace investigates global bank scam industry | Duration 1:47 Canadians who are scammed aren't likely to get their money back; banks have no obligation to reimburse clients. But in Britain, it's a different story. CBC's Marketplace travelled to the U.K. to see how that difference has banks taking action against scams.

Transactions that pass through Payments Canada systems include debit card payments, pre-authorized debits, direct deposits, bill payments, wire payments and cheques.

Henry Kim, a professor at York University's Schulich School of Business, said the announcement is a step in the right direction.

"There's a thread that we have to do this for our sovereignty, and we just have to keep up with the rest of the world. A lot of the world has real-time settlement," he said in an interview, adding it already exists in the U.S.

Payments Canada has been years behind schedule on getting real-time rail in place, which allows near-instant payments clearing 24 hours a day, along with other improvements. The organization originally aimed to have the system in place by 2019.

The ability to more rapidly clear payments is particularly helpful for businesses, Kim said

"It also means that if you're tight for cash, if you're a business and your working capital runs low, you can get paid much faster by other businesses," he said.

Payments Canada said the real-time rail system will also come with mandatory centralized fraud services and controls, including confirmation of payee, a fraud transaction safety score, a list of fraud risks and a platform for fraud reporting.

Kim, who works with U.S. credit unions on payment technology, said there are some concerns among U.S. financial institutions about fraud-related risks from real-time payments, with some U.S. banks electing not to provide the feature to customers.

"Because when you get rid of that lag, there's less time for verification so someone could actually make a fraudulent transaction. And with the real-time rail, oftentimes you don't get that back," he said.

"Canada's actually done something different from the U.S., and I think it's actually really good to have that centralized."

World.title: $276 for hair ties? Skims offers advent calendar refunds after online backlash
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The contents of the Skims 2026 accessories advent calendar have been described as what you might find in the bottom of your purse, on the floor of a car, or behind your dresser when you pull it away from the wall.

After intense customer backlash, Kim Kardashian's apparel brand is offering refunds to anyone who purchased the calendar. The package costs $276 Cdn (or $148 US — a relative premium), is advertised as "12 fun days of surprises" and contains an assortment of hair ties, bobby pins and key chains.

Viral unboxing videos posted over the weekend by disappointed customers have called the pricey calendar "a mess" and a scam.

"Are we serious right now?" exclaimed influencer Kayla Ryan as she opened the package for Day 4 to reveal three pink bobby pins. She called it "the worst advent calendar I have ever seen" in her Saturday video which accrued more than 20 million views as of Monday morning.

" I’m hoping this is a prank and the last one is a $150 gift card for all my money back," she added, after opening Day 9 to reveal an ornamental keychain comb that can't actually comb hair.

"This is the last one and it better be made of gold," another content creator says in a TikTok video with nearly 65 million views before opening Day 12 to reveal a furry compact mirror on a key chain and then grimacing.

"So, basically, everything that falls between my car seats," one person commented on the video; another described it as "wild for maybe $20 worth of stuff."

A composite of three screen grabs from TikTok unboxing videos for the new 2026 Skims advent calendar by, from left, @wetsloppyswollen, Brittany Shaw, and influencer Kayla Ryan. (@wetsloppyswollen/TikTok, @kaylaryan/TikTok, @brittanyshaw2.0/TikTok)

In statements provided to multiple media outlets, a Skims spokesperson said the company was " aware of the feedback" about the advent calendar and acknowledged that "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations."

The company told told Page Six they "personally contacted every customer who purchased the calendar" and offered either a full refund or credit towards their other products.

CBC News reached out to Skims for further comment but has not received a reply.

WATCH | Chanel dragged for $1,025 advent calendar: Chanel advent calendar lambasted on social media | Duration 2:07 Chanel’s limited edition advent calendar, priced at $1,025, has become the subject of backlash online after it left some consumers unimpressed. Strategists say it could serve as a reminder of how to market to a Gen Z audience.

'Disappointed they got what they paid for'

This is far from the first advent calendar controversy. In 2021, Chanel was roasted online for a $1,025 calendar full of stickers, a magnet, a keychain and other miscellaneous branded items in addition to a miniature lipstick, hand cream and small bottle of perfume.

A year later, Dior was slammed for a nearly $5,000 advent calendar that mostly contained candle accessories and scented soaps in addition to small bottles of perfume.

Some commentators have criticized high-end advent calendars for being little more than luxury status symbols driven by the unboxing craze. Last year, for instance, Dior sold an $11,000 calendar. In 2019, Tiffany & Co. released a limited advent calendar that contained 24 pieces of jewelry and cost $158,000.

The Skims advent calendar is currently sold out with a waitlist. Some people have noted, the product description online details exactly what can be found in the calendar each day: a bear keychain, hair elastics, scrunchies, bobby pins, a squishie, bra elastic hairbands, more bobby pins, a comb keychain, a logo keychain, more scrunchies and a faux fur compact mirror keychain.

"W hile I agree the contents are ridiculously overpriced, we need to have a conversation about personal accountability as consumers," one person wrote on Threads.

LISTEN | Extravagant advent calendars: Radio Noon Manitoba 18:11 Extravagant Advent Calendars and the Evolution of Adult Holiday Traditions Rob Warren, marketing professor at the University of North Dakota, speaks with host Marjorie Dowhos about the rise of high-end advent calendars for adults and why retailers are capitalizing on childhood nostalgia.

" If the contents were disclosed, you ignored the description, spent $148 [US], and then acted completely blindsided by what you received, some of that responsibility belongs to YOU."

A Toronto influencer who goes by the name Glamzilla online defended the advent calendar in a TikTok video, where she argued it's about the experience of opening something leading up to the holidays rather than a "big gift."

She was dragged in the video's comments, with some accusing of "gaslighting" and being insensitive to the price.

World.title: Top U.S. hedge fund executive named CEO of Canada's new sovereign wealth fund
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A top executive at one of the world's largest hedge funds is leaving her job in the U.S. to become the CEO of one of the Carney government's hallmark projects.

On Monday, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) announced that Karen Karniol-Tambour will become the CEO of Canada's nascent sovereign wealth fund.

A news release from the PMO said Karniol-Tambour has Canadian citizenship, though public records indicate she was born in Israel and has spent her professional career in the United States.

Her LinkedIn page says she has been at Bridgewater Associates for more than 20 years and rose to be co-chief investment officer. She graduated from Princeton University in 2006.

The financial magazine Barron's has named Karniol-Tambour in its list of the 100 most influential women in U.S. finance for the last seven years. She was also featured by Forbes.

At the helm of the new sovereign wealth fund, she will be tasked with identifying and investing in domestic projects with the goal of generating returns for investors and reinvesting them in new Canadian projects.

The federal government announced plans to create the fund, which it is calling the Canada Strong Fund, last spring. It has earmarked $25 billion in seed funding and committed to putting commercial asset revenue into the fund. Its goal is to finance "nation-building" projects while allowing Canadians to benefit from the returns.

The fund will also include a "retail" element for ordinary Canadians to be able to buy in directly. Last week's federal budget said those investments will take the form of notes similar to savings bonds, but details on when or how that will roll out haven't been announced.

"Under Ms. Karniol-Tambour’s leadership, the Canada Strong Fund will be professionally managed, operating at arm's length from the government, with its own board of directors," said the Prime Minister's Office.

"Together, the fund and its retail offering will create a new model of Canadian ownership, helping build national wealth while ensuring more Canadians share in the benefits of economic growth."

World.title: Like father, like son: Arnold Schwarzenegger’s son muscles into top 5 at bodybuilding competition
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

More than 60 years after Arnold Schwarzenegger first flexed his stuff on a bodybuilding stage, his youngest son is continuing the dynasty of muscle, scoring in the top five during his professional debut over the weekend.

Joseph Baena competed in the classic physique category at the INBA PNBA Pro/AM World Cup in California on Saturday.

The 29-year-old placed fifth and said in a video on Instagram that he was happy to have achieved his goal of cracking the top five.

"I'm extremely proud of myself," said Baena, who only started competing this year. "It was an incredible experience for my first show as a pro."

This was the third-ever show for Baena, son of bodybuilder-turned-actor-turned-politician Schwarzenegger and Mildred Baena.

Under a video Baena shared on Instagram of his posing routine at the competition, several commenters noted, "Like father, like son."

It’s perhaps no surprise that the son of a man who became famous for being impressively jacked is following in his footsteps. Schwarzenegger’s physique scored him the title of Mr. Universe five times at professional bodybuilding competitions in the 60s and 70s, and he remains one of the most enduring names associated with bodybuilding.

His 1977 docudrama, Pumping Iron, is credited with giving bodybuilding more exposure and having it treated more widely as a sport. High-profile roles for Schwarzenegger in Hollywood action films like Conan the Barbarian (1982) and The Terminator franchise further pushed muscle into the mainstream.

Arnold Schwarzenegger poses alongside dancers from the famous Parisian cabaret Le Paradis Latin on May 20, 1977, during the Cannes Film Festival in southern France. Schwarzenegger was there to present the docudrama Pumping Iron. (Raph Gatti/ AFP via Getty Images)

In his video reflecting on the competition, Baena said that bodybuilding was a solo sport where "it all comes down to your own discipline," but noted that he had a lot of support from family and friends.

"My father always says there's no such thing as a 'self-made man.' I have people in my corner," he said.

Baena called Schwarzenegger "the best training partner," in an interview with GQ earlier this year, saying his father makes sure he doesn’t "slack off in the gym."

He added that his father gave him "the bodybuilding encyclopedia" when he was in college, and that it sparked his interest in the sport.

World.title: Honda Canada announces plans to retool Alliston, Ont., plant for hybrid production
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Honda Canada says it will retool its manufacturing facilities in Alliston, Ont., to expand production of hybrid-electric and gasoline-powered vehicles.

The Japanese automaker announced Monday it is partnering with the federal and provincial governments to fund plant upgrades, including the reintroduction of engine manufacturing, with an initial $166-million investment.

It said that funding is part of a broader $867-million commitment that will enhance quality, efficiency and manufacturing flexibility. Of that total, the federal government said it will provide $313 million, while the Ontario government is kicking in $156 million.

"This renewed investment reinforces Canada's critical role in Honda's North American growth and hybrid-electric vehicle strategy and helps position our operations for long-term competitiveness and future opportunities," said Honda Canada president and CEO Dave Jamieson in a news release.

The funding will ensure Honda can maintain its workforce of 4,000 Canadian employees across two facilities at the Alliston plant, while supporting its Canadian auto production volumes.

The company said it will also strengthen the Alliston plant's operations to help meet growing customer demand for hybrid-electric vehicles in North America.

"This investment will strengthen our automotive supply chains, support thousands of well-paying jobs in Ontario and across the country, and help build a strong Canadian auto sector where workers build the cars of the future," said Industry Minister Melanie Joly in a statement.

WATCH | Honda pauses $15B EV investment plan: Honda pauses $15B investment in Canadian EV plants | Duration closed caption 3:54 Japanese automaker Honda says it's pausing a $15-billion investment plan that would have seen four new electric vehicle factories built in Ontario. Honda says it's because of slow market growth in the EV sector due to Trump's trade war.

Honda previously paused plant development in Ontario

In May, Honda announced plans to introduce 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by 2030, with North America expected to be the primary market for many of those vehicles.

The automaker said it is investing across its manufacturing network in Canada, Ohio, Alabama and Georgia to support that strategy.

That same month, the company indefinitely suspended its plans for a $15-billion Canadian electric vehicle complex in response to dwindling demand.

Announced in 2024, Honda's EV project would have included a vehicle assembly plant as well as battery production facilities. It had said that new EV plant could create 1,000 incremental manufacturing jobs in Alliston.

It was set to receive upwards of $5 billion in federal and Ontario funding, however no money had yet been transferred.

The decision to pause those plans did not affect current employment or production levels at the Alliston plant.

More than 400,000 vehicles were produced at the site last year. Honda is Canada's second largest auto manufacturer by volume.

World.title: Canada's secretary of sport casts doubt on Russia competing as neutrals at Alberta world juniors
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Adam van Koeverden, Canada's Secretary of State for Sport, has cast doubt on whether Russia can compete as a neutral team at the upcoming world junior hockey championship in Alberta.

The development follows last month's Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling the International Ice Hockey Federation must reinstate Russia in international hockey, after Russia and Belarus were barred from international hockey competition in 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said last week Russian and Belarusian athletes could not compete in Canada representing their countries while the war continues. The government's Nov. 3 statement, however, allowed individual athletes to compete as neutrals but did not clarify whether that provision could extend to a Russian team at the men's under-20 tournament, which opens Dec. 26.

However, Van Koeverden clarified Monday the neutral athlete designation used for Russians at other events applied to individuals, not teams.

Van Koeverden's comments come after Norway's hockey federation said Sunday the IIHF had informed it that Russia would be added to the world juniors in Edmonton and Red Deer next month at Norway's expense.

"This is a really quickly evolving situation with Norway," van Koeverden said from a sports summit in Ottawa. "I've had conversations with ministers of sport from Finland, from Sweden, and from Norway and from Germany. Hoping to meet with the minister from Czechia this week as well as others to discuss this quickly evolving situation.

"The Prime Minister was extremely clear that sport will not be used for propaganda on Canadian soil, and the notion that there, you know, might be accommodations is one that the Prime Minister was extraordinarily clear about.

"So we'll continue to move forward working with Hockey Canada. And you note that the IIHF, their previous position was aligned with Canada's, and we want to continue to ensure that great Canadian hockey, great international hockey is seen here on Canadian soil."

The IIHF has not formally announced any changes to the world junior participants, and its website still lists Norway among the 10 teams in the tournament.

The Swedish Ice Hockey Association said Monday it was also informed of the new development, while adding it will maintain its stance of not competing against Russia.

Sweden feels deeply for Norwegian junior team

The Swedish association told The Canadian Press on Monday it sympathized with Norway, which qualified for the tournament but now risks losing its place.

"I feel deeply for Norway's national junior team, which qualified for the world juniors but now risks losing its place in the tournament. It is difficult to see this as anything other than unfair," said SIHA secretary general Tony Wirehn.

The Finnish Ice Hockey Association also reiterated Monday it would not play Russia if the war against Ukraine continues. It said it would not speculate further and would wait for the outcome.

Neither federation said whether it would play a Russian team competing under a neutral designation.

Norway said Sunday it still hoped to compete in the tournament.

“The situation is still unclear," Norway's hockey secretary general Peter Salsten said in a statement posted on the association's website and translated from Norwegian. "This makes us hope that the last word has not been said about our participation in Canada."

Hockey Canada referred The Canadian Press to the federal government's Nov. 3 statement and said it had nothing to add.

The IIHF and Russian Hockey Federation did not immediately respond to requests for comment Monday.

Individual Russian athletes who have competed at the Olympics since the war began have done so as neutrals.

Russian and Belarusian professional tennis players have continued to compete as individuals under neutral status on the ATP and WTA tours, including at the National Bank Open events in Toronto and Montreal.

World Aquatics barred Russian and Belarusian athletes from its events in 2022, then allowed them to return as neutrals the following year. In April, it lifted restrictions on senior athletes, allowing them to compete under their national flags and with their anthems, subject to screening requirements.

World.title: De la Espriella claims ELN plans to attack Colombia’s corporate media
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella ordered State forces to protect corporate media, claiming alerts over “possible terrorist attacks by the ELN” guerrilla group.

De la Espriella said he issued “specific instructions to ensure that the full capacity of the State is directed toward protecting” private television networks RCN and Caracol, “their journalists, employees, and families” on social media platform X.

The president said he also ordered to increase the protection of Semana, a far-right magazine owned by the main sponsor of his campaign, the Gilinksi family.

Freedom of the press is sacred and must be respected! No narco-terrorist group will silence the media through threats, intimidation, or acts of violence. President Abelardo de la Espriella

According to the Bogota Mayor’s Office, the orders were issued hours after the prosecution’s Technical Investigations Unit issued a “security alert” to the media outlets and the local government.

In a response, Caracol evacuated its main office in the capital and allowed police to search the premise for bombs without result.

Press freedom foundation FLIP said that “we reject and express our profound concerns over the alerts of possible attacks against media in Bogota.”

“The fact that no explosives have been found does not mean that the risk has ended. These alerts require monitoring and effective protection,” the FLIP said on X.

The alert was issued amid increased violence between guerrilla groups and State forces, who have been ordered to carry out an offensive against insurgencies and organized crime groups by the president.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP announces steep measures after being forced to cut $53M from its budget
World.content:
The president of the JEP announced radical cuts in the war crimes tribunal’s spending, which was forced to cut $53 million (COP170 billion) from its annual budget by Colombia’s Congress.

In a press statement, JEP president Danilo Rojas said that the court would abandon its 15,000m² main office in Bogota and move to a much smaller building in March of next year.

The court president additionally announced that it would eliminate 85% of its temporary employees and force staff to absorb administrative, technical defense, and psychosocial tasks previously handled by external contractors.

Many of the remaining workers will largely be working from home to facilitate the aforementioned move.

The court will also abandon personal security details for magistrates and the court directors and ask the National Protection Unit to take on the protection of victims, witnesses and defendants.

Last but not least, the court announced partnerships with universities, the Inspector General’s Office and local governments to secure regional presence, which is necessary to investigate war crimes.

The radical austerity measures became a necessity after Congress agreed with President Abelardo de la Espriella and hi far-right National Salvation party to slash the JEP’s budget.

The war crimes tribunal seeks justice for millions of victims of the military and the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC, which agreed to demobilize and disarm in 2016.

The JEP has long been the target of criticism of the far-right, which has historically downplayed the war crimes committed by the State and regional elites that used the armed conflict to accumulate wealth.

World.title: Colombia’s labor unions and social organizations call national strike on November 19
World.content:
Colombia’s main labor unions and a collection of civil society organizations called a national strike “against the fascist government of Abelardo de la Espriella and his tax reform” bill.

In a press statement, the organizations accused De la Espriella of, among other things, dismantling the “social, environmental, trade union, and labor rights achieved during the government of Gustavo Petro,” and surrendering sovereignty and kneeling before the imperialist government of the United States.”

The government of Abelardo, like that of Duque and Carrasquilla, intends to reach into the pockets of the people and privilege the ultra-rich with its “economic rescue” bill, which imposes a 19% VAT on food and other basic goods in the family basket, higher taxes on earned income, raises health contributions up to 8%, and conversely reduces the corporate capital income tax from 35% to 31%, eliminates the wealth tax in 2031, and reduces the capital gains tax to 20% for investments in 2027 and 2028. Civil society organizations

The organizations additionally accused the government of seeking special powers to facilitate the privatization of state-controlled companies like oil firm Ecopetrol.

The organizations said they united with the main opposition party, the Historic Pact, “with the purpose of opposing this fascist government and decisively participating in the National Strike.”

The National Strike on November 19 constitutes a new stage in the organization and expression of growing popular discontent, which was also manifested in the successful national mobilization day of October 14. It is about strengthening a collective action process capable of confronting the Government’s regressive measures, demanding respect for hard-won rights, and opposing the deepening of its neoliberal and authoritarian project. Civil society organizations

The last time a national strike was organized was in 2021 when the labor unions and their allies from civil society shut down parts of the country for months.

At the time, a tax reform propose by former President Ivan Duque triggered the initiative.

World.title: Colombia’s government presents “Economic Rescue Bill”
World.content:
Colombia’s Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo on Thursday presented an Economic Rescue Bill that seeks to reduce government spending and increase its revenue.

The bill grants extraordinary powers to President Abelardo de la Espriella to slash government spending by decree and includes a tax reform that includes higher sales tax rates on gasoline, coffee, cigarettes and vegetables.

The bill also includes tax breaks for corporations in an attempt to increase investment.

Abelardo’s extraordinary powers

While on campaign, De la Espriella powers vowed a 40% reduction of the State, which the bill falls short of doing.

Article 7 of the bill does grant the president extraordinary powers to “abolish, merge, and split ministries and administrative departments, as well as to determine or modify their names, objectives, and organizational structure,” and allows De la Espriella to “abolish, merge, split, and change the legal status” of other State bodies like the superintendencies, agencies, special administrative units, and public institutions.

Article 96 allows the government to change the personnel hiring of tax agency DIAN, which “would allow for the elimination of annual competitive exams for entry into the DIAN and a return to the practice of appointing thousands of officials,” according to former DIAN director Luis Carlos Reyes.

Last but not least, the bill mandates a 20% reduction in salaries of State employees, excluding the security forces, and cut half of the costs in temporary contracts.

VAT reforms and squeezing the middle class

The bill seeks to remove popular products like cocoa, coffee, sugar and fruits from a VAT exemption list and introduce a 19% sales tac on them.

An increase in taxes on gasoline will inflate its price.

The bill additionally seeks to charge VAT on vice products like liquor and cigarettes, which would make them up to 53% more expensive.

The bulk of these tax increases wouldn’t take fore until after the November 2027 local and regional elections in an apparent compromise to Congress and Colombia’s political forces.

In an attempt to not impoverish the poor, the bill seeks a mechanism that would refund up to 100% of IVA payments to some 19 million of the country’s poorest citizens.

The increased pressure on the middle class has already resulted in opposition from within De la Espriella’s congressional coalition.

Tax benefits for the capitalists

The government seeks to gradually lower the corporate income tax from 35% to 31% and offer a reduced tax rate for large companies that decide to invest in new enterprises.

According to the Inter-American Development Bank, a similar scheme introduced by former President Alvaro Uribe “was ineffective in promoting investment.”

World.title: Accusations over De la Espriella’s narco ties “lack conclusive or solid evidence,” says Colombia’s justice minister
World.content:
Colombia’s Justice Minister, Ivan Cancino, downplayed the evidence of ties between President Abelardo de la Espriella and drug traffickers that was displayed in Congress by opposition Senator Ivan Cepeda.

In a video, Cancino said that “political oversight is a fundamental tool of our democracy. However, it cannot become an arena for launching accusations without proving and substantiating them.”

The justice minister admitted that the pieces of evidence provided to Congress “may seem serious,” but “lack conclusive or solid evidence, as well as any support that could jeopardize the innocence and the presumption of innocence of our president.”

It is not just about displaying organizational charts, deeds from over a decade ago, and business transactions to construct a narrative that supports neither judicial decisions nor the documentary, testimonial, circumstantial, or expert backing required for these types of accusations. Ivan Cancino

Cancino accused the opposition of remaining “silent regarding the grave scandals involving corruption, drug trafficking, and even alleged sexual abuse, as well as fiscal irresponsibility and possible links to criminal organizations that surrounded the previous government. ”

The justice minister was forced to come out after Cepeda showed Congress evidence of De la Espriella’s business ties with multiple convicted drug traffickers and announced criminal complaints against the president.

De la Espriella’s law firm rose to prominence during the demobilization of paramilitary organization AUC with whom he created a foundation that sought to justify the paramilitary violence that terrorized much of Colombia in the 1990’s and 2000s.

Once the ties between the AUC and elected politicians became known, the president ended up defending many of the “parapoliticians” in court.

According to Cepeda, De la Espriella plays a key role in a “revolving door” system that could end up benefiting the very drug traffickers and corrupt politicians that have paid the president for his legal defense in the past.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: “Brazil and Colombia need each other,” says De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella recognized the election victory of his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Ignacio Lula, who defeated far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Colombian President said that “in the Colombian presidential campaign, President Lula openly supported Ivan Cepeda, and I won. In the Brazilian campaign, I supported Bolsonaro, and Lula won.”

“Neither does Lula decide for Colombians, nor do I decide for Brazilians. THE PEOPLE DECIDE! And when the people speak at the polls, their will is respected because it is sacred,” the president added.

Lula and I have major and profound political and ideological differences, but we agree on one fundamental point: Brazil and Colombia need each other. No other consideration can take precedence over the interests of our nations. Colombia and Brazil are sister nations, facing enormous shared challenges and opportunities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella stressed that “we have much to do and much work to carry out for the benefit of our peoples” an ought to “fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining, the protection of the Amazon, and the well-being of our citizens.”

Lula was the first leftist candidate and critic of US President Donald Trump to win an election, triggering celebrations among leftists throughout the continent.

De la Espriella, a US citizen, has been among the most fanatic among Trump supporter in trying to align his domestic policies to US foreign policy.

World.title: International News Briefs for Monday, November 9, 2026
World.content:
HAVANA TIMES – We bring you some of the top international news stories compiled by Democracy Now on Monday, November 9, 2026.

Democrats Build on Sweeping Gains in Midterm Elections, Claiming 254 House Seats

Nov 09, 2026

Democrats are continuing to build on their sweeping gains in last week’s midterm elections as votes continue to be counted. They can now claim 254 House seats, compared to 162 for Republicans, with 19 House races yet to be decided. Democrats will also control at least 30 governorships and will control both legislative chambers and the governor’s office in 23 states — up from 16 before the election. Democrats also broke Republican “trifectas” in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio and in Texas, where 87-year-old Houston Democrat Senfronia Thompson says she has the votes to become the first woman and first Black speaker of the Texas House of Representatives. Retired Navy Vice Admiral Nancy Lacore, who was abruptly fired from her post as chief of the Navy Reserve by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in August 2025, won election to the House of Representatives, flipping a seat in South Carolina held by the GOP. According to Axios, the House is poised to impeach Hegseth this week.

Meanwhile, Houston, Texas, Mayor John Whitmire announced Friday the city would start limiting the collaboration of local law enforcement with ICE during traffic stops. The announcement comes amid pressure from activists and as Republican Governor Greg Abbott prepares to leave office. Abbott previously threatened to revoke more than $110 million in public safety funding to Houston over a policy granting officers discretion over whether or not to contact ICE. Houston has seen mounting violent incidents involving ICE agents during traffic stops and car pursuits, including the fatal shooting of Mexican father Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in July. This is Houston Mayor Whitmire.

Mayor John Whitmire: “This morning, I have directed the chief and HPD, through an executive order, that we will change our policy in regarding contact with ICE. I do this to begin a healing process, reduce fear and anxiety across our community. I also do this knowing that elections matter.”

Trump Replaces White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller

Nov 09, 2026

President Trump has replaced White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, the chief architect of his mass deportation policy, days after Republicans lost control of Congress. In a statement, the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, Democratic Congressmember Robert Garcia, said, “Just days after the American people rejected his corrupt and lawless presidency, Donald Trump is doubling down. Stephen Miller is the architect of the unconstitutional ICE raids that have terrorized our communities and kidnapped and killed American citizens and immigrant families. Stephen Miller should lawyer up.” Attorney General Todd Blanche responded on Fox News that quote “Stephen Miller has a lawyer, it’s me”. This is Blanche on CNN.

Attorney General Todd Blanche: “The Department of Justice represents members of the executive who are brought in front of Congress, so there is nothing unique to me saying that every attorney general in history represents members of the administration. And this idea that Congressman Garcia comes out and says, ‘Oh, no, no, Stephen Miller needs his own personal lawyer,’ I would suggest he read the Constitution.”

In that interview, Blanche also repeatedly dodged questions about whether he’d investigate Democratic members of Congress, after President Trump ordered probes against congressional Democrats for calling for the impeachment of certain Cabinet officials. Soon after, Democratic Congressmember Robert Garcia issued this response to Blanche.

Rep. Robert Garcia: “We have the attorney general saying to the American public that somehow he’s going to defend administration officials, when his job is to defend the Constitution and the Department of Justice to be the people’s lawyer.”

Meanwhile, President Trump offered the press secretary job to Ultimate Fighting Championship, UFC, chief Dana White. Trump later said that he was only kidding, but White is set to meet with Trump today at the White House.

Former Top Federal Health Official Accuses Wiles of Putting Lobbyists and Campaign Funds Ahead of Public Health

Nov 09, 2026

Calley Means, a top federal health official who resigned two weeks ago, went on Joe Rogan’s podcast to accuse outgoing Chief of Staff Susie Wiles of prioritizing lobbyists and campaign funds over public health initiatives. Means claimed Wiles refused to back his push for healthier children’s diets because she wanted the sugar industry’s money, and says her team pushed for more flavored vape approvals and looser restrictions on the largely unregulated drug kratom. Means said, “Susie said to me many times: ‘We need money for the midterms, Calley. We need money for the midterms.’” Calley Means also alleges that companies hiring Wiles’s daughter, a lobbyist, got special priority.

Petition Urging Jeffries to Remove Himself from Race to Become House Speaker Surpasses a Million Signatures

Nov 09, 2026

Calls from progressives demanding new leadership in Congress continue to grow. An online petition urging Democratic Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries to remove himself from the running to become the next House speaker has surpassed 1 million signatures. Jeffries has faced mounting opposition over his pro-Israel interests and continued acceptance of corporate PAC money, including from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, AIPAC. Incoming Congressmembers-elect Chris Rabb, Melat Kiros and Darializa Avila Chevalier, all members of the Democratic Socialists of America, DSA, have already declined to pledge support for Jeffries if he’s up for House speaker.

Chuck Schumer is facing similar calls to step down as Senate Democratic leader. Senators-elect Peggy Flanagan, Troy Jackson, Abdul El-Sayed, Juliana Stratton and Adam Hamilton have all said they won’t support Schumer.

30 People Killed in Yemen in Missile Attack

Nov 09, 2026

In Yemen, at least 30 people were killed and more than three dozen injured on Friday as a missile slammed into a market in the southwestern province of Taiz. Women and children are among the dead. Yemen’s Saudi-backed government blamed the attack on fighters with Ansar Allah, also known as the Houthis, while a Houthi-linked television channel reported the attack was carried out by Saudi warplanes. This follows the deadliest month of attacks on Yemen since 2017. According to the Yemen Data Project, Saudi-led attacks killed 426 civilians in October — almost a quarter of them children.

Meanwhile, a missile fired by Houthi fighters struck an administrative building run by the state oil giant Saudi Aramco in Riyadh on Sunday, shattering windows on several floors of one of the tallest buildings in the Saudi capital’s King Abdullah Financial District.

Israeli President Herzog Picks Opposition Leader Eisenkot to Form Next Government

Nov 09, 2026

In Israel, President Isaac Herzog has picked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, passing over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Sixty-seven lawmakers, including from Arab-led parties, backed Eisenkot, while 46 backed Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to build what he calls a “national emergency government,” but his bloc is divided over allying with Arab-led parties, which won a historic 19 seats in elections last month.

Israeli Forces Release Palestinian Journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh

Nov 09, 2026

Israeli forces have released Palestinian journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh without charge, five days after armed police and Shin Bet agents raided his Jaffa home. Police accused the +972 Magazine contributor of “contacting a foreign agent” after he interviewed exiled former lawmaker Azmi Bishara in Qatar ahead of Israel’s election last month. Adalah, a legal group that supports Palestinian citizens of Israel, said, “The message to Palestinian citizens is unmistakable: a public conversation with a political figure can land you in a cell. This is political persecution carried out through criminal law.”

Storm Triggers Mass Flooding in Gaza, Killing 5 Palestinians, as Israel Bars Imports of Shelter

Nov 09, 2026

In Gaza, health authorities say heavy rains collapsed a sandbank onto tents in Deir al-Balah, killing at least five people, including four children. Gaza’s Government Media Office says the storm flooded at least 70,000 tents, and the U.N. says about 950,000 displaced Palestinians live in areas exposed to flooding. Ahmad Alhendawi of Save the Children said, “This is not simply the result of bad weather. Tents, shelter kits and fuel are waiting at Gaza’s borders while children sleep in floodwater, because the Israeli authorities are blocking their entry. This is a choice, and children are paying the price.” This is a displaced Palestinian woman.

Olfat Magdoub: “This is the first day of rain, and of course we are already flooded. What will happen if it rains again the next day? This is only the first day, and we’re already overwhelmed. Two weeks ago, when it rained, I swear to God, I spent four days sleeping on blankets spread on the floor because the rainwater had flooded the bedding. Same now, the mattresses are wet, so we sleep on the ground.”

Hundreds of Thousands March in Amsterdam Demanding Action to Stop Gaza Genocide

Nov 09, 2026

In the Netherlands, more than 200,000 protesters marched through Amsterdam on Sunday demanding the Dutch government take action to halt Israel’s attacks on Gaza. Protesters wore red, many of them carrying signs reading “Stop the Genocide.” They’re demanding a halt to all direct and indirect arms trade with Israel, an expanded import ban on products from illegal Israeli settlements and for Dutch leaders to exert more political and diplomatic pressure on Israel to end its illegal occupations.

Protesters Take Direct Action to “Stop Dirty Data Centers” in Europe

Nov 09, 2026

In more news from the Netherlands, over 100 protesters broke into a construction site of a Microsoft data center in the ​outskirts ​of Amsterdam on Friday. It was the first of many direct action protests held across Europe in 16 countries over the weekend by the “Stop Dirty Data Centers” coalition. Protesters are calling for a large-scale pause on new data center construction.

bq. Protester: “There’s for sure a lot of opposition. I think it would be good for governments to do more research into what the people actually want. There’s very much opposition against Big Tech, against their surveillance, against the power that they have over democracies. And they should not be able to get away with that, especially since the people don’t agree.”

Nvidia Share Prices Plummet as CEO Jensen Huang Admits to Affair with Alleged Chinese Spy

Nov 09, 2026

The billionaire tech CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an extramarital relationship with a business executive who U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy. On Sunday, the chip maker Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into Huang after he apologized to his colleagues, his wife and their children. The New York Times reports Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation that sought to convince him to lobby U.S. officials to allow the export of advanced computer chips to China. According to the New York Times, President Trump eased some of those limits on the sale of advanced chips to China after Huang’s lobbying. Jensen Huang is a close ally of President Trump, and Nvidia is currently one of the world’s two largest publicly traded corporations, along with Apple. Nvidia’s stock tumbled on the news, wiping hundreds of billions of dollars from its nearly $5 trillion valuation.

U.S. Is Absent as United Nations Climate Talks Open in Antalya, Turkey

Nov 09, 2026

In Turkey, world leaders, delegates and climate activists are convening in Antalya today to mark the start of another round of U.N. climate talks. Heads of governments and officials from more than 190 countries are expected to attend — with the glaring absence of the United States, after President Trump last year withdrew the U.S. from the Paris Climate Agreement for the second time.

Nations in the Global South are again expected to pressure richer countries responsible for the climate crisis to commit to more financing of a loss and damage fund that was established at the U.N. climate summit in Egypt four years ago to cope with climate-related disasters. Though Turkey is hosting the U.N. talks, Australia is presiding over the negotiations.

Disgraced Paraguayan Ex-President Charged with Corruption over Bank Collapse

Nov 09, 2026

In Paraguay, former president and Trump ally Santiago Peña has been impeached and charged over his alleged role in the collapse of the major digital lender Ueno Bank. Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as interim president of Paraguay as Peña remains under house arrest. Alliana served as vice president under Peña. The collapse of Ueno Bank left at least 3 million people — nearly half of Paraguay’s population — without access to their money and froze hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds, including state pension money.

Cinthia Vargas: “I had my entire life savings in Ueno Bank. I’d been saving there for five years, and overnight I lost everything. I was left with nothing. Five years of savings, five years of honest work. I never stole from anyone, never bothered anyone. What for? So that Santiago Peña and his whole gang of criminals could come and rob us?”
