World.title: Polish government ministers suggest tighter gun controls after deadly terrorist shooting
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. In the wake of Saturday’s deadly terrorist shooting in Kraków, a deputy defence minister has called for debate on limiting the number and types of weapons people can own. Meanwhile, a deputy interior minister says the tragedy provides an “incentive” to revisit proposals to better register certain guns. Poland has among the lowest levels of gun ownership in Europe, though the number of firearms licences being issued has risen in recent years and some politicians have called for expanded access to guns. Saturday’s attack was carried out by a man who legally owned firearms. On Saturday, 24-year-old Michał Oksiński drove through the historic city centre of Kraków, which was packed with tourists and locals, firing at random from his car. He killed six people and injured over a dozen more. Later in the day, the bodies of the perpetrator’s parents and sister were found in his home, where they had been shot dead. Oksiński’s rampage was brought to an end in a shootout with two police officers, which left all three with serious injuries. On Monday morning, the police announced that Oksiński had died in hospital. One of the police officers remains in what is described as “serious but stable” condition. The man who carried out Saturday’s deadly terrorist attack in the Polish city of Kraków has died in hospital from the injuries he sustained during a shootout with police. One of the two officers who stopped him remains in serious but stable condition https://t.co/rT1YBXhkp7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 9, 2026 The incident has caused shock in Poland, a country that has never previously experienced this type of mass public shooting. Speaking to Polsat News on Sunday, deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka said that the tragedy “is the best illustration that it makes no sense to talk about expanding access to firearms”. She added that “it’s already relatively easy” to obtain a gun licence, which can be granted to anyone aged 21 or over who has passed the relevant tests and declared that the firearm is for sporting purposes. Both Oksiński and his father had such licences and legally owned 11 firearms. “I would like to start a discussion about whether access to such a large number of weapons should actually be so easy,” said Sobkowiak-Czarnecka. “This is also a question of whether someone who uses weapons for sporting purposes should have so many different types of weapons stored at home.” Also speaking to Polsat on Sunday, Czesław Mroczek, a deputy interior minister, said that “weapons are certainly a challenge for us”. He noted that “in Poland we have had many cases of killings using black powder weapons, for which there is not even a register, let alone a permit procedure”. Such weapons use traditional black powder rather than modern smokeless powder and include firearms manufactured before 1885 and their modern replicas. According to a recent study by researchers from the Jagiellonian University in Kraków, they make up a considerable proportion of firearm-related fatalities in the country. While noting that the issue is not directly related to the Kraków attacks, Mroczek said that plans to include these weapons in a register had already been drawn up and “this event [in Kraków] is an incentive for us to reexamine the matter”. 🇵🇱 Poland's interior ministry says black-powder guns, currently exempt from registration, will be entered into the register. The Krakow attack is described as an impulse to review the whole permit system.https://t.co/Nh7dr46MJ7 — Олег Рощин (@oleg_roshchin) November 9, 2026 On Monday morning, the spokesman for the National Prosecutor’s Office, Przemysław Nowak, held a press conference at which he provided further details on their findings so far. He revealed that Oksiński had been found with two AR-15 rifles and two handguns on his person and in his car, as well as around 500 rounds of ammunition. He had earlier fired “several dozen, possibly several hundred, shots”. A further seven guns had been found at Oksiński’s home. The total of 11 firearms matched the number of weapons there were permits for, noted Nowak, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska. “The entire matter related to the weapons and the firearms permits will be reviewed,” added the spokesman. “We know that, since March of this year, he [Oksiński] has held firearms permits for one rifle and one pistol.” Prosecutors have launched a terror investigation into Saturday’s shooting in Kraków, which left six dead. Three more bodies were later found in the suspect's home. Further details have also emerged about the heroic actions of police and medical personnel https://t.co/icBJWLRK7c — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 8, 2026 Although gun ownership in Poland is relatively low, it has been rising steadily in recent years, particularly since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, with the total number of registered firearms owned by Poles surpassing 1 million, up from around 380,000 in 2014. Last year, a record 50,709 new gun licences were issued in the country in 2025, up 10.6% compared to a year earlier. Under Polish law, civilians can apply for licences for sporting, hunting, collecting and personal protection purposes. To obtain one, applicants must undergo medical examinations, pass a test, and join a relevant association, such as the Polish Sports Shooting Association, the Polish Hunting Association, or a collectors’ group. Licences for sports and collection purposes are the most popular types of permits, together making up 76% of last year’s permits. But the number of licences issued for “personal protection” has grown from just 81 in 2021 to 7,254 last year. A record 50,709 gun licences were issued in Poland last year and the total number of registered firearms has now surpassed 1 million. Gun ownership in Poland has risen particularly rapidly since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 https://t.co/axt2YS044Z — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 11, 2026 Access to firearms widened in 2023 under the former government, when parliament passed a law removing “unnecessary administrative and legal barriers.” That allowed members of uniformed services to apply for personal protection permits, a change lawmakers said was intended to “strengthen Poland’s defence potential”. However, some politicians, especially on the right, have pushed for ownership rules to be further loosened. In September, speaking at the opening of a shooting range, President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, called for “public discussion about responsible access to weapons”. “Even in the European Union, Poland remains at the bottom of the list in terms of access to firearms,” he said, quoted by Polsat. “Only about 1% of Polish citizens have access to weapons and are skilled at using them. Fortunately, I’m in that 1%.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Fugitive Polish opposition politician attends gala at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Fugitive Polish opposition politician Zbigniew Ziobro, who fled to the United States rather than face criminal charges in his homeland, has been pictured attending a gala at Donald Trump’s luxury Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida. The US president himself spoke at the event. The Polish justice minister has responded by saying that he hopes the US will show “true friendship” by cooperating with Poland’s request to extradite Ziobro, just as Poland would do if an American fugitive was on its territory. Ziobro na przyjęciu w rezydencji Trumpa. Wiadomo, co podano na eleganckiej kolacji w Mar-a-Lago [ZDJĘCIA] https://t.co/geANxBTn0J — Andrzej Holinka 🇵🇱 #Nawrocki2030 🇵🇱 ✌️ (@HolinkaPis) November 7, 2026 On Saturday, Blask Online, a news website linked to conservative broadcaster TV Republika, published images of Ziobro at Mar-a-Lago alongside senior Republika figures. They were attending a “retreat and gala” hosted by CPAC, which also organises a major annual conservative political conference and has close ties to Trump. The cheapest tickets to attend the gala cost $2,500, ranging up to $7,500 for VIP access. Blask Online’s photos show Ziobro eating dinner at the event and speaking to former British Prime Minister Liz Truss. Trump himself addressed the guests, saying that he “wants to congratulate everybody here”. Nikodem Rachoń, an advisor to Polish President Karol Nawrocki – who is aligned with the opposition and is a close Trump ally – also attended the CPAC event, where he was listed as a speaker. Ziobro is a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party, which is aligned with Trump and his Republican Party. From 2015 to 2023, Ziobro served as justice minister in a PiS-led government, overseeing judicial reforms that are widely seen as having undermined the rule of law. After a new, more liberal ruling coalition led by the current prime minister, Donald Tusk, took power in December 2023, it launched a number of investigations into the actions of senior PiS officials. That led, last year, to prosecutors announcing that they want to charge Ziobro with 26 crimes, including leading a criminal group and approving the unlawful purchase of Pegasus spyware, which was used to surveil some of PiS’s political opponents. However, although parliament approved the lifting of Ziobro’s immunity from prosecution, he had by then already travelled to Hungary, which was at the time ruled by conservative PiS ally Viktor Orbán. In December 2025, the Hungarian government granted Ziobro political asylum. At this year’s Hungarian parliamentary elections in April, Orbán’s Fidesz party was removed from power and his successor, Péter Magyar, pledged to extradite Ziobro to Poland. But, just as Magyar was being sworn in in May, Ziobro left Hungary and flew to the United States, reportedly with the help of a senior US State Department official. In July, Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office announced that it was sending a request to the US authorities to detain and extradite Ziobro. In late October, the National Prosecutor’s Office told newspaper Fakt that “we have so far not received any response from the US”. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 On Saturday, Poland’s justice minister and prosecutor general, Waldemar Żurek, was asked by Fakt about the newly published images showing Ziobro attending the gala at Mar-a-Lago. “I’d like Polish-American friendship to be a true friendship,” replied Żurek. “If a fugitive from the US was being prosecuted by the US justice system for embezzling hundreds of millions, we would cooperate with the US [if that fugitive was in Poland].” “But when I see that, the day after the US elections, which should be a reflection for Republicans, the president [Donald Trump] is focusing on building a ballroom, nothing will surprise me anymore,” he added. “We’re doing our job and we’ll see this matter through to the end.” Ziobro na przyjęciu w rezydencji Trumpa. Reaguje Żurek ⬇️ https://t.co/JT8o7d2X1w — DoRzeczy (@DoRzeczy_pl) November 7, 2026 Last week, before the CPAC event at Mar-a-Lago, Żurek had joked that “Ziobro brings bad luck”, noting that Orbán had lost elections after sheltering him and that now so had Trump’s Republicans. Żurek added that he hoped the shifting balance of power in the US might weaken the “protective political umbrella” Ziobro had so far enjoyed there and make the American “administration more willing to cooperate with the Polish justice system”, reports news website Onet. Ziobro himself has denied any wrongdoing and claims that the prosecution against him is an act of “political revenge” by the current government. He says he is willing to face justice in Poland, but only “when the rule of law is restored”. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Perpetrator of Kraków terrorist attack dies of injuries in hospital
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This is a breaking news story and will be updated as further information becomes available. The man who carried out Saturday’s deadly terrorist attack in the Polish city of Kraków – and who can now be named as 24-year-old Michał Oksiński – has died in hospital. Oksiński suffered serious injuries in a firefight with two police officers, who heroically brought his rampage to an end. On Sunday, Krzysztof Klęczar, the governor of the Małopolska province in which Kraków is located, revealed that Oksiński remained in critical condition. On Monday morning, provincial police announced that “the perpetrator of the tragic events [in Kraków] died this morning in hospital”. “There was a constant struggle to save this man’s life, despite the evil he had committed,” Klęczar told broadcaster TVN after the death was confirmed. “He underwent at least three surgeries.” Informujemy, że sprawca tragicznych wydarzeń zmarł dzisiaj nad ranem w szpitalu. — Małopolska Policja (@kwpkrakow) November 9, 2026 The two police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who engaged Oksiński also suffered serious injuries, with Kulik’s condition the more critical of the two. The situation would have been much worse were it not for the fact that two leading local surgeons had, by pure chance, been eating a meal with their families in a restaurant near where the shootout took place, and provided emergency aid to the officers. There was also a huge public response to appeals for people to donate blood for Kulik, who underwent a series of surgeries. On Sunday, it was announced that both Kulik and Morański had come out of the comas they had previously been placed in. Kulik’s condition was described as “serious but stable” by Karolina Gałecka, spokeswoman for the interior ministry. CCTV footage shows the moment two police officers confront the Krakow shooter. pic.twitter.com/vcQ0Xvi1nX — WarMonitor🇺🇦🇬🇧 (@WarMonitor3) November 7, 2026 Just after 3 p.m. local time on Saturday afternoon, Oksiński drove through the historic city centre of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, including its famous market square, which was packed with tourists and locals. He fired at random from the car, killing six people. Four of those victims have been identified as Polish women, aged 47, 53 and 61, and a Polish man in his 50s. The other two were foreign nationals: a 32-year-old British man and a 51-year-old Austrian woman. A further 16 people were injured in the attack, 11 of them Polish. The interior ministry has said that, among the dead and injured are citizens of the UK, Austria, Germany, Russia and Portugal. On Saturday evening, it was announced that a search of the perpetrator’s home in the small town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski in southeast Poland, around 160 km from Krakow, had revealed three further dead bodies. They were later confirmed to belong to Oksiński’s parents, aged 53 and 52, and 21-year-old sister. Prosecutors believe Oksiński murdered them before launching his rampage in Kraków. Oksiński’s motive remains unknown. On Saturday evening, in the wake of the attacks, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński announced at a press conference that the information obtained so far indicated that the suspect had “very, very radical views” and “may have been fascinated by far-right ideologies”. However, when pressed on this claim during an interview with TVN on Sunday evening, Kierwiński refused to provide evidence, said that his remarks had referred to “initial hypotheses”, and confirmed that the potential motive was still being investigated. Poland's interior minister refuses to reveal on what basis he said the Kraków terrorist had "very radical views" and was "fascinated by the far right". "In cases like this, there are always first hypotheses, first clues. That's why I made this statement" pic.twitter.com/Wpud1FrAYM — Daniel Tilles (@danieltilles1) November 8, 2026 The incident has caused shock in Poland, where gun crime is exceedingly rare. The country has one of the lowest levels of gun ownership in Europe and has never previously suffered a mass public shooting of this kind. In response to the tragedy, a period of two days of official public mourning has been declared, with a decree to that effect signed by President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk. On Monday evening, a silent march will be held in Kraków at 8 p.m. to pay tribute to the victims. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Prosecutors launch terror investigation as Poland reels from fatal shootings
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish prosecutors have announced the opening of a terrorism investigation following Saturday’s attack in the city of Kraków, where a man opened fire from his vehicle, killing six people. Later, three further bodies – believed to be the perpetrator’s parents and sister – were found in his home. Further details have also emerged regarding the victims of the attack, the heroic actions of police and medical personnel, as well as the attacker himself – though the motive for his actions remains unknown. On Saturday, the suspected attacker, who has been named only as 24-year-old Michał O. under Polish privacy law, drove through the historic city centre of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, including its famous market square, which was packed with tourists and locals. He fired at random from the car, killing six people. Three of those victims have been identified as Polish women, aged 47, 53 and 61. Another was a 32-year-old British man. The final two victims were a foreign woman aged 51, whose nationality has not yet been announced, and a Polish man in his 50s. A further 16 people were injured in the attack, 11 of them Polish. The interior ministry has said that, among the dead and injured are citizens of the UK, Austria, Germany, Russia and Portugal. Two of the injured are police officers who pursued the attacker and engaged in a firefight with him. They and Michał O. were hospitalised with what have been described as critical injuries. Due to his ongoing medical treatment, law enforcement authorities have not yet been able to formally take the suspect into detention. CCTV footage shows the moment two police officers confront the Krakow shooter. pic.twitter.com/vcQ0Xvi1nX — WarMonitor🇺🇦🇬🇧 (@WarMonitor3) November 7, 2026 However, on Sunday morning, the National Prosecutor’s Office announced that it has launched a formal investigation into the killing of six people in Kraków and the attempted murder of numerous others. The actions are being treated as a terrorist offence. Meanwhile, they are also investigating the killing by gunshot of three people in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, also on Saturday. That is Michał O.’s hometown, and on Saturday evening Prime Minister Donald Tusk revealed that three bodies had been found at the address where he lived. Prosecutors say that “the evidence indicates that the same person committed the acts” in both Kraków and Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. Previously, on Saturday evening, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński announced that initial findings indicate the suspect had “very radical far-right views”. However, he cautioned that investigators were still seeking to confirm this, as well as to understand the possible motive behind the attack. Minister @MKierwinski na konferencji w Krakowie: 💬 Sprawca mógł być zafascynowany ideologiami skrajnie prawicowymi. Ten wątek będzie jednak szczegółowo weryfikowany. Czynności prowadzą funkcjonariusze @PolskaPolicja, jak i @ABW_GOV_PL – na miejscu zdarzenia oraz w domu rodzinnym… pic.twitter.com/PppmMPmWYW — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) November 7, 2026 Gun crime is exceedingly rare in Poland, which has one of the lowest levels of gun ownership in Europe. Saturday was the first time that the country has experienced a mass public shooting of this type. In response, a period of two days of official public mourning has been declared, with a decree to that effect signed by President Karol Nawrocki and Tusk. Meanwhile, political leaders have praised the heroic actions of police, especially the two officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were critically injured while bringing Michał O’s rampage to an end. “They are heroes,” said Krzysztof Klęczar, governor of the Małopolska province in which Kraków is located. “Considering how many weapons were still in the perpetrator’s car, if it weren’t for the effective and selfless intervention of these two young men, the number of victims could have been significantly higher.” It has also emerged that the police officers were treated by two leading surgeons who, by complete chance, had been eating dinner with their families at a restaurant near where the final shootout took place. One of them, Michał Pędziwiatr, a professor of surgery at the Jagiellonian University, told the media that he and fellow surgeon Mateusz Wierdak had seen the police subduing the attacker. While their families took shelter, the two doctors rushed to the scene once the shooting had finished. “Mateusz’s dedication in stopping the bleeding of the most injured police officer [Kulik] undoubtedly saved his life,” Pędziwiatr told the Fakt newspaper. Pędziwiatr himself called a local hospital that he knew would be best equipped to treat the officer so that they could prepare for his arrival. ⚫️"Tato, strzelają do ludzi!". Lekarz ujawnia kulisy zamachu Prof. Michał Pędziwiatr i dr Mateusz Wierdak byli w pobliskiej restauracji, gdy doszło do strzelaniny. Zanim przyjechały karetki, lekarze udzielili pomocy rannym. – Wyszliśmy na zewnątrz. Już się żegnaliśmy. Nagle mój… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) November 8, 2026 Public authorities in Poland, including the police and military, launched a drive for blood donations to help in the treatment of Kulik, who remains in critical condition. They said they had been overwhelmed by the number of people coming forward. The defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, also revealed that Kulik is a former soldier from the elite 6th Airborne Brigade, which is headquartered in Kraków. “The entire military community is proud of Jakub. We will support him and his loved ones,” wrote Kosiniak-Kamysz. A public fundraiser launched by Krzysztof Stanowski, a prominent media personality, has, at the time of writing, raised over 3.5 million zloty (€777,000) to support the police officers and their families. On Sunday morning, Klęczar also confirmed that Michał O. had “undergone several surgeries during the night” and “remained in critical condition”. ❗Kiedyś żołnierz 6 Brygady Powietrznodesantowej, dziś policjant i bohater- starszy posterunkowy Jakub Kulik, który wczoraj został ranny w zamachu w Krakowie potrzebuje naszego wsparcia. Ranny policjant przebywa w szpitalu. Potrzebna jest krew grupy AB Rh+. Krew można oddać… — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 8, 2026 The authorities have confirmed that Michał O. holds a firearms licence. During the incident on Saturday, he appears to have used an AR-15-style rifle, but police also found a number of other firearms in his vehicle. World.title: Six killed in terrorist shooting in Polish city of Kraków
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Six people have been killed and many more injured after a man opened fire from a moving vehicle in the historic centre of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, today. Police have apprehended the perpetrator. The interior minister says that the incident is being treated as a terrorist attack, and that preliminary indications suggest the perpetrator had “very radical far-right” views. Police later discovered three further dead bodies in the suspect’s home, who are believed to be his parents and sister. 📌Premier przekazał, że policja, służby specjalne, prokuratura zrobią wszystko, żeby jak najszybciej przekazać informacje opinii publicznej o powodach (strzelaniny – PAP) – powiedział w sobotę na briefingu premier Donald Tusk. 📌- Prawdopodobnie w domu zamachowca są nieżywi… pic.twitter.com/gnV7c1TALa — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) November 7, 2026 At around 3 p.m. local time on Saturday, a man who had driven onto Kraków’s market square – a large public space filled with tourists and locals – “began firing at random people from his car”, said police. They later confirmed that six people – four women and two men – have died and 15 were injured. Three of the deceased have been identified as Polish women, and one other as a British man. The two other victims have not been identified at the time of writing. The police also revealed that there is only one suspected perpetrator, that he is a Polish citizen, and that he has been detained and transported to hospital. ~aktualizacja Zmarła kolejna z osób poszkodowanych w zdarzeniu na Rynku Głównym w Krakowie. Na ten moment nie żyje 6 osób. 4 kobiety i 2 mężczyzn. pic.twitter.com/yK6a7fSj2P — Małopolska Policja (@kwpkrakow) November 7, 2026 Footage from Republika, a TV station that had been present in the city centre to report from an anti-government protest that was taking place today, showed paramedics appearing to treat victims on the square. The station also broadcast footage showing the car from which shots were fired driving through a street that leads away from the square. A police car can be seen behind it and the apparent sound of gunfire can be heard. Moment ucieczki czarnego Subaru w Krakowie, widać, że sprawca strzela z samochodu do ludzi… pic.twitter.com/VfWYtx8PYX — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) November 7, 2026 Further videos and photos shared on social media show the alleged perpetrator being apprehended by a police officer, with both men injured and requiring medical treatment. The suspect is wearing a military-style uniform, including some kind of helmet and face covering, while what looks like an AR-15-style rifle can be seen on the ground alongside him. A spokeswoman for provincial police headquarters in Kraków, Katarzyna Cisło, later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that police officers had fired at the suspect, who had returned fire. Two police officers were injured during the incident, with one undergoing surgery and described as being in critical condition. 🔴Strzelanina w Krakowie. Jest nagranie z momentu zatrzymania zamachowca pic.twitter.com/2EXVvLEoRY — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) November 7, 2026 A spokesman for national police headquarters, Andrzej Fijołek, told TVN that the suspect is a 24-year-old from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a small town in southeastern Poland. Fijołek revealed that the man has a firearms licence and had used an AR-15 rifle during the incident, which he fired randomly while driving the car. “I can confirm that his attire indicates he was well-prepared, well-armed and knew what he was doing,” he added. Defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz announced that, contrary to some rumours on social media, the suspect is not and has never been a member of the Polish military. Stanowczo dementuję informacje pojawiające się w przestrzeni publicznej, że zamachowcem, który dokonał dziś ataku w Krakowie był żołnierz Wojska Polskiego. Mężczyzna nie był i nie jest żołnierzem WP i nigdy nie mial nic wspólnego z wojskiem. — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 7, 2026 On Saturday evening, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński confirmed that “we are dealing with a terrorist attack”. He praised “police officers’ swift response for preventing a much larger massacre”. Kierwiński said that the perpetrator is currently in critical condition in hospital. He added that the information obtained so far suggests that the attacker had “very, very radical views” and “may have been fascinated by far-right ideologies”. However, the interior minister emphasised that investigations are still ongoing. Subsequently, Prime Minister Donald Tusk revealed that three further bodies – of two women and one man – had been found at the suspect’s home. He said they were likely his close family members. Minister @MKierwinski na konferencji w Krakowie: 💬 Sprawca mógł być zafascynowany ideologiami skrajnie prawicowymi. Ten wątek będzie jednak szczegółowo weryfikowany. Czynności prowadzą funkcjonariusze @PolskaPolicja, jak i @ABW_GOV_PL – na miejscu zdarzenia oraz w domu rodzinnym… pic.twitter.com/PppmMPmWYW — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) November 7, 2026 Gun violence in Poland is extremely rare, and this kind of mass shooting incident is unheard of. The country also has one of the lowest rates of gun ownership in Europe, though a record number of licences, 50,709, were issued last year. Kraków is by far Poland’s biggest tourist destination, receiving over 16 million visitors last year. The historic city centre, which is a UNESCO-listed World Heritage Site, would have been filled with locals and tourists on a Saturday afternoon. The market square itself, surrounded by historic townhouses, is the heart of the city’s life, filled with restaurants, cafes and bars, as well as St Mary’s Basilica, the famous Cloth Hall (Sukiennice), and the old town hall tower. Kraków has been named Europe's best city break destination by members of @WhichUK. The city's food and drink was rated as better than in Paris and Rome, while it also scored top marks for accommodation, ease of getting around and value for money https://t.co/U1P1QkQCm4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 19, 2025 President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine, Poland’s eastern neighbour, expressed his condolences and declared that his country “stands in solidarity with Poland”. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz also sent messages of condolence. The US ambassador to Poland, Thomas Rose, expressed his sorrow at the “savage and murderous attack” in Kraków and declared that “America stands with Poland at this dark hour”. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Rating agency S&P shifts Poland’s credit outlook to negative and lowers currency rating
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Credit rating agency S&P has revised Poland’s outlook to negative, saying that the country has seen “one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally” and that “political polarisation hinders fiscal consolidation”. It also lowered the country’s long- and short-term local currency ratings. S&P’s decision follows similar ones by the other members of the big three rating agencies. Fitch has had Poland on negative outlook since last year, while Moody’s cut the country’s credit rating in September this year to its lowest level since 2002. In a statement issued on Friday evening, S&P said that its “negative outlook reflects the risk that elevated budgetary deficits and rising government debt could constrain policy flexibility in the face of future shocks”. “This could expose Poland to shifts in investor sentiment or necessitate a sharp fiscal adjustment that would weigh on economic growth,” they added. 🚨Bardzo źle to wygląda! S&P o finansach Polski: „Takie pogorszenie sytuacji budżetowej należy do najpoważniejszych na świecie”. Dług netto ma wzrosnąć o ponad 20 pkt proc. PKB w 5 lat i przekroczyć 70% PKB w 2029 r. S&P obniżyła rating długu w PLN i perspektywę do negatywnej. — Piotr Nowak (@PiotrNowak_PL) November 7, 2026 Poland has struggled with ballooning budget deficits in recent years, driven by a rapidly expanding defence budget in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and longer-term increases in social spending. Last year’s deficit, at 7.3% of GDP, was the second-highest in the European Union. This year it is forecast to drop slightly, to 6.7%, according to recent finance ministry projections. But next year’s budget foresees a deficit of 7.1%. Those figures are much higher than those the government pledged to reach when, in 2024, Poland was placed under the EU’s excessive deficit procedure. For example, the deficit was supposed to fall to 3.7% of GDP in 2027. Moody’s, one of the big three global credit rating agencies, has cut Poland’s rating from A2 to A3. The last time the agency had Poland at such a low level was 2002. It is also the first time any of the big three agencies has downgraded Poland since 2016 https://t.co/qUAEouqhlx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 19, 2026 S&P says that it projects Poland’s net debt exceeding 70% of GDP by 2029. That rise of “more than 20 percentage points over five years marks one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally”. The agency notes that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in 2027, making any “meaningful consolidation unlikely” before then. Moreover, the veto power of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki means the government “faces constraints in advancing its legislative and fiscal consolidation agenda”. Pointing to the ongoing crisis around the constitutional court, S&P also warns that “renewed institutional tensions could weigh on policy predictability”. However, the agency notes that Poland’s economy remains “resilient”, with real GDP growth projected to average around 3% between 2027 and 2029. It also points to the fact that the country has seen a peak in EU-funded investment this year, while exports have picked up. As well as shifting Poland’s overall outlook to negative, S&P downgraded its local currency ratings – meaning its assessment of the country’s willingness and ability to service debt denominated in domestic currency – from A/A-1 to A-/A-2, the same level as its foreign currency ratings. “Our fiscal projections are now weaker than previously envisaged, and we note a track record of recent fiscal slippages amid a challenging policy environment, which underpin our assessment of Poland’s reduced fiscal flexibility,” wrote the agency. Finance minister Andrzej Domański acknowledged S&P’s decision to lower Poland’s outlook to negative in a social media post. However, he pointed to the section of the agency’s report in which it said that the government is constrained by presidential vetoes. Nawrocki has vetoed a record number of bills since becoming president last year, including several fiscal measures. “Despite the presidential vetoes, we will continue taking steps to strengthen the country’s finances,” wrote Domański. 🇵🇱 Agencja S&P utrzymała rating Polski na poziomie A-, obniżając jednak jego perspektywę do negatywnej. W uzasadnieniu decyzji czytamy wprost: „Rząd premiera Donalda Tuska napotyka ograniczenia w realizacji swoich planów legislacyjnych i konsolidacji finansów publicznych ze… — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) November 6, 2026 However, Nawrocki notes that the ballooning budget deficits preceded his coming to power, and has blamed the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk for overseeing budgetary “chaos” and causing “a deep crisis of credibility”. In response to S&P’s announcement, Marcin Ociepa, deputy head of the parliamentary caucus of Law and Justice (PiS), the largest opposition party, accused the government of “trying to shift responsibility for Poland’s credit rating downgrade [sic] onto the president”. “Any family that managed its finances the way Donald Tusk manages our country’s finances would drown in debt and go bankrupt,” wrote Ociepa. “That is exactly what awaits Poland if this government remains in power.” ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: 2,000-year-old Vandal artefacts anonymously handed to Polish museum
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A collection of artefacts associated with the Vandals and dating back almost 2,000 years has been handed anonymously to a museum in eastern Poland. The collection includes a sword, spear and javelin heads, shield components and spurs. Museum staff do not know who originally discovered the burial or exactly where it was located, leaving the circumstances of the find largely a mystery. The Father Stanisław Staszic Museum in Hrubieszów announced in a Facebook post that the objects had been passed to them anonymously through an intermediary. The items are in poor condition and will undergo urgent conservation, with the iron components of the weapons particularly vulnerable after centuries in the ground. They were also exposed to high temperatures during a burial practice in which the deceased was burned along with their personal belongings. The museum says that the nature of the objects indicates that their owner held a high social position. The most notable object is a sword preserved in three pieces, reflecting the Vandal practice of deliberately breaking or bending weapons and other grave artefacts as part of funeral rituals. The collection also contains two spearheads, both broken. Other items include a shield boss with a spike, a shield grip, a fragment of a knife, a belt buckle and two spurs. Fragments of a bone comb and a bronze fibula, used to fasten a cloak, were also recovered. The circumstances surrounding the discovery and recovery of the objects remain unknown, but the museum says that, according to the information it has received, the burial site was discovered in an agricultural field several years ago in the municipality of Werbkowice. “We intend to verify the exact location through archaeological excavations, most likely next summer,” they added. “Based on the information we have gathered, there are strong indications that there may be more similar burials in the area that have been disturbed by agricultural work.” The opportunity to recover the objects and transfer them to an appropriate institution arose only recently. The museum said that a local metal detectorist played a key role in arranging the transfer, acting as an intermediary in securing the artefacts. The recovery of the artefacts follows another recent archaeological discovery in the same region. In August, the museum announced that a metal boss from a warrior’s shield dating to the second century was found at a scrap metal yard near Hrubieszów. The Vandals were an ancient Germanic people believed to have reached the territories of present-day Poland around the 3rd or 2nd century BC. They lived in the region for several centuries and are generally associated by researchers with the Przeworsk culture, which flourished across parts of present-day Poland during the Iron Age and Roman period. Around the turn of the 4th and 5th centuries AD, amid the expansion of the Huns, they left Central Europe and moved westwards into the declining Roman Empire. As the Vandals left Central Europe, the Slavic population gradually moved into the region over the following centuries. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Three Days of Chocolate and Sweet Treats Await in Prague
World.content:
Chocolate lovers in Prague will have a sweet reason to head to Novo Plaza this weekend as ČokoFest arrives at the shopping centre for the first time.

The three-day chocolate festival will take place from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, offering visitors free entry and a programme filled with tastings, handmade sweets and activities for children.



Visitors can expect a selection of handmade chocolates, pralines, cakes and other sweet specialties, with plenty of opportunities to sample different products throughout the weekend.

Families with children will also find a range of activities, including chocolate workshops designed for young visitors. Meanwhile, Thermomix will host live demonstrations and chocolate tastings during the event.

ČokoFest will also offer the chance to win several prizes. One of the main giveaways is a weekend drive in a Chery Tiggo 7, provided by Mach Motors. Visitors can also enter to win a ČokoBox and other sweet prizes.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by ČokoFest / Čokoládový Festival (@cokofestcz)

With Christmas just around the corner, the festival could also be a good place to find original gifts for chocolate lovers.

ČokoFest takes place at Novo Plaza Shopping Centre in Prague 4, and admission is free throughout all three days.

World.title: Micro Praha Festival Returns With 93 Watch Brands From 27 Countries
World.content:
The fourth edition of the international watch festival will take place at Fantova budova on November 28–29. Admission is free with online registration.

The Micro Praha Festival will return to Prague on November 28–29, bringing together 93 independent watch brands from 27 countries.



The fourth edition of the event will take place at Fantův sál inside the historic Fantova budova, near Prague’s Main Railway Station. Visitors will be able to discover new collections, try on watches and meet the people behind the brands.

Organisers say this year’s edition will be the largest so far, with microbrands and established independent watchmakers exhibiting alongside each other for the first time.

Brands from countries including Switzerland, Germany, the United States, Canada, France, the Netherlands, Japan, Taiwan and the Czech Republic will take part. Several exhibitors will be appearing in Prague and Central Europe for the first time.

Among the newcomers are New York-based Brew, known for watches inspired by coffee culture; MING, which focuses on experimental designs and engineering; Atelier Wen, specialising in watches with hand-crafted guilloché dials; and Lorier, a brand recognised for its vintage-inspired designs.

Chrono24 Joins as Main Festival Sponsor

The 2026 edition will also see Chrono24, the international online marketplace for luxury watches, join the festival as its primary sponsor and partner.

Representatives from the company will be present throughout the weekend to discuss the watch market, industry trends and the platform’s latest features. KB Bank is also listed among this year’s primary sponsors.

The festival was founded in 2023 by Bhanu Chopra and Ondrej Vislocký, two watch enthusiasts who wanted to create a platform for smaller independent brands in Central Europe.

Chopra is a watch journalist who previously served as editor-in-chief of Revolution USA, while Vislocký is a Prague-based photographer whose work has appeared in international watch publications and brand catalogues.

The two also co-own INFINTY Watches, a specialist retailer of microbrand and independent watches in central Prague.

World.title: Record Number of Stores to Join Czechia’s National Food Collection
World.content:
On Saturday, November 14, more than 3,500 retail stores across the Czech Republic will take part in the national food collection, a major increase from last year’s 2,250.

The event, organized by the Czech Federation of Food Banks and the Czech Trade and Tourism Association, will run from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.



Donations will include non-perishable food and personal hygiene items, which will later be distributed to families and individuals in need. Starting Tuesday, people can also contribute through six online retailers, where the food collection will continue for two weeks.

Organizers say the number of participating outlets has been steadily growing, showing greater public involvement each year. When the initiative began in 2013, donations could be made at 750 stores.

During last year’s autumn round, 702 tons of food and hygiene products were gathered—34 tons less than the previous year. According to organizers, the lower figure may have resulted from earlier donations made in September, when the public responded to flood relief efforts.

The food collection takes place twice a year, in spring and autumn.

Aleš Slavíček, Chairman of the Czech Federation of Food Banks, noted that the two annual collections together provide about 10% of the non-perishable food needed each year by Czech food banks. “Many people in our society still struggle to put food on the table,” Slavíček said at a press conference in Prague. “The food collection is a simple way for anyone to help those who are facing difficult times.”

The federation recommends donating canned food, baby food, soups, powdered milk, butter, rice, legumes, pasta, and personal care products.

A large portion of the donations goes to single mothers, who are among the most frequent recipients of food bank assistance.

World.title: Prague Welcomed 2.3 Million Visitors This Summer, Up 3% Year-on-Year
World.content:
Prague welcomed nearly 2.32 million visitors between July and September 2026, a 3 percent increase compared with the same period last year.

The number of Czech visitors rose faster than international arrivals, although foreign tourists continued to account for more than 80 percent of all guests.



Visitors recorded a total of 5.51 million overnight stays in the capital, up 3.8 percent year-on-year, according to figures released Monday by the Czech Statistical Office (CZSO).

Accommodation establishments across Prague registered 402,021 domestic guests during the third quarter, a 9.4 percent increase from a year earlier. The number of international visitors reached more than 1.91 million, representing growth of 1.7 percent.

Foreign tourists accounted for approximately 4.79 million overnight stays, compared with 725,167 by Czech visitors. The average stay was 2.4 nights. International guests spent an average of 2.5 nights in Prague, while domestic visitors stayed for 1.8 nights.

Germany remained the largest source of international visitors, with 274,885 guests. The United States ranked second with 172,126 visitors, followed by Poland with 128,076.

Arrivals from Taiwan increased by 27 percent year-on-year, followed by Israel at 26 percent and Ireland at 23 percent.

Hotel occupancy in Prague has also continued to recover. According to PCT, the average occupancy rate reached 78 percent this year, approximately 12 percent higher than in 2023. In September, occupancy at luxury hotels stood at 83 percent.

PCT has increasingly focused its marketing campaigns on visitors over the age of 30 with an interest in culture, history and architecture. The strategy aims to strengthen Prague’s position as a cultural destination rather than a place primarily associated with cheap drinking and party tourism.

Across the Czech Republic, collective accommodation establishments recorded 8.17 million guests during the third quarter of 2026.

World.title: Prague Ice Rinks Guide This Winter: Opening Dates, Prices and Locations
World.content:
As temperatures fall, public ice rinks are beginning to reopen across Prague for the 2026–27 winter season.

Several districts have already confirmed opening dates, while others are still finalising their winter programmes. From free skating in Smíchov to rinks beneath the Žižkov Television Tower and on the Letná Plain, residents and visitors will have plenty of options in the coming months.

Here is what has been announced so far.



Prague 1

The Na Františku ice rink is scheduled to open on November 13. Public skating will begin at 8 a.m., with closing times varying between 6:30 p.m. and 8:30 p.m., depending on the day. Skate rentals, refreshments and a heated tent will be available.

A second rink is expected to open on Wenceslas Square on November 28. It will operate daily in four sessions between 9 a.m. and 10 p.m.

A two-hour ticket will cost 200 CZK for adults and 100 CZK for children under 15. Visitors will be able to rent skates and helmets, while skating aids for children, skate sharpening and storage facilities will also be available.

It remains unclear whether the rinks at Ovocný trh and Čapadlo will return this winter.

Prague 2

Three outdoor ice rinks are planned in Prague 2.

The rinks at Havlíčkovy sady, also known as Grébovka, and Svatopluk Čech Park are scheduled to open on November 20. A third rink, located in Folimanka Park beneath the Nusle Bridge, is expected to follow on December 1.

All three venues are expected to operate daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. On weekdays between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m., the ice will be reserved for kindergartens and primary schools in Prague 2. Public skating will take place in the afternoons and throughout weekends.

On December 24 and December 31, the rinks will close at 3 p.m.

Prague 3

Prague 3 will again operate two public ice rinks.

Both are scheduled to open on November 14. One will be located in Mahlerovy sady, beneath the Žižkov Television Tower. A two-hour ticket will cost 150 CZK for adults and 50 CZK for children.

The second rink will return to the Pražačka sports complex. It will be open from 1 p.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekends. All-day admission will cost 120 CZK for adults and 80 CZK for children.

Skate rentals and refreshments will be available at both locations.

Prague 4

So far, one public ice rink has been confirmed in Prague 4.

The rink near the Prague Congress Centre, close to Vyšehrad metro station, is scheduled to open on November 13. It will operate from 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. during weekends.

Admission will cost 120 CZK per hour for adults and 80 CZK for children. Skate rentals and refreshments will also be available.

The opening date for the public rink in Podolí has not yet been announced.

Prague 5

Residents will once again be able to skate for free at the Aréna sportu on Hořejší nábřeží in Smíchov.

The rink is scheduled to open on November 13, with the official launch of the winter programme planned for the afternoon of November 20.

The venue will also host several themed events during the season, including St. Nicholas on Ice, a superhero-themed skating event and a Valentine’s Day programme.

Prague 6

Two Prague 6 locations are expected to offer outdoor skating this winter.

The rink in Ořechovka is provisionally scheduled to open around November 20, although the final date has yet to be confirmed.

At Vypich, a trial operation is expected to begin on November 27. The official opening is planned two days later and will coincide with the lighting of the local Christmas tree.

Prague 7

The ice rink on the Letná Plain is scheduled to open on November 14 and remain in operation until March 7, 2027.

It will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. A two-hour ticket will cost 150 CZK for adults and 120 CZK for children under 15.

Children under 15 who live in Prague 7 or attend school in the district will be able to skate free of charge.

Prague 8

Three outdoor ice rinks are planned in Prague 8.

On November 17, rinks are scheduled to open in Libeňské podzámčí and near the Krakov Cultural Centre in Bohnice. A third location near the Ládví swimming pool is expected to open on November 20.

Further information on admission and operating hours is expected to be announced by the district.

Prague 9

The rink in Park Přátelství in Střížkov has already opened for the season.

It has been operating since November 5 and is open daily from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. Morning hours are reserved for schools, while skate rentals are available to visitors.

Another rink will open in Zahrádky Park on December 5. It will also operate daily from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.

On weekdays between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m., schools will be able to reserve the ice. Visitors will have access to skate rentals and refreshments from Café Park Zahrádky.

Prague 10

Prague 10 will again open a public ice rink in Heroldovy sady in Vršovice.

The rink is scheduled to open on November 29, 2026, and is expected to remain in operation until February. The final closing date will depend on weather conditions.

With opening dates spread throughout November and early December, Prague’s winter skating season is now gradually getting underway. Several districts are still expected to release further details, and visitors should check local announcements before heading to the rink.

World.title: St. Martin’s Day 2026 in Prague: Where to Enjoy Traditional Goose
World.content:
St. Martin’s Day, which Czechs celebrate on November 11, is a holiday of good food and drink. Autumn slowly alternates with winter, and it begins to snow.

In the past, the economic year was ending at this time, and the landowners were preparing a feast for their people as a form of thanks, when they were also paid out their wages.

St. Martin’s Day in restaurants

You can be sure that almost every restaurant around mid-November will be offering its visitors a special St. Martin’s Day menu. What does it feature?

According to a tradition that has lasted for several centuries, geese were always roasted in the autumn, fresh cabbage was processed, and wine or beer was drunk. And today’s restaurants and pubs remain faithful to these basic ingredients.

Typically, you will be served liver pâté as an appetizer, followed by a strong broth with liver dumplings and noodles, which the chefs usually leave to simmer overnight, with the main course being roast goose with red or white cabbage and dumplings.

World.title: Prague Welcomes Tea Experts and Producers from Around the World
World.content:
Prague will welcome tea producers, experts and enthusiasts from around the world next weekend as Euro Tea Expo returns to the Czech capital for its second edition.

The two-day event, taking place on November 14 and 15, will bring together 37 exhibitors and focus on tea traditions from different parts of the world.



This year’s theme is “Chinese White Tea – The Heritage of Fuding.”

One of the main guests will be Master Lin Zhenchuan, a recognised inheritor of the traditional Fuding white tea-making techniques and founder of PINPINTEA.

Fuding white tea production is listed as part of China’s National Intangible Cultural Heritage.

With more than 30 years of experience, Master Lin will introduce visitors to the craftsmanship and history behind Fuding white tea through presentations and guided tastings. Guests will also be able to compare fresh and aged white teas and learn more about the ageing process.

The programme will feature demonstrations and presentations covering several tea traditions, including a traditional Shē ethnic group white tea performance, Sichuan gaiwan tea culture and long-spout teapot demonstrations.

Visitors can also learn about Kenyan tea, Japanese hojicha, ancient tea trees in Guangxi and the connection between tea and wellbeing. Beyond tea, the programme includes Taiji sessions, a tea and Taiji performance, and a Japanese Nerikiri confectionery workshop.

Organisers say this year’s edition will also expand beyond tea. Five European vegan brands will present plant-based products and sustainable lifestyle concepts as part of the event.

The first Euro Tea Expo was held in Prague in 2025 and brought together 33 exhibitors from 15 countries, attracting around 960 visitors. The organisers say the event aims to further strengthen connections between tea producers, professionals and consumers across Europe.

Event information

Dates: November 14–15, 2026

Opening hours: 10:00–18:00

Venue: U Slavie 1540/2a, Prague 10 – Vršovice

Theme: Chinese White Tea – The Heritage of Fuding

Exhibitors: 37

World.title: Canva Closes Prague Office as More Than 1,200 Jobs Are Cut Worldwide
World.content:
Canva is shutting down its Prague office, leaving only six employees from a workforce of around 50 as part of a company-wide restructuring affecting more than 1,200 people.

According to a former employee familiar with the situation, staff first received a company-wide email from Canva CEO Melanie Perkins outlining major changes.

Around 20 minutes later, employees whose positions were being eliminated received individual notifications.



Those affected were reportedly given about a week to collect their belongings. Access to most internal work systems was cut immediately, with employees retaining access only to services such as Slack and email.

The Prague closure comes during what has been described as the largest restructuring in Canva’s history and the company’s first major round of mass layoffs.

The changes are expected to affect 1,271 employees, equivalent to roughly 22 percent of the company’s workforce.

Prague Staff Point to Structure and AI Costs

A former member of the Prague office said two factors appear to have contributed to the decision.

The first is the company’s organizational structure. Responsibilities were divided across several layers, making communication and decision-making more difficult. The problem was further complicated by the ten- to eleven-hour time difference between Central Europe and Sydney.

The second issue, according to the former employee, involves the cost of artificial intelligence.

Canva has invested heavily in AI tools and technology, initially facing significant costs associated with computing power. Over the past month, the company has begun introducing its own models, although it remains unclear how much this could reduce the cost of processing graphics and other AI-related tasks.

The company has integrated tools and services linked to platforms such as ChatGPT and Claude. At the same time, users are increasingly able to generate images, designs and other visual content directly through competing AI systems without relying on Canva’s traditional platform.

World.title: VIDEOS: Áron Orbán arrested in case involving more than 100 Vietnamese nationals smuggled through Hungary
World.content:
Áron Orbán, the younger brother of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, was among four people arrested in a suspected human-smuggling and corruption case involving more than 100 Vietnamese nationals. Photographs published by HVG on Monday evening showed him arriving at the Gyorskocsi Street detention facility in Budapest in a police car.

The National Bureau of Investigation (NNI) and the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) carried out a coordinated operation on Monday morning in Budapest, Fót and Dunakeszi. Police confirmed that three men and one woman were detained. Two arrests were carried out by the Counter Terrorism Centre (TEK), as investigators had reason to believe that firearms might be present at the properties.

HVG reported that its photojournalist photographed Áron Orbán outside the detention facility on Monday evening. Footage released by the police earlier in the day also showed the suspects being taken away in handcuffs, with Orbán identifiable among them.

Check out the photos here.

More than 100 Vietnamese nationals allegedly involved

According to investigators, the four suspects helped Vietnamese nationals obtain visas through Hungarian diplomatic missions over several months in 2024. They allegedly charged each person a so-called recruitment fee and divided the proceeds among themselves. Authorities believe they may have assisted more than 100 people.

The Vietnamese applicants reportedly stated that they intended to stay in Hungary temporarily to attend short training courses. However, investigators say most did not attend the courses listed in their applications. Even those who did take part allegedly failed to leave Hungary before their visas expired.

According to the police, the applicants’ actual intention was to use Hungary as a route to Western Europe, where they hoped to find better living conditions.

Orbán also suspected of influence peddling

The NNI suspects all four individuals of human smuggling committed as part of a criminal organisation for financial gain. The NVVH has additionally questioned one of the men on suspicion of influence peddling as an instigator.

In a separate statement, the NVVH said the person brought in had allegedly invoked political connections and influence to request an unlawful advantage through an intermediary from the head of a labour recruitment company. In return, he allegedly promised to arrange the company’s reinstatement on the register of priority employers. The authority did not identify the person by name, but the description matches the case involving Áron Orbán.

During searches at four locations lasting several hours, investigators seized documents, electronic data and other potential evidence. The NNI suspects all four individuals of human smuggling committed as part of a criminal organisation for financial gain. The NVVH has additionally questioned one of them on suspicion of influence peddling as an instigator.

The investigation is ongoing, and authorities are planning to seek measures restricting the suspects’ freedom. Europol also supported the coordinated operation.

Find our earlier relevant article here: PM Magyar: Viktor Orbán’s brother has been detained on human-smuggling suspicion

Earlier reports linked Orbán to visa arrangements

Áron Orbán’s business connections and alleged involvement in visa arrangements had previously been investigated by Telex. The news site published an extensive investigation into the matter in 2025, following the leak of a recording in which Orbán discussed visa applications with a government official.

On Monday, Prime Minister Péter Magyar initially said, citing press reports, that Viktor Orbán’s brother had been detained on suspicion of human smuggling. Former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán subsequently described the case as a political attack, writing that he was the real target and that his brother was merely being used as a tool.

World.title: Orbán government allegedly discussed a EUR 5 billion loan from China weeks before parliamentary elections
World.content:
Hungary’s Orbán government reportedly held discussions with China over a financing framework worth up to EUR 5 billion in the weeks before the country’s parliamentary elections, according to investigative outlet Átlátszó, which obtained a draft agreement between the Hungarian Ministry of National Economy and China’s state-owned Export-Import Bank (CEXIM).

Orbán government apparently wanted an even bigger loan from China

The document, prepared in spring 2026, outlines a possible expansion of financial cooperation between Budapest and Beijing. The proposed framework could have supported infrastructure, transport and energy projects across Hungary, including railway developments, geothermal energy, the battery industry and small modular nuclear reactors.

The EUR 5 billion figure, currently equivalent to approximately HUF 1.8 trillion, would have been five times the size of the EUR 1 billion Chinese loan Hungary drew down in 2024, widely described at the time as a major Chinese financing deal.

However, the draft does not represent a signed agreement or a confirmed loan. It contains no final interest rates, repayment periods or specific allocations for individual projects. Átlátszó claimed the inclusion of proposed amendments nevertheless indicated that substantive negotiations may have taken place.

Financing could have included yuan-denominated bonds

The draft reportedly envisaged several potential funding mechanisms, including project-specific loans, investment financing instruments and capital market transactions. It also mentioned the possibility of issuing so-called panda bonds and dim sum bonds, which would allow Hungary to raise funds in Chinese yuan on international markets.

Financing could have been denominated in euros, US dollars or yuan. The document did not establish whether the proposed framework would have resulted in a single borrowing arrangement or several separate transactions.

The Ministry of National Economy’s successor, the Ministry of Economy and Energy, and the Hungarian Government Debt Management Agency (ÁKK) were approached for comment by Átlátszó. The outlet said it had not received responses to its questions at the time of publication. It also remains unclear whether the negotiations led to any subsequent agreement or borrowing.

China’s expanding financial role in Hungary

CEXIM has already played a significant role in Hungary’s infrastructure financing. The bank provided funding for the Hungarian section of the Budapest–Belgrade railway, a project whose financial terms and costs have attracted sustained scrutiny.

In 2024, Hungary also drew down a EUR 1 billion loan from three Chinese financial institutions, including CEXIM, the China Development Bank and the Hungarian branch of Bank of China. The transaction was not publicly announced by the Orbán government at the time and was identified through debt management data.

Chinese financing has been a key component of the Orbán government’s ‘Eastern Opening’ policy, which sought to strengthen economic ties with Asian countries. Chinese companies have also expanded their presence in Hungary through major industrial investments, particularly in the battery and electric vehicle sectors.

The proposed EUR 5 billion framework could have extended this cooperation into additional areas, including geothermal energy and small modular nuclear reactors. The draft, however, did not identify specific projects or establish the conditions under which Chinese financing might have been provided.

Long-term costs and transparency concerns

The potential expansion of Chinese lending raises questions about Hungary’s future debt obligations and the transparency of financing arrangements. Foreign-currency borrowing can expose governments to exchange-rate risks, while the economic benefits of funded projects must be weighed against repayment costs.

The draft agreement does not establish that Hungary borrowed EUR 5 billion or that CEXIM committed to providing the funds. It does, however, suggest that the Orbán government was considering a substantial expansion of its financial cooperation with China shortly before the election.

World.title: Tragedy: Worker dies in fatal accident at industrial gas plant in Hungary
World.content:
A worker died in a fatal accident at the Kazincbarcika facility of Linde Gáz Magyarország on Monday morning, 9 November. The company confirmed the death and said it had immediately secured the area and suspended operations at the industrial gas plant.

Fatal accident at gas plant

The incident was first reported by RTL Híradó, which received confirmation from the company. Linde Gáz Magyarország said the accident posed no further risk to employees, people living nearby or the environment.

The company, a leading supplier of industrial, medical and speciality gases, also said it was working closely with the relevant authorities. It expressed its condolences to the deceased employee’s family and colleagues.

Police investigating the circumstances of the accident

World.title: Austrian woman kidnapped and tied up in van for three days by Hungarian man
World.content:
A 62-year-old Austrian woman was allegedly kidnapped, tied up and held captive in a modified van for three days during a short trip to Hungary with a 41-year-old Hungarian acquaintance.

Woman reportedly lured across the border by Hungarian acquaintance

The woman, from the Innviertel region of Upper Austria, reported the incident to police in Braunau on Saturday, claiming she had been assaulted, threatened with a firearm and detained in appalling conditions. The case was reported by Austrian media outlet Krone.

According to investigators, the pensioner had recently received a substantial sum of cash following the sale of a property. Her Hungarian acquaintance allegedly became aware of the money and persuaded her to travel to Hungary for a brief holiday.

Victim allegedly confined in van and threatened

The woman was reportedly taken to Győrújbarát, around 400 kilometres from her home, where the suspect allegedly knocked her down, restrained her and locked her in the cargo compartment of a specially prepared van in a wooded area.

She is said to have been held between 4 and 6 November, during which time the man allegedly demanded money and repeatedly threatened her with a firearm. The victim reportedly sustained significant injuries, including severe bruising, bleeding and marks from the restraints, and later required hospital treatment.

As the woman’s family repeatedly attempted to contact her, and amid increasing intimidation, the suspect allegedly abandoned his plan and drove her back to Austria. Before releasing her, he reportedly threatened to seriously harm her family if she reported the incident to police.

Hungarian suspect arrested in Austria

Following the woman’s report, Austrian police launched an investigation and established the identity and whereabouts of the suspect through cross-border inquiries. The Ried Public Prosecutor’s Office ordered his arrest, which was carried out by the Cobra special operations unit at a residential property in Maria Schmolln, Upper Austria.

During questioning, the 41-year-old Hungarian reportedly made a comprehensive confession. Prosecutors confirmed that the woman had been held captive from 4 to 6 November. The modified van allegedly used in the incident was recovered in Hungary. The suspect was subsequently transferred to Ried Prison.

He is being investigated on suspicion of unlawful deprivation of liberty, aggravated coercion and grievous bodily harm. Austrian authorities said he had not previously been known to the police in the country.

World.title: Hungarian bank OTP arbitrarily closes refugees’ accounts while asking for non-existent documents
World.content:
Hungary’s largest bank, OTP, is facing an investigation by the country’s ombudsman following allegations that it discriminated against officially recognised refugees by unilaterally closing their existing bank accounts.

Russian psychologist loses access to six-year-old account

The proceedings were initiated after the Hungarian Helsinki Committee, a human rights organisation, filed a complaint claiming that the bank had refused to accept documents confirming refugees’ legal status and had demanded residence permits they were not required to possess.

The Committee has highlighted the case of Aleksandr, a Russian psychologist who was forced to leave his home country and has lived in Hungary since 2019. He was officially recognised as a refugee last year, but subsequently lost access to his six-year-old OTP account.

OTP didn’t accept official documents

During a routine customer identification procedure aimed at preventing money laundering, Aleksandr sought to update his documents. According to the Helsinki Committee, OTP refused to accept his refugee status papers, including an official certificate issued by the immigration authority. The bank reportedly told him he could either close the account voluntarily or have it terminated by the institution, potentially losing access to his money.

He eventually transferred his savings to an account he had previously opened at another bank. The organisation says the case is not isolated. Other refugees, including Russian and Palestinian nationals, have allegedly faced similar treatment, with some having their funds frozen and bank cards blocked.

A separate case involved a Russian refugee student and his mother, whose accounts were terminated after the bank had previously apologised for requesting a residence permit on what it acknowledged was an incorrect legal basis.

Make things easier with professional support in English. Explore Daily News Hungary’s Services in English and find the help you need.

Refugees allegedly asked to provide documents they cannot obtain

The Helsinki Committee argues that the bank’s requirement is impossible to meet. Unlike other foreign nationals, officially recognised refugees and people granted subsidiary protection do not hold residence permits. Their legal status is closer to that of Hungarian citizens, who identify themselves using personal identity cards and address cards.

The organisation says no Hungarian law requires refugees to provide residence permits to access banking services. It alleges that OTP has nevertheless continued to rely on its internal rules and interpretation of legislation.

The bank has maintained its position in its response to the ombudsman, according to the Helsinki Committee. The organisation contends that internal policies or a mistaken interpretation of the law cannot override statutory requirements.

Investigation could have wider implications

The ombudsman’s investigation follows the Committee’s action as a public interest claimant. The outcome could have implications beyond OTP, with the human rights organisation hoping the proceedings will also provide guidance to other financial institutions.

The allegations have raised concerns about refugees’ access to essential financial services, including receiving wages and paying everyday bills. OTP has not been independently established to have acted unlawfully; the matter is now subject to the ombudsman’s proceedings.

World.title: Man sexually assaults 15-year-old girl then chases her with running chainsaw in Hungary
World.content:
Prosecutors in northeastern Hungary have brought charges against a repeat offender accused of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl at his home before chasing her and her boyfriend down the street with a running chainsaw. The prosecution is seeking a prison sentence, a ban on holding public office and no possibility of parole.

According to the Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén County Chief Prosecutor’s Office, the incident took place in January last year, when the accused invited several guests to his family home in Borsod County. Among them were a male acquaintance and another man who attended with his 15-year-old girlfriend. The group consumed alcohol during the evening.

The accused allegedly approached the girl on the veranda and made a sexual proposition. When she refused, he restrained her hands and sexually assaulted her, according to prosecutors.

She managed to escape by biting his arm.

Couple fled as man followed with chainsaw

The girl ran to her boyfriend and asked him to leave the house with her. The accused allegedly tried to prevent them from leaving, leading to a physical confrontation with the boyfriend, whom he struck once.

The couple eventually managed to escape when another guest arrived at the property.

However, the accused then allegedly followed them into the street carrying a running chainsaw, waving it around and threatening them. The girl sought police assistance from a public telephone box before taking refuge in a nearby house.

Prosecutors seek prison sentence without parole

The Sátoraljaújhely District Prosecutor’s Office has charged the man with aggravated sexual assault and other offences, the Hungarian news agency MTI reported on Monday, citing Zsolt Jogg, deputy press spokesperson for the county chief prosecutor’s office.

The accused has a criminal record and is classified as a repeat offender. Prosecutors are seeking a prison sentence and a ban on holding public office, and have also proposed that he should not be eligible for conditional release.

World.title: Airbnb says short-term rentals play small role in Hungary’s housing crisis – But bring millions to economy
World.content:
Airbnb says short-term rentals account for only a tiny share of Hungary’s housing stock, while making a significant contribution to tourism and the wider economy. According to the platform’s latest analysis, Hungarian hosts welcomed 1.4 million guests in 2025, with Airbnb-related activity contributing an estimated €351 million to the country’s GDP and supporting around 13,600 jobs.

The company argues that Hungary’s housing affordability problems are rooted primarily in insufficient new construction, rising property prices and the large number of vacant homes, rather than short-term holiday rentals. According to Portfolio, its findings come amid continuing debate over restrictions on Airbnb-style accommodation, particularly in Budapest.

How many homes are actually rented out?

Airbnb estimates that entire properties rented out for at least 120 nights in 2025 accounted for just 0.12% of Hungary’s approximately 4.6 million homes. The company describes the 120-night threshold as a strict illustrative measure, while acknowledging that it does not necessarily mean these properties would otherwise have been available for long-term tenants.

By comparison, the company cites Hungarian Central Statistical Office (KSH) figures showing around 564,000 vacant residential properties nationwide, equivalent to nearly 12% of the housing stock.

Airbnb also points to the scale of property price increases: between 2015 and the fourth quarter of 2025, Hungarian house prices rose by 290%, according to Eurostat data cited in its analysis. Rents increased by 105% over the same period.

What Airbnb guests bring to local businesses

The platform estimates that guests staying in Hungarian Airbnb accommodation spent more than €438.9 million in the country in 2025. Beyond accommodation, 38% of their spending went to restaurants and other hospitality businesses, while 20% was spent on entertainment and cultural activities.

Retail accounted for 18% of additional spending, groceries for 14% and local transport for 10%.

The company also says that around 80% of Hungarian hosts rented out just one entire property last year. Their average annual hosting income was approximately €4,600. In Airbnb’s own survey, 70% of respondents said they used the extra income to cover rising living costs.
