World.title: Making room
World.content: Explore “Tafasahu: Make Room,” an exhibition by Saudi architect and artist Nada Al-Mulla that reimagines the traditional majlis. It is taking place at the Ithra Museum gallery. More details on the Ithra app.

World.title: Moonlight Cinema
World.content:
Watch the latest films beneath starlit skies at VOX Moonlight Cinema, an open-air experience at OUR Habitas in Ashar Valley, offering panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Screenings run until Nov. 15.

For more details, check the experiencealula.com.

World.title: Canadian PM condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman held a telephone call on Monday with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.

At the beginning of the call, the Canadian prime minister expressed Canada’s condemnation of Houthi attacks against the Kingdom.

He also affirmed Canada’s solidarity with the Kingdom in the face of any threats to its security, the safety of its citizens, and the well-being of residents.

The two leaders also discussed relations between their nations, avenues for joint cooperation, and ways to further strengthen and develop these ties across various fields.

World.title: Saudi officials meet Norwegian and Swedish ambassadors in Riyadh
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Vice Minister of Finance Abdulmuhsen Al-Khalaf met Norway’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Kjersti Tromsdal at the Ministry of Finance in Riyadh on Monday.

They discussed economic and financial issues of mutual interest, as well as ways to strengthen cooperation in international development, the Finance Ministry said on X.

Saudi Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Adel Al-Jubeir received Sweden’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Maria Hakansson in Riyadh on Sunday.

The parties discussed issues of mutual interest, the Foreign Ministry said on X.

World.title: Saudi FM takes part in G7 session on AI
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan took part in an expanded session of the G7 and invited partners on artificial intelligence in Paris on Monday, the Saudi Press Agency reported.



The session discussed the implications of rapid advances in technology and frontier AI models for the global strategic environment and international security, as well as ways to strengthen international coordination to address AI-related risks.



Discussions also focused on balancing the pursuit of innovation with the safe and responsible development and use of these technologies in order to strengthen the ability to address challenges and safeguard global security and stability.



The G7 ‌comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States, as well as the European Union.



Ministers from Saudi Arabia, Egypt, South Korea, Ukraine, and Brazil are also attending the two-day summit.



The Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran conflict, energy and artificial intelligence are among the main topics for discussion.



On the sidelines of the summit, Prince Faisal met with his counterparts from Germany, South Korea, France, and Britain.



Topics of conversation with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul included regional developments, diplomatic efforts aimed at maintaining security and stability in the region, and ensuring freedom of navigation and the safety of maritime corridors.

Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul shake hands in Paris. (SPA)

Prince Faisal and South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun discussed avenues for cooperation and partnership between their nations and exchanged views on current regional issues and efforts being made regarding them.

Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun shake hands in Paris. (SPA)

The meeting with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot focussed on ongoing Houthi attacks on the Kingdom and joint efforts to contain crises in the region and mitigate their repercussions.

Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot shake hands in Paris. (SPA)

Prince Faisal and British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband addressed joint efforts to maintain the security of navigation and the safety of maritime corridors and restore security and stability in the region.

World.title: Krakow shooting rampage suspect dies amid hunt for motive
World.content:
KRAKOW: A Polish man accused of carrying out a deadly shooting spree in Krakow died in hospital on Monday, two days after he was critically wounded in a gun battle with police, authorities said.

But after he had originally been linked to the far right, prosecutors said that his reasons for killing nine people, including three family members, remained unclear.

The 24-year-old, dressed in military garb, allegedly opened fire with a semi-automatic rifle in a Krakow square, killing six people.

The bodies of his parents and a sister were found at the family home in another town.

Two police officers, who were seriously wounded in the chase, shot the man, named by media as Michal Oksinski, at an intersection near the city’s Main Market Square.

After three operations, the suspect was declared dead around 4:30 am (0330 GMT), regional authorities said.

“We inform you that the perpetrator of the tragic events died this morning in the hospital,” regional police said in a post on X.

Authorities had previously said the man had been “fascinated by far-right ideologies” and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the shooting — the deadliest in the country since the fall of communism in 1989 — an act of “terrorism.”

But at a press conference on Monday, prosecutors said that there was no evidence tying the suspect to any particular political bent.

“We do not have findings that we could, in a responsible way, categorically state that he was inspired by any particular ideology,” national prosecutor’s office spokesman Przemyslaw Nowak said.

“It is far too early to comment on the motives ... We have not found any obvious symbols that are generally associated with a particular political movement, whether far right or far left,” he added.

An interior ministry spokeswoman told Polish radio that the “many emblems and patches” on Oksinski’s clothing were being analyzed as part of the investigation.

- Firearms permit review -

Six people, including an Austrian woman and a British man, were killed in the Krakow shooting spree, and 15 others were wounded, according to authorities.

The wounded included Austrian, British, German, Portuguese and Russian nationals. Authorities said the injured were in “stable” condition on Monday.

While Oksinski’s motives are unclear, investigators are treating the shooting spree as a terrorist incident.

He had no prior criminal record, according to investigators cited by Polish media.

Along with his father, the suspect was a member of a shooting club. Investigators seized 11 firearms during the search.

His grandmother said Oksinski had obtained a gun license this year, according to Polish media.

Following the shooting, the interior ministry announced a review of the conditions for granting gun licenses, with the license-holder’s medical records to be updated regularly.

Poland has seen a sharp uptick in the number of firearms permits. In 2025, more than 50,000 new licenses were awarded, bringing the total to 411,000, according to the police.

World.title: What We Are Reading Today: ‘Rethinking the Tenth Century’ by Wu Hung
World.content:
In the standard narrative of Chinese painting, the half century spanning the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms (907–960 CE) is often considered a transitional period between the art of the Tang and Northern Song dynasties.

In this beautifully illustrated book, acclaimed art historian Wu Hung draws on new archaeological evidence and research methods to challenge this perspective, identifying a considerably broader period in which Chinese painting evolved in significant ways.

From the late ninth to the early 11th century, Chinese painters explored diverse new mediums, subject matter, brushwork, and styles. Providing a fuller assessment of landscape painting during this period, he establishes a new foundation for exploring stylistic inventions, architectural contexts, and symbolism.

World.title: Syria seeks to expand UNRWA cooperation on reconstruction projects
World.content:
DAMASCUS: Syria’s Ministry of Public Works and Housing and the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East discussed strengthening cooperation on reconstruction projects and the rehabilitation of public service facilities during a meeting in Damascus on Monday.

The talks brought together Minister of Public Works and Housing Mustafa Abdul Razzaq and Olaf Becker, UNRWA’s director of affairs in the Syrian Arab Republic.

The two sides reviewed their respective areas of work and ongoing projects, and discussed opportunities for cooperation through institutions affiliated with the ministry and vocational training centers.

They considered exchanging technical expertise and information, including guidelines for assessing building damage after disasters.

The meeting concluded with an agreement to designate a liaison point to coordinate the exchange of data and technical standards and maintain communication on areas of mutual cooperation.

The arrangement is intended to help align working methods and coordinate efforts, the ministry said.

Abdul Razzaq stressed the importance of cooperation among government institutions, international organizations and the private sector at the current stage.

The discussions come as Syria faces the need to rehabilitate infrastructure and public service facilities, strengthen technical expertise and make better use of available resources to support recovery and reconstruction and improve services for residents.

On Jan. 15, Abdul Razzaq held separate talks with a World Bank technical mission on reconstruction and the identification of priorities, particularly in heavily damaged and densely populated areas. The discussions included possible solutions for addressing stalled housing projects.

World.title: Iraqi oil price for Asian markets reduced by $6 per barrel
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The price of Iraqi oil destined for Asian markets has seen a further reduction for December 2026 shipments, reflecting ongoing adjustments to official selling prices for crude in response to shifts in global oil markets.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has decided to reduce the price of Basra Medium crude by $6 per barrel compared to the November pricing, setting the discount at $8.80 per barrel relative to the Oman/Dubai crude benchmark.

The reduction also extended to Basra Heavy crude; SOMO set its price for December at a discount of $11.80 per barrel against the Oman/Dubai average, compared to a discount of $5.80 per barrel in November.

The decisions follow months of dramatic swings in Iraqi oil discounts, interruptions to Gulf shipping, and an increase in the cost of insurance and transportation.

SOMO announced on Monday a reduction in the official selling price for Basra Medium crude destined for Asia for the month of December.

The state-owned firm set the price for this crude at a discount of $8.80 per barrel relative to the Oman/Dubai average, compared to a discount of $2.80 per barrel in the November pricing.

The company also set the official selling price for Basra Heavy crude destined for Asia in December at a discount of $11.80 per barrel.

This significant reduction in the price of Iraqi crude reflects an effort to enhance the attractiveness of Basra crude in Asian markets, which serve as the primary destination for the country’s oil exports.

World.title: Iraqi PM secretly visits Iran following Trump phone call
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – As part of regional mediation efforts, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi made an unexpected, secret visit to Tehran on Friday to meet with Iranian parliament speaker and senior negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

To help resolve the conflict between Iran and the United States, al-Zaidi’s short journey concentrated on diplomatic initiatives and de-escalation efforts.

The visit came after a phone conversation between al-Zaidi and US President Donald Trump, with the Iraqi government attempting to prevent the country from being involved in a larger regional conflict, according to reports quoting official and media sources.

Iranian officials, including top negotiator Ghalibaf, presented Tehran’s two-day plan at the discussions, stressing that Washington must respect Iran’s fundamental rights, lift sanctions, end naval blockade, and free frozen assets as part of the negotiations.

Iraqi Ambassador to Iran Yasser al-Hajjaj confirmed that a recent visit to Tehran—involving an Iraqi delegation or Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi—was private and unannounced, coinciding with reports of regional diplomatic discussions.

World.title: Iraqi, KRG PMs discuss 2027 federal budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi received on Monday the Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), Masrour Barzani, in Baghdad to discuss Iraqi Kurdistan’s financial entitlements and its share in the draft 2027 federal budget.

The precise amount allocated to the Kurdistan region of Iraq is a major source of disagreement. Approximately 12.7 percent is what the first draft budget suggests.

The KRG, on the other hand, is strongly advocating for 14.14 percent, claiming that the budget has to take into account Iraqi Kurdistan’s real population statistics from the most recent census.

Barzani has openly said that any distribution that falls short of this population-based proportion is unfair.

The discussions included establishing conclusive procedures to address persistent delays in the payment of salaries for Iraqi Kurdistan’s civil servants.

Recently, al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s resolve to ensure that Kurdish public sector workers receive the same treatment as their colleagues in other Iraqi provinces.

The diplomatic effort tackles long-standing disagreements on constitutional rights, compliance with Iraqi Federal Court decisions, and oil income sharing.

The meeting takes place at a critical time. The Iraqi cabinet is scheduled to discuss and submit the finalized draft budget bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq approaches OPEC to raise oil output ceiling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said that Iraq seeks to negotiate with OPEC to raise its oil output and obtain a larger export cap.

Although the country’s production capacity differs from its export capability, Khudair stated that Baghdad was still committed to the export quota set by OPEC.

Iraq’s discussions with OPEC took into account the challenges the country has faced over the past 50 years, as noted by Khudair.

The Iraqi minister indicated that Iraq deserves a rise in output to secure the financial revenues needed to expand infrastructure and implement government goals.

Additionally, Khudair reiterated Iraq’s commitment to the 4.43 million barrels per day production cap set by OPEC.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

According to al-Zaidi, the Oil Ministry will invite major foreign oil firms to a conference to attract investments, expertise, and technologies.

World.title: Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday.

Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections.

The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.”

“I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said.

Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday.

The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed.

“For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television.

“We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added.

– ‘They had enough’ –

Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat.

Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.”

“Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.”

In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms.

“They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.”

Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September.

Iranian state television said the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked overnight Sunday, hours after the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions there.

Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war.

Outright fighting has largely subsided, but Iran continues in its efforts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global energy supplies, while the US Navy maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

World.title: Drone attack targets Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A drone attack targeted on Sunday the Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq, forcing joint field operator Dana Gas to halt production entirely.

The strike hit a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tank, causing a large fire that was later extinguished.

The facility is the main source of energy for the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the largest gas field there.

Between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of power output have been cut off due to the stoppage of gas operations, reducing 70 to 80 percent of the energy grid’s overall capacity.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s major cities, including Erbil, Sulaimaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal, are no longer receiving direct electricity supply.

To safeguard vital infrastructure, including hospitals and water treatment facilities, Iraqi Kurdistan’s Ministry of Electricity declared that it is rerouting electricity from hydroelectric power plants and alternative fuel facilities.

Employees were evacuated to shelters, and no casualties or injuries have been reported, according to Dana Gas and Iraqi authorities.

The facility was temporarily closed in July due to security concerns resulting from escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, the scandal-hit AI visionary in a leather jacket
World.content:
New York – Chips made by US chip titan Nvidia push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, but its leader Jensen Huang is in the spotlight over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Unknown to the public just four years ago, the 63-year-old is a powerful entrepreneur, drawing stadium crowds as he presents cutting-edge components essential to the development of AI tools like ChatGPT.

Media reports last week said US intelligence officials believe Huang grew close to a Chinese executive who was funneling information to Beijing.

Nvidia’s board said on Sunday it had opened a probe into the CEO and co-founder, who acknowledged having been unfaithful to his wife and said he was “deeply sorry.”

Big tech’s insatiable appetite for chips designed by Nvidia, known as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), has catapulted the California chipmaker to a market valuation of $4.5 trillion, among the world’s largest.

Its meteoric rise has made Huang one of the world’s richest people — worth around $160 billion, according to Forbes — thanks to the roughly four percent stake he holds in the company he founded three decades ago with two friends in a Silicon Valley diner.

He has become a close informal adviser on AI to Donald Trump, traveling with the US president on Air Force One on a trip to Beijing earlier this year.

That is an area of concern to US officials who believe he has been involved with the alleged spy, Alice Huang, who is linked to a Singapore-based data center company, according to the New York Times.

Despite their shared surname, the pair are not related.

– Early life –

Born in Taipei in 1963, Jensen Huang — originally named Jen-Hsun — embodies the American success story.

At nine years old, he was sent away with his brother to boarding school in small-town Kentucky.

His uncle recommended the school to his Taiwanese parents believing it to be a prestigious institution, though it was actually a school for troubled youth.

Too young to be a student, Huang boarded there but attended a nearby public school alongside the children of tobacco farmers. With his poor English, he was bullied and forced to clean toilets — a two-year ordeal that transformed him.

“We worked really hard, we studied really hard, and the kids were really tough,” he recounted in an interview with US broadcaster NPR.

But “the ending of the story is I loved the time I was there,” Huang said.

Brought home by his parents who had by then settled in the northwestern US state of Oregon, he graduated from university at just 20 and joined AMD, then LSI Logic, to design chips — his passion.

But he wanted to go further and founded Nvidia in 1993 to “solve problems that normal computers can’t,” using semiconductors powerful enough to handle 3D graphics, he said during an interview on the “No Priors” podcast.

– ‘As fast as we can’ –

Nvidia created the first GPU in 1999, riding the intersection of video games, data centers, cloud computing and now generative AI.

Always dressed in a black T-shirt and leather jacket, Huang sports a Nvidia logo tattoo and has a taste for sports cars.

One former high-ranking Nvidia employee described him to AFP as “the most driven person” he’d ever met.

He has rejected calls to deliberately slow down AI development even as some insiders warn the technology could threaten human existence within a decade.

“That kind of narrative is dramatic, it gets a lot of attention,” but “it’s not grounded on facts,” he told CBS News in September.

“We should go as fast as we can” on AI, but labs should not release products that are not safe, he said.

– Street food –

On visits to his native Taiwan, Huang is treated like a megastar, with fans crowding him for autographs and selfies as journalists follow him to the barber shop and his favorite night market.

“He has created the phenomena because of his personal charm,” noted Wayne Lin of Witology Market Trend Research Institute.

“A person like him must be very busy and his schedule should be full every day meeting big bosses. But he remembers to eat street food when he comes to Taiwan,” he said, calling Huang “unusually friendly.”

Over the years, Nvidia has taken care to project a drama-free image of Huang.

But the former employee painted a more nuanced picture, describing a “very paradoxical” individual fiercely protective of his employees but also capable, within Nvidia’s executive circle, of “ripping people to shreds” over major mistakes or poor choices.

World.title: World Bank backs Iraq’s shift toward program and performance budgeting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The World Bank reaffirmed its institutional support on Monday, November 9, 2026, for the Iraqi Ministry of Finance’s ongoing modernization agenda, focusing on technical requirements to transition Iraq’s fiscal planning toward a program- and performance-based budgeting framework.

According to a Ministry of Finance statement reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Senior Undersecretary Abdul-Hasan Jamal convened an extensive technical working session with a World Bank mission.

The deliberations were attended by the directors general of the Public Debt and Information Technology departments, alongside the ministry’s dedicated project implementation task force, to evaluate core prerequisites and execution roadmaps for the budgeting shift.

Jamal emphasized the necessity of finalizing statutory and regulatory frameworks, conducting rigorous cost-benefit assessments, and clearly designating spending units across line ministries.

He noted that moving away from conventional line-item budgeting to performance-driven fiscal management aligns directly with broader economic and administrative reform programs, ensuring cohesive institutional alignment among spending entities.

For its part, the World Bank delegation reiterated its commitment to supporting public financial management (PFM) reforms across Iraq, underlining that digitizing accounting frameworks and automating treasury workflows remain essential catalysts for curbing fiscal leakage, improving capital allocation, and enhancing aggregate expenditure efficiency.

World.title: Chinese nationals stream from poor localities of Dhaka, claim those are in Delhi: Report
World.content:
The setting is Dhaka, but the audience in China is told it is Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The setting is Dhaka, but the audience in China is told it is Delhi. An estimated total of over 150 Chinese nationals have been livestreaming from an underprivileged neighbourhood in Dhaka, falsely presenting it to their viewers back home as everyday life in India, an investigation by the Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo revealed.Equipped with two smartphones each - one used to stream live and the other with scripts - they broadcast from early morning until late at night. According to the report, the streamers focus on Sector 12 and Tekpara, which are dense, low-income settlements along a canal in Uttara town, located north of Dhaka, where they film along the tin-roofed houses. Local guides, hired for Tk 700 to Tk 800 (Rs 525-Rs 600) a day, assist the Chinese nationals in navigating the area.While most of these creators refused to speak to Prothom Alo, some only gave their names and nationality. A Chinese national named Fangyou, after being persuaded by a guide, said that such streams are broadcast on China-based platforms such as WeChat and Douyin (the mainland version of TikTok) as "part of product promotion activities".Google translations of their commentary, verified by four Bangladeshis who know Chinese, revealed misrepresentation.In one instance, a Chinese woman identifying herself as Mianmian showed the tin huts and said, "This is Delhi. Their homes are extremely dirty... and the law-and-order situation is poor."At a bridge flanked by tea stalls, another creator named Wang Wei could be heard telling his audience that locals were drinking "cow urine tea" prepared with contaminated river water. Some streamers claimed they were Chinese women married to Indian men living in these neighbourhoods, while promoting Chinese air conditioner brands seen on building walls.The continuous broadcasts have sparked anger among residents over violations of privacy. Locals, who talked to Prothom Alo, said that streamers routinely enter homes unannounced, sometimes even filming into bathrooms. When residents protest, the streamers apologise and leave, only to return soon after.Despite months of complaints from residents, the police have not monitored or regulated this activity. Mohammad Khalid Mansur, officer-in-charge of Uttara West Police Station, told Prothom Alo that officers were aware of the filming but attempts to pursue the matter have been hindered due to language barriers.

World.title: SC: Govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire staffer, improve efficiency
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has ruled govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire an employee to improve efficiency of administration and that the person aggrieved cannot challenge such a decision on the ground that other similarly placed employees have not met the same fate.

Upholding Chhattisgarh govt's decision to compulsorily retire five employees, a bench of Justices Manmohan and Shree Chandrashekhar said the principle of "every person must be heard before being punished", as enshrined in Article 311(2) of Constitution, is not applicable to cases of compulsory retirement because it is neither punitive nor casts aspersion upon an employee's conduct.

Justice Manmohan said, "The decision is founded upon the subjective satisfaction of competent authority that the employee's continued retention in service is no longer conducive to public interest."



Retirement must be based on bona fide assessment, says SC

Writing the judgement, Justice Manmohan said, âThe ultimate assessment as to whether an officer has become âdead woodâ or whether his continuance would be detrimental to administrative efficiency falls within the domain of the executive.â

Chhattisgarh additional advocate general Rajat Nair said decisions to compulsorily retire the five âassistantâ grade officers was arrived at in public interest for maintaining efficiency of administration after a two-tier scrutiny of their performance, efficiency, track records, integrity and annual confidential records.





When such decisions are challenged by aggrieved employees, courts need to re-appreciate or re-evaluate material considered by authorities. âThe court is concerned only with whether relevant material existed, whether such material was taken into consideration by competent authority, and whether the conclusion drawn therefrom is one which a reasonable person could have arrived at,â it said while rejecting the appeals.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It said, âThe power to compulsorily retire a govt servant under applicable service rules is of wide amplitude and is conditional principally by the requirement that the authority must form its opinion bona fide and upon relevant material. Mere fact that another officer, who may appear similarly placed, was not compulsorily retired cannot constitute a valid defence to an otherwise lawful order of compulsory retirement.

â

World.title: Delhi pollution on Diwali rockets to worst in 5 years
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi saw its most polluted Diwali day in five years, with AQI touching 376 at 4pm Nov 8, the worst since 2021. The city, however, narrowly escaped its worst post-Diwali pollution day in five years, with Monday's AQI touching 370 at 11am before improving to 344 by 4pm, better than 2025's post-Diwali air quality.

Diwali AQI in 2025 (Oct 20) was 345, 328 in 2024 (Oct 31), 218 in 2023 (Nov 12), 312 in 2022 (Oct 24) and 382 in 2021 (Nov 4). Post-Diwali AQI in 2025 was 351, 339 in 2024, 358 in 2023, 303 in 2022 and 462 in 2021. Diwali-eve this year, Nov 7, was the most polluted since 2016, with AQI of 369.

Meanwhile, several monitoring stations failed to report crucial AQI data. Initially, hourly data went missing for 35 air quality monitoring stations.



Although DPCC later updated data at some of its stations, several went blank at peak pollution hours, and only 47 contributed to average AQI on Diwali day. Delhi has 60 monitoring stations managed by DPCC, CPCB, IITM and IMD, of which one had been defunct for a few months.

Firecrackers emerged as the biggest contributor a day before Diwali (Chhoti Diwali), accounting for 41.1% of the total load, according to IITM data till 9am Nov 8.





On a wind and prayer, capital braces for uncertain times as winter sets in

While traces of lead, potassium and sulphur in the air were confirmed, officials said they can confirm the presence of mercury only in a long-term study.

At midnight on Nov 8, IITM recorded its highest average PM2.5 concentration, at 671.1 micrograms per cubic metre (Âµg/mÂ³). Among individual stations, Jahangirpuri in northwest Delhi recorded a peak of 4,985 Âµg/mÂ³ Sunday night and Monday morning.

However, DPCC later updated to park PM2.5 level of 776Âµg/mÂ³ at 11am Sunday. Mundka in west Delhi recorded PM2.5 level at 3,744 Âµg/mÂ³ at 2am, which remained unchanged, followed by 3,023.2Âµg/mÂ³ at JNU.

The prescribed 24-hour average national limit for PM2.5 is 60 Âµg/mÂ³.

The average PM2.5 concentration on Diwali 2026 stood at 257 Âµg/mÂ³, against 228 Âµg/mÂ³ last year, 201 Âµg/mÂ³ in 2024, 134 Âµg/mÂ³ in 2023, 176 Âµg/mÂ³ in 2022 and 318 Âµg/mÂ³ in 2021.

On Monday, Delhi saw the seasonâs first dense fog, with visibility dropping to 50m at Safdarjung at 6.30am, which kept the AQI in the upper range of very poor levels. However, a sudden, unusual shift in winds from northwesterly to strong easterly, aided by faster dispersion, kept stubble smoke from Punjab and Haryana at bay, preventing a sharper spike, especially when Punjab on Nov 8 saw the highest farm fire incidents of the season, at 1,152.

The post-Diwali reprieve, said experts, was more meteorological than the result of pollution-control measures. With winter conditions setting in, the wind reversal could bring back the familiar pollution cocktail, they added.

Gufran Beig, founder of System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research (SAFAR) and chair professor at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (NIAS), said Delhi was âvery luckyâ this year, not cleaner.

âAn unusual weather development associated with an approaching cyclone and a western disturbance caused winds to turn easterly from their persistent northwesterly direction. These winds, travelling at around 6.7 metres per second from the surface to nearly 400 metres, against the usual 3-4 m/s, helped disperse pollutants rapidly and prevented stubble-burning smoke from reaching Delhi,â he said. The easterlies were expected to persist until Tuesday morning, before winds potentially reverted to northwesterly.

Calling the situation a reflection of the regionâs worsening pollution-control battle, Anumita Roychowdhury of Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) said, âThis post-Diwali pollution crisis is the direct result of a toxic convergence of adverse winter meteorology, escalating pre-Diwali traffic gridlocks and a rise in contribution of farm fires. Firecrackers were an uncontrolled tipping point.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Delhi and the wider region, she added, were losing the battle to curb emissions from both continuous local sources and episodic spikes, at a very high health cost.

The scale of the firecracker contribution was even more stark in an analysis by Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at Envirocatalysts. He estimated that crackers added roughly 450 Âµg/mÂ³ to peak-hour PM2.5 concentrations and contributed around 270-400 Âµg/mÂ³, or more than half the PM2.5 Delhi residents breathed, during the 9pm-2am period.

Dahiya said pollution began building from around 8pm, peaked between 1am and 3am, and remained above 500 Âµg/mÂ³ for four hours.

World.title: Now, Cong-led Keralam govt follows Karnataka on 'ethanol test'
World.content:
Cong-led Keralam govt follows Karnataka on 'ethanol test'

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU/NEW DELHI/T'PURAM: Following in Congress-governed Karnataka's footsteps, the Congress-led govt of Keralam Monday started collecting petrol samples to test whether their ethanol content was more than the prescribed 20%, setting up a likely Centre-state confrontation over E20 fuel.Keralam civil supplies minister Anoop Jacob said officials collected six samples each from nine petrol pumps across Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur, in the presence of OMC representatives.PESO-approved bottles and trained officials were used, he said, adding that further rounds of testing would follow and prosecution would be initiated if excess blending was detected.This prompted Union minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi to say that states were free to conduct tests but they should avoid political mudslinging. "Let them conduct the tests, whether it is Karnataka or Keralam govt. We have scientific support for it," he said. The minister warned that those creating controversies for political purposes would have to face consequences. Gopi said Centre had permitted 20% blending after assessing scientific feasibility and was implementing the transition gradually.On Monday, Karnataka defended its third-party laboratory findings about ethanol levels of up to 31.2%, rejecting a joint rebuttal by three oil marketing companies - IOCL, BPCL and HPCL.State food and civil supplies minister Rizwan Arshad termed objections raised by the three OMCs "illogical" and accused them of trying to push for a fresh joint survey after recalibrating the ethanol mix.He said state govt would send its findings to Centre, seek changes in testing protocols and demand discounted prices for E20 petrol, stressing that higher ethanol content reduced mileage and raised the effective cost for consumers.Arshad said alleged blending of up to 30% was happening at six terminals where ethanol was mixed with petrol before distribution, not at retail outlets. Karnataka said authorised officials followed prescribed sampling procedures, with labels jointly signed by officials and dealers. After OMC laboratories failed to provide ethanol percentages for the initial 63 samples, the state sent them to NABL-accredited, ISO-certified third-party laboratories.The three OMCs had challenged Karnataka's Oct tests, questioning its sampling and laboratory methodology. They said it did not follow statutory procedures under Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel Control Order, IS 17021 standards or prescribed gas chromatography dilution protocols.

World.title: Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Despite vaccines being available to prevent several infections that can be particularly serious for older people, adult immunisation remains low in India. Influenza, pneumococcal disease and shingles are among the key vaccine-preventable illnesses that pose a risk to older people, but studies point to poor awareness and low uptake of these vaccines.

Ahead of World Immunisation Day Tuesday (Nov 10), the findings highlight a significant gap in protection beyond childhood.

A multicentre study of 4,998 people aged 60 and above across Chennai, Ballabgarh, Kolkata and Pune found only 1.4% had ever received an influenza vaccine. While just 19.7% had heard of influenza, 35.9% considered vaccines safe and 65.3% were unwilling to pay for vaccination. However, uptake rose to 29.7% when vaccines were offered free of cost at community health camps.



Published in 'BMC Public Health' in 2026, the study highlights gaps in awareness, acceptance and access to vaccination among older people.

The disease burden is substantial. A separate study published in 'Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses' in April 2026 estimated that influenza among Indians aged 60 and above accounted for 5.3 million respiratory infections, 36,149 hospitalisations and 84,613 deaths in 2021.





The researchers found that an annual influenza vaccination programme for older adults could be cost-effective under most of the scenarios assessed.

"Influenza and pneumococcal infections cause a significant burden among older Indians, accounting for an estimated 1.2 lakh deaths annually. Studies show that influenza vaccination can reduce influenza-associated pneumonia cases by 52% and deaths by 70%, while pneumococcal vaccination can lower hospitalisations by around 27% and deaths by 34%.

Yet vaccination coverage among the elderly remains very low," said Dr Neetu Jain, senior consultant, pulmonology, critical care and sleep medicine, PSRI Hospital.

"Annual flu and pneumococcal vaccination is particularly important for people above 60 and those with COPD, asthma, diabetes or heart disease, as infections can lead to serious complications, including respiratory failure and prolonged hospitalisation," she said.

Evidence is also emerging of the economic value of pneumococcal vaccination. A study published in 'Infectious Diseases and Therapy' in Oct 2026 examined the cost-effectiveness of a single dose of the 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) for older adults and people at higher risk. It found that the vaccine could be a cost-effective option compared with existing vaccination approaches.

Another infection of concern among older adults is shingles, caused by reactivation of the virus responsible for chicken pox.

It can lead to prolonged nerve pain, known as post-herpetic neuralgia. A 2026 paper in 'Indian Journal of Community Medicine' noted the lack of robust population-based data on shingles in India, while citing an estimate of around 45 lakh cases annually. An Indian phase-3 trial of the recombinant zoster vaccine, published in 'Vaccine' in 2025, reported an immune response in 85.7% of participants aged 50 and above.

"Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines can reduce cases of severe illness, hospitalisation and complications, particularly among older people and those with chronic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and COPD. Both are non-live vaccines and can be given to elderly people, including those with multiple conditions," said Dr Jatin Ahuja, infectious disease specialist, Apollo Hospitals, Delhi.

"India also needs to expand adult vaccination to cover shingles.

The two-dose recombinant zoster vaccine is recommended for adults aged 50 and above and offers over 90% protection. Tdap or Td boosters, hepatitis B and, where indicated, Covid-19 and RSV vaccines should also be considered," he said.

Goa has taken a step towards expanding vaccination beyond childhood through its Life-course Immunisation Policy 2026-2036, launched in Sept. The policy identifies influenza, pneumococcal and hepatitis B vaccination among its priorities for elderly, those with chronic illnesses, immunocompromised individuals and healthcare workers.

World.title: Delhi Police issues notice to Mamata Banerjee as witness in 2013 protest case
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Monday served a notice to former West Bengal chief minister

, asking her to record her statement in connection with a 2013 case involving a confrontation with police, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.

The notice was issued to Mamata as a witness and not as an accused, the sources said.

The notice has been issued to record her statement as part of the investigation, they added.

The case relates to an incident in April 2013, when Mamata, accompanied by a delegation of Trinamool ministers and MPs, visited Delhi to protest against the alleged assault on then West Bengal finance minister Amit Mitra by members of the Students' Federation of India (SFI).

World.title: 'Scrap Rs 500 notes': CM Naidu seeks to phase out big currency to curb corruption
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief minister

on Monday renewed his call for withdrawing Rs 500 currency notes, arguing that limiting cash transactions to smaller denominations and encouraging digital payments could help curb corruption.

Naidu said he had previously raised the proposal in a report on digital currency submitted to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and intended to continue pressing for the change.

âI will keep speaking on this. The notes of Rs 500, Rs 1,000 and Rs. 2,000 should be scrapped. Only notes of Rs 100 and Rs 200 should be retained,â he was quoted as saying by news agency IANS.

Speaking at a press conference, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) chief argued that reducing the circulation of high-value currency would make it harder to use large amounts of cash for corrupt activities.



He also stressed the importance of technology in improving economic opportunities.

âIf technology is perfect, wealth creation and poverty alleviation are not difficult,â he said.

Naidu claims NDA cut money power in local polls

Turning to the recent local body elections in Andhra Pradesh, Naidu said the results showed growing public support for the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA). He also claimed that the alliance had managed to reduce the influence of money power in the polls.





According to figures shared by the chief minister, the NDA secured 58.9 per cent of the combined vote in urban local body and Parishad elections. This was 3.6 percentage points higher than the 55.3 per cent it received in the 2024 general elections.

The YSR Congress Party's (YSRCP) vote share, meanwhile, fell from 39.81 per cent in 2024 to 33.56 per cent in the local body polls, a decline of 6.25 percentage points. The gap between the two sides stood at 25.34 percentage points, Naidu said.

He said the alliance's vote share in urban local body elections was 59.9 per cent, compared with 34.3 per cent for the YSRCP. The NDA also recorded a strike rate of 94 per cent in urban areas.

In Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections, the alliance polled 57.6 per cent of the votes against the YSRCP's 39.7 per cent. The difference between their vote shares was 17.9 percentage points in rural areas.

NDA wins majority of ZPTC and MPTC seats

Naidu said the alliance won 575 of the 659 ZPTC seats across Andhra Pradesh, leading in 27 of the state's 28 districts.

The YSRCP managed to win more seats than the alliance only in Alluri Sitarama Raju district. It failed to secure even one ZPTC seat in seven districts.

In Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) elections, the NDA won 7,803 of the 9,818 seats. The alliance is also expected to capture around 90 per cent of the Mandal President posts across the state.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The chief minister said the alliance's performance was equally strong in urban local bodies.

Of the 100 Mayor and Chairperson posts, it won 94, including 12 of the 13 mayoral positions and 82 of the 87 chairperson posts.

The TDP secured 70 of these posts, while the Jana Sena Party won 20 and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) four.

The alliance also won 3,233 of the 3,941 municipal wards, accounting for 82 per cent of the total. It secured a majority in 95 of the 100 urban local bodies and won every ward in 16 of them.

The YSRCP, by comparison, won only four urban local bodies and 558 wards. It failed to win a single ward in 22 urban local bodies, Naidu said.

He described the results as a reflection of public backing for good governance, social justice, new leadership and democratic values, adding that the alliance's support had increased significantly since the 2024 general elections.

World.title: 'There is an old saying': BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari explains her 'firecrackers cure illness' remark, apologises
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP MLA

on Monday defended herself after facing criticism for claiming that bursting firecrackers helps kill germs and viruses.

The actor-turned-politician said her statements were being deliberately twisted to garner TRP.

"Whenever I say something, people who oppose me use it to increase their TRP and views. Even if I cough or sneeze, the 'seku-maku' (a Bengali slang meaning secular and Marxists) pick it up," Adhikari told a Bengali TV channel.

"What I meant was that bursting firecrackers during Diwali-Kali Puja night kills germs, as told by our grandmothers and elders for generations. Lighting lamps drives away evil forces," she added.



Later in the day, the BJP MLA apologised for her remarks and said: "There is an old saying from our ancestors regarding these traditions. In essence, this is a festival of lights - a festival of lighting lamps - meant to eradicate social evils. In the past, through rituals, many such evils were addressed. Now, however, we live in the era of firecrackers, and given how much science has advanced, perhaps that perspective is no longer appropriate.





"If anyone has been hurt, I apologise. I am willing to retract my statement; consider it withdrawn. But the core idea remains: such social evils were - and still can be - eradicated."

Adhikari was trolled for claiming at a

pandal inauguration in her Tollygunge constituency on Saturday that bursting firecrackers could cure several diseases.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While addressing a gathering, a firecracker exploded loudly in front of her.

Continuing her speech, she said, "You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases. Our chief minister has said that we will burst firecrackers. How can Kali Puja be complete without green firecrackers? We will definitely burst green firecrackers."

"However, we will follow the guidelines issued by the police," she added.

Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday said the administration had taken necessary measures to enforce the Supreme Court's guidelines on noise pollution, though he acknowledged that some firecrackers were burst beyond the permitted hours.

World.title: Gift a toy to a poor child battling cancer in Chennai
World.content:
It is preternaturally tough being a child cooped up in a cancer ward, a typical day filled with syringes, scans and chemo, when it ought to have been filled with play, play and more play, the room generously scattered with carelessly thrown toys. Even in the cancer ward, a toy can open up a cheerful vista beyond those grey walls for that child receiving it. For some children, that simple joy is a luxury, poverty queering the pitch already ravaged by cancer. Voluntary organisations working with children battling the double whammy of cancer and poverty seek to make room for those vistas of joy, relying on donations of used toys.

This intervention is two-fold as the voluntary organisation works in tandem with donors of used toys. Those donors are “us”: the general public that could be holding on to toys outgrown by the children of the house, but not by the adults who harvest nostalgia from those playthings. No censure here for latching on to those toys that are no more played with. A choice could be made between making those used toys really useful again by donating them to these underprivileged children or buying these kids new toys. As a society, this intervention is required of us. And this Children’s Day is the time to start it.

Two initiatives at ICH Egmore

Examples of this intervention are to be found at the Government Institute of Child Health and Hospital for Children (ICH), Egmore. Pephands Foundation, a voluntary organisation, runs what it calls PepCares Hub where play is promoted for these children with the help of volunteers as well as donors, particularly donors of toys. At pephands.org, a dedicated page invites old toys as donations to support its work among children with cancer in Chennai.

Also in ICH Egmore, there is what is called the Oncology Kitchen, being run by the voluntary organisation Myrtle Social Welfare Network (myrtleindia.org), to provide one nutritious meal from Monday to Friday to children undergoing cancer treatment at the hospital. In this manner, the NGO takes one worry off the parents’ plate. Williams, founder, notes that besides taking worries off the plate, his NGO is also focussed on placing joys in these children’s hands: toys, clothes and books.

Donations can be dropped off at three locations: the voluntary organisation’s Perambur office in Kennedy Square, Myrtle Women’s Shelter Home in Alwarpet, or at ICH’s A block, third floor. Williams emphasises that donated items should be in good condition, ensuring that children can really enjoy them.



A bank for toys

Early this year, The Toy Bank (toybank.in), headquartered in Delhi but active across India through partnerships with other NGOs and individual volunteers, lightened the murkiness engulfing the lives of children undergoing cancer in Chennai through what it calls the “giftofjoy” initiative. With the help of the Kodungaiyur-based Emmimah Charitable Trust (EMC Trust), it distributed toys and educational materials to underprivileged children battling cancer.

As one of its focus areas, EMC Trust works with children affected by cancer and accepts toys, books, and clothes for their young beneficiaries. According to Esther U, secretary of the trust, these gifts bring much-needed cheer to children spending a considerable amount of time in hospitals. The organisation regularly caters to around 80 young patients. The patients visit with their parents every month to collect the nutrition kits. For details, visit emctrust.org.

Online platforms

For those unsure about connecting directly with a voluntary organisation or want to have a wide choice of NGOS, online platforms might be the place to go. Among other things, they promote toy donations from the benefit of underprivileged children.

One such platform is Donateinkind.in which helps bridge the gap between prospective donors and NGOs. The website allows users to browse donation categories and find organisations across India, along with their addresses and contact details. It also features testimonials given by the users. They also provide guidelines for NGOs interested in getting listed. In the category “toy donation”, it entreats the public to “donate toys to children’s homes, toy banks and toy libraries run by Non Governmental Organisations”. For Chennai, it has listed ‘Toys for Tots’ Drive by HAPPY HANDS Spreading Smiles, noting that volunteers connected with the NGO collect toys for toy libraries. It adds that so far, seven toy libraries have been set up at primary schools in Chennai.

Share At Door Step (shareatdoorstep.com) is another platform that helps donors find a voluntary organisation engaged in a service they would like to support. In its bio, Share At Door Step (SADS) mentions toys among a prominent list of things that are donated for the welfare of the underprivileged. As its name implies, Share At Door Step provides the donor with the advantage of making the donation without leaving the comfort of their home. They can provide their location and seek a pickup slot. The website notes that a “convenience fee” would be applicable. Donors can also rack up what SADS calls “share points", by which they are eligible for rewards, all of which are listed on the website.

So, this Children’s Day, let us give them their childhood back by making it a little less about what they are going through and a little more about what they deserve to experience. Let us remember that the United Nations has declared an International Day of Play (June 11), asserting every child’s right to play, irrespective of their station in life. UNICEF promotes this day. After all, every child deserves the freedom to play, the joy of discovering something new, and the magic of simply being a child. Poverty and cancer should not be allowed to obstruct the delivery of this right.

World.title: Nvidia plunges but tech shares rebound, oil prices slump
World.content:
Technology share prices clawed back last week's sharp losses on Monday (November 9, 2026), despite a plunge in Nvidia following a probe into its boss Jensen Huang over claims of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Oil prices fell over 5% on hopes for diplomatic talks aimed at ending the U.S.-Iran war, before paring losses.

Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after last Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress, leading to speculation lawmakers would seek to rein in tech firms.

But Wall Street on Monday (November 9, 2026) rebounded, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing more than 2%.

Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare said the rebound in equities was due to more than just the drop in oil prices.

"What we also have this morning is an inclination to buy into last week's weakness, and specifically into the large losses seen in the AI trade," he said in a note to clients.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which includes major chipmakers and AI firms, jumped more than 6%.

But the gains did not extend to Nvidia, which saw its shares slump more than 8% as trading got under way in New York, but recovered to stand down more than 5% in early afternoon trading.

Mr. O'Hare said Nvidia was being treated as a one-off story by investors for the moment.

"In other words, the stock is being penalized for Jensen Huang's personal transgression, which has invited a great deal of uncertainty into the mix, but the market isn't caught up in the notion that this situation is going to have a systemic domino effect," he said.

The news that Nvidia's board would investigate whether Mr. Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot, following his admission he was unfaithful to his wife, brought fresh uncertainty in the markets.

The New York Times last month reported that U.S. intelligence officials concluded a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed had been funnelling information to Beijing.

The executive, Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Mr. Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.

In a message to company employees released to media on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologised to his family and company staff.

Nvidia is a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models and one of the world's most valuable companies, and last year became the first to reach a market capitalisation of $5 trillion.

Technology analyst Dan Ives, at the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said the crisis would at the very least spark congressional inquiries and "create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons".

China on Monday (November 9, 2026) said the claims that it had spied on Mr. Huang were "baseless".

Europe's main stock markets rose following gains across much of Asia.

The dollar fell against its main rivals.

Oil prices continued to slide as Iran and the United States continued talking instead of fighting.

"Two month lows in oil have done much to bolster bruised sentiment in global markets, and the admittedly small signs of progress in peace talks adds to downward move," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at online trading and investing platform IG.

World.title: Hegseth faces expected U.S. House impeachment vote this week
World.content:
Pete Hegseth, the U.S. Defence Secretary, calls himself the Secretary of War, part of his effort to rebrand ‌a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year. Now, with ​a House impeachment vote expected this week, he could soon share something in common with an ⁠actual secretary of war.

William Belknap, who held that title in 1876, became the first, and to date only, civilian leader of the U.S. military to be impeached by Congress.

U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday (November 9, 2026), setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power.

Congressional sources say the resolution may have the simple majority needed to pass the Republican-controlled ‌House before Democrats take over on January 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds ‌majority ⁠is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats.

House Speaker Mike Johnson opposed the effort, saying impeachment “in ⁠the middle of hostilities abroad” would be “a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see.”

Voter anger over the war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections, intensifying Republican divisions over a conflict that Vice-President J.D. Vance has publicly questioned and Mr. Hegseth has ​defended as “courageous and historic.”

Accused of taking huge kickbacks, ‌Belknap handed President Ulysses Grant his resignation ahead of his scheduled impeachment vote and, according to a Senate history, “burst into tears.” The House impeached him anyway, but the Senate later acquitted him after falling short of the required two-thirds majority.

By contrast, Mr. Hegseth is promising to stay and fight.

Hegseth defiant

Mr. Hegseth has mounted a social media campaign, saying ‌in a defiant video message last week that he would not back down. He also drew a ​comparison to President Donald Trump, who was impeached twice, saying: “It didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”

Asked if he had enough Republican support to defeat the impeachment push, Mr. Hegseth ⁠said on Monday (November 9, 2026): “We’re not worried about that.” He announced a Tuesday (November 10, 2026) press conference, his first at the Pentagon since May.

Mr. Trump has backed Mr. Hegseth and condemned the impeachment push in an interview with CBS’s “60 Minutes” broadcast on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

“They want to impeach him. ‌Very unfair. We had two wars, we won both,” Mr. Trump said, according to a CBS transcript of the full interview.

Mr. Trump referred to both the Iran war, which is at an impasse, and to Venezuela, where the U.S. military deposed that country’s president, Nicolás Maduro, in a surprise January commando raid on his compound in the Venezuelan capital.

Defence spending at risk?

Some Republican lawmakers have expressed concern that if Mr. Hegseth stays, his strained relationship with Congress will undermine the Trump administration’s push for a $1.5 trillion defence spending package.

Mr. Massie, a Trump critic who is leaving office in January, warned in a statement on Monday (November 9, 2026) ‌that impeachment would be “much gentler” than what’s in store for Mr. Hegseth once Democrats take control in January.

“They will hold hearings and trials. President ​Trump should replace Secretary Hegseth now while he can still get a replacement confirmed in the Senate,” Mr. Massie said.

Democrats have promised to investigate Mr. Hegseth over issues including the firing of the chairman of the ⁠Joint Chiefs of Staff and other senior leaders.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Sunday (November 8, 2026) he was a “hard yes” on a ⁠measure to impeach Mr. Hegseth.

Mr. Massie’s articles of impeachment accuse Mr. Hegseth of “high crimes and misdemeanours” ranging from waging the Iran war to various alleged abuses of power, including violating the free speech rights of U.S. Senator Mark ‌Kelly, an Arizona Democrat.

Last year, Mr. Hegseth sought to prosecute Mr. Kelly after he and five other Democrats in Congress with backgrounds in the military and intelligence urged U.S. troops to refuse illegal orders. Mr. Hegseth accused them of sedition, something ​Mr. Trump at the time said in a social media post was “punishable by DEATH!”

World.title: Opposition accuses Delhi government of manipulating air pollution data; BJP alleges conspiracy behind Punjab farm fires
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Congress on Monday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Delhi government of manipulating air quality data a day after Deepavali, even as Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra alleged a “conspiracy” behind a sudden spike in stubble-burning incidents in AAP-ruled Punjab.

“The government which shuts down air quality monitoring stations on the night of Diwali, the government that does data fraud, how will you trust such a government?” asked AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj in a video posted on X.

Mr. Bharadwaj alleged that the government is manipulating pollution readings by installing monitoring stations near green areas and sprinkling water around them.

He warned that understating pollution levels could have serious public health consequences, including heart attacks, asthma attacks and respiratory failure.

The AAP had last week written to the Commission for Air Quality Management and the Central Pollution Control Board, accusing the Delhi government of manipulating air quality data.

Senior Congress leader Ajay Maken said PM2.5 data was available from only 23 of Delhi’s 59 monitoring stations at 1 a.m. on Monday.

In a post on X, he called for an inspection of stations from which no data could be retrieved and urged the authorities to rectify any defects immediately to ensure effective monitoring of air quality.

Meanwhile, Mr. Mishra alleged that the sharp rise in farm fires in Punjab on Deepavali was suspicious and warranted an investigation.

According to official data, Punjab recorded 1,152 farm fires on November 8, the highest single-day count this season, taking the cumulative figure to 4,459.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Mishra said satellite data showed around 100 to 125 farm fires daily on November 5, 6 and 7, before the figure surged to nearly 1,200 on Deepavali.

“We got calls from farmers in Punjab saying that stubble was being set on fire. Someone was setting stubble on fire and running away while farmers were celebrating Diwali with their families. This is a very serious issue and a conspiracy against Delhi, Punjab and farmers,” he said.

Mr. Mishra urged Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann to order an inquiry, register FIRs in cases of deliberate burning and examine the phone records of local representatives in the affected areas.

He also accused AAP leaders of running a campaign against Deepavali, firecrackers and “Sanatan traditions”.

Rejecting the allegations, Mr. Bharadwaj said the government should follow scientific principles while discussing pollution.

“Even if your Punjab theory is believed, smoke takes 2-3 days to travel from Punjab to Delhi. Stubble burnt on Diwali night in Punjab cannot reach Delhi in 10 minutes,” he said in a post on X.

He also questioned why Delhi alone is witnessing high pollution levels if farm fires in Punjab are responsible, arguing that the smoke would first have to pass through Haryana.

Mr. Mishra, however, claimed that the rise in Delhi’s pollution levels after Deepavali was lower this year than in previous years. He said pollution had increased by 43.33% in 2023 and around 10% in 2024, while this year it had declined by 1.33%.

Punjab rejects charge

Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema on Monday rejected Mr. Mishra’s allegations, accusing the BJP of deliberately defaming the State’s farmers.

“Kapil Mishra is lying,” Mr. Cheema told reporters in Chandigarh, responding to the Delhi Minister’s claim that farmers had reported their fields being deliberately set ablaze while they were celebrating Deepavali.

“Is Punjab the only paddy-producing state?” he asked, questioning why the BJP was blaming Punjab while overlooking stubble-burning incidents in neighbouring Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.

Mr. Cheema alleged that the BJP was targeting Punjab’s farmers because of their prolonged agitation against the three farm laws, which the Centre subsequently repealed.

He said the Punjab government had taken steps to discourage stubble burning, including providing farmers with modern machinery and equipment for stubble management.

Punjab AAP media in-charge Baltej Pannu also accused the BJP of attempting to divert attention from its failure to tackle air pollution in Delhi.

He claimed that Punjab had achieved “nearly 90% control” over stubble burning this year, following an 80% reduction last year, and cited a Union government reply in Parliament to support his assertion.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
World.content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

World.title: Bengaluru family murders: All seven bodies recovered
World.content:
In a significant development in the case of the murders of seven members of a family, which has sent shockwaves across Karnataka, the police have now successfully recovered all seven bodies. The recovery of the bodies was a crucial step in the probe into the ghastly murders, to build a strong case.

The latest breakthrough came on Monday (November 9, 2026), with the police recovering two more bodies from Shiradi Ghat, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka. The bodies have been identified as those of Shankar, the accused Indushekhar’s brother-in-law and his wife, Nalini, who were among the seven victims.

The development comes a day after the police recovered two bodies of the accused’s brother-in-law, Shivakumar and his wife, Divya, from the foothills of Chamundi Hills on Sunday (November 8, 2026). A day before that, the police had recovered two more bodies of the accused’s wife, Sunita and her mother, Roopavathi, from Salem, Tamil Nadu. On November 6, they had recovered the body of a minor boy, Puneeth, 7, from the foothills of Nandi Hills.

The families have decided to conduct the last rites for all seven together in one place. The bodies, most of them found in a highly decomposed state, will be handed over to the family after autopsies have been conducted.

Following a missing complaint by the deceased Nalini’s mother, Tungamma, the Srirampura police on November 5 detained Indushekhar and his 17-year-old minor daughter and rescued an 11-year-old boy from them. The duo confessed to having killed seven members of their family. Indushekhar’s wife, mother-in-law, two brothers-in-law, and their families. The accused has reportedly claimed that marital discord and humiliation by his wife’s family spurred him to take revenge.

Probe

Meanwhile, police teams investigating the ghastly murders are tracking down shops from which the accused allegedly purchased materials used to dispose of the bodies. Investigators are checking CCTV footage from these shops and recording statements from shop owners and staff to establish the purchases made by the accused and reconstruct his movements before and after the murders.

World.title: Ethanol blend row: Minister stands firm on claim, demands independent fuel testing
World.content:
Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Rizwan Arshad on Monday said that he stands by the test reports on ethanol blending in petrol that were released by him on November 6.

Addressing the media on Monday, Mr. Arshad said, “We stand by our test reports as the tests were done as per the prescribed procedure in laboratories recognised by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), which is a constituent board of the Quality Council of India (QCI).”

Failed to answer

He added, “As an elected government, I was expecting an official response from the Union government, whereas they have made the oil companies respond to us. I have examined their statements on our E20 findings. The OMCs’ release is more about technicalities, but they have failed to answer how much ethanol is in the petrol at our pumps.”

The Minister had on November 6 released the test reports of 63 petrol samples collected from petrol bunks across Karnataka. Of the 63 samples, those from Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) showed ethanol-blending levels of more than 20%, at 31.2%, 30.5% and 24.2%, respectively.

He slammed the oil companies for stating that the samples were not tested as per the prescribed procedure and that the laboratories used for testing were not those specified under the Order.

“The initial 63 samples were first given to the OMCs’ own laboratories at IOCL, BPCL and HPCL for testing. Not one of their test reports stated the ethanol percentage. IS 17021:2018, the standard the OMCs themselves cite, clearly lays down the procedures for testing ethanol content. Yet not a single OMC report gave that figure. It was the OMC laboratories’ failure to provide the required result that raised suspicion. On no grounds can the State’s tests be discredited for this. To protect consumers, the samples were then sent to NABL-accredited and ISO-certified laboratories,” he said.

Automobile manufacturers’ concern

Highlighting concerns raised by vehicle manufacturers, he said, “On July 28, 2026, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) wrote to the Union Petroleum Ministry flagging chloride and sulphur in E20 fuel and the damage it was causing to vehicle parts. Within a week, amid pressure from the Centre, the letter was withdrawn. ACKO Insurance told a customer that engine damage from ‘incorrect fuel usage’ would not be covered under insurance. Hyundai, Toyota and other automobile manufacturers wrote in their manuals that using fuel other than E10 would void the warranty.”

The Minister also noted that the report on the same subject by the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) remains hidden from the public. He added that the Attorney General had told the Supreme Court that E20 was still an experiment, but later issued a clarification.

He said the Karnataka government cannot be silenced and will not step back like industry bodies, companies and other individuals who, he claimed, had been silenced or may step back due to pressure.

Mr. Arshad also expressed his disapproval of the Union government’s call for a joint inspection of E20 blending in petrol. He said, “A few months ago, when I wrote to the Union government seeking inspection and testing, they did not respond. Now, when the test reports are out, they are asking for a joint inspection. What is the point of conducting an inspection after setting the system right?”

Quality monitoring

Responding to the OMCs’ statement that the problem exists only in samples collected from particular petrol pumps and not elsewhere, the Minister said, “The OMCs’ own statement says ethanol blending is ‘a controlled and automated process’ carried out at their refineries and depots. If so, the blend in every litre of petrol is decided at the OMCs’ six terminals serving Karnataka, not at the pump. A dealer only sells what the tanker delivers and has no role in the blend. The excess ethanol found is a failure at the source, and the responsibility lies with the OMCs alone.”

He maintained that by conducting this exercise and exposing these gaps in the OMCs’ systems, the Karnataka government has created a sense of deterrence across the country.

‘Take fuel testing out of OMCs’ hands'

Stating that his department wants to hold a meeting with the OMCs, he said, “The meeting aims to inform them about conducting periodic tests of petrol samples by the State government. However, they cannot be tested at the OMCs’ laboratories. They have to be tested at third-party laboratories because when OMCs test samples in their own laboratories, they will provide reports as per their convenience. That is a clear conflict of interest. We will try to convince them, or else the matter will be escalated.”

Later in the day, while sharing a clip from a press conference of Union Minister H.D.
